# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-23

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The one question that decides Toronto's July: which of the club's role gaps can the coach close by dressing someone already on the roster, and which require a trade or a signing? With the season finished at 59-13-5, every gap is now a construction problem, not a tonight problem.

**Toughness is missing.** Zero players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Jackman tops the club at 75, Roberts at 73, McCabe at 73. This is not a form artifact; these are base grades. The coach quantified it on April 9 (fourth-line mean 57), and the March 19 structural finding is confirmed by this final sample. No internal move fixes it. Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 24, 82 base) remains the only league-wide player closing this gap alongside faceoffs simultaneously. Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 25, $400K, 2 years) is the cheaper alternative. One of them has to come.

**Faceoffs are thin.** Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ draw-taker. Chlup at 75 is next. Lines 3-4 have no credible option above 75. Richards at 70 is the best the coach can deploy internally, which is what he did on March 16. The coach flagged this again on April 21: "no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 80." Bell's 82 FACE solves both gaps in one acquisition. Avery's 93 FACE over-solves faceoffs but under-solves toughness.

**Checking is covered but aging.** Six players at 80+: Jackman 87 (24), Roberts 86 (38), McCabe 86 (29), Tucker 83 (30, not lined), Fischer 82 (24), Upshall 80 (21). Roberts carries the heaviest defensive load at 21.4 MPG and he is 38 with an expiring contract. Remove him and the club drops to five, with Tucker unlined and Upshall at 21 still developing. Dress Tucker for the playoffs if possible; he is a 30-year-old chip and the GM already holds him as a trade asset.

**Scoring is covered in volume but the age curve is dangerous.** Mogilny at 94 is the top scorer but he is 36 and his rate fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g this season. Roberts at 88 is 38 and expiring. The young scorers are Gaborik 92 (23), Afinogenov 90 (25), and that is it. The club needs a second young top-six winger. Iginla (CGY, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, 27, $6.50M expiring) supersedes Heatley and Doan per the April 12 note. CGY cannot retain him at $14.43M profit with 10 expiring deals.

**Durability is thin.** Only four at 80+ INJU: Roberts 98 (38), Afinogenov 95 (25), Fischer 92 (24), Abid 90 (25). Eminger at 75 (21) is the young one who must climb. A third or fourth-line injury to the top four would expose this. Not a trade target; a development priority for Eminger and whoever fills the fourth line.

**Goalies are solved for the playoffs but not after.** Belfour (40, $6.50M, expiring) is the best goaltender on the roster at GAA 1.93 and SV 0.931 in 37 games. He walks in July. Luongo (26, 2 years, GAA 2.67, SV 0.889) is the starter. The backup situation after Belfour leaves is Ouellet at 23 (INTE 69, REBC 75, ENDU 60) and Tellqvist at 25 (REBC 64, INTE 66). Neither reads as a capable number-two. The Jan 15 standing order to fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender is still open and becomes the priority once July opens.

**Speed, playmaking, stamina, and clutch are all covered.** Speed has 21 at 80+; playmaking 11; stamina 11; clutch 9. No action needed.

## Trajectory

**Is this club aging into a cliff?** No. The age shape is correct for a contender that becomes a dynasty: 13 players at 23 or under, 12 at 24-29, and four veterans at 34+ who are all at the end of their careers. Three of those four (Belfour $6.50M, Roberts $2.70M, Mogilny $5.50M) either walk or are walking. The real danger is not the age curve. It is that 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire in the same July, and six of them are the future core.

**The $60M payroll has room.** Revenue is $106.07M, profit $31.56M, and there is no cap. The club can absorb $15-20M in new contracts in July 2005 and still profit by $10M+. Money is not the constraint. The constraint is whether the players sign, because 13 of 30 rostered players are free agents in the same summer.

**The renewal order, in priority:**

**Gaborik** is the single most important contract on this roster. 99 points in 82 games at age 23 on $1.10M with POTE 90. If he reaches the market he commands $5-7M. A 5-year deal at $3-4M is the target. If we lose him, the 2005-06 lineup has a 30-point hole on the first wing.

**Richards** at 66 points and $1.00M is the second lock. The coach flagged his decline from 1.08 to 0.71 pts/g, which is a system-fit question, not a value question. At 24 with POTE 88, a 4-5 year deal at $2-3M is cheap insurance. His trade value peaks the moment people believe he is stalling.

**Nash** at 20, 39 points, POTE 95: 5-6 years. **Eminger** at 21, POTE 99, 23 points: 5-6 years. Both are blue-chip futures whose prices reset the instant they have a full season in the top four.

**Abid** at $400K for 66 points and POTE 94 at 25 is the cheapest player on the roster by a wide margin. His renewal will reset to $2-3M regardless. Sign him to 3-4 years in July and the cost is locked. If he leaves as a UFA we lose the only 80-TOUG forward we have.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M with 44 points: 3-4 years at $3-4M. Not a star, but a proven top-pairing right defenseman who won't get better. Get the years done.

**The 2006 summer is lighter but has one problem.** The 2-year group (9 players, $15.44M) is dominated by Mogilny at $5.50M, who will be 37 and producing 0.5-0.7 pts/g. That contract expires naturally. No action needed. Chlup at $2.34M and Luongo at $1.60M both have two years left, so they are safe through 2006-07.

**The sunk-cost contracts that constrain 2007-09:** Fischer at $3.70M for four more years with production falling from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g. Sundin at $8.40M for five more years at age 34→39 with POTE 60. Neither can be renegotiated mid-contract. Together they lock $12.10M for 2007-08 and 2008-09 with declining returns. Fischer is a summer-2008 trade-bait candidate once he has a season of low production to make him cheap for a contender. Sundin at 38 with $8.40M will be untradeable.

**Draft capital is zero.** Only a 4th-rounder. Every trade this summer must be funded with players, and the only chips are Tucker ($1.30M, 3 GP, 30 years old) and the 4th. This means the Iginla pursuit must work as a UFA signing, not a trade, unless a third-party package materializes.

**The three moves that protect the next three seasons:**

1. Lock Gaborik, Nash, Eminger, and Abid on long deals in July 2005. Richards follows. This is the entire dynasty hinges on this one summer.
2. Sign Iginla (93 base, 140 pts, 27, POTE unknown but TOUG 85) as a UFA or trade target to close the RW scoring void Mogilny leaves. He is not available at the deadline (CGY still in contention), but at 70 points with $14.43M profit and 10 expiring, they cannot retain him.
3. Sign Chlup to a 5-6 year extension before his $2.34M rookie price evaporates. At 19 with POTE 95 and 59 points, one more season at 60 points makes him a $5M player.



**On the outstanding task #2** (Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for the goalie trade window): This is delivered and closed. Luongo arrived on the roster in early February 2005 at 91 base, 26 years old, $1.60M with 2 years remaining. The January 15 mandate for a high-90s goalie is fulfilled. DiPietro was eliminated as a target on March 14 at 79 base after a full 52-game sample. The goalie situation is solved: Luongo is the starter, Belfour and Ouellet provide playoff cover, and Tellqvist is depth. No further monitoring needed.

## Calendar

The trade deadline passed 35 days ago on March 19, so the buyer/seller question is resolved: we finished first in the East at 133 points, and the deadline is gone. What remains is the summer plan for 13 expiring contracts worth $22.10M and the off-season target list.

**Gaborik** is the immediate priority. At 91 base, 131 points in 82 games, age 23, $1.10M — he is the second-best player on the roster behind Sundin and his contract expires. Lock on 6 years the day free agency opens. Every other renewal waits behind him.

**Richards** at 82 base, 66 points, age 24, $1.00M is the second lock. His rate dipped from 1.08 to 0.83 this season but the coach notes the expected direction is up at 24. Five years.

**Eminger, Upshall, Nash** are the developmental core: three players aged 20-21 carrying POTE 99 and base grades of 76-78 at $1.20M or less. Renew all three on 5-6 years. Upshall's 47 points in 55 games at a 0.85 rate this season says the development is on track. Nash at 39 points in 69 games is behind schedule but he's 20.

**Chistov** at 78 base, age 22, 20 points, earned his look per the coach (minutes rose to 14.0 and rate held). Renew 5 years. **Alexeev** at 76 base, POTE 94, age 23, 30 points in 55 games: same treatment, 5 years.

**Kaberle** at 84 base, age 27, 44 points: two years. He's a good top-four D but not a franchise anchor and two years is cheaper.

**Abid** at 79 base, age 25, 66 points on a $0.40M deal: two years. The coach's checking-wing gap is structural (zero players above 80 TOUG in stored grades), and Abid at 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG is the only roster answer.

**Tellqvist** at 77 base, age 25: three years per the GM's standing order to let him develop with potential in the high 90s. He costs $0.80M. With Luongo at 91 (2 years left) and Ouellet at 81 (2 years left), he provides the third body.

**Belfour** at 92 base, age 40, $6.50M: let him walk. The GM confirmed this. He carries the team through the playoffs; then the $6.50M is freed. The over-80 pick mechanic is worth one test in July — if a non-contender will send a pick for a one-year 92 goalie, take it — but the GM has said he walks and there is no urgency.

**Roberts** at 87 base, age 38, $2.70M, 88 points in 75 games: let him walk. The coach flagged his 21.4 MPG at that age as unsustainable. His production is real but the injury risk rises each year, and the $2.70M buys a replacement.

**Mogilny** is NOT expiring. He has 2 years left at $5.50M. His 94-point season (1.15/g at age 36) is the best of any 36-year-old you will find, and the March panic about a collapse to 0.79 was a mid-season stretch that recovered. Ride the two years. At 38 the decline will be severe, but the contract structure means the problem is solved in 2007, not today.

**Tucker** is NOT expiring either. Two years at $1.30M, 79 base, POTE 79, 8 points in 40 games this season. He contributes nothing. At below-80 the over-80 mechanic does not help, so no pick comes back. Keep him as fourth-line depth or move him in July to any club that will take a $1.30M salary for a body. Low urgency.

**The summer target list, in order:** Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 points, $1.10M expiring) is the cheapest high-upside signing available. Iginla (CGY, 27, 93 base, 140 points, $6.50M expiring) is the big swing — he closes Mogilny's void and the toughness gap in one player. The freed $9.20M from Belfour and Roberts covers both if CGY can't retain him. Bell (CHI, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG) addresses the coach's checking gap directly. Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, POTE 91) replaces Roberts at defence. All four are realistic because their clubs are either rebuilding or cash-strapped.

**Draft capital is nil.** We hold only a 5th-rounder (our own). Every package must be player-for-player. This limits how we acquire Bell or Stuart if those clubs want a pick in the return.

## League scan

The July market decides whether Toronto defends this 133-point season or watches the core scatter as free agents. With no draft picks and a single tradeable chip (Tucker plus the 4th), every acquisition must be a UFA signing, which makes the expiring-player pool the entire board. I queried toughness leaders, faceoff leaders, high-point expirers, goalies, and young high-potential players across all 30 clubs. Three names stand above the rest.

**Scatchard** is the player the coach has been asking for by name without naming him. NYI, C, 29, 85 base, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 84 FACE, $1.40M expiring. He is the only player in the league closing toughness, checking, AND faceoffs simultaneously whose contract actually ends this July. NYI at 84 points with 13 expiring deals and $12.46M profit cannot retain everyone. He carries only 26 points in 78 games at 10.9 MPG, which is fine; that is a third-and-fourth-line role, exactly where the gap lives. Bell from CHI is still better (80 base, 88 TOUG, 82 FACE, 24 years old) but has two years left and is untradeable without a protected player.

**Iginla** closes the Mogilny hole and the structural toughness ceiling in one signing. CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring. CGY at 70 points with $14.43M profit and 10 expiring deals cannot retain a $6.50M wing. The question is whether $6.50M plus whatever Iginla demands in new terms fits the $31.56M profit window. At our $106M revenue it should. If CGY finds a trade partner first, we miss him. The only counter is speed: be ready to offer on July 1.

**Lalime** at 92 base is the backup goalie the January standing order demanded. OTT, G, 30, $1.90M expiring, 28 wins in 68 starts. OTT at 77 points with 11 expiring on $42.80M payroll and $32.36M profit are pure sellers. Nabokov (SJ, 90 base, POTE 90, GAA 2.66, SV 0.872, 29, $3.60M expiring) is the alternative if Lalime signs elsewhere, and arguably the better long-term option given the POTE 90 and superior actual numbers. Both hit UFA July 1.

**Barnaby** is the best available value. NYR, LW, 32, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 53 points in 78 games at 17.8 MPG, $1.50M expiring. NYR carry $78.14M payroll at zero profit; they are shedding contracts by any means available. He does not solve faceoffs (59 FACE) but at 88 TOUG he is the highest-toughness player with real production on a cheap expiring deal. If Scatchard and Barnaby both arrive, lines 3 and 4 have a checking centre and a tough wing respectively.

**Belanger** is the faceoff insurance policy. LA, C, 27, 82 base, 97 FACE, 79 TOUG, 83 CHKG, $700K expiring. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll are selling. If Scatchard is taken, Belanger at 97 FACE still wins draws on lines 3-4, and 79 TOUG is within one point of the 80 threshold. At $700K he costs almost nothing.

**Bouwmeester** is the surprise on the defence market. FLA, D, 21, 81 base, POTE 95, 27 points in 79 games, already playing 33.3 minutes a night, $1.20M expiring. He is not a prospect waiting for minutes; he is a 21-year-old carrying a top-pairing role right now. FLA at 76 points with 19 expiring and only $13.64M profit cannot retain everyone. He would pair with Eminger or take a slot alongside Roberts if we keep him, or replace him outright.

**Drury** and **Havlat** are the top-six forward alternatives if Iginla goes elsewhere. Drury (BUF, LW, 28, 89 base, 99 points, 79 TOUG, 84 FACE, $2.00M expiring) is the better player but arrives without the RW fit. Havlat (OTT, LW, 24, 87 base, 103 points, $900K expiring) is the cheapest elite scorer available and the same age as our core.

**Vandermeer** and **Orpik** are the cheap tough-defence depth. Vandermeer (PHI, D, 25, 76 base, POTE 91, 86 TOUG, 84 CHKG, $400K expiring) from a 82-point club with $2.14M profit. Orpik (PIT, D, 24, 70 base, POTE 97, 84 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $1.10M expiring) from 85-point PIT. Neither starts on night one but both at 76 and 84+ TOUG give the back end the toughness the club currently does not have.

**What I would NOT pursue:** Daze at CHI. Confirmed age is 29, TOUG 57, and he carries only 57 points despite 127 total (wait, that is points = 127 in the query). At 29 with 57 TOUG he fails the toughness gap, and at $3.00M expiring from a $31.73M-profit CHI club he is not cheap. Kovalchuk from ATL is better than Heatley in age and production but both are LW/RW with low toughness, and ATL will fight to keep at least one. Heatley at 91 base and 131 points is the fallback if Iginla walks to another club, but ATL at 84 points with $25.99M profit may re-sign both.

## Trade construction

With the regular season finished at 133 points and zero draft capital beyond a 4th-rounder, almost every target on the July board is a UFA signing, not a trade. Iginla, Lalime, Nabokov, Scatchard, Barnaby, Havlat, Belanger, Bouwmeester — all expiring, all signable on July 1 without giving up a player. The trade market matters only for the two targets who have years left and therefore cannot be signed as UFAs: **Bell** (CHI, 2 years remaining) and **Avery** (LA, 2 years remaining). These are the only two acquisitions that require a proposal the other side accepts, and both packages close the same gaps (toughness and faceoffs) that zero internal options fix.

**Avery via Koltsov** is the cleanest proposal on the board. We give Koltsov (LW, 24, POTE 94, $1.10M, 2 years left, 19 points in 38 games at 0.28 pts/g). We get Avery (LW, 25, 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 years left). LA at 48 points with 14 expiring deals on $52.43M payroll needs young talent for their rebuild, and a POTE 94 forward at $1.10M is exactly what a selling club collects. We pay less than half the salary, get 83 TOUG and 93 FACE (both above the 80 threshold the coach demanded), and LA gets their best version of a rebuilding asset. This package was confirmed viable on April 19. Acceptance is likely but not certain — the AI's player valuation is unknown.

**Bell via Koltsov plus Tucker plus the 4th** is the stronger hockey outcome but the harder negotiation. Bell is 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 — a cleaner solution than Avery on every defensive grade. CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit and 10 expiring deals are sellers of veterans, but Bell has two years left and POTE 81. The argument for CHI: Koltsov's POTE 94 exceeds Bell's POTE 81 by 13 points, Koltsov is the same age, and they collect a depth veteran plus a 4th-rounder on top. They are effectively swapping a high-floor player for a higher-ceiling one plus assets. The risk: CHI may value Bell's proven 82-base over Koltsov's 19-point season, or may not value a 4th-rounder enough to close.

**If neither lands**, the summer still works without a trade. Scatchard (NYI, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 84 FACE, $1.40M) is expiring and hits UFA on July 1 — he solves the same gaps without requiring a package. Barnaby (NYR, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, $1.50M) is also expiring from a $78M-payroll club at zero profit. Two UFA signings cover what a trade would. The trade proposals are the premium path; the UFA path is the insurance policy.

**What I would not do**: offer any core defenseman, any top-six forward, or Chlup. The March 19 standing order holds and the trajectory analysis confirms: lock Gaborik, Nash, Eminger, Abid first, and the core stays together.

## Owed

**Luongo monitoring and DiPietro tracking (asked 2005-01-19, due by 2005-02-20):** This job is complete. The outcome was better than the February window required.

**Luongo** is on Toronto's roster. 94 overall, 26 years old, $1.60M, 2 years remaining, 45 starts this season. He arrived through the season and the GM closed all goalie monitoring on 2005-03-19 with the order "Keeping him and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs." The trade window this task existed to serve is shut because the target walked in the door.

**DiPietro** was eliminated on 2005-03-14 at 52 GP reading 79 base overall. No sample size closes an 11-point gap to the "high-90s" standard the GM set on 2005-01-15. He is permanently off the list.

Nothing to report that has changed in the last two weeks. The task is dead in the best possible way.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-23
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-23

Next game vs PIT on Sunday 24 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

With 6 games left and a 24-34 Pittsburgh club coming to town, this is the window to put opportunity behind the kids who have earned it and been benched for it.

**Chlup** at 19 is the model answer. 16.9 minutes a night, 59 points in 71 games, line two, morale 98. He is getting everything he has earned and more. Leave him exactly where he is through the final stretch.

**Gaborik** at 23 plays every game, 20.5 MPG, 99 points in 82 games. No development question exists. He is past that stage.

**Nash** gets 13.1 MPG on the third line and 39 points in 69 games. His production problem is real but it is an offseason system-fit review, not an opportunity problem. He is getting his games.

**Klesla** plays all 82 games at 14.8 MPG. His issue is 30 points at 0.37 per game on flat minutes for a second straight year. Opportunity is not the gap. The offseason sell decision is.

**Eminger** at 64 games and 15.5 MPG is getting top-four defence minutes and returning 23 points. He has been given the chance and is not taking it. His contract expires and that is a GM offseason problem.

**Chistov** at 13.1 MPG on the third line, 20 points in 68 games, sits in the right spot for his role. No change.

**Upshall** has recovered from his March minutes collapse. 7.9 MPG on the fourth line, 20 points in 68 games, morale back to 91. Fourth line is his level. No change.

**Spacek** at 19 on the fourth line with 7.6 MPG and 17 points in 50 games is getting an appropriate depth role. The 10 MPG target is gone. No change.

**Colaiacovo** has 17.9 MPG in 31 games and 12 points. The GM has made clear that his limited games are deliberate rotation to develop younger players. That reasoning stands. No change.

**Ouellet** as backup at 13 starts, 40.2 MPG when he plays. Appropriate. No change.

**Alexeev** at 23 is the problem. 30 points in 55 games is 0.55 per game, which beats dressed wingers Chistov at 0.29 and Upshall at 0.29. He has been scratched despite outproducing them. That is not a development call, that is a production-to-ice-time mismatch and someone in the lineup does not deserve their spot over him.

**Spezza** at 21 with POTE 99 is the biggest development failure on this roster. 6.7 MPG across 46 games, 15 points, morale at 88, which is the lowest of any young player on the roster. The season was flagged as a write-off in late March, but there are 6 games left and a bad opponent on Sunday. Even two or three games in the lineup starts the habit of giving him the puck that camp is supposed to build on.

**Stahle** at 20 has played 4 games all season. POTE 96, morale 99, and he has been invisible. Six games remaining, one bad opponent on Sunday, and he is getting zero. Give him a shift or two over the final stretch simply to get him in the game.

## Development trends

This is the final development read of the season, and the defensive evaluation the GM asked me to deliver each game lands here with season totals locked. The question: who moved, who stalled, and what does the answer change for next year?

**Chlup** is the only young player ascending. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while minutes went from 11.0 to 18.2 across 71 games. He kept his production rate even as his load nearly doubled, which at 19 is the profile of a first-line centre built to handle it. Everything the April 12 call said holds. He is the centrepiece of the next two seasons and no offseason decision should compromise his role.

**Kaberle** is the other man moving up. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes up from 19.4 to 21.5 over 74 games. At 27 he is entering his prime and the numbers are climbing. He is the keeper and the top pair anchor. No question.

**McCabe** needs the GM's attention. His full season rate is 0.76 pts/g, which clears the 0.60 threshold and keeps him off the sell list. But the inside of the season tells a different story: 1.42 pace through the first 24 games, then 0.48 over the last 58. At 29 with 4 years and $3.0M remaining, a player who finishes at 0.48 pace is trending toward a number well below 0.76 next year. I am not selling him now. But I would plan for 0.50-0.60 from him in 2005-06, not 0.76, and if his first 20 games come in under 0.50 he goes straight onto the trade block while he still has market value.

**Jackman** at 0.39 pts/g on 29.4 MPG over 80 games is the confirmed sell the April 7 call identified. The load is the problem and nothing fixed it. $0.70M x 3 is his selling point: the cheapest top-pair minutes available. Move him this summer.

**Klesla** at 0.31 over 82 games is the third straight declining season: 0.38 at 22, 0.36 at 23, 0.31 at 23. Minutes flat at 14.9. Sell at $0.90M x 2. The April 7 call is locked.

**Eminger** at 0.37 on 15.9 MPG over 64 games is the expiring chip. $1.2M is gone in July and the slide never stopped. Any return beats a UFA loss.

**Fischer** at 0.63 to 0.50 looks like a decline but his minutes went from 20.8 to 22.9. He is absorbing more defensive-zone work and his rate diluted. At 24 with the two-way game the GM values, the GM's keeper call stands and the numbers back it.

**Spezza, Spacek, Upshall** all collapsed on minutes. Spezza: 0.24 pts/g on 4.6 MPG. Spacek: 0.28 on 5.2. Upshall: 0.27 on 4.8. None of them got enough games to judge development. They need a real camp audition next September or they stop being dressed.

**Sundin** (34), **Mogilny** (36), **Roberts** (38): all declining on pace. Sundin went 1.46 to 0.97, Mogilny 1.62 to 0.83, Roberts 1.29 to 0.86. All got more minutes (21.7, 19.1, 21.4) while scoring less. The aging core is doing more and producing less. Planning for next year should assume continued decline across all three.

**Richards** at 0.71 over 80 games on flat minutes is still the April 7 flag: system-fit review before he is pencilled as a first-line centre again.

**Delivering obligation #1** (defensive evaluation, every game): Season-end defensive grades are Kaberle keep and ascend, Fischer keep and stable under increased load, McCabe trajectory flag at 29, Jackman sell, Klesla sell, Eminger trade before free agency, Colaiacovo at 31 games needs a camp look.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Every player is trending up and the vast majority are at 100.

**Spezza** is the lowest man on the sheet at 88, up 3 from the last save. He's scratched, running 6.7 minutes a night in 46 games. At 0.33 pts/g on those minutes he's not earning a recall on production alone, and his morale is recovering. Nothing to fix tonight.

**Upshall and Spacek** sit at 91 and 91, both climbing. They're on the fourth line at 7.9 and 7.6 MPG respectively, squarely in the depth-forward band. Their morale reflects their role and the team's winning streak. No adjustment.

**Everyone else** is at 96 or above with positive or flat movement. **Jackman** at 29.6 MPG carries the heaviest load on the roster and is still at 100 with a +5. **Richards** at 98 and 16.1 MPG on the third line is slightly below the 17-minute band I'd expect for a player with 66 points, but at 98 and rising there's no friction to address. The winning is doing the work.

No change.

## Role composition

Are the units built for the jobs you ask of them, and if not, is the fix a lineup change or a phone call? For tonight against a 24-34-15 Pittsburgh club, the answer is mostly that the units fit and the one thing that doesn't is beyond my control.

**L1 and P1** are the best units on the roster by every role metric and need no touching. Sundin (faceoffs 91, clutch 95, scoring 93) and Gaborik (scoring 98, playmaking 99, speed 99) are elite. Roberts (checking 85) and Jackman (checking 90, toughness 77) give the line a defensive spine that most scoring lines lack. Kaberle and Fischer on the blue line round it out. No change, any direction.

**L2** is built to score and scores. Mogilny (94 scoring, 94 speed), Afanogenov (92 scoring, 92 playmaking), Chlup (faceoffs 80, the only reliable draw man outside Sundin). Checking mean 70 and toughness 64 are the lowest of the four lines, but that is what a second scoring line looks like and the pairing of Chlup as the center means at least the draws aren't hopeless. Leave it.

**L3** is where I'd look for problems and what I find is a mismatch on stamina. Checking mean 75 is the best of the four even-strength lines, and Richards at 75 checking and 75 faceoffs is a reasonable third-line centre. But stamina mean 63, with only Richards (87) above the line, means Nash, Chistov, Eminger, and Klesla will be gassed by mid-shift in a physical game. The fix isn't to swap players, it's to keep this line's shifts shorter and give L4 more of the game. Reason class: matchup.

**L4 faceoffs are a roster gap, not an arrangement problem.** Spacek, Abid, and Upshall produce a faceoff mean of 52 and a best of 55. Nobody on the roster outside our top-three centres wins a draw above 75, and all four are already slotted higher. The fourth line cannot win a puck clean in their own end on a draw, which means every zone start is a coin flip at best. This is the thing the GM needs to hear: **we need a bottom-six centre who wins faceoffs above 60.** The next draft or waiver wire is the only source. I have raised this before and it persists.

**K1 versus K2** is the one composition question worth a note. K2 (Chlup, McCabe, Jackman, Abid) has checking mean 84 against K1's 79, with Jackman (90) and McCabe (85) as two of our four best checkers. K1 runs Sundin (91 faceoffs, 92 checking) and Roberts (85 checking), which is arguably a waste of two top-six players on the kill. For tonight against a 24-34 team, it doesn't matter. Against a quality opponent, I'd make K2 the primary unit and save K1's players for 5-on-5. No change tonight.

**The fourth-line checking gap I flagged on April 13** recorded checking mean 62 and toughness mean 57. The current brief shows 74 and 65 for L4, which is a substantial shift in the right direction, likely from players moving between units over the last ten days. I'm not retiring the memory yet; the faceoff problem is unchanged, and I'll re-read checking at season's end before drawing a conclusion.

## Opponent matchup

**PIT is not a team that can punish us, and our current structure already has advantages at every position, so the right call is no change.**

**The matchup at centre.** Sundin (FACE 91) draws Lemieux (FACE 68). That's a 23-point gap at the dot on their first line. Chlup (FACE 80) faces Eastwood (FACE 80), a wash. Richards (FACE 75) draws Holzinger (FACE 50), another easy win. Spacek (FACE 55) gets Fata (FACE 81) and we lose that one, but it's the fourth line. We win three of four draws without changing anything.

**Fischer and Jackman against Lemieux.** The auto-pairing already puts our first pair (Fischer CHKG 92, Jackman CHKG 92) against their most dangerous player. Lemieux at 39 has PASS 99 and DEKG 98 but CHKG 66 and TOUG 61. Two 24-year-olds with 92 checking will make him earn every puck. This pairing needs no adjustment.

**Their blue line is soft everywhere.** Lupaschuk (OVR 70) and Pushor (OVR 67) are their third pair. Our L3 (Richards/Nash/Chistov) will get those matchups through auto-pairing, and Gaborik at OVR 98 will feast on whoever he draws regardless. Their best D is Rozsival/Tarnstrom at 76/77 — below our worst pair.

**Their power play is 32/276, which is 11.6%.** They generate volume (4 chances per game) but score less than a half-goal per game on the man advantage. Our PK1 of Sundin/Roberts/Fischer/Kaberle doesn't need to be sharp against this group.

**Luongo** starts. OVR 94, morale 100, no injury flag. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order.

## Owed

**The standing job: defenceman evaluation for end-of-season cuts.** The season is at or near completion for every D on the roster, so these are final or nearly final numbers. That's the only thing that's changed since my last delivery: the samples are now locked.

**McCabe** finished at 82 GP, 62 points, 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG at 29. He cleared the 0.60 sell threshold and his season rate held through every re-read. At $3.00M x 4 years he's the anchor. He stays, period.

**Fischer** at 77 GP, 41 points, 0.53 pts/g on 22.4 MPG. The GM called him a keeper and I conceded. No new argument. He stays.

**Kaberle** at 74 GP, 44 points, 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG with a career year. $1.90M expiring is the only open question, but the GM said "star defenseman" and I'm not reopening that.

**Jackman** is now at 80 GP, 37 points, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. That's slightly worse than the 0.48 I noted on March 23. The load is still eating his production. $0.70M x 3 years makes him the cheapest top-pair minutes available anywhere. Sell this offseason. Final call.

**Klesla** finished at 82 GP, 30 points, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Two consecutive declining seasons locked (0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23). $0.90M x 2. Sell.

**Eminger** at 64 GP, 23 points, 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG. Even worse than my 0.38 note from March 30. Contract expires in July; after that he's a UFA loss with zero return. Trade before July or lose him for nothing.

The bottom four (Colaiacovo, St. Jacques, Safronov, Stahle) are development depth. No sell case, no roster spot problem.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-21

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The defining structural problem going into July is that Toronto has zero players at 80+ toughness and exactly one elite faceoff man in a 34-year-old — these two gaps are the same gap, and no amount of line shuffling fixes them.

**Toughness — missing.** The roster tops out at Jackman's 75. Tucker, the internal band-aid from December, is at 70 and not even lined. The Coach reconfirmed this on April 15: "no forward outside L1-L2 who checks above 75." This is structural, not form-based, confirmed since March. Six teams in the league have a 90+ toughness forward; we have none within 15 points.

**Faceoffs — thin, and aging.** Sundin at 90 is the only 80+ draw-taker and he is 34 with one year left. Roberts at 75, Chlup at 75, Richards at 70. If Roberts walks (he is 38 and expiring), we drop to one elite faceoff man on a one-year deal, with no successor. This gap widens every year we do not address it.

**Checking — adequate on defence, thin up front.** Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86 give us three 80+ blueliners. On forward positions, only Fischer at 82 and Upshall at 80 clear the bar. Tucker at 83 is sitting on the roster unlined; lining him is free but his toughness (70) means he fixes checking without touching the real problem.

**Durability — thin and collapsing.** Only Roberts (98), Afinogenov (95), Fischer (92), and Abid (90) sit at 80+. Roberts is 38 and expiring. That removes the single most durable player on the roster, and nobody at 80+ replaces him on defence.

**Scoring and speed — covered.** 10 players at 80+ scoring, 21 at 80+ speed. These are not gaps. Mogilny (36) and Roberts (38) walk, but Gaborik (23), Richards (24), Nash (20), and Eminger (21) are the future core and they are lined.

**The coach can fix checking by lining Tucker.** He gives a fourth 80+ forward checker at 83 CHKG for zero cost. This does not fix toughness. The toughness and faceoff gaps require acquisition.

**Bell and Avery remain the two targets.** Bell (CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) closes all three gaps in one player and is 24. Avery (LA, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years) is the cheapest fix but lower ceiling. Neither deal can happen at a deadline; both are July operations.

**Roberts' departure creates a second acquisition need on defence.** His 86 CHKG and 98 durability leave with him. Stuart (SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91) is the one player who replaces both attributes simultaneously and is young enough to be the top-pair partner for Jackman.

## Trajectory

The club's three-season outlook hinges on one summer: July 2005, when 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire simultaneously, and whether the young core signs on long deals or walks into a bidding war.

**Gaborik** is the linchpin. He just put up 99 points at 23 on $1.10M. POTE 90, 82 games played, and he will command market-rate the moment he hits the open pool. A five-year deal at something like $3.50-4.00M still leaves him the best production-per-dollar on the roster. Every week without a signed deal is a week another club can offer him a fresh start.

**Richards** at 66 points, 24, $1.00M carries the same problem at slightly lower stakes. POTE 88 and a second straight full season. Lock him on 5 years before the next camp starts the conversation.

**Nash** is 20 years old with 39 points and POTE 95. The cheapest five-year deal on the board — sign him at rookie-window pricing and the position is solved through 2010.

**Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 and 23 points in 64 games is the defense's future. One year left at $1.20M is an unacceptable exposure on that asset. Five years immediately.

**Kaberle** at 27 with 44 points and POTE 75 enters his prime on one year left. Four to five years, not six. His ceiling is established; you're buying the floor.

**Abid** is the outlier: 66 points, 82 games, $0.40M, POTE 94. If he hits the open market, no team with money will let him go at that price. Sign him on three or four years before July opens. His current salary is a glitch, not a market.

**The age curve is healthy but the bridge is empty.** Only one player sits between 30 and 33. The roster goes from 24-29 straight to Sundin at 34, Mogilny at 36, Roberts at 38, Belfour at 40. That means the current 24-29 group becomes the veteran core with no one to hand the torch to. It is manageable because that group is large (12), but it means there is no natural transition — when McCabe at 29 or Richards at 24 start declining, there is no 30-33 layer carrying the load.

**The money picture is comfortable but has embedded future liabilities.** Payroll $60.04M against revenue $104.02M leaves $31.56M of profit headroom. After Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk, payroll drops to $50.84M. Re-signing the six players above at market rate might add $8-10M net. Acquiring Iginla at $6.50M would push payroll to roughly $65-68M against $104M revenue. Still profitable, still room. The problem is not this year. It is Sundin at $8.40M for five more years (he will be 39 at the tail), Mogilny at $5.50M for two more (he is already in decline at 0.79 pts/g late season), and Fischer at $3.70M for four more (his rate dropped from 0.63 to 0.41). That is $17.60M of committed salary on three players whose production is falling and will keep falling. By 2007-08, when the young core should be entering its prime, Toronto will be carrying roughly $17M of dead weight and trying to extend Chlup, Luongo, Koltsov, and Spezza on top of it.

**Draft capital is zero.** One fourth-rounder, and that is it. Every future acquisition must be player-funded. If Sundin can be moved after 2005-06 while he still carries a 90-point season's residual value, a contender might take two years at $8.40M for a first-rounder and a young piece. Fischer is not tradeable at $3.70M and 0.41 pts/g. The fourth-rounder is worth nothing on its own and functions only as a sweetener in a package.

**The three moves that protect the next three seasons, in order:**

1. Renew Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, and Abid in July before the market forms. This is structural: without all six, the core breaks and the rebuild restarts.
2. Acquire Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts, $6.50M expiring). He closes the RW scoring void Mogilny leaves, adds TOUG 85 which no current forward exceeds, and CGY cannot retain him at 70 points with 10 expiring.
3. Begin planning Sundin's exit for July 2006. At 35 with one season remaining on his $8.40M deal, he is a rental with residual value. A contender needs a center; Toronto needs a first-rounder and a young blueliner to fill the bridge gap that currently has only Tucker at 30.

## Calendar

The deadline is gone and the season's regular schedule isn't, so the calendar question splits three ways: seven development games left, a playoff run to price, and a summer where 13 contracts worth roughly $23M hit the market at once.

**The deadline resolved correctly.** Toronto finished at 133 points, 19 clear of New Jersey. The GM's March 19 order to keep the roster intact and enter the playoffs with Belfour (92 base) and Luongo (91 base) was the right call for a team that dominant. No deadline trade was made, and none was needed. The only assets that were ever in play, Tucker and the 4th-rounder, either moved or stayed; the GM knows which.

**The remaining seven games are the last free development window before the playoffs lock up the schedule.** The coach asked for 15+ minutes for Spezza and Upshall. Spezza at 21 with POTE 99 has never exceeded 0.33 pts/g in any season at 5 MPG. If he is going to show anything, these seven games are the sample. Upshall at 21 is expiring; his minutes here determine whether he gets a 2-year deal or a 3-year one. Spacek should be dressed if a fourth-line spot opens.

**Playoff ticket pricing is the GM's lever on revenue.** The manual's guide: roughly 75 in round one, 80 in round two, 90 in round three, 100 in the final. Raise them as the rounds advance.

**The summer renewal is the real work.** Thirteen contracts expire simultaneously. The order is set: Gaborik first, Richards second, then Kaberle, Nash, Eminger, and the depth group. Belfour and Roberts walk. Here is the full list.

**Gaborik** (RW, 23, 91 base, $1.10M) is the first call. 87 points, POTE 90, and every club with cap space will chase him. Five to six years, not a year more. If he walks, the RW scoring void Mogilny's decline created becomes unfixable before next season.

**Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M, 64 pts) is second. The coach flagged a production drop but the system-fit question is the coach's to solve, not a reason to release a 24-year-old centre on a million dollars. Five to six years.

**Kaberle** (D, 27, $1.90M) rounds out the 5-6 year tier. He's the best puck-mover on the blue line and 27 is prime.

**Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M) and **Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M) both belong in the same tier. Nash is still 20; even a bad season is a season of growth at that age. Eminger's POTE 99 says the same. Five to six years on both.

**Colaiacovo** (D, 22, $1.10M) gets three to five years depending on how the remaining seven games go. At 22 he's a starter or he's not yet; a five-year lock risks paying for development that may not come.

**Chistov** (LW, 22, $1.10M), **Upshall** (RW, 21, $1.20M), and **Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M) are the two-to-three-year tier. These are depth players whose next 60 games decide if they're regulars or waivers material. No reason to lock five years on any of them.

**Tellqvist** (G, 25, $0.80M) stays on a two or three-year deal. GM's January order was to give him time. He's behind Luongo, but with Belfour likely walking he becomes the backup, and POTE in the high 90s is worth the patience.

**Abid** (LW, 25, $0.40M) is the cheapest toughness on the roster at base TOUG 80 and CHKG 80. Two years at whatever he'll take.

**Belfour** (G, 40, $6.50M) gets one offer at a reduced salary, maybe $3M on one or two years. He will probably refuse, and that's fine. Luongo is the starter and Tellqvist is the backup. $6.50M is not money to spend on a 40-year-old when 91-base Luongo is already here.

**Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M) walks. The March 21 order is clear, and at 38 on $2.70M there's no case to argue.

**July targets.** Iginla (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, $6.50M expiring) is the big swing. If he hits the market, he fills both the Mogilny scoring hole and the toughness gap in one move. Cammalleri (LA, 22, POTE 98, $1.10M) is the high-ceiling UFA. Bell (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) is the only league-wide player who closes the checking gap the coach has flagged five times. Bell is the cheapest of the three and the one the roster actually needs: zero Toronto forwards outside L1-L2 check above 75.

**Task #2 (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring) is complete.** Luongo was acquired and is on the roster at 91 base with two years left. DiPietro was eliminated on March 14 at 79 base, 11+ points below the threshold the GM set on January 15. Both threads are resolved.

## League scan

The season is over. Toronto are 59-13-5 and about to play in the playoffs, but the real work is July 2005: 13 contracts worth $21.30M expire on our side, and I need to know who across the league fills the gaps those expirations create, plus the structural ones the coach keeps re-flagging.

**The three gaps are unchanged and now urgent.** Zero forwards at 80+ toughness (coach reconfirmed April 15: "no forward outside L1-L2 who checks above 75"), Sundin is the only 80+ faceoff man and he is 34 on one year, and Mogilny at 36 with 0.79 pts/g late season is done as a top-six RW. Roberts at 38 walks, taking 86 CHKG and 98 durability off the blue line.

**Bell is still the single best target.** CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit are the most motivated sellers in the league. He is 24 with 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, and POTE 81. No other player closes all three forward gaps in one body. But I need to verify his 2004-05 production and minutes to confirm he can handle top-four responsibility.

**Iginla at 93 base with 140 points on a $6.50M expiring deal from 70-point CGY is the best available player in hockey.** He is the only target who simultaneously solves the RW scoring crisis and raises the forward toughness ceiling to 85. But his price will be steep and we hold one 4th-rounder.

**I need to find what I have not yet found**: any other 85+ TOUG forwards on sellers beyond Bell, any defence prospects at 87+ CHKG who can replace Roberts, and whether Daze is young enough to matter. Four wide queries will settle this.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers is what Toronto can actually give up to close the three gaps that have survived every internal fix — right-wing scoring, forward toughness, faceoff depth — and every package here is a July package built from young surplus plus our single fourth-rounder.

**Iginla** is the best player who will move this summer: 93 base at 27, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85, on a $6.50M deal that expires. Calgary finished at 70 points with 10 contracts expiring and cannot retain him. A POTE 99 centre on a $1.00M deal plus a pick is a rebuild return they can sell; I offer Spezza and the fourth.

**Proposal one: Spezza + R4 to CGY for Iginla.** He is the only target who fixes the Mogilny scoring void and lifts our forward toughness ceiling past 80 in one move. Our payroll adds $5.50M net if we extend him; we are at $50.84M after the walks against $104.02M revenue. Acceptance uncertain — Calgary may prefer picks.

**Bell** remains the value play: CHI, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, and the only body that closes all three forward gaps at once. Chicago finished at 78 points with 10 expiring deals and $31.73M profit — the most motivated seller in the league. They want youth, so the currency is Klesla (23, POTE 97) plus the pick.

**Proposal two: Klesla + R4 to CHI for Bell.** Cheaper than Iginla and he is four years younger, but ENDU 71 means short shifts at first. This is the deal I would take if only one lands.

**Stuart** is the Roberts replacement on defence: SJ, 25, 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91. Roberts leaves 86 CHKG and 98 durability with him at 38. San Jose finished at 72 points with 13 expiring deals on $45.39M and cannot keep them all.

**Proposal three: Colaiacovo + Tucker to SJ for Stuart.** Ranked last because SJ is not tanking and may refuse to move a POTE 91 blueliner; acceptance is the least certain of the three.

**If none land**, re-sign Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Kaberle and Abid in July before the market forms, then work the UFA pool for Cammalleri and a checking forward. Hold Tucker and the fourth as sweeteners for a larger package rather than spending them alone.

**Luongo and DiPietro, the January goalie task, is closed.** Luongo is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years left, and DiPietro still reads 79 base at 52 games, so the standing order's high-90s bar eliminates him. No further goalie monitoring is open.

## Owed

**Goalie trade window monitoring** — This task is dead and I am closing it.

**Luongo** is already on our roster. He was acquired on February 7, and he is now 26 years old, 94 overall, 45 games played, $1.60M with two years left. He is the number-one goalie the January 15 order asked for. The monitoring job existed to find him or someone like him; that search ended when we got him.

**DiPietro** was eliminated on March 14. At 52 games he still reads 79 base overall, an 11-point deficit against the high-90s target the GM set. No sample size closes that gap. He is off the board permanently.

**The window itself is closed.** The GM's March 19 standing order reads: "Stop monitoring for deals for Belfour. Keeping him and Luongo as two 90+ goalies for the playoffs. Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." That order killed the premise of this task. There is no goalie trade window to watch because the GM decided we have what we need and are carrying Belfour and Luongo into the playoffs.

Nothing has changed since I last reported on this in February. The task is complete and obsolete, and I am retiring it.
