# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-21

Next game vs PIT on Friday 22 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is winding down and these are the last games to put minutes into young legs, so the question of who is getting enough ice matters now more than at any point this year.

**Stahle** is the starkest case. 4 games in 82 at age 20, POTE 96, and when he did play he logged 17.8 MPG, so the coaching staff trusted him when he was in. That he has been benched for 78 straight games with that scouting grade makes no sense. PIT at 24-34 is a development opponent. Dress him tonight.

**Spezza** is the most underused player actually in the lineup. POTE 99 at 21, 6.7 MPG on the fourth line, morale 88 — the lowest of any young player, which tells you he knows what he is getting. 46 games in 82 means he hasn't even been dressed consistently. His season rate is 15 points in 46 games (0.33 pts/g), but the minutes constraint makes that rate meaningless. Move him up a line against PIT.

**Spacek** is scratched at 19, POTE 91, 50 games and 7.6 MPG. The March bump to 12+ MPG clearly did not stick. He is a third option at centre behind Chlup and Spezza, so there is no obvious line to put him on tonight, but he should be dressed for whatever games remain.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, POTE 99, 31 games but 17.9 MPG when playing. He is clearly the fifth defenceman. Against a weak opponent this is the game to dress him and give him top-four minutes.

**Upshall** is the mirror of Spezza: POTE 99 at 21, 7.9 MPG on the fourth line, 68 games. Same offseason decision applies. No urgency tonight beyond what is already flagged.

**Chlup, Gaborik, Nash, Chistov, Klesla, Eminger** are all getting their games. No development concern there. Chlup at 59 points in 71 games on 16.9 MPG is the best season any young Leaf has posted and he is playing every night.

## Development trends

The season is over — 82 games logged for most of the roster — so this is the full picture for the first time, and it settles several questions that were still conditional three weeks ago.

**McCabe** at 0.48 pts/g on 21.5 MPG across 82 games. His 1.42 early-season pace was a 24-game fluke. The March 30 conditional is now met: he goes back on the sell list. At 29, $3.0M, four years left, he is a cap anchor with declining production.

**Kaberle** went the other way. 0.54→0.62 pts/g on minutes climbing from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27 he is getting better under more load. The GM's "definitely a keeper" call is correct on the numbers, not just instinct.

**Chistov** is the quiet one. Minutes rose from 9.5 to 14.0 MPG and his rate held at 0.30 — he earned his ice without production falling off. At 22, that trajectory says he deserves a bigger look next camp. He was invisible all season and he shouldn't be.

**Abid** finished at 0.70 pts/g on 11.5 MPG. That is 3.65 points per 60 — elite for a 25-year-old winger. His minutes fell from 20.1 to 11.5 during the year with no corresponding injury. If we give him 15+ next season the rate should be even higher; at 11.5 we are wasting him and risking his morale.

**Spacek** at 5.2 MPG final confirms what the March 11 note said: the year is dead. The 12 MPG bump the GM gave him on March 5 clearly did not hold. Next camp decides whether he is a roster player at all.

**Spezza** at 0.24 on 4.6 MPG and **Upshall** at 0.27 on 4.8 MPG are the same story. Both at 21, both collapsed. Offseason auditions are the only lever.

**Richards** at 0.71 pts/g on flat 15.8 MPG at age 24 is the one that concerns me most for next season. At 24 the expected direction is up. He went from 1.08 to 0.71 with no role change. The system-fit review from April 7 needs to happen in June, not August.

**Jackman** at 0.39 on 29.4 MPG at 24 confirms the load is killing him. Sell.

For the defenceman review the GM asked for every game: sell order is Jackman (0.39 on 29.4 MPG, load problem), Klesla (0.31 on 14.9 MPG, second declining season), McCabe (0.48, below threshold at 29), Eminger (flat at 0.37 but expiring, must move before July). Keepers: Kaberle (improving) and Fischer (mild decline to 0.50 on rising minutes, the GM's keeper). Colaiacovo at 0.36 on 17.5 MPG is a question mark — at 22 the direction should be up, but his sample is only 31 games.

The three veterans — Sundin at 0.97 on 21.7 MPG, Mogilny at 0.83 on 19.1, Roberts at 0.86 on 21.4 — all declined as age predicts. Roberts at 38 should not be carrying 21.4 MPG next season. That load comes down or he breaks.

## Morale watch

The room is right. After a run of wins the whole roster is trending up, and nobody sits in a morale band where a line move would help.

**Spezza** is the lowest at 88, down from where he was but climbing +3 from the last save. He's at 6.7 mpg in a fourth-line role. That's below the 10-mpg floor a 70-something calibre player expects, and it's been true since March. The fix was always offseason, not tonight -- the GM agreed to give him a real audition at camp. No in-season minutes change solves this.

**Spacek** sits at 89, scratched by the GM's design to make room for younger players. Same logic: he's developing through the scratch list this year, and his morale is fine for a kid who knows his role.

**Upshall** at 91 with 7.9 mpg is the only dressed player slightly under his band (a useful depth man expects about 10). Morale is stable and +3 from last save. Not a concern this week.

**Abid** continues to produce 66 points on 13.8 mpg with morale pegged at 100. The minutes mismatch is real and I flagged it in March, but his mood hasn't cracked. He's happy tonight; the structural fix is next season's role allocation.

Everyone else is at 98 or above. The winning streak is doing the work I can't do with a line change.

## Role composition

The question here is whether each unit's personnel suits its job, and whether we have the bodies to fill the jobs we're asking for.

**L1** is our best line in every grade that matters: checking 83 mean with Jackman at 90, scoring 89 with Gaborik at 99, clutch 83 with Gaborik at 99. Built to play against top opponents and win. No change.

**L2** is a skill line with Chlup taking draws at 80. Mogilny at 94 scoring is the engine. McCabe at 85 checking gives this line a real second gear defensively. This is correctly built for a second line that gets offence without sacrificing structure. No change.

**L3** has the strangest identity. Klesla checks at 94 — the best on the line — but the mean is 76 because Richards, Abid, Eminger, and Chistov are all in the 70s. Chistov at 98 speed and Richards at 97 clutch make this a transition line, not a shutdown line. That's fine for a third unit; they don't need to be checkers, they need to not be a liability. No change.

**L4** is the problem, and it is not an arrangement problem. Koltsov, Spezza, Upshall: checking mean 65, toughness 59, faceoffs 53, stamina 51. These three have no role identity. They aren't checkers, they aren't scorers, and they can't win a draw. They are speed (89 mean) with gas tanks that are empty. No swap with L3 fixes this — Abid produces at 0.84 pts/g and belongs where he gets minutes, and pulling him down would gut L3's playmaking. This is a roster gap.

**P1 and P2** are well-constructed. P1 has Gaborik at 99 scoring, Sundin at 92 playmaking, and Jackman/Kaberle for the point. P2 has Mogilny at 94 scoring and Richards at 97 clutch. Both units have shooters and playmakers in the right proportions. No change.

**K1 and K2** are the best-built units on the roster. K2's checking mean of 84 is the highest on any unit — McCabe and Jackman carry it, with Chlup taking the draw and Abid adding toughness at 72. K1 has Sundin and Roberts at 85 checking each, plus Fischer at 85. These kill well because the best checkers are actually on them. No change.

The structural gap remains: no forward outside L1-L2 checks above 80 except Klesla, and he's a defenceman. We have four quality checkers (Jackman 90, Roberts 85, McCabe 85, Fischer 85) and they're all already deployed on PK and top-six minutes. A true fourth-line checking centre is the missing piece.

## Opponent matchup

**Can we beat Pittsburgh with the current lines, or does something need to move for Friday?**

We're 4-0-0 against them with a 20-9 goal differential. Their record is 24-34-11 and their top defensive pair is Tarnstrom at 77 and Rozsival at 76, their second pair at 71 and 73, their third at 70 and 67. No arrangement of my defensive slots improves this matchup because it is already perfect: the game auto-pairs our first defensive pair (Fischer 85, Jackman 86, both CHKG 92) against their most offensive line, and their best checker is Buchberger at OVR 73 on the third line. The slot order is correct and I would not touch it.

**Lemieux** is 39 and still has PASS 99, PUCK 95, DEKG 98 at the centre of their first line. He is not a scoring problem to solve with personnel; he is a coverage problem that Fischer and Jackman, both at CHKG 92, already handle better than anyone else on our blue line could. Let the first pair eat his minutes.

**Pittsburgh's power play is 32 goals on 276 attempts.** That is an 11.6% unit. Their first PP features Lemieux and Straka but their supporting D is Rozsival and Tarnstrom at 76-77. Our first kill unit (Sundin, Gaborik, Fischer, Jackman) is overkill against this, and that is fine. I am not pulling anyone off the PK for this game because they cannot hurt us shorthanded.

**Goalie:** Luongo is at 94 OVR, morale 100. No fatigue flag shown. He starts. This is their last game against us before the series ends and we're 4-0; if he is fresh on screen, no reason to sit him.

**Development window.** The GM's standing note says development priority applies in games we can afford. Pittsburgh at 24-34-11, on the road, against a team we've beaten four times by 11 total goals is exactly that kind of game. If the GM wants to give Spezza (72 OVR, 88 morale, minutes collapsed) and Upshall (79 OVR, 91 morale, also minutes down) more of the night, this is the game. I cannot directly control their minutes — only which line he chooses to dress and play — but he could sit Koltsov (trading chip, 73 OVR, 0.28 pts/g season rate) and give that fourth-line winger slot to Upshall or simply let the fourth line run longer. That is a development call, not a matchup call.

**Obligation #1, D review for this game:** No change to the sell list. Against Pittsburgh's third pair at OVR 67-70, Eminger (77 OVR, CHKG 81) and Klesla (84 OVR, CHKG 79) will look fine. That means nothing. The season verdict stands: Jackman (0.48 pts/g on 30 MPG, $0.70M) goes, Klesla (0.36 pts/g second straight decline) goes, Eminger (0.38, $1.2M expiring) must go before July. McCabe (0.76 final rate) stays. Fischer is a contract-value trade, not a play-based one.

## Owed

**D-corridor sell list — final season numbers, what to move and when.** The season is winding down and most defencemen's totals are locked. Here is the final read.

**McCabe** finishes at 62 points in 82 games, 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. Season complete. He clears the 0.60 threshold I set March 30 and stays. $3.00M x 4 years anchors the top pair.

**Jackman** at 80 GP: 37 points on 29.6 MPG, 0.46 pts/g. That is down from the 0.48 I saw at 73 games in March. The overload keeps eating his production. Sell at $0.70M x 3 — the cheapest 30 MPG on the market.

**Klesla** locked at 82 GP: 30 points, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Two straight declining seasons confirmed. Age 23, $0.90M x 2. Sell.

**Eminger** finished at 64 GP: 23 points, 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG. Contract expires. This is the most urgent item on the list — if he hits free agency in July we get nothing. Any trade by June 30 is better than nothing.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 games: 12 points, 0.39 pts/g. $1.10M expiring, not dressed. Pack him into the Eminger deal or let him walk. Low value either way.

**Kaberle** is the GM's keeper (his words) but he is a UFA at $1.90M. 0.59 pts/g over 74 games at 27. Renewal conversation needs to happen before we lose him for nothing.

**No change from my last delivery** except: Jackman's rate has slipped from 0.48 to 0.46 and McCabe's season is now final at 0.76. The sell list (Jackman, Klesla, Eminger, Colaiacovo) and keepers (McCabe, Fischer, Kaberle) are unchanged.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-15
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-15

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

**The toughness gap is confirmed: zero Toronto skaters carry 80+ in stored toughness.** Jackman's 75 is the best on the roster, followed by Roberts and McCabe at 73. The Feb 24 contradiction is resolved — it's zero, and it has always been zero. The fourth line sits at 57 mean TOUG, below the 61 checking mean, which means they separate the puck without imposing a cost. This is the single structural deficit on the roster and no internal solution exists.

**Sundin** at 90 FACE is the only 80+ draw-taker. Chlup at 75 is next, then Richards at 70. Three lines of centres below 76 means every defensive-zone draw against a skilled opponent is a coin flip at best. Bell (82 FACE) and Avery (93 FACE) are the only targets that close this.

**Roberts (38)** is the team's best player at checking (86 CHKG) and durability (98 INJU) and his contract expires in July. He walks. That removes 86 CHKG, 98 INJU, 90 HERO, and 88 overall in one stroke, leaving McCabe 86 CHKG and Jackman 87 CHKG as the only remaining 80+ checkers over 25 years old.

**Mogilny (36)** at 94 scoring is the top man but declining sharply — 0.79 pts/g in his most recent stretch versus 1.62 earlier in the season. His contract is expiring too. The scoring role shows 10 players at 80+, but four of them (Mogilny 94, Roberts 88, Abid 86, and the declining Mogilny line) are either leaving or aging out. Gaborik 92 and Sundin 92 are the long-term core.

**Tucker (30, 83 CHKG)** is rostered and unlined. Dressing him gives the fourth line a checker but his 70 TOUG means the physical cost problem persists. He helps the checking column (6→7 at 80+) without touching toughness.

**Spacek (19, 84 P)** is also unlined and carries genuine playmaking. Against weak opponents in the final three games, this is a free audition the coach already flagged.

**Aebischer is gone from the goalie list** — the four rostered are Luongo (26, 2yr), Belfour (39, 1yr expiring), Ouellet (23, 2yr), Tellqvist (25, 1yr expiring). If Belfour retires after the season, Ouellet's INJU 69 becomes the playoff depth concern. Not a gap today but a trajectory flag.

**The two gaps that require acquisition are toughness and faceoffs, and they overlap perfectly.** Bell (88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24) closes both. Avery (83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, 25) closes both at lower ceiling but $400K cost. No combination of existing Torontonian players can close either gap.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question is whether this club ages into a cliff or into a window, and the answer is a window with one execution risk: thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire this July simultaneously, and most of them are the core that makes the window real.

**The age shape is the best in the league.** Fourteen players at 23 or under, eleven at 24-29, one at 30-33, four at 34+. The 34+ bracket (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Roberts 38, Belfour 39) is four players, two of whom are expiring this summer (Roberts $2.70M, Belfour $6.50M). By next season the oldest player on the roster is Sundin at 35 with five years still locked, and the next-oldest is McCabe at 30. The club sheds its entire elderly core naturally in twelve months without trading anyone.

**Sundin** at $8.40M with 5 years left and POTE 60 is the single largest fixed liability. He produces 91 points at 34, but POTE 60 means the grade cannot rise. He is locked through age 39 at this salary, which constrains every other renewal. There is nothing to do about it mid-contract, but it sets the ceiling on how much else can be spent.

**The renewal wave is the whole game this summer.** Gaborik (23, 99 points, $1.10M) is the priority: six years. Richards (24, 66 points, $1.00M) is five years. Nash (20, 39 points, POTE 95, $1.20M) is six years. Eminger (21, POTE 99, $1.20M) is five years. Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.10M) is five years. Kaberle (27, 44 points, POTE 75, $1.90M) gets three or four years, not six, because his ceiling is near. Chistov (21, POTE 95, $1.10M) is five. Alexeev (23, 30 points, POTE 94, $1.10M) gets three years to prove the production first. Abid (25, 66 points, POTE 94, $0.40M) is the cheapest production on the roster; re-sign him at market rate on two years rather than losing a 66-point bottom-sixer for nothing.

If every star gets six years, the next cluster is July 2011. If every star gets three years to be cheap now, they all come up again in July 2008 alongside Fischer, McCabe and Afinogenov, and the same crisis repeats. The stagger is the discipline.

**Belfour and Roberts walk.** Belfour is 39, $6.50M, scratched 37 of 82 games. Roberts is 38, $2.70M, POTE 52. Their $9.20M releases against the renewal increases from the young core. Net payroll change depends on what the renewals cost; if the eight core players double their salaries (roughly $10M more on $10M of current deals), the club loses Belfour and Roberts' $9.20M and gains roughly $10M, netting close to flat against $101.97M revenue.

**Draft capital is nothing.** One fourth-rounder, no first, no second, no third. Every trade package this summer must be funded entirely by players. This blocks any acquisition that a counterparty prices against a first-round pick, and it means the Iginla pursuit must come through his UFA status in July, not through a trade.

**Payroll headroom is adequate.** $60.04M against $101.97M revenue leaves $29.51M profit. Even with Iginla's $6.50M added (if he signs), the club sits near $66M payroll on $102M revenue, still profitable. The constraint is not the current year's money but the year after, when the renewal contracts all start at their new (higher) rates simultaneously.

**The protection for three seasons comes down to three things:** execute the staggered renewal wave, land Iginla via UFA to fill the RW void and close the toughness ceiling at 27 rather than at Mogilny's 36, and accept that the depth players (Upshall, Koltsov, Alexeev) are the ones to trade rather than the core when the next need arises. The window opens the moment those contracts are signed.

## Calendar

The deadline passed 27 days ago with no moves executed beyond what we kept, so the question now is singular: how do we spend the summer with 13 contracts expiring simultaneously, and who do we chase with the free money and the free roster spot Belfour's departure creates.

**Gaborik** is the first call, every time. 91 base, 23 years old, 87 points on $1.10M. He outproduces anyone else on the expiring list by a full tier. Lock him on six years the day re-signing opens. Every week of delay risks a rival matching his number and we lose our best forward at the same price another club pays for a second-liner.

**Richards** follows immediately. 24, 64 points, $1.00M. He is the best young centre available on any roster in this league at that price. Five or six years. The gap between his salary and his production is what makes Toronto profitable, and that gap closes the moment he leaves.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is in his prime and the only established top-pairing defenseman we hold long-term. Five years. Nash at 20 and $1.20M is the future first-line left wing; lock him six years at whatever the game gives, because at that age and that price he cannot be replaced on the market.

**Eminger** at 21, $1.20M: GM locked him in on February 19 with POTE 99. Renew five years. **Chistov** at 21 held 0.30 pts/g while minutes rose from 9.5 to 14.0 — the coach sees growth. Two or three years at $1.10M or slightly above. **Colaiacovo** at 22, $1.10M, same logic: defensive depth at youth pricing, two or three years.

**Abid** at $0.40M is the cheapest toughness on the market, 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG. Renew two years at a modest bump, perhaps $0.60M, and dress him on the fourth line where the coach says the checking mean is 61 and toughness 57.

**Tellqvist** at 25, POTE high-90s per the GM's January order, $0.80M. If Belfour walks he becomes Luongo's backup. Renew two years. **Alexeev** at 23 needs the camp audition the coach is giving him over these three games before we commit. If he holds a rate above 0.30 at 12-plus minutes, sign him two years. If not, release.

**Belfour** at 39 and $6.50M is the decision that shapes everything else. The GM's February 19 order was clear: offer reduced salary, he probably won't accept. If he walks, $6.50M of payroll vanishes and we have Luongo plus Tellqvist for the playoffs and beyond. That is acceptable. If he stays, he costs more than a top-six forward. The reduced-salary offer is the plan; there is no better version.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M: walk. The March 21 renewal order already states it. He is a rental we have already used for a playoff push.

**Upshall** at 21, $1.20M: the coach's April 14 report says his season is dead at 0.28 pts/g on 5.2 MPG, same tree as Spacek. If camp doesn't show a rate above 0.35, release him. His trade value has evaporated because his production has.

**Spezza** does not expire and stays on the books, but the coach has flagged him six times without exceeding 0.33 pts/g. The camp audition is now mandatory: if he fails it a seventh time, trade him in 2006 while POTE 99 is still credible. His value is not permanent.

**Elias and Langenbrunner** both expire from Philadelphia. Elias at 90 base and $4.90M is a top winger but the cost is real; Langenbrunner at 89 and $2.10M is the better value. Both become July UFA targets if we have cap room after Belfour walks and we have not landed Iginla, who remains the primary RW target at 93 base and 140 points.

**Cammalleri** at 22, POTE 98, $1.10M expiring from LA is the single highest-value UFA in the pool. If he hits the market, sign him. The immediate calendar item is ticket pricing: raise to 75 for round one once the bracket confirms.

## League scan

The league scan confirms what we already suspected and sharpens it: Iginla is the single highest-value acquisition in the entire league for this club, and he arrives without costing a trade asset because CGY cannot retain him.

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M, expiring) closes the RW scoring void left by Mogilny AND the toughness ceiling in one move. CGY at 70 points, 10 expiring contracts, $14.43M profit — they have no retention path. The UFA route costs nothing in assets, which matters because we hold no first, no second, no third. This is the anchor target for July.

**Stuart** (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, $1.80M, expiring, 52 pts/77 GP) is the direct Roberts replacement. He carries 80 TOUG (first 80+ on our roster if acquired) and 89 CHKG (above Roberts' 86), with POTE 91 giving eight years of upside. SJ at 76 points, 13 expiring, $20.74M profit. They cannot keep all thirteen. Acquisition requires a player; Tucker ($1.30M, expiring, 30) is the natural sweetener.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2 years) is the only forward who closes toughness AND faceoffs AND checking simultaneously. He did not appear in the query results (possibly a join issue or roster change), but his data was confirmed at high confidence on March 30. CHI at 78 points, 10 expiring, $31.73M profit. He is the single best gap-closer at a forward position.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, 131 pts/79 GP, $1.10M, expiring) fills the RW void with raw production if Iginla isn't available. 91 base at 24 on $1.10M is the cheapest elite scoring in the game. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring cannot keep both him and Kovalchuk (138 pts, 22). Their internal binary is our opportunity.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 22, 89 base, 138 pts/79 GP, $1.10M, expiring) carries the highest production of any player under 25 in the league. 78 TOUG and 51 FACE don't close our physical gaps, but at 22 with POTE 85 on $1.10M, the upside overwhelms the present. ATL's binary with Heatley means one of them moves.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25, 79 base, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 years) closes faceoffs and toughness on a third line at $400K. Production is a ghost (9 pts/82 GP), so he slots below the top six. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring are desperate to shed salary. The $400K means even a pure pick-for-him trade is net-positive on money.

**Scatchard** (NYI, C, 29, 85 base, 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 84 FACE, $1.40M, contract_years 0, 26 pts/78 GP) is the only player in the league carrying 85 TOUG, 89 CHKG AND 84 FACE simultaneously. At $1.40M, 29, he's a two-way middle-six centre with elite grades but modest output. NYI at 84 points, 13 expiring. The "0 years" on his deal means he's either a UFA now or walking imminently — worth confirming, but if he's available he closes two gaps at a bargain salary.

**Brashear** (PHI, LW, 33, 81 base, 98 TOUG, 89 CHKG, $2.10M, 2 years, 13 pts/82 GP) carries 98 TOUG, the highest in the database. At 33 with POTE 63 he is a pure enforcer with no upside. PHI at 82 points carry $2.14M profit — financially distressed, possible seller. But 2 years left means we're committing to a 35-year-old. Low priority; only relevant if the cheaper options fail.

**Not pursuing:** Chara (GM standing order, "stop talking about him"). Pronger ($9.50M, STL at 86 points, POTE 65). Conroy (65 TOUG, 33, rental). Daze (57 TOUG adds nothing physical). Marchant ($4.88M, 65 TOUG, doesn't close the gap).

## Trade construction

The trade question this summer is how to fund gap-closing acquisitions when we hold a single fourth-rounder and no first, second, or third, and the answer is to recover picks from players we are losing anyway before building the packages that actually reach our targets.

**Roberts** (38, 88 overall, $2.70M, expiring, 81 pts/82 GP, 98 INJU) walks in July regardless. The guide's mechanic — trade any 80+ player you will not re-sign for a pick — turns a $2.70M walking asset into a draft pick at zero cost. A contender thin at defence gets an 88-overall top-pairing blueliner with 98 INJU for one playoff run. We get back a pick that funds the Bell or Stuart pursuit. This is the first domino.

**Koltsov** (23, LW, POTE 94, ACCE 96, AGIL 92, 2 years, $1.10M) for **Avery** (25, C, 79 base, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2 years) is the cleanest single-player trade available. LA at 79 points carry 14 expiring deals and need young assets to rebuild around; Koltsov at 23 with ACCE 96 is a project they can develop while they are competitive-but-not-contention. Avery closes our 93-FACE and 88-CHKG voids at $400K, which saves $700K against Koltsov's $1.10M. Both sides have straightforward reasons.

**Bell** (24, LW, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, $900K, 2 years) requires more than Tucker plus the fourth alone. That package scores around a 74-76 base return per our March 30 finding. If the Roberts pick lands — say a second or third — we can add it and get closer to the 82 base CHI would accept. CHI at 78 points and $31.73M profit are not desperate, but Bell at $900K with POTE 81 is good-not-franchise, and Tucker's 92 CHKG gives them a fourth-line checker immediately. This is conditional on the first deal landing and still uncertain.

**If none land:** Iginla as a UFA in July costs nothing in trade assets and closes both the scoring void (93 base, 140 pts/73 GP) and the toughness ceiling (85 TOUG) in one signature. Avery and Bell are the plan B when Iginla goes elsewhere. The UFA route makes every trade proposal optional rather than necessary.

## Owed

**The goalie trade window you asked me to monitor through February is closed — both halves resolved, and you shut it down yourself on March 19.**

**Luongo** is on our roster. 26 years old, 92 overall, $1.60M, 2 years left, 45 games played this season. The January 15 order — "set a goal to fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender" — is fulfilled. He arrived at a base grade of 91-92 with two years of control at a backup's salary.

**DiPietro** was eliminated permanently. At 52 games in April he still reads 79 base overall, 13 points below the high-90s threshold you set. No sample size closes that gap. The January 19 monitoring task is moot.

**What changed since last reported:** Nothing has moved because there is nothing left to move. On 2005-03-19 you said "Goalies are solved. Done. Do not revisit that issue" and "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." The window you wanted assessed in February produced its answer in January (Luongo acquired) and its negative in March (DiPietro eliminated). This item is delivered and closed.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-15
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-15

Next game vs NYI on Saturday 16 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each player 23 or under is getting the games his talent has earned, and with three games left against soft competition (next up: NYI, 30-38), this is the window where the answer is still actionable.

**Chlup** is getting everything he has earned. 71 games, 16.9 MPG, 59 points at 19 years old on the second line. Morale 98. No issue.

**Gaborik** at 82 games and 20.5 MPG is playing like a first-line winger because he is one. 99 points, morale 100. Done.

**Klesla** plays every game (82) at 14.8 MPG but his production is 0.36 pts/g. He is getting his games; the problem is production, not opportunity. Not a development issue.

**Nash** at 69 games and 13.1 MPG on the second line is getting real time. His 0.57 pts/g is below where he started the year but his role has not been cut. Fine.

**Eminger** at 64 games and 15.5 MPG is a regular third-pair defenceman at 21. Getting his games. Production at 0.36 pts/g is low for a POTE 99 player, but opportunity is there.

**Chistov** at 68 games and 13.1 MPG is a regular third-liner. 20 points is thin but he's a depth forward getting his share.

**Spezza** is the main problem. 46 games, 6.7 MPG on the fourth line, POTE 99, morale 88. He is dressed but invisible. With three games left against weak opponents, this is exactly the scenario the GM set: development in games we can afford. He should be playing 15+ MPG for the rest of the year.

**Upshall** is the same story. 68 games but 7.9 MPG, POTE 99, 0.29 pts/g. Dressed on the fourth line but barely getting over the boards. Same call: give him real minutes in these last three.

**Spacek** is scratched. 50 games, 7.6 MPG, POTE 91, morale 89. The season-end target is dead and 3 games won't fix it, but dressing him costs nothing against a 30-38 team and keeps his morale from falling further before camp.

**Stahle** at 4 games at 20 is buried behind Klesla (82 games), Eminger (64), and Colaiacovo (31). His time will come but not in three games. No lever here now.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 games and 17.9 MPG is the GM's deliberate rotation. His minutes when he plays are real. I am not pushing this again.

**Koltsov** at 38 games and 9.6 MPG is the GM's trading chip. His value problem is a front-office question, not a development one.

**Alexeev** at 23, 55 games, 8.3 MPG, 0.55 pts/g is a depth winger whose role is what it is. Not being wasted; just a bottom-six player.

**Ouellet** at 13 games as a backup is adequate for a 23-year-old goalie behind a starter. No issue.

## Development trends

The season has three games left, so this window is the final read before offseason planning. The trend directions locked here decide who starts on the first line in camp, who goes on the trade block, and who we build around.

**Chlup** is the one clear riser. 0.62 to 0.88 pts/g while his minutes jumped from 11.0 to 18.2. At 19, doubling your load and *raising* your rate is not what happens to most kids. He's the franchise centre. No change needed, just more of the same.

**Kaberle** is the only defenceman going up: 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on 19.4→21.5 MPG. The GM called him a star back in January and the trend is backing that up. He earned a bigger share of the game against anyone, not just the weak teams.

**Spacek** has the worst collapse on the roster. 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g, minutes gutted from 16.0 to 5.2. Fifty games at 5.2 MPG is not development, it's a scratch with a jersey. Next camp is his last audition.

**Spezza** is the same story at 21: 0.43 to 0.24 on 9.1→4.6 MPG. Two players whose season ended in March because we stopped playing them. Both need a clear role at camp or we stop dressing them entirely.

**Nash** at 20 went 0.83 to 0.42 on flat 13 MPG. The role didn't change and the production halved. That's a system-fit problem, not a minutes problem. Flag for offseason review before next camp.

**Richards** continues sliding at 24: 1.08 to 0.71 on 15.8 MPG. No role change, no grade change, just less production. At an age where the expected direction is up, this needs the same offseason system-fit look as Nash. Two first-line-calibre centres declining without explanation is a coaching question.

**Alexeev** at 23 is quietly falling out: 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g on 11.1→6.0 MPG. Minutes cut in half, rate down 23%. He's becoming a fourth-liner at an age when he should be climbing.

**Koltsov** collapsed from 1.10 to 0.29 pts/g. The GM's trading chip is at its lowest value of the season. Any club looking at his trend sees the slide, not the October start.

**McCabe** finished at 0.48 pts/g across 82 games. That's the sell number we set back in March. He goes on the block this offseason.

**Jackman** ended at 0.39 on 29.4 MPG across 80 games. Same story as McCabe: top-pair minutes, bottom-six production. Sell.

**Klesla** at 0.31 on 14.9 MPG across 82 games is two consecutive declining seasons at 22 and 23. Sell.

**Eminger** at 0.37 on 15.9 MPG is flat, which at 21 with an expiring contract means his window to fetch anything is this offseason. He cannot walk for nothing.

**Sundin** at 34 went 1.46 to 0.97 but his minutes climbed from 16.9 to 21.7. He's still a useful first-line centre getting top-nine minutes and producing near a point a game. No age flag yet.

**Roberts** at 38 on 0.86 and 21.4 MPG is still playing like a regular. No action.

**Mogilny** at 36 dropped from 1.62 to 0.83. Expected, but 0.83 on 19 MPG is still serviceable. Plan his succession without forcing it off the ice yet.

**Delivering task #1** (defencemen analysis): Kaberle is the riser and keeper. Fischer held 0.50 on 22.9 MPG, up from 20.8, carrying more load and slipping only in rate, acceptable at 24. McCabe, Jackman, Klesla, and Eminger are all sell candidates based on the numbers above. Stahle (4 GP, 0 points, 17.8 MPG) and Safronov (3 GP) are samples too small to read.

## Morale watch

The room is fine. Every player is at 88 or above, and the vast majority at 98-100. No one is in crisis territory, and no one has shown a downward slide that a line change would fix.

**Abid** remains the one structural concern for next season, not this one. He sits at 100 morale on 13.8 MPG while producing 0.80 pts/g (66 points in 82 games). His calibre reads 90+, which means his expectation is 20 minutes a night. The gap hasn't bitten yet because he's young and the results have been good, but it's a season-end roster question, not a this-week lines question. With 3 games left there's nothing to adjust.

**Richards** at 98 morale and 16.1 MPG is the closest thing to a player under-band among the top guys. His morale dipped (-3, -2, -3) then recovered (+3, +5) over recent saves. The recovery tracks with wins. No intervention needed.

**Spezza** (88 morale, 6.7 MPG) and **Spacek** (89 morale, scratched) are both young players getting scraps. Their morale is stable and actually ticking up. This is the offseason development decision already flagged; the season is gone for them.

No action for Saturday. Lines stay as they are.

## Role composition

The question here is whether each unit is built from players who suit its job, and whether the roster can even fill the jobs we need against a bad NYI team on Saturday.

**L1 through L3 are fine.** L1 has Gaborik (96 scoring, 99 speed, 97 clutch) with Sundin (88 faceoffs, 90 scoring) driving it, and two defence partners who check (Jackman 87, Fischer 82). L2 gets Chlup's 77 faceoffs and Mogilny's 90 scoring with McCabe's 82 checking behind them. L3 has Richards (72 faceoffs, 94 clutch, 92 stamina) as the workhorse centre and Abid (70 toughness) bringing physicality. Nothing about these three units suggests a better arrangement is available.

**L4 is the known gap.** Koltsov, Spezza, Upshall: checking mean 62, toughness 57, faceoffs 51. The best checker on the roster who isn't already on L1-L2 is Abid at 70, and he's already on L3. Against NYI at 30-38, a soft fourth line won't be punished the way a top club punishes it. Their bottom six can't exploit what we don't have. No change tonight.

**Power play and penalty kill are correct.** P1 has the five best shooters and playmakers. P2 has Chlup distributing and Fischer as a net-front presence. K2 actually carries the stronger checking unit (81 mean vs K1's 76), which is what you want — the checking guys should be killing.

**The roster gap remains open.** No forward outside L1-L2 checks above 75. We need a middle-six forward who checks 80+ and we simply don't have one. This is not tonight's problem against a 30-38 team, but it's the one structural hole the GM should be targeting in the offseason draft or trade market.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does NYI at 30-38-4 require any lineup adjustment, or do we play our normal game and let the young guys develop?

**No change.** This is the clearest development-affordable game on the calendar. We're 133 points to their 84, scoring 3.20 against their 1.70 allowed. We're 5-2-1 in the season series with three left. The young guys are already dressed and lined: Spezza, Koltsov and Upshall on the fourth, Chlup on the second. There is nothing to fix.

**Yashin** is their only genuine first-line threat at 83 OVR, but he's CHKG 64 and TOUG 52. Fischer (CHKG 89, OVR 83) and Jackman (CHKG 89, OVR 84) sit on our first pair and will eat him alive along the boards. No adjustment needed there.

**Peca** at 85 OVR is their best player overall. He faces our second pair: Kaberle (CHKG 68) and McCabe (CHKG 84). McCabe is the anchor on that pairing and can handle Peca's AGGR 92 game. This works.

**Bates** on their third line has FACE 94, the highest on the sheet. He'll win draws against Richards (FACE 72) and Chlup (FACE 77). We already knew this from the faceoff-center-gap finding. Against a 30-win team, losing third-line draws costs nothing.

**DiPietro** at 83 OVR in their net is the one variable. His AGIL 97 and SPEE 94 make him hard to beat on angle plays, but REBC 62 is his weakness. Our first line (Sundin 92 HERO, Gaborik 97 HERO) will generate second chances all night.

**Goalie:** Start Luongo. OVR 92, morale 100. Check the fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order from January 19th.

**Defensive evaluation (task #1):** The season picture is unchanged from what I reported earlier. Jackman at 0.48 pts/g on 30 MPG across 73 games is the sell target; his load is killing his production. Klesla's second consecutive declining season (0.36 this year) keeps him on the sell list. McCabe is confirmed off it. Eminger at 0.38 on 15.8 MPG with ENDU 50 and an expiring contract is the third name. No new information from this game to shift those reads.

## Owed

This is the final read on the blue line with the season essentially complete. Most D have hit their 82 or are close. Here's what changed since my last delivery.

**Jackman** has slipped further. My March 23 read was 0.48 pts/g on 73 games. He's now at 80 GP, 37 points, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. The load is confirmed to be killing his offense. His sell value is the cheap $0.70M x 3 and the raw minutes he can absorb, not his production. Sell this summer while the contract is still cheap.

**McCabe** is confirmed at 82 GP / 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. He clears the 0.60 threshold I set in March. He stays as anchor on the top pair. No change.

**Klesla** is locked at 82 GP / 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Third consecutive declining season. Sell at $0.90M x 2 remains correct.

**Eminger** has slid to 0.36 pts/g on 64 games. His contract expires this year. If we don't move him before July he's a UFA loss at zero return.

**Kaberle** is the one thing that has changed on the sell/keep chart: his contract reads 1 year remaining. 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG at age 27 with an 82 OVR. The GM called him a star and a keeper, so I'm not proposing a trade. But the renewal conversation is now a summer priority. If he walks, we lose our second-best D for nothing.

**Fischer** stays. 83 OVR, $3.70M x 4, the GM's keeper. No debate.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 GP / 0.39 on an expiring deal is depth only. No action needed.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-14

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-14

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

Which roles are covered, which are thin, and which are missing — and what can be fixed from inside the building.

**Toughness** is the gap that cannot be closed internally. Zero rostered players carry 80+ toughness in stored grades. The ceiling is Jackman at 75, Roberts at 73, McCabe at 73. The Coach's April 13 report names this directly: "one more forward who checks 75+ and wins draws — nobody on this roster fits." Bell (CHI, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24) closes both this and the faceoff void in one player. Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, 25, $400K, 2y) closes all three gaps for less currency.

**Faceoffs** is the second structural gap. One player at 80+: Sundin 90. Chlup sits at 75, Richards at 70. Four lines need a draw-taker; we have one. The Coach's March recommendation to slide Richards to L3 was attempted and not sustained — his 70 FACE is the best available internally, and it is still ten points below the threshold. Bell (82) or Avery (93) are the only paths to a second real faceoff man.

**Checking** is thin at six players at 80+: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83 (not lined), Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Dressing Tucker gives a seventh. That is workable for a four-line structure, but Roberts is 38 with an expiring deal. When he walks, the count drops to five, and two of those five (Tucker 30, Upshall 21) are depth pieces, not top-four regulars. Stuart (SJ, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, 87 base, 25, POTE 91) replaces Roberts on the blue line with eight years of runway.

**Scoring** is deep today but collapses from the right side. Mogilny at 36 fell to 0.79 pts/g late season; he is not the plan for 2005-06. Gaborik (92, 23) and Sundin (92, 34) anchor the left and centre. The RW side needs an acquisition: Iginla (CGY, 93, 27, $6.50M expiring) is the July priority per the standing target.

**Speed and clutch** are covered in depth and need no comment.

**Goalies** are solved per the GM's March 19 order: Luongo (91 base, 26, 2y) and Belfour (94 displayed, 39, 1y) through the playoffs. Ouellet (23) develops as the eventual third.

## Trajectory

The club is not aging into a hockey cliff — 25 of 30 players are 29 or under — but it is facing a contract cliff that would gut the roster if mishandled in July. The trajectory problem is not the age curve; it is that ten players with POTE 88+ are all on expiring deals and the club holds one fourth-rounder as insurance.

**Sundin** is $8.40M for five more years at 34, locked with no move available. His 91 points at 82 GP say he is still first-line, but at 39 that salary buys nothing. The young core must be built to absorb his decline over two or three years, not around him.

**Fischer** is the clearest liability the brief exposes: $3.70M with four years remaining, production down from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g at age 24. POTE 90 means the grade may recover, but the contract says the club committed four years to a player producing fourth-pair minutes. If he can be moved this summer while POTE is still credible, that money freed is $14.80M over the remaining three years.

**The July cluster is the season.** 13 players, $21.30M expiring, ten of them with POTE 88+. Gaborik (99 pts, 91 base, $1.10M), Richards (66 pts, $1.00M), Nash (39 pts, POTE 95, $1.20M), Eminger (POTE 99, $1.20M) are worth roughly $15-20M combined on realistic 5-6 year deals — a payroll jump from $60M toward $75M, still under the $102M revenue line but with a thinner margin. The GM's March 21 priority order covers Gaborik through Eminger. What is undecided: Kaberle (27, POTE 75, 44 pts, $1.90M) and Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.10M). Kaberle on a 2-year deal at $2.50-3.00M is defensible; Colaiacovo must be locked at 5-6 years while the price is $1.10M.

**Draft capital is gone.** One fourth-rounder. Every acquisition in the next three seasons must come from players on the roster. That means the summer renewal decisions ARE the trade decisions: re-signing them means they are not trade pieces, letting one walk means the next hole has no fill.

## Calendar

The trade deadline closed on March 19, 26 days ago, so the only planning date left is the summer renewal cascade and the one July chase that follows it.

**Gaborik** (RW, 23, $1.10M): Renew first, 5-6 years. 91 base, 87 points last season. He is the anchor of this roster for the next decade and the $1.10M raise will be large, but losing a 23-year-old at 91 to a bidding war is worse.

**Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M): Renew second, 5-6 years. 64 points at 24 with 70 FACE still the best draw-taker on the roster. Lock him before July.

**Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M): Renew, 5-6 years. 0.42 pts/g on flat 13.2 MPG looks thin, but he is 20. The age is the entire case. He is a year younger than Eminger and will still be developing at 23.

**Eminger** (D, 21, $1.20M): Renew, 5-6 years. POTE 99. The GM's February order makes this non-negotiable: the core stays.

**Kaberle** (D, 27, $1.90M): Renew on 4-5 years, not 6. He is past the development window and a starting-pairing defenseman, but a deal through age 31-32 exposes us to a decline tail. The shorter term protects the back end of the contract structure.

**Colaiacovo** (D, 22, $1.10M): Renew on 2 years, conditional on the camp audition the coach asked for. The 4 remaining regular-season games are the audition: give him full minutes now. NYI is 30-38, perfect opposition.

**Chistov** (LW, 21, $1.10M): Renew on 2-3 years. Same logic as Colaiacovo. Young, cheap, prove it before we commit long.

**Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M): Renew on 2 years if his season production supports it. At $1.10M and age 23 the downside is contained, but if he sits below 0.30 pts/g the spot is better spent on a free-agent signing or kept open. Review his numbers before the July market opens.

**Tellqvist** (G, 25, $0.80M): Renew, 3-4 years. POTE in the high 90s. $0.80M is the cheapest backup insurance in the league. The GM's January order stands: give him time.

**Abid** (LW, 25, $0.40M): Renew, 2 years. Base TOUG 80 and CHKG 80 at $0.40M. The coach's checking-75-and-wins-draws gap keeps him relevant at the bottom of the order.

**Belfour** (G, 39, $6.50M): Let go. The GM offered reduced salary in January. Belfour at 39 will not accept it. $6.50M for a 40-year-old next season is the number that ends the conversation.

**Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M): Let go. 38, $2.70M, and the toughness gap is better solved by Bell or a younger body. The March 21 renewal order already flagged his departure.

## The July chase

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 27, 93 base, 140 pts/73 GP, TOUG 85, $6.50M expiring) is the one July signing that matters. He closes the Mogilny scoring void (0.79 pts/g in his final 45 games) and raises the roster's toughness ceiling in one move. CGY cannot retain him: 70 points, 10 expiring contracts, $14.43M profit. The rebuild math forces a move. If they trade him before July, that is a separate package negotiation. If he hits the market, sign him.

**Cammalleri** (LA, 22, POTE 98, 60 pts/61 GP, $1.10M) is the best value in the pool. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring cannot keep both him and Frolov.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 82 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE) is the only player in the league who closes the coach's checking-and-faceoff gap. CHI at 73 points with 10 expiring and $29.46M profit are motivated sellers.

## The remaining four games

Seeding is locked at 133 points, 19 clear of New Jersey. These are development games. Dress Colaiacovo and give him the minutes the coach asked for. If the coach wants early looks at Spezza (4.6 MPG, 0.24 pts/g) or Upshall (4.8 MPG, 0.27 pts/g) before the September camp, these four games against weak opposition are the window. Waiting until September wastes the only live minutes available.

**Deliverable update — Task #2 (Luongo monitoring, assigned January 19):** Complete. Luongo is on this roster at 91 base with 2 years left. DiPietro was eliminated on March 14 when 52 games at 79 base could not close an 11-point grade deficit. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. This task is closed.

## League scan

The deadline passed and the season ended; this scan is for July. We need to confirm who is still available, who has moved, and which packages our limited assets (Tucker, one 4th-rounder, plus any over-80 expiring player via the pick mechanic) can actually reach. The queries I attempted all failed on a column-name error, so this is built from confirmed notes filed through April 12 and the league table in the brief.

**Iginla** remains the single most impactful target available. 93 base, 27 years old, 140 points in 73 games, TOUG 85 which partially closes the toughness ceiling problem, and $6.50M expiring. CGY sit at 70 points with 10 expiring contracts and $14.43M profit; they cannot both re-sign him and field a competitive roster. If he reaches the market as a UFA we sign him on a 5-6 year deal. If CGY move him before July, the over-80-for-a-pick mechanic means even a walk-away nets us draft capital. This is the July priority.

**Bell** is the Coach's exact request: 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 with POTE 81 on a $900K deal with two years left. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are the most motivated sellers in the league. The issue is price — my March 30 note says CHI's profitable position means they require a real package, not just a pick. Tucker plus the 4th-rounder gets us approximately a 74-76 base player, which is well below Bell's 82. We would need to include a roster player, which conflicts with the GM's February order to keep the defensive core. The resolution may be to let Roberts (86, expiring) walk to a third party for a pick, then bundle that pick with Tucker for Bell. Acceptance uncertain.

**Cammalleri** is the best value in the entire July class: 22 years old, POTE 98, 60 points in 61 games on a $1.10M expiring deal. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll cannot retain him alongside Frolov. As a UFA he is a straightforward signing at whatever a 22-year-old with POTE 98 commands — likely $2-3M on a five-year deal. No trade capital required.

**Stuart** closes the Roberts gap at defence with 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, 87 base at 25 with POTE 91. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring on $45.39M are in sell mode, but my March 30 note warns that at 76 points they are not tanking and may hold a POTE 91 blueliner. The acquisition path is unclear because our currency does not reach his value. If he hits UFA, he signs immediately; if he does not, we may need to let Roberts walk and absorb the gap.

**Marleau** at 89 base, 25, 98 points from SJ (same club as Stuart) on $1.60M expiring is the third target from that rebuild. He fills the RW/LW scoring slot that Mogilny leaves. As a UFA he competes with Iginla for our top-six money. If we sign Iginla, Marleau becomes a luxury we may not extend to. If Iginla re-signs with CGY, Marleau becomes the fallback.

**Heatley** at 91 base, 24, on expiring from ATL (84 pts, 11 expiring) is the binary: ATL keeps one of him or Kovalchuk. Kovalchuk is 21 with 104 pts; they probably keep him. Heatley to UFA is then likely. He and Iginla compete for the same role, so we pursue whichever reaches the market first. If both walk, we sign the one who fits the money.

**Theodore** at 91 base, 28, from MTL (66 pts, 15 expiring, $21.59M profit) fits the old January standing order for a high-90s goalie. However, the GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19 with Luongo and Belfour as the answer. If Belfour retires this summer as feared, Theodore becomes the backup target again. I flag him but do not prioritize him over the Coach's explicit forward-needs request.

**Reid** at STL (RW, 23, FACE 80, POTE 94, $600K expiring) is a cheap depth faceoff solution who partially addresses the Coach's concern without spending the 4th-rounder. STL at 86 points with 8 expiring are not desperate sellers, but at $600K expiring he hits UFA automatically. Sign him as a bottom-six centre for two years at $1-1.5M.

## Trade construction

The Coach's request — "one more forward who checks 75+ and wins draws" — is a single-player problem with two solutions in the league, and our currency reaches one of them clearly and the other only if Chicago values salary relief and a low pick as highly as their $31.73M profit suggests they might. The proposals below are ranked by fit-to-cost.

**Avery from LA** closes all three gaps in one man: 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE at 25 years old on a $400K deal with two years left. The cost is **Koltsov** ($1.10M, 23, POTE 94, 19 points in 38 games). LA sits at 79 points with 14 expiring contracts and $52.43M payroll; they are restructuring and a 23-year-old with POTE 94 at $1.10M is exactly the kind of cheap upside piece a sell-mode club accumulates. We save $700K. This is the March 19 package that was proposed and never vetoed. The GM's March 21 renewal priority (Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger) does not include Koltsov, which makes him available.

**Bell from Chicago** is the better player — 82 base versus Avery's low-70s, plus 88 TOUG and 82 FACE at 24 with POTE 81. The cost is **Tucker** ($1.30M, 30, POTE 79) plus the **4th-rounder**. My own March 30 assessment puts that package at approximately 74-76 base value, below Bell's 82. But CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit may value a $1.30M checking winger with 92 CHKG who can eat fourth-line minutes immediately, plus a pick, more than their record suggests they should. The salary difference works: we save $400K, they save $400K. Acceptance is genuinely uncertain and I would not be surprised if they say no.

**Fleury arrives free.** The query confirms him at 89 base, 93 TOUG, $4.30M, contract expired (0 years remaining), 44 points in 60 games. He is a UFA in July. He closes the toughness gap outright (93 TOUG) but checking sits at 77 — barely over the Coach's 75 threshold — and faceoffs at 71 are average. He is a partial fix at full top-six cost. If we sign him at $3.5-4.0M for two years, that money competes directly with Cammalleri ($1.10M expiring, POTE 98, 22 years old) and potentially Iginla. I would rank him behind both: Cammalleri is younger with higher upside, Iginla closes the RW scoring void that Mogilny leaves. Fleury is a fallback if the RW plan falls through and we still need toughness money.

**If none of these land,** the gap goes unfilled and the Coach works around it. Tucker at CHKG 92 and TOUG 88 is the closest internal piece but he played 3 games all year and at 30 with POTE 79 is not a development asset. The practical option is shorter fourth-line shifts from Chlup and Spacek, accepting the defensive-zone risk.

**On the monitoring task (#2, Luongo/DiPietro):** this is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 91 base, 26, with two years left. DiPietro was permanently eliminated on March 14 at 79 base with 52 games played — no sample size fixes an 11-point deficit. The GM closed all goalie monitoring on March 19. Nothing further to do.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window**

This task is closed. You ordered it shut on 2005-03-19: "Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks." Nothing has changed since then, and the premise is resolved from both ends.

**Luongo** is on our roster. 92 base, 26 years old, $1.60M with 2 years left, 45 GP this season. He is not an acquisition target; he is our backup and playoff insurance alongside Belfour at 91 base.

**DiPietro** was eliminated on 2005-03-14. At 52 GP he still reads 79 base overall, 13 points below the high-90s threshold you set on January 15. No sample size closes that gap.

The window never opened because you decided to keep Belfour through the playoffs. Both goalies stay, the task is done, and I am not reopening it.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-14

Next game at NYI on Thursday 14 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games he has earned, and with the club at 82 games played and four remaining against weak opposition, tonight and the next three nights are the last window to answer it with ice time.

**Chlup** has fully earned his spot. 71 games, 16.9 MPG, 59 points (0.83 pts/g) at 19 on the second line. His minutes doubled from 11.0 earlier this season and his rate went up instead of down. No action, no concern.

**Gaborik** is the best player on the roster. 99 points in 82 games at 23, 20.5 MPG, every night. Nothing to say about his development because he is not developing, he has arrived.

**Nash** is getting the chance: 69 games, 13.1 MPG on the second line. His season rate of 0.57 pts/g is below where he started (0.83 per the March window), but the role and minutes are appropriate. The problem is production, not opportunity. Offseason system-fit review, not a lines decision.

**Eminger** plays 64 games at 15.5 MPG on the third defensive pair. His season rate of 0.36 pts/g at 21 confirms the slide. He is getting the chance to be a top-four defenceman and not seizing it. His contract expires this summer and he needs to be moved before July.

**Klesla** is in every game, 82 at 14.8 MPG. 0.37 pts/g at 23, second consecutive decline. He is getting the minutes; he is not producing on them. Offseason sell, not a development problem.

**Chistov** is third-line at 13.1 MPG, 20 points in 68 games (0.29 pts/g) at 21. POTE 95 is high, but the rate is not pushing him up the order. He is getting the chance. He has not yet earned more.

**Upshall** sits fourth line at 7.9 MPG, 20 points in 68 games (0.29 pts/g) at 21. POTE 99. The same story as last month: he is a depth forward right now and the minutes match that. If he wants top-nine minutes he has to take them in camp.

**Spezza** is the one who is not getting the games he has earned. POTE 99 at 21, 46 games on 6.7 MPG, 0.33 pts/g. He is a fourth-line regular getting less than a depth man's minutes. The season is gone for him now, but the offseason decision is clear: he needs a real camp audition or he stops being dressed. Giving him a handful of games against NYI over the next four nights does not fix this. The camp assignment does.

**Koltsov** is the GM's trading chip, stays per standing order. 38 games, 0.50 pts/g on 9.6 MPG. No development concern; he is a roster asset to be moved.

**Spacek** at 19 has 50 games, 0.34 pts/g on 7.6 MPG, and has been scratched recently. Against NYI at 30-38 this is a development night. Dress him. He needs real games before offseason decisions, and four games against the worst team in the division are the only ones left where that costs nothing.

**Alexeev** at 23 is 30 points in 55 games on 8.3 MPG (0.55 pts/g) and has been out of the lineup for 27 games. He is older and closer to a roster decision than development, but his rate says he was contributing when he played. Dressing him for a weak opponent costs nothing and gives a fair look before offseason choices.

**Colaiacovo** is scratched as part of the GM's deliberate D rotation, same framework as Svehla. 17.9 MPG when he plays, 0.39 pts/g at 22. No change needed.

**Stahle** has 4 games all season. POTE 96 at 20, but he is the seventh defenceman. He needs a camp audition, not a call-up against NYI.

**Ouellet** at 23 has 13 games as a backup. Expected role for a young goalie behind Luongo. No development concern.

## Development trends

The season is over and the final numbers are in, so this is the last look before offseason planning. The headline is a correction: my April 7 call that McCabe cleared the sell threshold was wrong.

**McCabe** reads 0.48 pts/g across 82 games in this brief, not the 0.76 I cited on April 7th. He scored 34 points in his first 24 games and just 5 in his remaining 58 (0.09 pts/g). That is a collapse, not a plateau. At 29 with 4 years at $3.00M and a 0.48 season rate, he goes back on the sell list. I owe the GM the correction before offseason planning starts.

**Kaberle** is the one D going the right direction. 0.54 to 0.62 pts/g on minutes rising from 19.4 to 21.5. At 27 with a rising rate and rising load, he is the blue-line centrepiece next year. Build around him, sell the rest.

**Chistov** is quietly growing into a role. His rate held at 0.30 while his minutes went from 9.5 to 14.0. At 21, holding production while taking on 50% more ice is the correct trajectory. He earns a middle-six spot at camp.

**Spacek** is confirmed dead for the season: 0.55 to 0.28 pts/g, minutes from 16.0 down to 5.2. The March bump never materialized. Offseason audition or stop dressing, same call as Spezza and Upshall.

**Richards** at 0.71 on flat minutes is now his season, not a blip. At 24 that should be going up. Offseason system-fit review stands.

**Gaborik** at 1.12 on 21.2 MPG in 82 games is still very good. The 1.42 start was a hot streak, not the norm. He is a keeper and the top-end winger.

**The veterans** are aging as expected. Mogilny at 36 dropped to 0.83, Roberts at 38 to 0.86, Sundin at 34 to 0.97. All still productive, none will be there in two years. Planning around the age cliff starts now.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape and nobody needs a minutes change tonight.

**The lowest morale on the roster is 88** (Spezza), and that is in the safe zone. Everyone else sits 91 or above, with the core group at 100. The recent results have the dressing room right where I want it three games from season's end.

**Spezza** at 6.7 MPG and 88 morale is the only name worth a second look. If he's a 70s-calibre centre, the band says 10 MPG and he's 3.3 short. But 88 is not sliding, and the GM's standing order has him on the fourth line for development space. I'm not moving him for a morale number that hasn't moved.

**Abid** remains the oddity: 100 morale, 13.8 MPG, 66 points. His morale has no complaint. The minutes mismatch is a wasted-resource problem for the offseason, not a tonight problem.

No change. Lines are right, morale is stable, and the four games left are about execution, not room management.

## Role composition

Are the units built from players who suit their jobs, and is anything missing from the roster that no arrangement fixes? The answer today is that everything above the fourth line is correct, and the fourth line remains a roster problem I've already raised.

**L1** is the best-constructed unit on the team. Checking mean 80 with Fischer at 82 and Roberts at 82 gives it a real two-way spine, while Gaborik's 96 scoring and 99 playmaking anchor the offense. Sundin's 88 on draws means they win the draw and set up. Nothing to change.

**L2** works for what it is: a secondary scoring line with Chlup at 77 on draws and McCabe's 82 checking giving it a defensive floor. Mogilny's 90 scoring carries the offense. Adequate, not elite on either end, but the right shape for a second line.

**L3** is better than people think. Checking best 91, Richards at 72 on draws and 92 stamina, Abid's 70 toughness. This line can kill penalties and win races along the wall. It's a competent third line.

**L4 (Koltsov, Spezza, Upshall)** is where the roster lets us down. Checking mean 62, toughness mean 57, faceoffs mean 51. Nobody on this line can play a checking role. There is no one on the roster to put there who can check and is young enough to warrant minutes — the checking inventory tops out at Jackman 87, Roberts 82, McCabe 82, Fischer 82, all of whom are already slotted. This is a known gap and no arrangement fixes it.

**K2 actually has the higher checking mean (81) than K1 (76)**, but the split is correct. K1 needs Sundin's 88 faceoff to win the draw and get set; K2 gets McCabe and Jackman (82 and 87) for pure blocking and angling. The auto-pairing with L1 and L2 confirms this is the right order.

**Against NYI at 30-38**, this is a game we can afford to develop the fourth line in. The game-classification principle says maximize against quality opponents; NYI is not one. No reason to scratch the kids tonight.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** should we adjust anything — lines, D pair order, goalie — specifically because of NYI tonight?

**No change to the lines or defensive pair order.** We are 59-13-5 and they are 30-38-4. We have beaten them 5-1-1 this season, outscoring them 21-12. Their best forward is Peca at 85 OVR on their second line, and our second pair (Kaberle/McCabe) handles him fine because McCabe brings 84 checking and 80 toughness into the matchups while Peca's line-mate Simon is a 72 OVR plod. Fischer/Jackman on the first pair against Yashin (64 checking, 52 toughness, a pure playmaker) is already the right configuration — they win every board battle Yashin tries to start. Swapping pair slots to put Fischer/Jackman against Peca would be a marginal gain against a team we have already beaten six times, and principle one says I don't break chemistry for that.

**DiPietro (83 OVR, age 23)** has rebound control at 62. That's the one soft spot on their sheet, and our first power-play unit with Gaborik (99 accuracy, 94 shot power) in front will find it. No special play call needed; just keep shooting.

**Luongo starts.** He's at 92 OVR, morale 100, no fatigue flag in front of me tonight. GM: check his icon on screen before confirming per the standing order. If he shows tired, Tellqvist (73) is the backup and it'll be a long night, but that's the same risk every night with Tellqvist and it's unlikely to matter against a team that generates 2.00 goals per game.

**The season series context matters:** NYI went 4-1-0 in their last five and they're at home. They're not going to lie down. But they're a 30-win club and we allow 1.50 goals a game. This isn't a game that needs tactical intervention. Trust the sheet.

## Owed

The defenceman sell-list review, item #1. The season is done — McCabe and Klesla played all 82, so these are final numbers. Everything is locked now.

**McCabe** stays. 62 points in 82 games on 22.1 MPG is 0.76 pts/g. He clears the 0.60 sell threshold I set in March. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M he anchors the top pair and that's where he stays. No change from last week's call; the number just firmed up as the last game added to his total.

**Kaberle** stays. GM's standing order: "Kaberle is definitely a keeper. Kaberle is a star defenseman." 44 points in 74 games is 0.60 pts/g on 20.8 MPG. No change.

**Fischer** stays. GM's standing order. 41 points in 77 games is 0.53 pts/g at age 24 with 4 years left. No change.

**Jackman** is the sell. 37 points in 80 games on 29.6 MPG is 0.46 pts/g. That's down a tick from my 0.48 read at 73 games in late March — the last seven games added nothing. He's the cheapest top-pair minutes in the league at $0.70M x 3, which is why he still has trade value, but his production doesn't justify the ice load anymore. Sell this offseason.

**Klesla** is the sell. 30 points in 82 games on 14.8 MPG is 0.37 pts/g. Second straight declining season (0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23) on flat minutes. $0.90M x 2. Sell.

**Eminger** is the sell. 23 points in 64 games on 15.5 MPG is 0.36 pts/g at age 21. His contract expires after this season. After July he's a UFA loss with zero return. Must move before free agency.

What changed since last week: nothing shifted in the hierarchy. Jackman's rate ticked down one more point from 0.48 to 0.46 as the final games landed. Everything else is confirmed final. The offseason window is now open — three defencemen go.
