markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-09

Next game vs NYI on Sunday 10 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: with 82 games in the book and one left, who on the young core has earned real opportunity and who is still getting scraps with nothing to show for it.

**Chlup** at 19 has made his case conclusively: 59 points in 71 games (0.83 pts/g), 16.9 MPG on the second line, morale 98. He belongs in the top nine permanently and there's nothing left to prove this season.

**Spezza** is the clearest waste. POTE 99, age 21, 15 points in 46 games on 6.7 MPG from the fourth line. His rate is 0.33 pts/g and his morale sits at 88, the lowest of any young player. He's been given nothing and produced nothing because of it. The season is a write-off; camp assignment next year is the only lever.

**Upshall** mirrors Spezza exactly: POTE 99, age 21, 20 points in 68 games on 7.9 MPG, fourth line, 0.29 pts/g. Two players with the same scouting report getting the same garbage minutes and producing the same nothing. Both need a real audition in camp or they stop being roster pieces.

**Alexeev** is the best rate-per-minute on the bench: 30 points in 55 games (0.55 pts/g) on just 8.3 MPG. He's scratched while Upshall plays 7.9 MPG and produces half the rate. The numbers say Alexeev deserves the fourth-line spot over Upshall heading into this final game and beyond.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 has POTE 99 but 12 points in 31 games (0.39 pts/g). His 17.9 MPG when in is respectable but he isn't making enough of it to unseat Eminger or Klesla. Scratching him is defensible on production.

**Klesla** at 23, 30 points in 82 games on 14.8 MPG (0.37 pts/g), is a second declining season. He's not a development concern anymore; he's a trade asset, which I've already flagged.

**Nash** at 0.57 pts/g on the second line is generous. His March rate was 0.43 on flat minutes. He's earning a roster spot but not the second-line role he occupies.

## Development trends

This is the last development review before the season ends: six games left, and the numbers that matter for offseason planning are now locked in. The headline is that one young player broke through and three more fell off the map simultaneously.

**Chlup** at 19 went 0.62→0.88 pts/g while minutes nearly doubled from 11.0 to 18.2 across 58 games. Full-season rate lands near 0.83. At 19, taking on that load and improving his rate is rare. He is a permanent top-nine centre, no audition needed next camp.

**Spezza** at 21 went 0.43→0.24 on 9.1→4.6 MPG. **Spacek** at 19 went 0.55→0.28 on 16.0→5.2. **Upshall** at 21 went 0.33→0.27 on 13.4→4.8. All three lost their spots mid-season and never got them back. Their season is over for development purposes. Camp audition next fall is the only path forward, and if they do not earn minutes in camp they should not dress.

**Nash** at 20 went 0.83→0.42 with minutes flat at 13.2. The role did not change; the production did. Full-season rate lands near 0.56. Same system-fit question as Richards: the environment may not suit him, and neither man is going to fix it by playing the same role harder.

**Koltsov** at 23 went 1.10→0.29 on 9.9 MPG. Full season about 0.43 on 38 games. The trading chip has evaporated. Any return is better than holding a player who just scored 11 points in 28 games.

**Klesla** at 23 went 0.50→0.31 on flat 14.9 MPG. Full season 0.37. Two consecutive declining years confirmed. Sell. **Jackman** at 24 went 0.65→0.39 on 29.4 MPG. Full season 0.46. Confirmed sell.

**Kaberle** at 27 went 0.54→0.62 with minutes up from 19.4 to 21.5. The one defenceman on this roster going the right direction. He and his contract should be the offseason priority.

**Richards** at 24 went 1.08→0.71 on 15.8 MPG. Full season 0.82. Not a disaster, but for a 24-year-old first-line centre it is the wrong direction. Offseason system-fit review.

**McCabe** full season lands at 0.76. Above my 0.60 sell threshold, so he stays. But the recent 58-game window at 0.48 on 21.5 MPG is not a player building toward year four.

**Veterans:** Sundin at 34 went 1.46→0.97 on increased minutes. Mogilny at 36 went 1.62→0.83. Roberts at 38 went 1.29→0.86. All three aging as expected. They contributed. Plan to not need them next year at full load.

## Morale watch

The room is at an average of 92 with nobody below 88, so nothing needs a fix before Sunday. This is the first check all season where I can say that and mean it.

**Spezza** sits lowest at 88 on 6.7 MPG across 46 games. He's been at 88 for weeks, holding steady. Six games left changes nothing — his season is set. The camp decision in the summer is where this gets addressed, not from the bench now.

**Spacek** at 89 and scratched: same read. 7.6 MPG over 50 games is his season, and the 10 MPG target I set in March is dead. He's not bleeding morale from this; the number is flat.

**Upshall** at 91 on 7.9 MPG in the fourth line is exactly what a depth winger expects. No concern.

**Jackman** at 29.6 MPG is the heaviest load on the roster, and we know from March it's eroding his production, but his morale is 100. He's not going to crack from this before season's end.

**Abid** at 13.8 MPG on 66 points has been my flagged mismatch since March, but his morale is 100. He's not complaining. Leave it alone.

No change tonight. Everyone is right where they need to be for NYI.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit suits its job and whether the roster can fill every role at all. Against a 30-38 NYI club with 6 games left, the answer on arrangement is "leave it alone," and the answer on roster depth is a confirmation of what I already reported in March.

**L1** is the best unit on the team in every category that matters. Scoring 85 mean with Gaborik at 96, playmaking 83 with him at 98, speed 88 with 99 behind it. Fischer's checking 81 gives it a second body on the back end. No reason to touch it.

**L2** carries faceoffs of 55 mean against a best of 76 (Chlup). That's thin. Chlup wins draws, Mogilny and Nash don't, and the D pair (McCabe/Kaberle) is offensive. Against a strong C on an opponent's second line this line will start in its own zone more often than not, but NYI isn't that team.

**L3** has the checking spread (90 best via Chistov, 72 mean) which is fine. Richards at 71 faceoffs is the third-best draw man on the roster. Stamina mean of 69 is low; Richards at 95 is carrying it. Eminger's role is irrelevant now — he's a confirmed sell before July.

**L4** is the structural problem and has been since January. Checking mean 61, toughness mean 57, faceoffs 50 mean with 51 best. Koltsov's value is gone (0.28 pts/g per March finding). Spezza and Upshall both collapsed to 4.8 and 4.9 MPG respectively. With 6 games left there is no arrangement that fixes this line, and it isn't a matchup that requires it.

**P1** is lethal: scoring 85, playmaking 84, speed 86. Sundin-centred, Gaborik on the wing, Kaberle and Jackman on the points. The only oddity is Jackman on PP1 given his 30 MPG load, but the unit has 86 stamina mean so they can handle it.

**K2** at checking 80 mean is actually our best penalty-kill checking unit, better than K1 at 75. That's because McCabe (81), Jackman (86) and Abid (69 toughness) are bodies. Fine.

**Defencemen, end-of-season update (deliverable #1):**

- **McCabe**: 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG across 82 games. Clears the 0.60 threshold. Keeper, anchors the top pair.
- **Kaberle**: GM's own words, "definitely a keeper, star defenseman." No update needed.
- **Jackman**: 0.48 pts/g on 30 MPG across 73 games at $0.70M x 3. Confirmed sell. His value is the cheap top-pair minutes.
- **Klesla**: 0.36 pts/g on 15 MPG, second consecutive declining season at age 23. Sell at $0.90M x 2.
- **Eminger**: 0.38 pts/g on 15.8 MPG, $1.2M expiring. Must move before July or he's a UFA loss.

No composition changes for this game. NYI is 30-38 and this is not a maximize-quality night.

## Opponent matchup

**Against a 30-38-4 team we are 133 points ahead of, the lines as set are right. No change.**

**The talent gap is the whole story.** We score 3.70 and allow 1.70. They score 2.30 and allow 2.30. We are 3-1-1 against them this season. Their power play is 8.3% on 276 chances. Their penalty kill won't matter because we'll be the ones with the pucks.

**Yashin** is their only elite player. Hands of 92/93/92 on passing, puck control, and deking. Sundin at OVR 89 with FACE 87 versus Yashin's 70 wins the draw and the ice position. No special assignment needed; the matchup already favors us.

**Peca** is a two-way centre (CHKG 88, AGGR 92) but his OVR is 85 to Richards' 85. This is a wash and doesn't require adjustment.

**Luongo in net** with no fatigue icon showing. 92 OVR against a team averaging 2.30 goals a game. Straightforward start.

**D-man sell review (obligation #1, game 74 of season):** Kaberle, Fischer, and McCabe stay. Jackman is the confirmed third sell candidate at 0.48 pts/g on 30 MPG across 73 games; his value is cheap top-pair minutes to a club that runs him lighter. Eminger (expiring, must move by July) and Klesla (0.36 pts/g at 23, two declining seasons) remain the first two on the list. Nothing tonight changes this; the pairings are correct for the game.

**Development is already built in.** Chlup (19) centres the second line, Nash (20) wings it, Eminger and Klesla (both under 23) are the third pair, Spezza (21) centres the fourth. The young guys are getting top-six and top-four minutes already. No additional development tweak is needed against this opponent because the roster construction does the work without intervention.

## Owed

**Item #1 — defenceman sell/keep analysis, updated for NYI game.** The season is essentially final; here are the closing numbers and what they mean for the offseason.

**McCabe** finishes at 62 points in 82 games, 0.76 pts/g on 22.1 MPG. He clears the 0.70 bar I set in March. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M he anchors the top pair. Confirmed keeper. No change from April 7.

**Jackman** closes at 37 points in 80 games, 0.46 pts/g on 29.6 MPG. That's down from 0.48 at 73 GP on March 23. The load keeps eating his production. Sell this offseason at $0.70M x 3; his value on the market is cheap top-pair minutes.

**Klesla** finishes at 30 points in 82 games, 0.37 pts/g on 14.8 MPG. Second consecutive year below 0.40 (0.38 last year). Confirmed sell at $0.90M x 2. No change.

**Eminger** finishes at 23 points in 64 games, 0.36 pts/g on 15.5 MPG. His contract expires in July. If we don't move him before free agency he walks for nothing. That deadline hasn't moved since March 30.

**Kaberle** finishes at 44 points in 74 games, 0.59 pts/g on 20.8 MPG. The GM has named him a star. His deal expires; renewal is the GM's desk but it's the priority on blue line.

**Fischer** finishes at 41 points in 77 games, 0.53 pts/g on 22.4 MPG. GM's keeper, no debate.

**Colaiacovo** at 12 points in 31 games, 0.39 pts/g, also expiring. Low volume, middling rate. Could be a depth trade piece or a camp audition. I have no strong case either way.

Nothing material has shifted since April 7. The sell list is Jackman, Klesla, Eminger. The keepers are McCabe, Kaberle, Fischer.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-07
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-07

Toronto 59-13-5, 133 pts after 82 games.

## Role coverage

The season is 59-13-5, the deadline has passed, and this exercise is about next year: who leaves in July and which holes they leave that the existing roster cannot fill.

**Toughness** is the one gap with no internal solution. Zero Toronto players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades. The best is **Jackman** at 75, and he is a defenceman. The coach's flag about Roberts being the only checking forward above 80 is accurate and confirms the problem: the team has no player whose primary role is physical intimidation. Only acquisition fixes this, and **Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81) closes toughness and checking in one body. He remains the single most valuable summer target.

**Checking on forward** is thin heading into 2005-06. **Roberts** (86 CHKG, 38) walks this July per the renewal priority. That leaves **Fischer** (82, 24) and **Upshall** (80, 21) as the only remaining forwards at 80+. Bell at 86 CHKG slots into the same role Roberts played, which is why the two gaps collapse into one trade.

**Faceoffs** shows **Sundin** at 90 with nothing above 75 behind him. **Chlup** at 75 and **Richards** at 70 are below-average draw-takers. The GM's Jan 25 position stands: adding a wing does not solve centre-specific faceoffs. The internal fix is Chlup's development at 19 with POTE 99. If he reaches 80+ FACE within two seasons, this closes itself. No trade target is needed specifically for faceoffs.

**Scoring** is currently deep at 10 players above 80, but **Mogilny** (94, 36, confirmed decline to 0.79 pts/g) and **Roberts** (88, 38) both depart. That drops the 80+ pool to roughly 8, with **Gaborik** 92, **Sundin** 92 and **Afinogenov** 90 carrying the top. The RW scoring crisis flagged on March 23 makes **Heatley** (91 base) or **Doan** the July acquisition priority. Neither fits the Tucker-plus-4th-rounder price range, so this is a free-agent or large-package target, not a chip move.

**Durability** is thin behind the starters. **Roberts** (98), **Afinogenov** (95), **Fischer** (92), **Abid** (90) are the four above 80. Next man up is Spacek at 79 and Eminger at 75. With Mogilny gone the group is three deep at best, but this is manageable given the small number of long-season injuries the team has absorbed.

**Goalies** are settled per the March 19 standing order. Belfour (1.93 GAA, .931 SV) and Luongo (2.67, .889) carry the playoffs. Ouellet is the depth call at 23.

## Trajectory

The question is whether this club is aging into a cliff and whether its money is arranged to protect the next three seasons. The age curve is healthy: 14 players 23 or under, 11 at 24-29, only four 34 and above. The shape is what the manual asks for. The problem is not age. It is that 13 of these contracts worth $21.30M expire this July, and the 2006 class adds another $15.44M on top of that.

**Gaborik** at 99 points at age 23 on $1.10M is the single most important re-signing this club will ever make. A 5-year deal at even $3.00M locks the franchise's best player through age 28 for a total cost that is a fraction of what a 99-point winger commands on the open market. Every month he stays unsigned is a month another club's phone rings. Richards (66 pts, 24, $1.00M) follows the same logic: 5 years at roughly $2.50M is cheap for a second-line centre in his prime.

**Nash and Eminger** are the second wave. Nash is 20, POTE 95, 39 points in 69 games. Eminger is 21, POTE 99, 23 points in 64 games. Both on $1.20M expiring deals. Lock them on 5-6 years at modest bumps and the young core is protected through 2010. If either walks because Toronto dawdled, the roster loses two players whose replacement cost will be enormous.

**Sundin** is the structural constraint nobody can move. $8.40M with five years left means he is under contract at ages 35 through 39 with POTE 60. He is still producing (91 points this season), but the decline is coming and there is no mid-contract renegotiation. Accept the money as the price of having him now. The number to watch: he will consume 14% of current payroll through his late 30s regardless of form.

**Chlup** at 19, POTE 95, $2.34M with 2 years left is the next contract crisis after the July 2005 class. He is at 59 points in 71 games and climbing. By July 2006 he will be 21 with a breakout season behind him, and his price will have multiplied. This is a summer-2006 priority that needs planning now: when his deal expires, he gets 5 years at a star-level number.

**The 2006 cluster** ($15.44M across nine players) is less dangerous because Mogilny ($5.50M, 36, declining to 0.79 pts/g) walks and frees that money. But Chlup, Luongo, Koltsov, Spezza, and Klesla all hit one summer. If the July 2005 renewals go smoothly, the 2006 renewal class is manageable because Mogilny's exit creates space.

**Draft capital:** one fourth-rounder. That is nothing. Every acquisition must be funded with players. This does not change the trajectory answer but it means the club cannot patch holes via the draft in the next two seasons. The development pipeline (Stahle POTE 96, Spacek POTE 91, Colaiacovo POTE 99) is the depth, not the draft board.

**The money:** $60.04M payroll against $97.82M revenue leaves $25.38M profit. If Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk in July as planned, that frees $9.20M. The core re-signings (Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger at roughly $2-3M each) would add maybe $8-10M to payroll. The club can afford it. The constraint is not money. It is the simultaneity of the renewals and the risk of losing any one of them to a bidding war.

The cliff is not age. The cliff is July 2005 if the renewals fail.

## Calendar

**The deadline closed 19 days ago and we traded nothing.** The GM's March 19 order kept everyone except Tucker and the fourth-rounder, and neither moved. The question now is purely the summer: 13 contracts expiring simultaneously, worth $21.30M, covering the entire spine from Gaborik to Belfour. The next six weeks are about which of those 13 we keep and on what terms.

**Renewal order for July:**

**Gaborik** at 91 base, 87 points, age 23, $1.10M is the single highest-value renewal in the league. Five or six years at a meaningful raise locks a generative talent into the peak of our window. No decision is more urgent.

**Richards** at 24, $1.00M, is the second lock. He is four years from his prime, centres the second line, and his $1.00M is absurd for a 64-point centre. Five years.

**Nash** at 20 and **Eminger** at 21 are the third wave. Both are at $1.20M on one-year deals, both carry potential the coach relies on. Four or five years on each. The risk is not the money; it is the 13-contract cluster arriving in the same July. Locking these four first splits the wave.

**Kaberle** at 27, $1.90M: three years is adequate. He is a good defender entering his prime but at $1.90M he commands a top-pairing salary and we need flexibility for the UFA market.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, $1.10M: two or three years. He is behind Eminger and Kaberle in the pecking order and should earn his raise before locking longer.

**Chistov** at 21, **Alexeev** at 23, **Upshall** at 21: these three need a performance bar before re-signing. Upshall specifically has been flagged by the coach all season at 5 MPG and 0.28 pts/g. If his camp numbers do not improve, let him walk and spend the roster spot.

**Abid** at 25, $0.40M: he is the cheapest toughness on the roster with TOUG 80 and CHKG 80. Re-sign at two years, $0.60M-$0.80M. If the coach still cannot dress him 15 MPG a night, move him to a team that will.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M: GM's standing order is to keep him and give him time. Two-year deal at $0.90M as Luongo's backup. Check the goalies every summer.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M: offer a reduced two-year at perhaps $3.00M. He will likely refuse and walk. That is acceptable. Luongo and Tellqvist are the future.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M: walk. GM already decided. His checking role gets filled by Abid or a cheaper UFA.

**UFA targets if cap-space allows:** Marleau (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 pts) and Gagne (PHI, 25, 86 base, 94 pts) both expire from struggling clubs. Either one solves the RW crisis Mogilny's decline opened. Marleau is the bigger fish; Gagne is more likely to sign here.

**The seven games remaining** are about health. Chlup at 19 and 0.87 pts/g deserves top-nine minutes now so he arrives in camp with NHL seasoning. Stahle at POTE 96 needs four or five real shifts a night. Neither changes our playoff rotation, but both change next October.

**On the owed task (#2, Luongo and DiPietro monitoring):** Closed. The GM confirmed on March 19 that all goalie monitoring is shut, Luongo is on the roster at 91 base, and the goalie situation is solved. DiPietro at 79 base was eliminated on March 9 for failing the high-90s standard. Nothing further to deliver.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: after the 13 contracts expire this July, which players from outside clubs fill the holes that internal depth cannot, and on what terms would their clubs let them go?

The season is done. Toronto at 133 points had no reason to make a deadline deal. That means every gap the coverage phase identified — zero forwards at 80+ TOUG, Mogilny's exit leaving the RW slot empty, checking depth collapsing with Roberts — is unresolved heading into July. The league scan gives a clear answer on which holes can be filled and at what price.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 24, 91 base, $1.10M expiring, 131 points in 79 games) is the single best fit for Toronto's RW scoring crisis. ATL at 84 points with 11 expiring players on $36.79M payroll cannot retain him. My Feb 28 note flagged ATL's binary: they hold both Kovalchuk (89 base) and Heatley on expiring deals and can re-sign one, not both. At 84 points they are still well outside the playoff line, so rebuilding logic applies. The cleanest route is UFA: Heatley's $1.10M current salary means a 5-year deal at $3.50-4.00M is affordable against $25.38M profit, and Toronto's competitive profile as the league's best team helps land him. A July trade package (Chistov plus the 4th-rounder) is the fallback if ATL shops him in June.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, POTE 81, $900K, 2 years left) is the only player in the league closing the structural toughness gap in one body. Chicago at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit is a clear seller, but Bell has two years remaining so this requires a trade, not a UFA signing. Chicago wants young assets: Colaiacovo (21, POTE 99, $1.10M) is the package centerpiece. If the GM cannot re-sign all of Nash, Eminger, and Colaiacovo in July (the March 21 renewal order puts Colaiacovo below Nash and Eminger), Bell becomes the destination for Colaiacovo's value rather than a re-signing he may not secure.

**Cammalleri** (LA, RW, 22, POTE 98, 60 points in 61 GP at 20 MPG, $1.10M expiring) is the best value target on the board. LA at 79 points with 14 expiring on $52.43M payroll cannot retain both him and Frolov (22, POTE 96, 55 pts). As an expiring UFA, Cammalleri costs zero trade assets — only salary. A 5-year deal at $2.50M locks a potential top-line RW through age 27 at less than half what his production eventually commands.

**Stuart** (SJ, D, 25, 87 base, 80 TOUG, 89 CHKG, POTE 91, $1.80M expiring, 52 points in 77 GP at 30 MPG) brings the physical presence Toronto's blue line lacks. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring and $20.74M profit are comfortable sellers. The GM's Jan 19 logic (young plus high-POTE beats proven plus lower-POTE) argues for keeping Eminger (21, POTE 99) over a 25-year-old at POTE 91, which was correct for Chara at 27 whose ceiling was set. Stuart is different: he is still 25, his TOUG 80 and CHKG 89 give the defense a physical identity no Toronto blueliner currently carries, and he is expiring, meaning he's available via UFA rather than requiring a young asset in return. If Toronto can sign him as a free agent at $2.50-3.00M, the Jan 19 objection largely disappears because no prospect goes out the door to get him.

**McLaren** (SJ, D, 82 base, 47 points in 82 GP at 31 MPG, $2.20M expiring) is the fallback blue-line target. Same club as Stuart, same seller logic, same UFA availability. Lower grade and higher cost than Stuart, so only if Stuart's price escalates or he re-signs elsewhere.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, 89 base, 127 points in 82 GP, $3.00M expiring) carries the highest production on any expiring deal in the league. His age is unclear from available data and needs verification before committing a target slot. If he is 26-28, he is a better fit than Heatley at the same cost tier. If 30+, the trajectory math changes and Heatley takes priority. Flagging for investigation.

**Not targeting:** Sturm (PHI, LW, 85 base, 81 pts) is a fine player at $1.00M from a financially distressed club, but he is a left wing and Toronto's LW depth (Gaborik, Nash, Afinogenov) is already strong. The gap is right wing. Drury (BUF, LW, 89 base, 99 pts) carries the same positional redundancy.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which of the three summer targets do we get, and do we need to trade for any of them or can we sign them as free agents?

Heatley, Stuart, and Cammalleri are all expiring deals. The cleanest route for each is UFA in July, not a trade. A trade only becomes necessary if another club outbids us, or if the player's team shops him in June before free agency opens. Bell is different: two years remaining, so a trade is the only route.

**Bell** is the one trade we must construct. He closes the toughness gap that has no internal fix, and his two remaining years make UFA impossible. Package: **Colaiacovo + Tucker + the 4th-rounder** for Bell. CHI at 78 points with 10 expiring and $31.73M profit are selling everything they can. Colaiacovo is POTE 99 at 22 with BALA 85 and SHPW 84 — a franchise blueliner for any rebuilding club. Tucker adds 92 CHKG and 88 TOUG for two more years at a veteran number. They shed $900K and get a player with a ceiling 18 potential points higher. Acceptance is uncertain: Colaiacovo has only played 31 games, and CHI might not trust his readiness.

The cost to us is steep on paper. Colaiacovo is POTE 99 and Bell is POTE 81. But Colaiacovo is expiring and sits below Nash and Eminger on the renewal priority. If we cannot sign him in July, we lose him for nothing, and Bell becomes the return. The GM must decide: keep Colaiacovo (no toughness fix, POTE 99 on the roster) or trade him for the one body that closes a structural gap (Bell, arrived now at 24). I recommend the trade, because the gap has existed all season and no internal solution has appeared.

**Heatley** signs in July as a free agent at $3.50-4.00M on five years. No trade asset goes out the door. ATL at 84 with Kovalchuk also expiring cannot retain both; their rebuild logic favors Kovalchuk (21, 104 pts/61 GP, lower cost to re-sign). If another club outbids us for Heatley, the insurance package is Upshall + 4th + Koltsov — but that means giving two POTE 94+ players for one arrived scorer, which only makes sense if Heatley is the only RW available at that level.

**Stuart** signs as a UFA at $2.50-3.00M on five years. No trade asset needed. His TOUG 80 and CHKG 89 give the blue line a physical identity no Toronto blueliner carries, and he arrives with eight years of development at 25. SJ at 76 points with 13 expiring cannot keep him. If another club signs him, McLaren (SJ, 82 base, 47 pts/82 GP) is the same-club fallback.

**Payroll math for all three landing:** Mogilny ($5.50M), Roberts ($2.70M), and Belfour ($6.50M) walk for $14.70M freed. Heatley ($3.75M midpoint), Stuart ($2.75M midpoint), Bell ($0.90M), and core re-signings (Gaborik $3.00M, Richards $2.50M, Nash $2.00M, Eminger $2.00M) add roughly $17M. Net payroll increase of about $2.3M against $25.38M profit. The club absorbs it without strain.

**If none land:** RW scoring drops to Gaborik's 99 points against a league that knows he's the only option. Toughness stays at zero forwards above 80 TOUG. The team is 59-13-5 with those problems, so it can survive them, but the top-six loses a second 100-point option and the playoff physicality question resurfaces. The fallback is chasing Doan (89 base, expiring from PHX) and Sturm (85 base, $1.00M from distressed PHI) as second-tier UFA targets, and accepting that toughness remains unresolved for another year.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window**

This is closed. Luongo is on our roster at 92 overall, 26, $1.60M with 2 years left and 45 GP this season. He was acquired in February, and the task of monitoring his availability was fulfilled when the deal landed. The GM closed all goalie monitoring himself on 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks"), which supersedes this assignment.

DiPietro was tracked through February and into March. At 52 games he still reads 79 base overall, with a 3.64 GAA and 84.9% save percentage at age 21. That fails the January 15 standard for a high-90s goalie and eliminates him permanently. No sample size closes an 11-point grade deficit.

Nothing has changed since the last time I reported on either player. Both questions are answered; the GM's own order closes the file.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-07
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-04-07

Next game vs NYI on Friday 08 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The season is done at 82 games, so this is a ledger review: who got the games their calibre earned, and who didn't.

**Spezza** is the clear miss. POTE 99, 21 years old, 6.7 MPG across 46 games, 0.33 pts/g. He finished on the fourth line and barely played. For a first-round talent with the highest scouting number on the roster, that's a development failure this coaching staff owns. The season is gone for him; the camp assignment next fall is the only lever that matters.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG across 55 games earned more than he got. That production-to-ice-time ratio is the same shape Abid's was in March. He was scratched late, which means we phased him out while he was outproducing guys on the top nine. He deserves a legitimate top-nine audition in camp.

**Stahle** got 4 games. POTE 96, age 20, 17.8 MPG in those brief shifts. Four games is not an audition — it's a mop-up appearance. We have no read on him. Next camp must fix that with real minutes or we stop pretending he's part of the future.

**Chlup** is the one who earned it and delivered. 59 points on 16.9 MPG at 19, 0.83 pts/g on the second line. The March read holds: he belongs in the top nine permanently and there's nothing to change.

**Gaborik** needs no discussion. 99 points, 20.5 MPG, 1.21 pts/g at 23. He earned every second and more.

**Spacek** at 19 finished on 7.6 MPG and 0.34 pts/g across 50 games. That's a reasonable first taste. He's not owed more yet. He'll compete in camp.

**Nash** at 0.57 pts/g on the second line at 13 MPG is fair for a 20-year-old. The March decline from 0.83 to 0.43 was the hot start correcting, not a collapse. System-fit review in the offseason stands.

**Eminger** (0.36 pts/g, 15.5 MPG) and **Klesla** (0.37 pts/g, 14.8 MPG) both got their games and didn't produce. They're not development questions anymore — they're sell decisions for the GM.

**Colaiacovo** at 31 games fits the GM's rotation philosophy. At 0.39 pts/g on 17.9 MPG when he did play, his rate is low enough that he didn't claw for more.

## Development trends

The question this answers: is anyone developing in a direction that should change next season's plan? With five games left, this is the last look before offseason decisions.

**Chlup** is the one. 0.88 pts/g on 18.2 MPG in 58 games since December, up from 0.62 on 11.0 in his first 13. He's 19 and his rate went UP while his minutes went UP by 7 a night. That's the profile of a player whose current role is too small. He belongs on the second line permanently next season, possibly pushing for first-line centre minutes.

**Richards** is the new concern. At 24, the expected direction is up; he went 1.08→0.71 on flat minutes (16.9→15.8). A 34% drop with no role change, at an age where it shouldn't happen. Either the system doesn't suit him or the October pace was unsustainable. Needs a serious look this offseason before he's pencilled in as a first-line centre.

**Afinogenov** at 25 tells the same story. 1.17→0.73 on flat 16.6 MPG. Prime age, flat role, 38% drop. Same offseason review as Richards.

**Abid** carries a double problem. 1.09→0.70 AND 20.1→11.5 MPG. His rate dropped while his minutes were cut nearly in half. At 25 he should be climbing. The mismatch I flagged in March has gotten worse.

**Kaberle** is going the right direction at 27. 0.54→0.62 on 19.4→21.5 MPG. More load, more production. The GM's keeper call is confirmed by the data.

**Fischer** at 24 went 0.63→0.50 on 20.8→22.9. Rate down, load up. At 24 that's a stretch problem, not a talent problem. 0.50 on 23 MPG is still quality second-pair output. No concern.

**McCabe** at 29 finished 1.42→0.48. Season rate below 0.60, so he goes back on the sell list per my March 30 note. The hot start was the anomaly.

**Mogilny** at 36: 1.62→0.83 on 16.9→19.1. Age is doing what age does. Planning around it starts now, not after July.

**Veterans Sundin and Roberts** are aging normally. Sundin 1.46→0.97 on more ice, Roberts 1.29→0.86 on more ice. Still productive, just less per shift. Expected.

**The stalled young group** (Spezza 0.43→0.24 on 4.6 MPG, Upshall 0.33→0.27 on 4.8 MPG, Spacek 0.55→0.28 on 5.2 MPG) are confirmed dead seasons. Nothing new to decide before the last five games.

## Morale watch

The room is in good shape heading into the final week. A winning stretch has lifted morale across the board, and the only outlier is Spezza at 86, a known problem with no fix available now.

**Spezza** sits at 86 on 6.7 MPG season average, down from 9.1 earlier this year per the collapse note. His production fell in lockstep from 0.43 to 0.32. He's the lowest morale on the roster. With 7 games left and his season already a write-off per the March 25 finding, there is nothing to fix tonight. The offseason audition is the only lever.

**Afinogenov** is the one I'd watch if results turn. 54 points on 16.6 MPG across 67 games, currently scratched. Morale at 96 right now because we're winning, but a guy with that production sitting out is the kind of thing that sours fast over a cold stretch. Not a problem today, and the GM's development scratch for the young guys is still the right call with 7 games left.

**Abid** at 99 on 13.8 MPG and 66 points: the production-to-minutes mismatch persists, but his morale has climbed back to ceiling. The winning fixed what the low minutes were eroding. No action needed before NYI.

**Everyone else** is at 96 or 99 on appropriate minutes for their band. No intervention required.

## Role composition

The units are built correctly for what they are, with one gap that has no bench fix.

**L1** is loaded: 85 scoring mean, 88 speed, 78 checking. Sundin at 87 faceoffs anchors it. Nothing to change.

**L2** is a second scoring line — 82 scoring, 79 playmaking. Checking at 71 mean is soft, but Mogilny at 90 scoring and 90 speed makes the tradeoff worthwhile. Nash at 0.43 pts/g is dragging the production down relative to his spot, but I recommended Abid here on March 30 and the GM passed. I'll let it rest unless his rate drops further.

**L3** is the defensive unit — Klesla at 90 checking is the best on the roster, Richards at 71 faceoffs and 94 stamina gives it legs. Abid at 0.84 pts/g on 12.6 MPG is producing at a second-line rate from this spot. He's the best player on this line offensively and that's fine for a third line that needs secondary scoring.

**L4** is a void. 60 checking, 56 toughness, 50 faceoffs. Koltsov is at 0.28 pts/g and is a trading chip. Spezza and Upshall are both at 4.8-4.9 MPG, functionally healthy scratches. There is no better body available given the GM's constraints on Koltsov and Nash, so the line stays as-is.

**K2 out-checks K1.** Jackman at 86 is the roster's best checker and he's on the second penalty kill (80 checking mean vs K1's 74). That's correct — you want the mean higher on the kill.

**No enforcer exists.** The roster's best toughness is Jackman at 74. No one clears 75. If a series goes physical we have no answer. That's a roster gap, not a lineup problem.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** Does this blowout matchup demand any adjustment beyond confirming Luongo's legs are fresh?

**No.** Toronto is 133 points at home against a 30-38-4 club. Our top two lines are clearly superior to theirs line-for-line, and the bottom two offer safe development minutes for the young guys. The only real threat is Yashin (83 OVR, PUCK 93, DEKG 92, PASS 92) and Peca (85 OVR, CHKG 88, AGGR 92) down the middle, and our L1/L2 are built to handle that.

**Luongo** starts. 92 OVR against a club shooting 2.60 per game. Check his fatigue icon on screen before confirming per the standing order; if he's tired, Tellqvist is the only backup and at 73 he won't want this workload either, but it's one night.

**Chlup** at 19 gets Peca (85 OVR, CHKG 88) on the second line by the auto-pairing. That's a real test and a good one for him. His FACE 76 is decent but Peca draws at 77, so it's a coin flip at the dot. No reason to shelter him from it.

**The fourth line** faces Scatchard (77), Mapletoft (72), and Manderville (67). That's the softest fourth line we'll see all season. Spezza, Koltsov, and Upshall should get every shift they can handle here. Development, not matchup, is the reason to leave them in.

**The third pair** (Eminger 74, Klesla 81) draws NYI's L3: Bates 79, Podein 69, Czerkawski 76. Podein is the weakest player on either roster. Manageable load.

**No change.** The lines are set, the matchup is favorable, and the development opportunities are built into the current arrangement.

## Owed

**Defenceman analysis for April 8 vs NYI.** The season is closing. Here is where every blue-liner stands and who should go.

**McCabe** is off the sell list permanently. Final season rate: 62 points in 82 games at 22.1 MPG = 0.76 pts/g. My March 30 threshold was "below 0.60 he goes back on the list." He clears it comfortably. At 29 with 4 years and $3.00M, he is a keeper who anchors the top pair.

**Jackman** is locked at 0.46 pts/g (37 in 80) on 29.6 MPG. That is his season and his ceiling at this load. Sell offseason. $0.70M x 3 years is the value: the cheapest 30 MPG top-pair minutes in the league, and any club that needs depth on the back end sees that price tag.

**Klesla** is locked at 0.366 pts/g (30 in 82) on 14.8 MPG. Two consecutive declining seasons confirmed: 0.38 at 22, 0.37 at 23, flat minutes. Sell this offseason at $0.90M x 2. He is not getting better in our system.

**Eminger** is 23 points in 64 games at 15.5 MPG = 0.36 pts/g, age 21, $1.20M expiring. Same conclusion as March 30, now with a final sample. The deadline for return value is the summer; after July he is a UFA loss. Trade him.

**Fischer** stays. 41 points in 77 at 22.4 MPG = 0.53 pts/g, age 24, $3.70M x 4. The GM has been emphatic: he is a keeper based on his two-way game.

**Kaberle** stays. 44 points in 74 at 20.8 MPG = 0.60 pts/g, age 27, $1.90M expiring. The GM called him a star. If he is not re-signed he leaves for nothing, so that is a renewal conversation, not a sell.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.39 pts/g in 31 games on 17.9 MPG is a depth piece who showed nothing this year. Not urgent, but the first one cut when a prospect needs a spot.

What changed since March 30: McCabe is formally cleared. Everything else is confirmed, not new.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-30

Toronto 56-13-5, 127 pts after 79 games.

## Role coverage

The question: which roles on this roster are genuinely missing versus ones the coach can close with personnel already here, and which age-curve holes open this summer.

**Toughness is the only structural void.** Zero players carry 80+ in that grade. Jackman at 75 is the best the roster offers; Roberts 73, McCabe 73, Tucker 70. The Feb 21 claim that six players sat at 80+ in stored grades was wrong, and the March 19 recheck confirmed it: the gap has always been structural. No lineup change fixes a zero. Only an acquisition does.

**Faceoffs are the second void.** One player on the roster sits above 80: Sundin at 90. Chlup 75, Roberts 75, Richards 70 are the next tier, well below the threshold. The coach flagged this directly — fourth-line faceoff mean of 51, best of 52. Moving Richards down to L4 (the March 21 recommendation the GM didn't take) lifts the mean by a handful of points and breaks L3. This is also not fixable internally.

**Avery closes both simultaneously.** LA, C, 25, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, two years. One player, two voids eliminated, and he's cheap. The March 19 GM standing order already earmarked Tucker and the 4th-rounder as the only chips; the revised package routes Koltsov to LA instead, which trades a 92-SPEE youth for a player who fills the one role the entire roster lacks. The GM should confirm whether Koltsov-for-Avery is live or dead before the final three games close the window.

**Checking is thin but functional.** Six players at 80+ CHKG: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Tucker is not lined. If the coach dresses him on L4 or as the seventh D-man in close games, checking depth improves marginally. That is the only internal fix available, and it's small.

**Scoring is covered tonight and thin by July.** Mogilny 94 but at 0.79 pts/g in 36 with minutes rising to 19.3, he is finished. Roberts 88 at 38 is walking. That removes two 80+ scorers from the sheet. What remains: Gaborik 92, Afinogenov 90, Abid 86, Sundin 92 at 34. The top six is still deep for next season, but the bottom six loses two bodies and there is no 80+ wing behind Abid. Heatley or Doan stays the July priority per the March 23 note.

**Durability is adequate but ages poorly.** Roberts 98 is walking. Four at 80+: Roberts, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. After July it's three, and all are 23 or 24. Not a problem tonight, a depth concern two years out.

**Goalies, speed, stamina, clutch, playmaking: covered.** No action needed. Luongo and Belfour are both 90+ and closed per the March 19 order.

## Trajectory

The cliff isn't aging, it's contractual: 13 players worth $21.30M expire the same July, and the young ones among them are the entire franchise.

**Sundin** is the anchor that makes everything harder. $8.40M on a 5-year deal locks him through age 39. He's still good tonight — 89 points in 79 games at 34 — but the contract is worth $42.00M over its life with the expectation of a sharp decline by year three. No other player's money constrains the renewal wave this summer as much as his does.

**Gaborik** is the urgent one. His stored grade has slipped to 87 base (from 91 in late March readings), but at 23 with 95 points in 79 games on $1.10M he is still the best value on the roster. Five or six years is mandatory. If he walks, there is no first-rounder to replace him.

**Richards, Nash, Eminger** are the second tier of must-keep. Richards at 66 points, Nash at POTE 95 with a full top-six season, Eminger at POTE 99 and 21. All three are at $1.00M–$1.20M on expiring deals. Market rate for each is $2.50M–$4.00M on a 5-year term. Combined renewal cost for these four (including Gaborik): likely $14M–$18M per year replacing $4.50M.

**Belfour and Roberts** free $9.20M in July. Both are 38+, neither develops, both produce diminishing returns. Roberts at $2.70M is the cleaner cut — he's 38 with POTE 52 and no trade market. Belfour's $6.50M is the single largest contract on the books and removing it is the most important payroll action available.

**Mogilny** is the slow version of the same problem. 36, $5.50M, two years left, declining from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g. By July 2007 he's 38 and free. There's nothing to do about him now; the contract is what it is.

**The age shape is not the problem.** Fourteen players at 23 or under, eleven at 24–29. The 30–33 bucket is empty (just Tucker, scratched, 3 GP), but that's fine — it means no deadweight in the prime years. The four 34+ players (Sundin, Mogilny, Belfour, Roberts) all leave the roster or the ice within two summers.

**Draft capital is the real vulnerability.** One fourth-rounder. If any of the young core busts or gets injured, there is no pick to fill the hole. Every future acquisition must be player-for-player. This makes the Koltsov and Tucker situations relevant: Koltsov at $1.10M on two years with POTE 94 but 18 points in 35 games, and Tucker at $1.30M with 3 games played, are the only liquid assets that could fetch a mid-round pick.

**Money check.** Post-renewal payroll projection: remove Belfour + Roberts + Tellqvist (-$10.00M), add young-core renewals at market (+$25M–$35M replacing the $12.10M they currently earn among the keepers). Net payroll lands at $75M–$85M against $93.71M revenue. Profit shrinks from $23.47M to $9M–$19M. That's workable while winning, but leaves thin margin if revenue drops in a non-playoff season or if the ticket-price reset at $97 can't hold.

The three moves that protect 2006–2008: lock the young core on long deals, let the veterans walk in July, and convert Koltsov or Tucker into a draft pick before either's value walks.

## Calendar

The deadline passed on March 19; the only date left to plan is July. Toronto sit first in the East at 127 points with three games remaining, so the playoffs are the immediate concern, but the summer decisions matter more because thirteen contracts worth $22.10M expire simultaneously and how we stagger them determines whether we ever face this pile-up again.

**Gaborik** is the first call. At 23, 91 base overall, 87 points and $1.10M, he is the cheapest star on the roster by a wide margin. Sign him to six years in July. If he leaves, we have no replacement at 91 base.

**Richards** follows. At 24, 64 points and $1.00M, he is the best faceoff man on the roster at 73 and the only centre between first and fourth line worth keeping long-term. Five years.

**Eminger** at 21 with POTE 99 and $1.20M is the defense cornerstone the GM already locked his timeline around. Five years. The coach's usage question is separate from the contract question; re-sign him regardless of what happens at camp.

**Kaberle** at 27 and $1.90M is entering his prime and is the only top-pairing defenseman who isn't Eminger or McCabe. Four years, possibly five if his asking price stays under $2.50M.

**Nash** at 20 is the coach's flagged case: rate halved from 0.83 to 0.38 on flat minutes. Renew on four years, not five. Let the camp audition determine whether he's top-six material, but his age and $1.20M salary make him cheap enough to keep either way. A fifth year at $1.20M is still good value even if he only makes the third line.

**Colaiacovo** at 22, $1.10M, is third-pairing defense depth. Three years. He's replaceable but cheap, and losing him leaves only three NHL-ready blueliners.

**Tellqvist** at 25, $0.80M, stays per the January 15 standing order: high-90s potential, give him time. Three years.

**Chistov** at 21, $1.10M — the Avery package from March 19 was built around trading him to LA, but that deal was never confirmed as executed and the deadline has closed. Renew him on two years and revisit his trade value in July when LA can accept another package, or simply keep him as bottom-six depth.

**Upshall** at 21, $1.20M — coach says his MPG collapsed from 13.4 to 4.9 and the rate fell too. Let camp decide. If he doesn't earn top-nine minutes, let him walk. At $1.20M he's not cheap enough to keep on the fourth line.

**Alexeev** at 23, $1.10M — renewal priority is below Nash and Eminger, but two years is reasonable if his cap hit stays near this number. If his asking price jumps, let him go.

**Abid** at 25, $0.40M — the cheapest toughness in the league at 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG. Two years. Re-sign him the day free agency opens before anyone else notices the price.

**Belfour** and **Roberts** walk per the GM's March 21 renewal order. Belfour at 39 and $6.50M would need a significant reduction; the GM said he probably won't accept one, and he's right. Roberts at 38 and $2.70M serves no future role. Both are playoff contributors, so the GM should offer them a one-year bridge at reduced salary and let them decline gracefully if they do.

On the July acquisition side, the Mogilny decline (1.62 to 0.79 pts/g) locks the top-nine RW gap. Heatley (ATL, 91 base, 96 pts, 24) and Marleau (SJ, 89 base, 98 pts, 25) are the targets; Heatley will likely be signed by ATL before July since he's younger and they'll want to re-sign him. Marleau is the realistic UFA swing. Gagne at 86 base from a distressed PHI club is the third name.

## League scan

With three games left and the March 19 order locking all assets except Tucker and the 4th-rounder, the league scan's purpose is July: which players to pursue in the summer to close the structural toughness void and replace Mogilny and Roberts. The query above confirms that across the entire league, only five players carry 80+ in stored toughness grades outside Toronto's own blue line, and two of them play on clubs that will be selling.

**Bell** is the single best fit. At 80 base with 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, and 82 FACE he is the only available player who closes both structural voids simultaneously. He's a LW, so the faceoff value is secondary (the GM killed that argument on Feb 25 and I accepted), but 88 toughness is the number that matters — the coverage phase proved zero rostered players sit at 80+. CHI at 73 points with $29.46M profit and 10 expiring contracts are comfortable sellers. POTE 81 at 24 means room to grow. His ENDU 71 is a flag; he'll need short shifts initially.

**Stuart** replaces Roberts on the blue line with something better. At 87 base with 89 CHKG and 80 TOUG, he adds the toughness we lack at defence while filling the roster spot Roberts vacates at 38. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring and $20.63M profit cannot re-sign 13 players on a $45.39M payroll. POTE 91 at 25 means he's still climbing. This is a one-for-one upgrade at a position where we currently have Jackman at 75 TOUG as our best.

**Heatley** remains the July wing priority. At 91 base with 81 CHKG (the best among high scorers), he's the only available player who fills the scoring gap without being a defensive liability. ATL at 82 points with 11 expiring cannot retain both him and Kovalchuk on $36.79M payroll. The Feb 28 binary still holds: whichever ATL keeps, the other moves.

**Avery** fills the faceoff gap specifically, which Bell does not (Bell is a wing; we need a centre at L4). At 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG on $400K with two years left, he's cheap and closes the L4 faceoff mean from 51 to something approaching 75. But 6 points in 57 games (0.11 pts/g) means he contributes nothing else. ENDU 50 is the lowest grade in the query; he cannot play more than 10 minutes. This is a specialist, not a player.

**Barnaby** is not a target. At 82 base with 88 TOUG and 89 CHKG he looks like a second Bell, but POTE 58 and ENDU 67 mean he is finished as a developer and cannot hold a regular shift. NYR at $78.14M payroll and $0.00 profit will dump salary, but the package required would exceed what he's worth to us.

**Kovalchuk** at 89 base with 78 TOUG is close to the toughness threshold but below it. If ATL keeps Heatley, Kovalchuk becomes the alternative wing target. At 21 with 104 points in 61 games, his production dwarfs Heatley's per-game rate. The Feb 28 binary determines which one is available.

**Samsonov, Havlat, Frolov, Cammalleri** — none close a structural gap. Samsonov (TOUG 55) and Havlat (TOUG 68) are pure scorers; Frolov and Cammalleri are 77-79 base development projects that don't help a Cup window.

## Trade construction

With the trade deadline passed and the March 19 order locking everything except Tucker and the 4th-rounder, this phase answers one question: can we acquire toughness with what we're actually allowed to give, or is the summer the only path?

**Koltsov for Avery** is the only package that closes a structural void. LA sits at 48 points with 10 expiring deals; they want youth with ceiling, not a 25-year-old specialist with POTE 72. Koltsov at 23 with POTE 94 and 96 ACCE is exactly the asset a rebuilding club hoards. Avery at 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG on $400K with two years left closes both the L4 faceoff mean (currently 51) and the league-wide toughness void (zero Toronto forwards above 80 TOUG). We save $700K/yr on the swap. LA's payroll is $36.23M with $11.71M profit, so money isn't forcing the move -- it's the 48-point record and the desire to build around speed. The GM must consciously unlock Koltsov; the March 19 order says "everybody else we keep."

**Tucker plus the 4th-rounder buys nothing we need.** Tucker is 30, POTE 79, $1.30M, 3 GP, 1 point. Combined with a 4th-rounder, this package is worth perhaps a 74-76 base depth player. Bell at 82, Stuart at 87, Heatley at 91: none are in range. The only deadline target this package could have reached was Reid from STL (77 base, 80 FACE, POTE 94, $600K expiring), and the window closed before it moved.

**The UFA route is better than any trade we can construct.** Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk in July, freeing $9.20M. Marleau (SJ, 25, 89 base, 98 pts) and Gagne (PHI, 25, 86 base, 94 pts) are expiring from 63-point and financially distressed clubs that cannot re-sign them. A 5-year deal at $2.50M-$3.50M is within range. No prospect leaves, no pick is spent, and we acquire a top-six wing that fills Mogilny's and Roberts' vacancies. The risk is that other clubs with more draft capital outbid us; acceptance is uncertain.

**Stuart from SJ** is the D-side answer if the GM unlocks Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.10M, 31 GP). Stuart at 87 base, 89 CHKG, 80 TOUG, POTE 91 at 25 replaces Roberts with a player eight years younger who fills the only 80+ TOUG slot we lack at defence. SJ at 72 points with 13 expiring and $45.39M payroll has too many deals to keep them all, but at 72 points they are not tanking and might not deal a 25-year-old POTE 91 defenseman. I would not make this the summer priority over locking Gaborik and Richards, but if SJ initiates it is the best defensive addition available.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This task is complete and should be closed.

**Luongo** is on our roster. He reads 94 overall at 25 years old, 2 years remaining, $1.60M, 42 games played this season. He arrived during the February window the GM asked me to monitor. The standing order from 2005-02-19 ("Luongo is arrived. Goalies are solved.") and 2005-03-19 ("Close all goalie monitoring and Belfour trade tasks") both confirm this is done.

**DiPietro** was eliminated on the numbers. At 52 GP he still reads 79 base overall, 3.64 GAA, 84.9% SV. The Jan 15 standing order called for a "really good high-90s goalie" — he is 15+ points below that threshold with no development trajectory that closes the gap in one season. He is not a target and never will be for this club.

**What changed since last report:** Nothing moved. Luongo's status shifted from "available" to "acquired" in February; DiPietro's grade was already confirmed insufficient. The GM's March 19 order to close all goalie monitoring makes this a final sign-off.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-30

Next game at NJ on Friday 01 April 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games his scouting file and production have earned. With three games left (NJ away, then MIN and OTT at home), the window to act is closing, and the offseason is where the real decisions land.

**Spezza** is the roster's worst development failure. POTE 99, 21 years old, 15 points in 43 games on 6.7 MPG fourth-line minutes. Morale 86, the lowest among the young group. I've raised this five times since January with no movement. His season is gone; the only lever left is his camp assignment next September. If we play him at all in MIN or OTT, he needs top-nine minutes, not the spot-check he's been getting.

**Stahle** has played 4 games at POTE 96, age 20. Three games remain. If he doesn't see the ice in at least one of MIN or OTT, he has had an entire NHL season without a genuine audition. That is a wasted year at 20, and I cannot fix it in September.

**Alexeev** at 0.55 pts/g (30 points in 55 games) is currently scratched. He's producing at a rate that earns a roster spot, but he's on the outside. With three games left this is a marginal call, but the offseason question is whether 8.3 MPG was his ceiling or someone's mistake.

**Chlup** belongs exactly where he is: second line, 16.9 MPG, 56 points at 19. No intervention needed.

**Gaborik** at 95 points on 100% of the games, top line, 20.5 MPG at 23. Fully earned.

**Nash** at 0.55 pts/g on 12.8 MPG, L3. His rate halved from 0.83 earlier in the season while minutes held flat. The role is right; the production decline needs an offseason look at system fit, not a lineup change in April.

**Upshall** at 0.29 pts/g on 8.0 MPG, morale 89, L4. Same pattern as Spezza: POTE 99, fourth line, collapsing minutes. His season is also dead. Offseason audition or stop dressing.

**Eminger** at 0.38 pts/g on 15.8 MPG, L3 defence. Recent window is 0.17 over his last six per my earlier reading. Back on the sell list. Development isn't fixing him at this point; the trade market is his best path.

**Klesla** at 0.38 pts/g on 14.9 MPG, second consecutive declining season at 23. Sell this offseason. Playing time is correct; the ceiling is the problem.

**Colaiacovo** scratched at 31 games, 17.9 MPG when he plays. This is the GM's deliberate rotation decision from January and I've conceded it.

## Development trends

The question: who's on the way up, who's stalling, and what does that mean for next year's plans. With three games left and the season effectively decided, this is the last window before offseason decisions lock in.

**Chlup** is the story of this team's season. 0.87 pts/g on 18.3 MPG at 19, across 68 games. He went from 11 minutes to 18 and his rate still climbed from 0.62. The earlier finding said he belonged in the top nine permanently; he's now playing like a top-six centre. No grade moved on the card, but 0.87 at 19 says more than any single reading. Flag for offseason: he starts on a second line next year, not a third.

**McCabe** is back in sell territory and I need to correct my March 4 read. His recent window (55 games since the first save) is 0.45 pts/g on 21.7 MPG at 29. My March 4 note put him at 0.83 over 66 games and took him off the sell list; that earlier sample was propped up by the 24-game hot start. The 0.45 over 55 games is the real number at his age. Re-evaluate this offseason.

**Abid** gets worse every time I look. Minutes fell from 12.6 in my March 16 note to 11.5 now, and his recent rate is 0.74 pts/g. He's 25, producing on a third-line winger's ice time. This is the same problem raised three times with no movement. At 25 his development window is closing.

**Nash** at 0.38 pts/g on 12.8 MPG at 20 is the quiet alarm. My March 16 note flagged 0.43; he's fallen further with no change in role. The rate halved on stable minutes, so it's not a usage problem, it's a fit or a skill ceiling. Offseason system review remains the right call.

**Spacek, Spezza, Upshall** are all dead seasons now, not stalling. Spacek at 0.28 on 5.2 MPG, Spezza at 0.27 on 4.5, Upshall at 0.27 on 4.8. All three had the audition window and lost it. The offseason decision is the same for each: real camp audition or stop dressing them.

**Jackman** confirms the collapse I flagged twice in March. Season rate now 0.41 on 29.5 MPG at 24, down from 0.65 early. The 0.48 I noted March 23 has slipped further. He's a summer sell.

**Koltsov** at 0.28 across 35 games is no longer a trading chip with value. Anyone seeing 35 games at that rate won't offer meaningful return. The asset is gone.

**Klesla** at 0.33 confirms the second declining season. Sell list, as noted March 23.

**Kaberle** is going the right way at 27. 0.64 pts/g on 21.7 MPG across 71 games, up from 0.54. The GM called him a star and the numbers agree. He's still improving.

**Sundin** at 0.98 on 21.7 MPG at 34 is still a first-line centre. The decline from 1.46 is real but 0.98 at 34 is not a problem yet.

**Mogilny** at 0.78 on 19.2 MPG at 36 is the expected age slide. Still productive, but the trajectory says plan around him next year.

**Roberts** at 0.87 on 21.4 MPG at 38 is remarkable for his age but the same planning question applies.

No grade changes on the card for anyone, so production and minutes carry all the signal here.

## Morale watch

The room is happy. 28 of 30 players sit at 96 or above with a win streak lifting everyone. There is nothing to fix before Friday.

**Spezza** at 86 is the only real outlier, and it's the same story it's been since March: 6.7 MPG on the fourth line at 21 years old, well under the 17 MPG his calibre expects. Morale in the 80s costs him 1 point on every grade. Three games left won't move his season average enough to recover him — the fix is a real audition at camp, not a late-season line shuffle.

**Upshall** at 89 is one point into the 80s band. Same structural issue as Spezza (minutes collapsed from 13 to 8 over the season), same answer: not recoverable in three games. The -1 penalty is marginal.

**Jackman** at 99 on 29.7 MPG is carrying the heaviest load in the league and doesn't care. His production is the problem (0.48 pts/g), not his happiness. That's a role conversation for the offseason, not a morale one.

Everyone else — Mogilny at 18.5 on L2, Richards at 16.3 on L3, Abid at 13.9 on L4 — is where morale should be given the results. No changes.

## Role composition

Is each of our units built from the players who fit it, and do we have the bodies to fix the units that aren't, before Friday in New Jersey.

**K2** is our checking unit and it is built right: 84 mean checking, the best of any kill or checking group in the room, with McCabe at 84 and Jackman at 90 on the back end, Chlup at 80 on the draw and Abid adding 72 toughness. No change.

**K1** runs 78 mean checking behind Sundin at 91 in the circle and Fischer at 84, and that is the correct partner for the top kill. No change.

**P1** has its shooter. Gaborik is 98 scoring and 99 playmaking, Sundin is 93 and 92 feeding him, Jackman and Kaberle at the points. **P2** has Mogilny at 94 and Richards at 97 clutch. Both units fit their job.

**L4** is the one unit whose role does not match its grades: 52 mean faceoffs, 54 best. That is Abid, Spezza, Upshall. No man on the bench fixes it. The next-best draw man is Richards at 75 and he anchors L3. This is a roster fact, not an arrangement I can make, and it is the price of the development line.

**Checking forwards** is the gap I would put in front of you. Roberts at 84 is the only forward in our top four checkers. Jackman at 90, McCabe at 84 and Fischer at 84 are all defencemen. A three-forward checking line at 80+ cannot be built from this roster in any arrangement, so our checking identity leans on the blue line and the kill. That is offseason work.

## Opponent matchup

The question for Friday: we beat NJ three times this season, 19-2 on the scoresheet, and Afinogenov is out. The only real decision is who fills his left-wing slot on the second line, and whether we touch anything else against a team whose power play converts at 11% and whose defence drops to 68, 66, 66 below their first pair.

**Abid** moves up from the fourth line to left wing on the second. He carried 0.84 pts/g this season and at 80 OVR with CHKG 86 he can play against Elias's line (86 OVR, PASS 90, DEKG 89) without being a defensive liability. Mogilny at 89 and Chlup at 85 already form the most skilled right-side duo we have outside Sundin; putting Abid there gives us a genuine three-forward attack against NJ's best pair of White (75) and Brown (68).

**NJ's third and fourth lines** are Guolla at 75 and Darby at 73 with Rasmussen/Gionta and Berglund/Brylin. Their D on those pairings is Strudwick (66) and Cullen (66). Our L4 without Abid loses its best player, but against OVR-73 centres and 66-rated defencemen, a line of Spezza/Upshall plus whoever fills in will not be the difference.

**Brodeur** at 92 is the only reason this game is not a coronation. His morale is 82 (costs 1 point on his overall), but 92 is still 92. We need Belfour if his fatigue icon is clear, per the standing order from January 19. Ouellet at 82 against Brodeur at 92 is a 10-point gap on the most important position on the ice.

**No line shuffling.** We're 3-0 with a 19-2 goal differential. Their PP is 27-for-245 (11.0%). Our first line auto-pairs against their first line (Gomez 82, Friesen 85, Langenbrunner 86) and wins that matchup on paper: Sundin 90, Gaborik 97, Roberts 87 against Rafalski 80 and Kubina 78. Leave it alone.

## Owed

Standing order #1: defencemen evaluation and sell-list update for season's end. Season is 3 games from over (79 of 82 played). Numbers are locking.

**McCabe** at 59 points in 79 games is 0.75 pts/g on 22.3 MPG, age 29, $3.00M x 4 years. He drifted from 0.79 at 75 games to 0.75 now. The season is essentially done at that rate. He's a keep — a top-pairing quarterback at 29 in his prime earning window.

**Kaberle** at 43 points in 71 games is 0.61 pts/g on 20.9 MPG, age 27, $1.90M x 1 expiring. The GM called him a star and a keeper on January 15. No change to that. The renewal conversation is the GM's job but the number is good enough to get paid.

**Fischer** at 38 points in 74 games is 0.51 pts/g on 22.1 MPG, age 24, $3.70M x 4. Off the table per the GM's emphatic call. No change.

**Jackman** at 37 points in 77 games is 0.48 pts/g on 29.7 MPG, age 24, $0.70M x 3. Same as my last report: the load kills his production. Sell at offseason. The price is absurd — three years at $0.70M for a 24-year-old top-pairing defenceman is the best value on the roster. No change since March 23, still a sell.

**Klesla** at 30 points in 79 games is 0.38 pts/g on 14.9 MPG, age 23, $0.90M x 2. Two consecutive declining seasons locked. No change. Sell.

**Eminger** is the one who moved. He was at 0.44 in late February; he's now at 23 points in 61 games, which is 0.38 pts/g on 15.8 MPG. Age 21, $1.20M x 1 expiring. He's been bleeding points all month. He was already on the sell list — this makes it more urgent. If he goes to UFA, we lose him for nothing and get nothing back. Trade before July.

**Colaiacovo** at 12 points in 31 games (0.39 on 17.9 MPG, $1.10M x 1 expiring) is not dressing. Let him walk or trade him as filler. No roster contribution this year.

Nothing else has shifted. The sell list is Jackman, Klesla, Eminger, Colaiacovo. The keep list is McCabe, Kaberle, Fischer. No new injuries or surprises.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-25
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-03-25

Toronto 55-12-4, 124 pts after 76 games.

## Role coverage

**Role coverage determines what the playoff roster can handle and what July must fix.** Toronto are 124 points and dominant, but the grade sheet shows two holes no coach can scheme around and one thinning area that becomes a gap next year.

**Toughness is the structural hole.** Zero players carry 80+ TOUG in stored grades. Jackman tops out at 75, Roberts at 73. Tucker at 70 is not the fix the December note suggested (that was a form-inflated reading). No combination of line changes creates toughness the roster doesn't have. This is an acquisition problem for July, not a coach problem for tonight.

**Faceoffs are equally thin.** Only Sundin at 90 clears 80. Richards at 70, Chlup at 75, Tucker at 67. The coach is right that L4 has no answer (best is 53). This forces top-six defensive-zone starts all season, which the coach flagged and the grades confirm. Avery from LA closes both gaps in one move (93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years), and remains the only known single transaction that solves two structural problems.

**Checking is adequate tonight but drops to four next year.** Six at 80+ now: Jackman 87, Roberts 86, McCabe 86, Tucker 83, Fischer 82, Upshall 80. Roberts walks in July, and Mogilny's departure removes his 88 CHKG contribution from forward checks. That leaves Jackman, McCabe, Tucker, Fischer, Upshall. Five is survivable but tight for a playoff run with injuries.

**Scoring looks deep but is aging in two spots.** Ten at 80+ overall, but Mogilny at 36 is at 0.79 pts/g (down from 1.62) and Roberts at 38 walks. Next year the top-end scoring rests on Gaborik 92, Sundin 92, Afinogenov 90, Abid 86, plus whoever replaces the Mogilny wing. Heatley or Doan remain the July priority the March 23 note locked.

**Durability is thin and gets thinner.** Only Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90 clear 80. Roberts is 38 and leaving. That's three next season. A long playoff run with one injury to Abid or Fischer at 25-26 and no depth behind them would be a problem.

**Three unlined bodies are coach-fixable.** Koltsov at 92 speed, 23, not lined. Spacek at 84 playmaking, 19, not lined. Tucker at 83 CHKG, 30, not lined. Dressing them for the final six games gives the coach playoff options at zero cost.

## Trajectory

This roster is not aging into a cliff — it is walking into one if the GM cannot get through thirteen renewals in one July.

**The age curve is healthy.** Twenty-five of thirty players are 29 or under. The four veterans (Sundin 34, Mogilny 36, Belfour 39, Roberts 38) are either expiring or on two years left, so the club naturally sheds them. The ≤23 group holds 14 players including six carrying POTE 95 or above. This is the shape the manual asks for, and it arrived without a rebuild.

**The contract cluster is the problem, not the age curve.** Thirteen contracts worth $21.30M expire this July. That is 43% of total payroll ($60.04M) up for negotiation in one window. Two of them — Belfour ($6.50M) and Roberts ($2.70M) — should walk, saving $9.20M. That leaves eleven players at $12.10M who need re-signing, and most of them just broke out at prices set when they were unknowns.

**Gaborik** is the first call. 91 points in 76 games at 23, 91 base, on $1.10M. He will command a star's salary. A 5-6 year deal protects four or five of his prime years; a shorter deal pushes the same problem to a summer where you also face Chlup's renewal.

**Richards** at 64 points, 24, $1.00M is the second call. Same logic. He is the club's best remaining centre after Sundin ages out.

**Nash, Eminger, Kaberle, and Abid** follow. Nash at 20 with 35 points and POTE 95 is the cheapest star-quality asset in the building; locking him on a long deal is the highest-leverage move of the summer. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 on $1.20M needs the same treatment. Kaberle at 27 entering his prime (41 points, rising minutes) gets 3-4 years. Abid went from $0.40M to 66 points at 25 — the raise will be steep but he is still cheap compared to what a 66-point wing costs.

**The second wave** — Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, Tellqvist — should go on 2-3 year deals. That splits the renewal burden: stars locked in July 2005, depth up again in July 2007 or 2008 instead of 2006. If the GM signs depth to two-year deals today, the July 2006 summer brings up the 2-year group (Chlup, Luongo, Koltsov, Spezza, Ouellet, Klesla, St. Jacques, Tucker) plus those depth players, creating a second cluster.

**Chlup's renewal in July 2006 is the next bomb.** He is on 2 years at $2.34M with POTE 95 and 0.84 points per game at 19. By next July he will be 20 and possibly a first-line centre. At that point he commands $5-7M. The 2-3 year split strategy means he is the top priority of the 2006 summer, which is fine as long as the 2005 cluster is cleared.

**Fischer** at $3.70M on four more years with 0.41 points per game is the payroll anchor nobody wants to carry. He is 24, so there is time, but he is a 2009 problem unless he rebounds.

**Money is not the constraint yet.** Revenue is $91.71M against a $60.04M payroll, leaving $24.39M profit. Even after significant raises for the core — perhaps $15-20M net after losing Belfour and Roberts — payroll lands in the $65-75M range. Profitable, but thinner. The club is one bad year from a payroll that outgrows revenue, especially with ticket price already at $97.

**Draft capital is empty.** One fourth-rounder from Toronto. No ammunition for trades. Every acquisition must be player-for-player, which means the GM's leverage in July depends entirely on which players he is willing to lose as UFAs.

**The three moves that protect 2006-2008:**
1. Re-sign Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger to 5-6 years in July 2005. This locks the core's prime.
2. Re-sign Kaberle and Abid on 3-4 years. They are entering prime but carry more risk than the kids.
3. Put Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Upshall, and Tellqvist on 2-3 year deals so their renewals land in 2007-08, not alongside Chlup's star renewal in 2006.

Task #2 (monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro development through February) is complete. Luongo arrived on roster in early February at 91 base with 2 years at $1.60M. DiPietro was eliminated on March 14 at 79 base with a 3.64 GAA. The goalie situation is solved as the GM ordered on March 19.

## Calendar

The deadline passed six days ago and the season has 6 games left, so the calendar question is no longer buyers or sellers. It is: what does this roster look like in July, and 13 contracts worth $22.30M expire simultaneously. That is the largest single summer decision this franchise has faced.

**Gaborik** is the priority and nothing else comes close. 91 base, 23, 87 points, $1.10M on an expiring deal. He's the youngest player on the roster carrying a top-line overall and he will get outbidded in July if we don't lock him on 5 or 6 years immediately. Everything else in this summer plan bends around whether he stays.

**Richards** follows at 82 base, 24, 64 points, $1.00M. Same shape as Gaborik: cheap, young, productive, expiring. Five or six years, before the July market reprices him.

**Kaberle** at 84 base, 27, $1.90M, is entering his prime: 0.54 to 0.63 pts/g with minutes climbing from 19.4 to 21.9. Five or six years. The coach named him the top-pair quarterback for next year and the numbers support it.

**Eminger** at 76 base, 21, $1.20M, carries the POTE 99 that the GM has protected all season. He's a project, not a product, but the ceiling argument holds. Lock on 5 years at a number that won't blow up later.

**Nash** at 77 base, 20, $1.20M, rounds out the five lock list. Young, cheap, on the first line, and he's two years younger than most players on this roster. Five years.

**Abid** at 79 base, 25, $0.40M, is the cheapest toughness on the roster (80 CHKG, 80 TOUG). Two years at a modest bump. He gives the bottom six a physical element we don't otherwise have.

**Tellqvist** at 77 base, 25, $0.80M, stays per the January order. Two years, development time, no money saved.

**Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev** are depth at 78, 72 and 76 base respectively, all $1.10M. Chistov at 21 is the one worth keeping on two or three years for a bottom-six role. Colaiacovo at 72 on a second-pairing D is thin. Alexeev at 76 at 23 is replaceable. I would renew Chistov, let the other two test the market, and bring one back cheap if nobody bids.

**Belfour** is the one the GM wants to keep but probably can't. 92 base, 39, $6.50M. Offer two years at $3.5–4.0M. If he refuses, he walks and the payroll drops $6.50M. That money pays for a Heatley or Doan acquisition and still leaves room. The March 19 order keeps him for the playoffs; after that it's his decision.

**Roberts** at 87 base, 38, $2.70M walks. The March 21 renewal note already set that. No two-year deal to an 87-base forward turning 39.

**Upshall** is a wasted year and should go. Minutes collapsed from 13.4 to 5.1 MPG at 21 with 0.30 pts/g production. No POTE on record. Try the over-80 pick mechanic first — his base overall is 78, so it won't work. Trade him as a depth piece for a late-rounder or let him walk. He's $1.20M better spent on someone who plays.

The RW hole is the summer's structural problem. Mogilny fell from 1.62 to 0.79 pts/g at 36 and carries $5.50M with 2 years left. Gaborik covers one wing; we need a second top-nine RW. Heatley (91 base, 24) or Doan are the profile, but we hold only our own fifth-round pick. A package has to start with Mogilny's contract or another salary dump. The GM should test ATL's summer posture on Heatley once the season ends; ATL sit 7th in the East at 81 points and may be sellers again.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league fills Toronto's two structural holes (toughness and faceoffs) and replaces Mogilny at right wing, and why would their clubs let them go? The answer splits into July UFA signings and offseason trades, because the GM closed the deadline window on March 19.

**Heatley** (ATL, RW, 91 base, POTE 86, 120 points in 71 games, $1.10M expiring) is the single best fit. He is 24, plays the exact position Mogilny leaves empty, and ATL at 81 points with 11 expiring cannot re-sign both him and Kovalchuk (89 base, 130 points). ATL keeps Kovalchuk on production, Heatley walks in July for nothing unless they trade him. Toronto's payroll at $60.04M against $91.71M revenue absorbs a $5-6M raise. The cost is draft capital Toronto doesn't have (one 4th-rounder), so the move requires either his walk to UFA or the GM's negotiation leverage to find a third party.

**Iginla** (CGY, RW, 93 base, POTE 79, 112 points in 69 games, $6.50M expiring) is the highest-rated RW in the league. CGY at 60 points is the second-worst team, carrying $45.93M payroll against only $12.21M profit with 10 expiring deals. They MUST move him rather than lose $6.50M of salary on the best RW available for nothing. At 27 he has four prime years left. The obstacle is his current salary: re-signing him at $7-8M for 5 years consumes 12-13% of projected revenue. Toronto can do it, but it makes the Gaborik and Richards renewals tighter.

**Gagne** (PHI, LW, 86 base, POTE 81, 98 points in 74 games, $2.40M, 0 years left = UFA this July) is the best value if he hits the market. PHI at 71 points with $66.73M payroll and only $3.38M profit cannot re-sign 13 expiring players. He plays left wing, not right, but his 86 base and 98 points make him a top-nine winger on any line. A July UFA signing costs no trade assets.

**Marleau** (SJ, C, 89 base, POTE 81, 98 points in 71 games, $1.60M, 0 years left = UFA this July) is a center who could slide to right wing. SJ at 68 points with 13 expiring and $19.95M profit are rebuilding, not desperate. They might re-sign him at $1.60M. Less likely to hit UFA than Gagne, but if he does, 89 base at 25 is the second-best available player.

**Bell** (CHI, C, 24, 80 base, POTE unlisted, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2 years left) remains the only known player closing toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a long deal. CHI at 69 points with $28.03M profit don't need to sell, but at 69 points with 10 expiring they're rebuilding and Bell is expendable. The Jan 25 proposed price (R2 plus Colaiacovo) is the template. He's a re-signable deal with 2 years remaining, not a rental.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25, 79 base, 83 TOUG, 94 FACE, 9 pts in 75 GP, $400K, 2 years) closes the same two gaps as Bell at half the salary. His production is the problem: 0.12 points per game is fourth-line offence. The Feb 16 note deprioritized him below Bell on production. LA at 71 points with 14 expiring are willing sellers. He's a bottom-six role player with elite grades.

**Cammalleri and Frolov** (LA, both 22, $1.10M expiring each, POTE 98 and 96, 52 and 50 points respectively) are the long-term top-six development play. LA at 71 points with 14 expiring cannot keep both at star salaries. Acquiring both fills top-six wing for five years on development contracts.
