# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-21

Next game at MTL on Tuesday 22 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they've earned, and as of tonight three names stand out in different directions.

**Stahle** has POTE 96, is 20 years old, and has played 4 games out of 60. That hasn't moved since I raised it January 25th. There are 22 games left; even a full run from here gets him to 26, which is a half-season of development instead of a full one. I have no injury showing against him. At some point this stops being a rotation choice and becomes a decision not to develop him.

**Spezza** sits at 7.5 MPG in 37 games, 15 points (0.41 per game), POTE 99, age 21, currently scratched. I have raised this six times across five weeks. The pattern is clear: he plays a game, scores nothing, and comes back out. That is not a development plan, that is spot duty. Either he goes into a fixed fourth-line role at 10+ minutes for a stretch, or we accept 2004-05 is a lost year for him and focus on next season. I would rather know which one we are in.

**Spacek** is at 9.7 MPG now, up from 8.3 when I last flagged him. 16 points in 37 games (0.43 per game), 19 years old, POTE 91. Slight improvement. Not enough for a 19-year-old with that potential grade, but the direction is right and the GM's rotation philosophy explains the ceiling. I am not pressing this one further this season.

**Smirnov** has 0 games and POTE 70. He's a depth prospect with a modest scouting grade and no claim on anyone's minutes. No concern.

**Safronov** has 3 games, 0 points, POTE 91, age 23. At 23 with nothing to show in three appearances, the scouting number may just not be translating. I would not allocate remaining games to him over Stahle.

**Eminger** at 44 games, 16.3 MPG, 20 points (0.45 season, 0.57 recent) and currently scratched. His recovery cleared the trade threshold on February 19th. He is being developed and it is working. The scratch tonight is a matchup or rotation call, not a signal.

## Development trends

The window is 82 days and the stories are clear: one teenager is arriving, one young defender is falling back, and the old core is being paid in minutes that no longer buy points.

**Chlup** is the finding of this window. 18 years old, 0.62→0.83 pts/g with minutes up from 11.0 to 17.3. He went from bottom-six role player to 17 minutes a night and scored more per minute while doing it. At 49 games and 0.83, he is a top-six centre in this league. No change needed — he is where he belongs.

**Eminger** cleared the threshold and is staying. 0.35→0.57 on minutes up from 15.0 to 17.8. His season total sits at 0.57 over 44 games now, not 0.45. He earned the second pair and belongs on it next season.

**Stahle** finally played: 4 games at 17.8 MPG, 0 points. That is progress from zero. At 20 with potential to develop, the next step is consistency — dress him every night for the final 22 games and accept the zeroes while he learns.

**Klesla** is the concern on the blue line. 0.50→0.31 pts/g on unchanged minutes (14.9). At 22, the expected direction is up, not down. His season rate sits at 0.31 over 60 games, which is a third-pair number. If that holds through March he becomes a trade candidate before his contract forces a decision.

**Spacek** and **Spezza** remain the two biggest wastes. Spacek: 0.55→0.38, minutes down from 16.0 to 7.1. Spezza: 0.43→0.38, minutes down from 9.1 to 5.3. Both are getting nothing. I have raised this six times; the rotation philosophy explains why, but 22 games left means this year is nearly gone for both of them.

**Nash** cooled from 0.83 to 0.52 on steady minutes (12.5). At 20, his early-season rate was probably inflated by a hot stretch, and 0.52 is closer to where he sits. Not alarming, but it means he is a middle-six winger who needs to earn more, not a top-six player being underused.

**Fischer** keeps sliding: 0.63→0.39 on minutes that went up from 20.8 to 22.2. At 24, four years left on the deal. He is not a trade target, but the planning question is real: the team is giving a declining player the heaviest defensive load on the roster.

**The aging core** (Sundin, Mogilny, Roberts, Svehla) all produced less since December despite carrying more minutes or similar. Sundin: 1.46→0.97 on minutes up from 16.9 to 20.8. Mogilny: 1.62→0.91 on 19.2. Roberts: 1.29→0.92 on 20.8. Svehla: 0.78→0.53 on minutes down from 23.8 to 20.8. These are age curves doing what age curves do. The l3-stamina ceiling means the bottom nine cannot absorb more load, so the team is running these men harder while they produce less. That is unsustainable past this season.

**McCabe** at 0.50 is the confirmed sell. 1.42→0.50 on 21.9 MPG. Four years at $3M. He stays on the list.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy; one man is not.

**Spezza** is the only concern. Morale 86 is the lowest on the roster by 6 points and has been flat or dropping all season. He is getting 7.5 MPG while scratched. A 21-year-old centre at 0.41 pts/g over 37 games with that calibre of prospect expects more than scratch minutes. This is entirely a minutes problem, and I have raised it every activation since January 31st with no movement. The GM controls whether he plays.

**Chlup** sits at morale 92 with 15.6 MPG on the second line. If his grade puts him at 90+, the band says 20 and he is 4.4 short. But his morale is rising (+5 recent) and the team's results are covering the gap. No change needed for morale purposes, though it is a workload flag for late in the season.

**Spacek** at 9.7 MPG on the fourth line, morale 96. Below what a 19-year-old at 0.43 pts/g should see for development, but morale is fine and the winning is insulating him. Not a morale issue today.

Everyone else is at 99 or rising with the winning streak. The results are doing the heavy lifting, and the only fixable outlier is the one the GM has declined to fix eight times running.

## Role composition

**The question is whether each unit's personnel matches its job. The short answer: yes, with one structural limitation the GM already knows about.**

**L1** is the most complete line on the roster. Sundin wins draws at 90, Fischer and Roberts check at 83, Gaborik scores at 98 and plays at 99. Checking mean 75 is the best of the top three. This line can handle every matchup and is correctly built. No touch.

**L2** has the lowest checking mean of the top three at 64, because Mogilny and Afinogenov contribute nothing to that role. Chlup carries it at 79 checking and 79 faceoffs, which is fine for a second scoring line. This is a by-design tradeoff: the second unit scores (80/94 scoring, 79/97 playmaking) and accepts that it gets out-muscled against top pairs. Against a bad team like Montreal tonight, that costs almost nothing.

**L3** is the most versatile unit. Chistov brings 97 speed, Richards brings 74 faceoffs and 89 stamina (best on the roster), and the shown checking best reads 93 — Richards carries that. This line can be sent against anyone. No change.

**L4** has a faceoff problem: 51 mean, 54 best. Nobody on that unit can win a draw. Against teams with good centres, a defensive-zone start becomes a possession loss before play begins. This is not fixable within the lineup — the only centres above 74 are Sundin, Chlup, and Richards, and all three centre the top three lines. It is a roster gap: the club needs a fifth centre who wins draws, and the trade deadline was a week ago.

**K1** is correctly built. Sundin wins the draw at 90, Roberts and Fischer deliver 83 checking. Three of the four best checkers are on this unit. That is the right allocation — you want your best penalty killers killing penalties, not playing even strength.

**K2** uses Abid (82 checking) with Chlup, McCabe, and Kaberle on the back end. Reasonable. The toughness here (65 mean) is thin for a kill, but Abid (71 toughness) and McCabe (72) provide something.

**P1** has no composition problem: Gaborik shoots at 98, Kaberle and McCabe can move the puck, Sundin controls the draw on entries. P2 with Mogilny and Afinogenov is the scoring unit. Both are built for their jobs.

**No enforcer exists.** The best toughness on the roster is McCabe at 72, nobody above 75. The team plays skill and checking, not intimidation. Against a physical team this is a structural disadvantage, but there is no trade fix available now.

No unit changes. The roles are right; the gap is at roster depth (a fifth centre with faceoff skill), not in how the units are assembled.

## Opponent matchup

**What changes for Tuesday against Montreal, and what doesn't.**

**Luongo** starts. 93 OVR, 99 morale, no fatigue showing. MTL scores 2.40 per game. He's not going to work.

**The lines stay put.** MTL's top unit is Nylander (78), Bulis (78), Sundstrom (74). Our second line (Mogilny 88, Chlup 84, Afinogenov 84) is better than their first. Even our fourth line (Spacek 75, Abid 79, Upshall 77) outclasses their third and fourth. There is no matchup problem to solve.

**Kaberle and Svehla** carry the second pair. Against MTL's second defensive unit (Beauchemin 76, Brisebois 77), Kaberle's 84 SPEE and 84 PASS will find room. No reason to shuffle the D slot order; our auto-paired mismatches all go our way regardless.

**Their power play is 8-for-179.** Four and a half percent. We don't need to worry about short-handed situations this game. Our PK units can be relaxed.

**Their penalty kill** won't help their cause either. We're 22-for-57 (38.6%) and their kill has no one above 90 checking except Komisarek (90) on their first unit. Sundin (94 HERO) and Fischer (88 SHPW, 93 SPEE) will have space.

**Defencemen assessment** (deliverable #1, 22nd game analysis): McCabe at 82 OVR remains the weakest link on the blue line per his recent 0.33 pts/g window against a 0.89 season rate (noted Feb 12). Fischer (83), Kaberle (82), and Svehla (83) are all stable at 99 morale. Klesla (82, age 22, POTE 98) continues as the third-pair defenceman. Salo (81, age 30) rounds it out. The sell-list hierarchy hasn't shifted since my last read: McCabe first, Colaiacovo and Eminger behind him pending their season rates.

**Development opportunity:** This is a 16-35 opponent on a 2-7-1 slide. If the GM wants to give Spacek extra of the game or dress Smirnov (50 OVR at 20), Tuesday is the night. I'd give Spacek more minutes rather than dress Smirnov at his current level.

## Owed

**Item #1 — defenceman sell list update for Monday Feb 21, game at MTL Tuesday:**

**McCabe** — 52 points in 60 games, 0.87 pts/g, 22.6 MPG. Since Jan 26 (when he sat at 48/50, 0.96) he has added 4 points in 10 games, a 0.40 rate that confirms the February slump is real and not one bad week. Age 29, $3M for 4 more years. Still the loudest sell on the blue line. No change from Feb 12.

**Eminger** — 20 points in 44 games, 0.455 season rate, 16.3 MPG. The Feb 19 finding stands: his recent window hit 0.57 and he cleared the trade threshold. Off the sell list, stays for development. Nothing has moved in two days.

**Colaiacovo** — 12 points in 31 games, 0.39 pts/g, 17.9 MPG. Age 22, $1.10M expiring. Still a sell at deadline. No change.

**Salo** — 8 points in 25 games, 0.32 pts/g, 18.0 MPG. Age 30, $2.60M with 2 years left. Dead cap hit. If we can move him this summer, the money buys a top-pair replacement.

**Klesla** — 23 points in 60 games, 0.38 pts/g, 14.8 MPG. 82 OVR at 22 getting 2 minutes below the morale-model expectation for his rating tier. He stays (young, cheap at $0.90M/2yr), but if his minutes keep sitting at 14, watch his morale in March.

**Stahle** — 4 games played, 0 points. POTE 96, age 20. I raised this Jan 25 and it's still the same. If the GM wants him developed, dress him. If not, stop carrying him on a $0.97M deal.

Nothing has changed materially since Feb 19. McCabe remains the sell, Eminger remains the keeper. The sell list for end of season: McCabe first, Salo second, Colaiacovo third.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-19
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-19

Next game at WSH on Sunday 20 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether the young players are getting the games their production and potential have earned — and the one clear failure this season is Spezza, whose morale at 86 is the lowest among every young player on the roster and the only one below 90.

**Spezza** — 37 GP, 7.5 MPG, 15 points, POTE 99, morale 86. His rate when he plays is 0.41 pts/g, which is competitive with players getting double his ice. The morale number tells me he knows it too. At 21 with POTE 99, this is the sixth time I am raising it, and the only new evidence is that his morale has slipped to 86 while every other young player sits at 95 or above.

**Stahle** — now at 4 GP out of 59, POTE 96, 17.8 MPG when he plays. He moved from zero, which is an improvement, but a 20-year-old with the second-highest potential grade on the blue line playing 7% of the games is still wrong. His production (0 points in 4 games) is small sample noise, not evidence against him.

**Alexeev** — 55 GP, 8.3 MPG, 30 points, 0.55 pts/g. That is the same production rate Koltsov produces on 9.9 MPG. At 23 the development window is closing, but the efficiency is there. He should be seeing 10+ minutes even on a fourth-line role rather than 8.

**Smirnov** — 0 GP at 20, POTE 70. The lowest potential grade among the young group. He is not being wasted. The scratch is the correct call.

**Safronov** — 3 GP, 0 points, POTE 91. He got three games and produced nothing. The opportunity was there and he didn't take it. No grievance.

**Colaiacovo** — 53% share but 17.9 MPG when in. That is real second-pair responsibility. At 22, alternating with Svehla is fine development. No change.

**Chlup** — 48 GP, 15.4 MPG, 37 points at 18. He has earned the second line entirely. No concern.

**Everyone else** — Nash (46 GP, 32 pts), Gaborik (59 GP, 77 pts), Klesla (59 GP), Eminger (44 GP, 16.3 MPG), Upshall (45 GP, 10.7 MPG), Spacek (36 GP, 10 MPG), Chistov (45 GP), Koltsov (35 GP, 0.51 pts/g) — all are getting ice in proportion to what they produce. Upshall's rate faded to 0.38, so 10.7 MPG matches. Spacek's 10 MPG is the floor for the fourth line given its endurance ceiling. No calls to make on any of them.

## Development trends

The window from December 1 to now shows a club splitting apart: four young players are genuinely getting better, two are stalling badly, one has collapsed beyond recovery, and the aging core is doing exactly what aging cores do. The deadline is close and these trends determine who stays, who goes, and who you build around next year.

**Chlup** is the story. 18 years old, went from 0.62 pts/g on 11 MPG to 0.83 on 17 MPG in 35 recent games. Both numbers climbing at the same time means the coaching staff trusts him and he's paying them back. At 18 that trajectory is rare and he is a top-six centre next season unless something breaks.

**Eminger** has recovered from his early-season slump and is no longer a trade candidate on production. First 23 games: 0.35. Recent 21 games: 0.57. His recent window is well above the 0.45 threshold I set in January. Minutes up from 15 to 17.8. I was wrong to call him a sell; he is a keeper or at minimum a player you don't move in a panic.

**Chistov** (LW, 21) went from 0.29 on 9.5 MPG to 0.39 on 15 MPG. Rate up, minutes up, same direction. Quietly becoming a regular and worth keeping in the development rotation.

**Kaberle** (D, 26) moved from 0.54 to 0.59 with minutes up from 19.4 to 22.4. He's taking on more and producing more. Already the GM's stated keeper and the trend confirms it.

**Spezza** (C, 21) is still stuck. 0.43 to 0.38 rate on minutes that fell from 9.1 to 5.3. POTE 99 and 5.3 minutes a night. I've raised this five times. The window is closing and this is the last February where "give him 12 minutes" is even an option before other young centres arrive.

**Spacek** (C, 19) went from 0.55 on 16 MPG to 0.40 on 7.4 MPG. At 19, losing his minutes mid-season is worse than never getting them because he was starting to show (0.55 is good for a 19-year-old). The GM's rotation philosophy explains the benching but not the collapse in rate too. He needs a clear decision: regular minutes or a full year off.

**Koltsov** (LW, 23): 1.10 down to 0.28. At 23 the expected direction is up and his has fallen off a cliff. GM has him as a trade chip, and this trend makes him harder to sell by the day. The window to move him is now.

**Klesla** (D, 22): 0.50 to 0.31 on steady 15 MPG. At 22 he should be climbing. A second-year defenceman going from 0.50 to 0.31 while getting the same ice is a sign the game has caught up to him. Watch whether February recovers him or confirms he is what he is now.

**Fischer** (D, 24): 0.63 to 0.40 on minutes that rose from 20.8 to 22.1. More ice, less production. The GM's keeper, but the four-year deal at his current rate is a problem that compounds every week. Not a trade call, a "plan around this" call.

**McCabe** (D, 29): 1.42 to 0.49. Confirmed beyond doubt. At 29, four years, $3M, and no recovery in February. He is the clearest sell on the roster.

**Alexeev** (RW, 23): 0.62 to 0.48 with minutes cut from 11.1 to 6.0. Falling out of the plans while still young. If he doesn't fit, the time to move him is now while he still has some trade value.

**The veterans:** Sundin (34) went 1.46 to 0.91, Mogilny (36) went 1.62 to 0.90, Roberts (38) went 1.29 to 0.94. All three are getting more minutes while producing less per game. The L3 stamina ceiling means someone has to carry them. This is not a problem to fix this season but it defines next season: the top six cannot look like this.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy except for one man, and it is the same man I have raised five times since January.

**Spezza** sits at 86 morale, the lowest on the roster by six points, and his 7.5 MPG across 37 games explains it. At 21 producing 0.41 pts/g he belongs in the 10-MPG band, not 7.5. The 80s morale costs him 1 point on his displayed overall, so he is underperforming his own rating on top of the development waste. The GM has not moved him despite repeated raises. I will raise it once more: either put him back at 10+ MPG in games we can afford, or accept the full scratch and the -1 overall as a known cost. The middle ground of 7.5 MPG on a scratched line does neither his growth nor tonight's quality any good.

**Tucker** at 90 with 3 GP is fine. He is the checking guy the GM kept on purpose and the low games are the GM's rotation call. No concern.

**Everyone else** sits at 92 or above. The first line at 96, the dressing-room regulars at 99. The results are doing their job, and no minutes adjustment is needed for anyone outside Spezza.

## Role composition

The question is whether our units are built from players who suit their jobs, and whether we have enough of each role to cover a full game against a team that just put 11 on us.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Gaborik + McCabe, Fischer)** is the best-constructed unit we have. Gaborik at 98 scoring, 99 playmaking, 99 speed is the engine. Sundin covers the draw (91 faceoffs) and clutch (95). Roberts and Fischer at 84 checking each give it a real two-way game. McCabe brings toughness (73, team best) and stamina (87). No change. This line does everything.

**L2 (Chlup, Mogilny, Afinogenov + Kaberle, Colaiacovo)** checks at 66 mean. That's our exposed unit. Mogilny (94 scoring) and Afinogenov (92 scoring, 92 playmaking) are there to score, and they will. But Kaberle and Colaiacovo are the weakest D pair available, and with auto-pairing this is the line that gets the opponent's second-best matchup. The fix isn't personnel — it's usage. Chlup at 80 faceoffs is the only thing keeping this line from getting buried in the defensive zone. No composition change, but the GM should be aware this is where Washington will push.

**L3 (Richards, Nash, Chistov + Klesla, Stahle)** is anchored by Richards: checking 94, clutch 97, stamina 92. He's carrying this unit's identity. Nash provides scoring depth, Chistov brings 98 speed for rush offense. This is a well-balanced third line. No change.

**L4 (Spacek, Koltsov, Abid)** has a faceoff mean of 54 and a best of 55. Nobody on this line wins a draw. Koltsov at 99 speed is the weapon; Abid at 83 checking and 72 toughness gives the physical edge. Fine as a fourth line. Spacek continues to play limited minutes (flagged repeatedly at 8 MPG). This line should never be sent into a defensive-zone faceoff.

**P1 (Sundin, Roberts, McCabe, Kaberle, Gaborik)** is loaded. 92 clutch mean, 99 playmaking best, 99 scoring best. This is a first-unit PP built to score on anyone. No change.

**P2 (Stahle, Chlup, Mogilny, Richards, Fischer)** carries Mogilny's shooting and Chlup's playmaking, with Richards for defensive transition. Functional. No change.

**K1 (Stahle, Sundin, Roberts, Fischer)** is the correct PK1. Roberts and Fischer are our two best checkers (both 84) together. Sundin at 91 faceoffs wins the draw to start the kill. No change.

**K2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Chistov)** is the one that concerns me. McCabe (84 checking) is carrying this unit. Kaberle's checking doesn't crack the top four (all above 83). If McCabe draws a second penalty, this unit has no answer. Chistov's 98 speed creates a shorthanded threat, which is the tradeoff. I won't change it because there's no better option — Abid (83 checking) is the fifth man and he's the only real addition we could make, which would gut L4's physicality.

**Roster-level gaps:**

**Fifth checker**: Roberts 84, McCabe 84, Fischer 84, Abid 83. That's it. Four players. We run them on multiple units simultaneously (Roberts on L1, K1, P1; McCabe on L1, K2, P1). One injury to any of these four and we have no replacement at that level. This is a deadline problem.

**Faceoff depth**: Sundin 91, Chlup 80, Roberts 76, Richards 75. Nobody else above 75. Against Washington's centers, our third and fourth lines will lose draws consistently. No solution in-house.

**Enforcer**: Highest toughness on the roster is McCabe at 73. We cannot physically deter anyone. Against a team that just scored 11, the inability to push back is a structural weakness, not a lineup adjustment.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether Toronto lines up differently for Washington given Jagr and Kolzig, or plays the same game that's produced a 41-10-4 record.

**The goalie.** Luongo is 94 OVR, Ouellet is 82. This is a road game against a 93-OVR Kolzig on a quality opponent where the Jan 15 standing order says maximize. I have recommended this four times in two weeks and it hasn't landed. Luongo starts. No other reasoning changes that answer.

**Line 1 vs Jagr.** Sundin (90), Gaborik (97), Roberts (87) against Jagr (90), Lang (81), Bondra (87). Roberts is the answer to Jagr physically: 89 toughness, 87 checking, 94 balance. Our centre is better than theirs. Their wing pair is elite but our top line out-grades them as a unit. No change.

**Lines 2 and 3 favor us heavily.** Chlup (85), Mogilny (89), Afinogenov (85) versus Halpern (78), Grier (82), Dupuis (80). Richards (86), Chistov (81), Nash (82) versus Metropolit (69), Zubrus (80), Radivojevic (77). That's a combined OVR gap of 259 to 239 on two lines. We should outscore their middle six. No change needed.

**Defensive pairs.** Fischer/McCabe (84/83) on D1 against Witt/Gonchar (79/84) is the right allocation. Kaberle (83) and Colaiacovo (72) on D2 face Yonkman (76) and Belak (69), so Colaiacovo's weakness is hidden by the opposition's own depth. No change.

**Washington's PP is 24 goals on 200 attempts (12%).** Our PK units should cruise against that. No structural adjustment to the kill needed.

## Owed

**Owed item #1: defencemen analysis and sell order.** Here's the blue line update for Washington.

**McCabe** sits at 51 points in 59 games (0.86 pts/g) on 22.6 MPG. He was 0.89 on Feb 12; the slide continues but slowly. At 29 with $3M and four years left, he's still the loudest sell. The good news: 0.86 over 59 games is a tradeable number if you shop him as a top-pairing scorer with mileage on the clock.

**Eminger** is frozen at the threshold: 20 points in 44 games (0.45 pts/g). One game, one point since Feb 6. No recovery, no further collapse. Age 21, $1.2M expiring. He is exactly what I said on Feb 6: a sell at the deadline unless something breaks upward, and nothing has.

**Colaiacovo** has dropped out of the dressing room. 12 points in 31 games (0.39 pts/g), 17.9 MPG, $1.1M expiring at 22. Same sell profile as Eminger but less production. If you're clearing bodies, he's next after Eminger.

**Fischer** at 26 in 54 (0.48 pts/g) is the GM's keeper and stays off the list. His decline from 0.63 to 0.48 is the planning concern, not a sell case.

**Stahle** has finally played: 4 games up from zero on Jan 25, still 0 points. The POTE 96 kid at 20 is at least in the building now. No sell case, he's the future if it materialises.

**Klesla** is the one to keep. 23 points in 59 at 14.9 MPG, $0.9M for two more years at 22. Cheap, young, every-night player. No reason to move him.

**Salo** is cut material. 8 points in 24 games (0.33 pts/g), 30 years old, $2.6M with two years left, and not even dressing. If you need cap space or a roster spot, he goes.

**Sell order unchanged**: McCabe first (best return, hardest move), Eminger and Colaiacovo in the same window (cheap expiring assets), Salo as a cap dump. Stahle, Klesla, Kaberle, Fischer all stay.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-19
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-19

Toronto 41-10-4, 94 pts after 59 games.

## Role coverage

Two structural gaps define this roster at the deadline: toughness at zero players above 80, and faceoffs at one player above 80. Everything else the coach can fix by dressing players he already has.

**Roberts** at 38 is the best checker on the roster at 86 CHKG, and he is the best durability player at 98 INJU. He is also the best toughness player at 73, which tells you how thin that group is. The next-best toughness reading is McCabe at 73, then Chlup at 70. There is no 80 on the entire sheet. No lineup card closes a gap where the ceiling is 73.

**Tucker, Svehla, Upshall** all carry 80+ checking and none are lined. Tucker at 83 CHKG and Svehla at 83 CHKG are on the roster. Upshall at 80 CHKG is on the roster. The coach's checking problem is a dressing problem, not a personnel problem. Three players at 80+ checking sitting in no unit while the top pair relies on Roberts at 38.

**Sundin** at 90 FACE is the only centre above 80 on faceoffs. Chlup at 75 and Richards at 70 are the next reads. That 15-point cliff means every defensive draw against a strong opposing centre falls to a sub-75. The GM killed Bell for this reason on Jan 25 (both wings), so the internal fix is Chlup taking more draws at 75, which is marginal. If the club acquires Chara (95 CHKG) or another physical forward, the faceoff depth issue compounds but the toughness gap is the binding constraint.

**Salo** at 88 scoring, 30 years old, $0.97M expiring, not lined. He is a depth asset the coach does not use and the GM can move for a pick via the over-80 expiring mechanic if he wants to convert him rather than lose him in July.

**Belfour** at 21 GP, 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SV, $6.50M expiring, age 39. With Luongo at 40 GP and 2.87 GAA as the starter, Belfour is either playoff insurance or a pick-recovery asset. His trade value peaks now.

## Trajectory

The question this answers is whether Toronto drifts off a cliff in 2006, and the answer is no — the age shape is sound. The risk is entirely in the summer 2005 re-signing window, where six future stars at rock-bottom salaries hit the market simultaneously and could leave for nothing.

**The 34+ group** costs $26.70M across five men: Sundin $8.40M (5yr), Belfour $6.50M (expiring), Mogilny $5.50M (2yr), Svehla $3.60M (expiring), Roberts $2.70M (expiring). Three of those five expire this July. By 2006-07 only Sundin (age 37) and Mogilny (38) carry the veteran money, and Mogilny drops off after that. The cliff is already happening — the question is whether Toronto gets compensated for it.

**The age shape is fine.** 16 players at ≤23, 10 at 24-29, only Salo (30) in the 30-33 bracket. The manual wants 5-7 veterans and 20 young. Toronto has 5 veterans and 27 under 30. The hollow middle fills automatically: Nash (20→23), Chlup (18→21), Eminger (21→24), Colaiacovo (22→25), Klesla (22→25) all step into that 24-29 bracket by 2007-08. Nothing structural to fix here.

**The 1-year cluster is the problem.** 15 contracts worth $25.30M expire this July. Of those, six are future top-six players on deals that will re-price by 300-500%: Gaborik ($1.10M), Richards ($1.00M), Nash ($1.20M), Kaberle ($1.90M), Eminger ($1.20M), Colaiacovo ($1.10M). Together they earn $7.50M. Realistic renewal at 5-year terms puts them at $18-22M combined. That is a $10-14M payroll jump in a single offseason.

**The money handles it.** Payroll $65.94M against revenue $80.10M leaves $14M of headroom. Profit of $24.06M confirms the club is healthy. If Belfour ($6.50M), Svehla ($3.60M) and Roberts ($2.70M) walk or get moved for picks, that frees $12.80M immediately. The young core re-prices INTO that freed space rather than on top of it. The arithmetic works, but only if the expirings are moved.

**Fischer is the known anchor.** At $3.70M with four years left, 26 points in 54 games (0.48 ppg), POTE 90 that has not translated since his rookie year. He is not a trade candidate at 24 with four years — no one takes that package at this price with declining ice. He is a sunk cost to work around until 2008.

**Draft capital is nil.** One fourth-rounder from Toronto. Every trade must be funded by players. The over-80 expiring mechanic is the only way to manufacture picks: Belfour (92 base), Svehla (85 base, over-80 in multiple attributes), Roberts (85 base). Each one is a pick waiting to be harvested before July.

**The three moves that protect the next three seasons:** Move Belfour for a pick before March 19 (his value is peaking at 18-3, 2.27 GAA). Move Svehla and Roberts via the over-80 expiring mechanic before they walk in July. Re-sign Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle, and Eminger on 5-year deals at renewal, staggering the announcement so the salary jump is manageable. These three actions together remove $12.80M of dead money, recover two or three draft picks from nothing, and lock the core through 2010 at a combined payroll that stays under revenue.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers at the March 19 deadline, and what happens to the 15 contracts that expire in July? The answer is both, and the window to open negotiations is now: the GM's own standing order from January said late February is when trade talks begin, and today is February 19.

**Sellers first, because the clock is absolute.** Belfour at 92 base and $6.50M expiring walks for nothing in July if he isn't moved by March 19. Luongo (91 base, 2 years, $1.60M) is already the starter, so Belfour is pure trade capital. Svehla (36, $3.60M) and Roberts (38, $2.70M) are the same mechanic: over-80, expiring, no future here. Together they carry $12.80M in salary that either converts into picks and youth this month or evaporates. The standing order from January 15 protected Belfour as the number one, but Luongo's arrival on February 7 superseded that. He is now a deadline asset.

**Buyers second, because we are dominant and should get better.** Toronto at 94 points, 15 clear of second-place New Jersey, are the clearest contender in the conference. The manual says buy for need when contending, and the coach's flags point at a top-pair defenceman and physicality. Chara at Ottawa (27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring from a 52-point seller) closes both. The problem is funding: we own no pick better than a fourth-rounder, so the Belfour-plus-package structure from the January stack cannot include a first. Belfour alone, or Belfour plus a depth player like Chistov, has to buy Chara. Acceptance is uncertain.

**The summer list, contract by contract:**

**Gaborik** at 91 base, 23, $1.10M, 67 points in 45 games is the one non-negotiable renewal. Five or six years, lock him before July when every team with cap space calls. He is the most urgent renewal on the roster and the January note about urgency was wrong only because the game doesn't allow mid-contract renegotiation. On the day his contract opens, he gets the extension.

**Kaberle** (26, D, $1.90M) and **Eminger** (21, D, POTE 99) are the defensive core. Both on five or six years. Kaberle at 26 is entering his prime; Eminger at 21 with the highest potential grade on the blueline is the reason Colaiacovo becomes expendable.

**Richards** (24, C, $1.00M) gets five or six years. He is the centre for the next window and at $1.00M the cost is trivial relative to his value.

**Nash** (20, LW, $1.20M) gets five or six years. Age 20 on an expiring deal is the worst possible position; lock him or lose him cheap.

**Alexeev** (23, RW, $1.10M, 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG per the coach's report) gets two or three years. He has earned a longer look next season, not a five-year commitment yet.

**Tellqvist** (25, G, $0.80M) gets two years as the backup. The standing order from January said give him time to develop, and at 25 with POTE in the high 90s that advice still holds. Luongo is the starter, Tellqvist is the insurance.

**Abid** (24, LW, $0.40M) gets two or three years. Forty thousand a month for a 24-year-old with 80 toughness and 80 checking is the cheapest physicality in the league. Renew cheap or lose him for nothing.

**Upshall** (21, RW, $1.20M): let him go unless his February and March production says he has made the jump to a top-nine role. At $1.20M for depth with no demonstrated production, the money is better spent elsewhere.

**Colaiacovo** (22, D, $1.10M): trade bait at the deadline or in the summer. Eminger and Stahle are ahead of him on the depth chart, and the coach has already moved Stahle up to pair 3. He fills the void if someone gets injured, but he is not the plan.

**Chistov** (21, LW, $1.10M): deadline trade bait. He is already in the Bell package and the Kovalchuk structure. Move him in February, not June.

**Smirnov** (20, LW, $0.40M, zero games this season): let him go. Four months of watching the coach dress 23 other forwards at 20 years old is the answer. If he develops elsewhere, fine; we cannot dress everyone.

**The decision that needs to happen this week:** Open the Belfour conversation with Ottawa or any contender needing a backup goalie. He cannot walk in July. Every day after that is a day closer to losing $6.50M of tradeable salary for nothing. The Chara ask runs through Belfour, so the two conversations are one conversation.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league closes our two structural gaps (toughness ceiling at 73, faceoff depth below 80) at a price we can actually pay with roster players rather than picks we do not own?

**Chara** at 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 points in 56 games, 27 years old, $1.70M expiring from OTT (57 pts, 11 expiring, $27.44M profit). He closes the toughness gap and adds top-pair offence. The GM vetoed the January double because the price was Eminger, and Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 is worth more to our timeline than Chara at 27. A single Chara acquisition at a lower price (Tucker plus Chistov plus the 4th) is a different question. OTT has no reason to keep him past July and cannot command a high price at 57 points.

**Bell** at 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K with two years left, 24 years old, on CHI (51 pts, 10 expiring, $24.65M profit). He closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously on a re-signable deal. The GM's Jan 25 veto was about using faceoffs as the sole argument; the toughness and checking case is separate and the coverage phase confirms those gaps are binding. CHI at 51 points with 10 expiring is rebuilding, but their profit of $24.65M means they have no financial pressure. They need a real package: Colaiacovo plus Safronov fills their need for young D with upside.

**Komisarek** at 83 TOUG, 66 points in 58 games, 23 years old, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring from MTL (48 pts, 15 expiring). Best value-to-cost ratio on the board. MTL at 48 points with 15 expiring deals cannot re-sign him and are in full teardown. Price: St. Jacques plus Safronov plus the 4th. His 66 points as a defenceman at 23 with POTE 90 is close to what Stahle projects at his best, acquired ready now rather than in two years.

**Thornton** at 91 base, 82 TOUG, 80 FACE, 66 points in 40 games, $4.00M expiring, 25 years old, on BOS (65 pts, 13 expiring, $28.17M profit). He is the most complete player available: closes toughness and faceoffs while adding 1.65 pts/g of scoring. The problem is BOS at 65 points is in the race, and $4.00M is our third-largest contract. If they fall back by late February, they will shop him. If they stay at 65 and push for the playoffs, they will not.

**Conroy** at 94 FACE, 63 points, 31 years old, $2.00M expiring from CGY (48 pts, 10 expiring). Pure rental faceoff centre. CGY at 48 points with the worst record in the league is rebuilding and will deal him for anything. Price is low: Chistov plus the 4th fills the faceoff gap for a playoff run. He is not a solution for toughness (his TOUG is not in the 80+ group), only faceoffs.

**Kudroc** at 80 TOUG, 76 base, 30 points in 52 games, POTE 90, 28 years old, $1.00M expiring from FLA (50 pts, 19 expiring). FLA is in full teardown with 19 expiring contracts. He fills the toughness gap at defenceman with decent offence and a high ceiling for a player whose POTE suggests he has been underused. Price should be cheap given FLA's desperation.

**Marleau** at 89 base, 78 points in 50 games, $1.60M expiring, 25 years old, on SJ (55 pts, 14 expiring). The highest-production player available. SJ cannot re-sign him and are rebuilding. He does not close toughness or faceoffs but at 78 points he is a first-line winger who would replace Mogilny (0.87 pts/g declining) with a five-year extension. The cost would be the first-round pick plus a young player, which conflicts with the ATL Kovalchuk/Heatley pursuit. Pick one.

**Savard** at 89 FACE, 48 points in 43 games, $1.00M expiring, 27 years old, on ATL (60 pts, 11 expiring). Cheaper faceoff option than Conroy, but ATL at 60 points is in the race and may keep him. If the ATL binary (Kovalchuk vs Heatley) is resolved and one stays, Savard might be the throw-in.

**What I am not pursuing:** Avery at 6 points in 57 games is a non-starter. DiPietro at 79 base and 3.65 GAA has not translated his POTE. The ATL stars at 60 points may not sell. Belfour, Svehla, Roberts, and Salo are our over-80 expiring assets and are outgoing (pick recovery), not incoming.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what do we send and what comes back, given that our only draft asset is one 4th-rounder and every move must be funded with bodies?

**Belfour** is the highest-confidence action on the board. At 92 base, 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP, he is the most valuable expiring asset in the league. Luongo is confirmed starter (40 GP, 2.87 GAA, 91 base). Belfour's trade value peaks today and dies March 19. The over-80 expiring mechanic converts him to a pick even without a perfect hockey fit. Any contender with a shaky backup gets playoff insurance for two months at $6.50M. No second goalie in the league reads above 93, and most contenders would welcome a 92-base number two for a run.

**Chara** is the single player who closes the binding gap. At 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 points in 56 games, $1.70M expiring, he solves toughness where our ceiling is 73 and adds top-pair offence we do not have. OTT at 57 points with 11 expiring deals and $27.44M profit has re-signed nobody and is collecting. They will not keep him past July. The package is Tucker (29, $1.30M, 2yr, not lined, 3 GP) plus St. Jacques (24, $0.80M, 2yr, 1 GP, POTE 94, surplus behind five younger D) plus the 4th. Tucker gives them a physical body for the remaining games; St. Jacques gives them a young D with upside. Neither is a player the coach dresses.

**Komisarek** is the fallback if OTT holds. At 83 TOUG, 66 points in 58 games, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring, 23 years old, he closes the same gap for less production than Chara but from a more desperate seller. MTL at 48 points with 15 expiring contracts cannot re-sign him and are collecting whatever they can. Package: Tucker plus Safronov (23, $0.90M, 3yr, 3 GP, POTE 91, surplus D depth) plus the 4th. This is mutually exclusive with Chara — same Tucker, same 4th.

**What I would not do:** Give Chistov (POTE 95, age 21, 16 pts in 45 GP) or Upshall (POTE 99, 17 pts in 45 GP) for Conroy or Savard. Those are core development pieces for a two-month rental. The faceoff gap (next man at 75 behind Sundin at 90) is real but secondary to toughness, and no available faceoff centre is worth gutting the youth pipeline.



## If none of the Chara or Komisarek deals land

The toughness gap stays open. The coach's only internal options are Tucker (TOUG 88 shown, but 3 GP all season — unproven at NHL pace) and dressing Abid (TOUG 80 stored, 64 pts/59 GP, already the only physical forward). Neither reaches 90. The realistic move is to accept the gap and lean on Roberts (73 TOUG, 86 CHKG) and McCabe (73 TOUG, 89 CHKG) plus the checking trio of Tucker/Svehla/Upshall sitting in no unit, and hope the playoff bracket does not match us against a power forward line. The Belfour pick (proposal 1) still stands regardless and is the guaranteed asset on the board.

## Owed

The GM asked on January 19 to monitor Luongo's availability and DiPietro's development through February for a goalie trade window. The task is now complete and the answer is: the window has closed without a trade, because we already have the goalie we were looking for.

**Luongo** is at 40 GP, 18-21-1, 2.87 GAA, 0.877 SV%. He has been Toronto's starter since February 6 and is improving: his GAA has dropped from 3.07 at 19 GP to 2.87 at 40. At 94 overall / 91 base, age 25, $1.60M with two years remaining, he is the high-90s goalie the January standing order was seeking. He is already on this roster. No further action is needed on acquisition.

**DiPietro** at NYI has gone from 7-12-0, 3.65 GAA (the February 6 reading) to 22-18-0, 2.97 GAA, 0.870 SV% in 43 GP. That is real improvement and makes him a better asset for NYI, not a worse one. They are starting him every game, which confirms the February 6 read: NYI will not deal their 21-year-old franchise goalie mid-season. He is not available, and the improvement in his numbers makes him less available, not more.

**What changed since the last report (February 13):** Luongo added three starts and his GAA held at 2.87 with SV% at 0.877, identical. DiPietro added two or three starts and his GAA dipped from ~3.02 to 2.97. Nothing that shifts a decision.

**The live goalie decision is Belfour.** At 93 overall / 92 base, 21 GP, 39 years old, $6.50M expiring, he is a premium rental for any contender and our best pick-recovery asset via the over-80 expiring mechanic. With Luongo starting 40 of 59 games and performing, Belfour's on-ice role is backup. The deadline is March 19. The trade window for Belfour is open now; the goalie trade window for acquisition is not.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-16
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-16

Toronto 40-10-4, 92 pts after 58 games.

## Role coverage

The question this phase answers: can Toronto win the Cup with this roster, or are there holes only a trade fills? The answer is two holes — toughness and faceoffs — and neither has an internal fix at an adequate level.

**Toughness is zero above 80.** The best the roster offers is Roberts at 73 and McCabe at 73, and Roberts is 38 with production already halved. Tucker's 70 TOUG, Chlup's 70, Svehla's 69 — nobody on this roster is an enforcer by the sheet. The only real solution is **Chara** at OTT: 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 points in 56 games, $1.70M expiring from a 52-point seller with 11 expiring deals. No internal reorganisation produces what he provides.

**Faceoffs: one man above 80.** Sundin at 90 carries every important draw. The next best are Chlup 75 and Roberts 75 — neither is a reliable third-or-fourth-line option. Spacek, the coach's bottom-six centre, is below 60. Avery at LA (93 FACE, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years, age 25) closes this gap and the checking gap simultaneously for the cheapest contract on the board. If LA won't deal, Conroy at CGY (94 FACE, 63 pts, $2.00M expiring from 40-point CGY) is the rental fallback.

**Checking is thin but fixable internally.** Tucker at 83 CHKG and Svehla at 83 CHKG are both "not lined" — the coach has 166 combined points of checking-grade sitting on the bench. Upshall at 80 adds a third body. Dressing these three is the internal answer for this season. But Svehla is 36 and Tucker has played 3 games all year, so this is a patch, not a plan.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, stamina: all covered.** The aging trio (Mogilny 94 at 35, Sundin 92 at 34, Roberts 88 at 38) carry the load now, and their production has already dropped (Mogilny 0.90 pts/g, Sundin 0.94, Roberts 0.97). But Gaborik at 92 and 23, Afinogenov at 90 and 25 are the future top two. No acquisition is needed here for this season or next.

**Durability is thin at 4 above 80.** Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. Eminger at 75 and Spacek at 79 are concerning for 21 and 19. This is a development concern more than a trade target — durability is rarely the thing you can buy at a deadline.

**Goalies are solved.** Luongo at 25 with 2 years left is the starter. Belfour's 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP makes him a premium rental whose trade value peaks now and dies March 19.

## Trajectory

The question this phase answers: can this roster sustain itself financially and structurally through 2007-08, or does the summer of 2005 blow it up?

**The age shape is two clusters with no bridge.** Five players at 34+ (Sundin 34, Mogilny 35, Roberts 38, Svehla 36, Belfour 39) carry $26.70M and declining production: Mogilny from 1.62 to 0.90 pts/g, Sundin from 1.46 to 0.94, Roberts from 1.29 to 0.97 per the Coach's report. Below them, 16 players aged 23 or under. Between those groups sits one man: Salo, 30, $2.60M, 24 GP, scratched. The usual bridge tier (27-32 role players) does not exist. When the 34+ men leave, the young core steps up with no transitional group behind them. That is a cliff unless it is managed now.

**The contract cluster is the immediate problem.** Fifteen players and $25.30M come up in the same July. Gaborik (77 pts, POTE 90), Abid (63 pts, POTE 94), Richards (55 pts, POTE 88), Nash (32 pts, POTE 95 at age 20), Kaberle, Chistov (POTE 95), Eminger (POTE 99), Colaiacovo (POTE 99), Alexeev (30 pts, POTE 94), Upshall (POTE 99) are all free simultaneously. Re-signing all ten on the same timeline means their agents all ask at the same time, and every raise compounds.

**Fischer is the hidden liability nobody can touch yet.** $3.70M for four more years, 0.41 pts/g and falling from 0.63. At 24, he's not a rental or a pick-recovery asset. He's a summer-2008 problem dressed as a roster player.

**Sundin's deal is the single worst money commitment.** $8.40M, five years left, POTE 60, age 34. That is 12.7% of payroll locked to a player whose production curve is already declining. Nothing can be done: contracts cannot be renegotiated mid-term. It simply consumes $8.40M every year through 2009-10, when he'll be 39.

**Payroll against revenue leaves room, but not much after the renewals.** Current: $65.94M payroll, $78.45M revenue, $23.20M profit. Trading Belfour, Svehla and Roberts removes $12.80M, dropping payroll to $53.14M. Then re-signing ten young players at star rates: Gaborik maybe $3-4M, Abid $2.5-3.5M, Richards $3-4M, Nash $2-3M, the rest at $1.5-2.5M each. That's roughly $20-25M in new money on top of the remaining $53.14M, landing near $73-78M. Profit compresses from $23M to perhaps $5-8M. Tight but workable. The problem is if you fail to trade the three veterans: you'd be paying $65.94M plus $20M in raises against $78M revenue, which is a loss.

**Draft capital is gone.** One fourth-rounder, nothing better. Every deadline trade must be player-for-player. Every young player you re-sign at a team-friendly price is, functionally, a draft pick you didn't have to spend. This makes the renewal window more important than the trade window.

**Three moves that protect three seasons:**

**1. Trade Belfour, Svehla and Roberts before March 19.** All three are over-80 base with expiring deals, so the pick-recovery mechanic applies. Belfour (92 base) is the most valuable rental a contender will accept in February or March. Svehla (80+) and Roberts (80+) round out the package. Together they free $12.80M and should generate two to four picks. Without these trades, the payroll math above collapses.

**2. Lock Gaborik, Abid, Nash and Richards on five or six years in July.** These four are the engine of the next three seasons and their current salaries ($1.10M, $0.40M, $1.20M, $1.00M) are absurd relative to production (77, 63, 32, 55 points). A five-year deal at $2.5-4M each locks the core at a price the trade market would never offer.

**3. Stagger the second tier.** Chistov, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Kaberle on three or four years rather than all five or six. This splits the next renewal wave across 2007 and 2008, preventing a repeat of the 15-player cluster.

---

**On deliverable #2** (Luongo/DiPietro monitoring through February): Luongo arrived on roster before the deadline; he is Toronto's starter at 91 base, 25, $1.60M, two years left, POTE 97. The Jan 15 mandate to fetch a high-90s goalie is fulfilled. DiPietro monitoring confirmed he is not a realistic target (79 base, 3.65 GAA, NYI will re-sign). The remaining goalie question is now Belfour: trade for the pick before March 19, or run him as playoff insurance. That is the GM's call, not a monitoring task. This item is closed.

## Calendar

We are both a buyer and a seller at the March 19 deadline, and the two roles do not conflict: we move end-of-life veterans we won't re-sign into draft capital, and we acquire Avery to close the Coach's bottom-six centre gap. The 92-point position makes buying easy to fund because we have three over-80 expirers whose only alternative is walking for nothing in July. Negotiations open late February per the GM's standing order; 31 days from today.

**Belfour** is the engine. At 93 displayed, 92 base, $6.50M expiring, and 39, he is the club's only high-value pick-recovery asset this deadline. His last-playoff form (18-3, 2.27 GAA in 21 GP) makes him a premium rental for any contender. Primary target: Chara from Ottawa (94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring, 52-pt seller with 11 expiring deals). Fallback: straight pick via the over-80 mechanic. If no trade is agreed by March 15, pull him from the playoff lineup anyway — his value is in the trade, not the minutes. No trades after March 19.

**Svehla** is 36, 84 base, $3.60M, expiring. At 36 with Eminger at 21 (POTE 99) pushing for minutes, Svehla's role shrinks regardless. He is over-80 and expiring; that is a pick. Moving him before March 19 recovers capital. If the GM wants his playoff experience for 24 games plus a first round, the cost is that pick — a fair trade, but only if Eminger or Colaiacovo aren't getting those minutes instead.

**Roberts** is 38, 87 base, $2.70M, expiring, producing 0.97 pts/g (down from 1.29). The Coach's trajectory report names him as declining. We are not re-signing a 38-year-old at any price. Move him before March 19 for a pick. Koltsov at 1.09 pts/g at 23 with 92 speed replaces his production curve going forward.

**Avery** from LA is the buy-side acquisition. 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years, age 25. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals is a motivated seller. Package per the Feb 12 note: Tucker (29, $1.30M, 83 CHKG, currently in no unit) for Avery. Zero on-ice cost to us; closes the bottom-six checking-centre gap the Coach has flagged every report since January.

**Summer renewals — the 12 expiring players remaining after the three depart:**

- **Gaborik:** 5-6 years. 91 base, 67 pts/45 GP, age 23, POTE 90, $1.10M. The most urgent renewal. July is the only window (no mid-contract renegotiation exists).
- **Kaberle:** 5-6 years. Age 26, $1.90M. Top-pair D entering his prime.
- **Nash:** 5-6 years. Age 20, $1.20M. Young winger with a long runway.
- **Richards:** 5 years. Age 24, $1.00M. Centre prospect.
- **Eminger:** 5-6 years. Age 21, POTE 99, $1.20M. GM's explicit development priority.
- **Chistov:** 2 years or move at deadline. Age 21, $1.10M. If he's not trade bait for Avery or another package, renew short and reassess.
- **Colaiacovo:** 3 years. Age 22, $1.10M. Eminger fills his slot long-term, but he's useful depth.
- **Alexeev:** 3 years. Age 23, 0.55 pts/g on 8.3 MPG. Efficient; earn more ice and re-sign cheap.
- **Tellqvist:** 2 years. Age 25, 77 base, $0.80M. GM's Jan 15 call holds — give him time to develop as Luongo's backup.
- **Abid:** 3 years at $0.40M. Coach's toughness target. Cheap.
- **Upshall:** 2 years. Age 21, $1.20M. Depth winger.
- **Smirnov:** 2 years. Age 20, $0.40M. Cheap forward depth.

The staggered-lock principle holds: five stars on long deals, seven depth on short ones. No single summer renews the whole core again.

**On the Luongo/DiPietro monitoring task:** Luongo is on the roster (91 base, 65 GP this season, 35-30, $1.60M, 2 years). He is the number-one goalie. DiPietro at 79 base has produced 7-12, 3.65 GAA and NYI will re-sign him. The goalie acquisition window closed the day Luongo arrived; the task is complete.

## League scan

Which players across all thirty clubs close Toronto's toughness, faceoff and checking gaps, and whose club will actually deal? The answer is Bell and Jackman first, Chara and Komisarek second, Conroy and Bates for the centre slot, with the ATL duo (Kovalchuk, Heatley) as the ceiling if a package works.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 80 base, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE, $900K, 2 years, age 24) is the single best gap-to-cost trade in the league. He fills toughness, checking and faceoffs simultaneously at $900K on a deal that runs through 2006-07. CHI at 50 pts with 10 expiring contracts is a seller. He's only 21 points in 58 games, so he's not a scorer, but the Coach's gap is a checking centre, not a goal-scorer. Package: Colaiacovo (POTE 99, age 21) plus Safronov. Eminger fills the Colaiacovo slot internally.

**Jackman** (STL, D, 80 base, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 29 pts/57 GP, $700K, 3 years, age 23) is new to the board and the best long-term toughness defenceman available. 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 29 points from the blue line at 23 years old on $700K with three years left. STL at 56 pts with 9 expiring deals are not desperate but not contending either. The problem: STL has profit ($14M) and prestige (427), so they need a real package. Our fourth-rounder plus a young player (Chistov, POTE 95, or Safronov) is the ask. Three years of retention at $700K makes this a trajectory move, not just a deadline rental.

**Chara** (OTT, D, 85 base, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 55 pts/59 GP, $1.70M expiring, age 27) remains the highest-value single deadline acquisition. 55 points from a defenceman who hits like a forward. OTT at 55 pts with 11 expiring deals is the perfect seller. The TOUG reads 90 here, not 94 as noted on February 12 (likely form-adjusted difference; base is 90). Package idea: double acquisition with Havlat (OTT, 87 base, 75 pts/59 GP, $900K, 23, POTE 86) in one negotiation. OTT gets youth; we get elite D and top-six LW for $2.60M combined.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 77 base, 66 pts/59 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 23, POTE 90) is the best offensive defenceman on the board. 66 points at 23 from the blue line. MTL at 48 pts with 14 expiring contracts cannot re-sign him. Package: St. Jacques plus Safronov plus our fourth-rounder. His overall is only 77 but the point production says the grade understates his offensive game.

**Conroy** (CGY, C, 85 base, 87 FACE, 70 pts/58 GP, $2.00M expiring, age 33) is the cleanest rental centre. 70 points at 87 FACE from the worst team in the league (18-32-6). CGY is rebuilding and will deal him for anything with future value. Cost: Chistov plus our fourth-rounder. He's 33 and expiring, so this is a two-month fix, not a plan. If we want to solve faceoffs permanently, Bell is the answer, not Conroy.

**Bates** (NYI, C, 83 base, 94 FACE, 79 CHKG, 30 pts/43 GP, $900K expiring, age 29) has the best faceoff grade in the league at 94 and solid checking at 79, all for $900K. The problem is NYI at 59 pts — they are in the playoff race and may not sell. 30 points in 43 games is modest production. Only pursue if NYI clearly fades by late February.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 79 base, 88 FACE, 58 pts/56 GP, $1.00M expiring, age 27) is the faceoff answer that folds into any ATL negotiation for Kovalchuk or Heatley. ATL at 56 pts with 11 expiring deals. At 88 FACE and 58 points for $1M, he is cheap insurance on any ATL package.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 87 base, 75 pts/59 GP, $900K expiring, age 23, POTE 86) is the add-on to Chara. 75 points at 23 for $900K is the best production-to-salary ratio on the entire board. If OTT wants youth in return, he travels with Chara in one deal.

**Avery** (LA, C, 79 base, 90 FACE, 84 CHKG, 79 TOUG, $400K, 2 years, age 24) needs a correction on our file. The grades say he is what we want — 90 FACE, 84 CHKG, 79 TOUG — but the production says he is a ghost: 6 points in 57 games. At $400K he costs almost nothing to acquire, but his ice value on a contender is questionable. I would not spend a roster spot on a player producing 0.11 points a game unless the Coach thinks the grades translate in playoff minutes. Deprioritise below Bell.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 89 base, 97 pts/56 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 21, POTE 86) and **Heatley** (ATL, RW, 91 base, 88 pts/53 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 24, POTE 86) remain the ceiling. 97 points at 21 is the best production on the board. But we own no first-round pick, and ATL has no reason to take players-only unless they want to rebuild immediately. The prior Koltsov-plus-pick package is dead because we do not own a first-rounder. Any ATL deal needs a real young piece: St. Jacques or Nash or even Gaborik, and the GM will not trade those. I would not chase ATL unless they explicitly signal a fire sale.

**Cammalleri** (LA, RW, 79 base, POTE 98, 39 pts/36 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 22) and **Frolov** (LA, LW, 77 base, POTE 96, 40 pts/37 GP, $1.10M expiring, age 22) are the development targets for summer rather than the deadline. Both are on expiring deals at LA (54 pts, 13 expiring). At 22 with POTE 96-98 and 39-40 points in limited games, they are re-signable for five years at modest cost. LA at 54 pts is a seller by mid-March. These belong in the summer plan, not the February one.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which two or three proposals should we open by late February, what do we send, and why do the other clubs agree? We are 92 points with three structural gaps (nobody above 73 TOUG, one man above 80 FACE, checking thin), no picks beyond a fourth-rounder, and Belfour's value dying March 19. Every package must be player-for-player funded from surplus and expiring contracts.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE, $900K, 2 years) is the single best gap-to-cost deal on the board: closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs at once on a contract that runs through 2006-07. Give Colaiacovo (22, POTE 99, $1.10M exp) and Safronov (23, $0.90M, 3 years, 3 GP). Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 and ACCE 85 fills Colaiacovo's top-four slot immediately. CHI at 50 points with 10 expiring deals is a clear seller. They collect a POTE 99 blueliner at 22 and a young depth D. Net payroll: $1.10M saved.

**Chara** (OTT, D, 27, 85 base, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 55 pts/59 GP, $1.70M expiring) is the highest single-player gap-filler in the league. The Jan 19 veto killed giving Eminger for him. This package does not touch Eminger. Give Tucker (29, $1.30M, 2 years, 3 GP, 1 pt) and Salo (30, $2.60M, 2 years, 24 GP, 8 pts, scratched). Both are dead weight. OTT at 55 points with 11 expiring deals is a seller, and they receive $3.90M in salary they can use or waive: a CHKG 92 winger plus a SHPW 95 blueliner with two years left. We dump dead money and acquire 55 points from a defenceman who hits like a forward. Net payroll: $2.20M saved. Acceptance uncertain — OTT at 55 points is not desperate.

**Belfour** (39, 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, 18-3 2.27 GAA .916 SP in 21 GP) is not a gap-filler acquisition; he is the pick recovery the GM must execute by March 19. Trade him to a 1-3 seed with a shaky backup for the over-80 expiring pick, plus whatever player that club offers alongside. His value peaks this week: the form is elite, the market is thin, and every day past March 19 costs us a pick for nothing. He saves $6.50M. The GM's Jan 15 order protected him; Luongo's arrival on roster at 91 base with two years left supersedes that.

**If none land:** Dress Tucker (83 CHKG, TOUG 88) and Svehla (83 CHKG) for this season's checking, and accept Sundin at 90 FACE carrying every draw. Do not chase Chara if OTT holds. Belfour is non-negotiable: if no player package works, take the pick alone.

## Owed

**Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window** — this task is complete, and I'm closing it out.

**Luongo** arrived before this window opened (Feb 6, confirmed on roster). He is 94 displayed / 91 base, 25 years old, $1.60M with 2 years remaining, 40 GP. The Jan 15 mandate to find a high-90s goalie is fulfilled. There is no goalie trade window for Toronto to monitor because we already have the franchise goalie.

**DiPietro** has played himself into legitimacy since my Feb 6 note. He's gone from 7 GP / 3.65 GAA to 41 GP, 22-16, 113 GA in 2,305 minutes (2.94 GAA, .871 SP) on 56.2 minutes per start. He is every-game starter at NYI. His base is 79, displayed 81, POTE 98. His weaknesses remain positional and rebound control (both in the 50s-60s), but his speed grades are elite (95 AGIL, 92 SPEE). At $1.10M with 1 year left, if NYI miss the playoffs he's available this summer.

None of that changes our plan. We have Luongo at 91 base and 25, and Belfour at 92 base as a rental or pick-recovery asset. DiPietro at 79 base is a step below Luongo at the same age, and we don't need a second starter. He would only matter if Luongo regressed or got hurt, and right now Luongo is at 99 morale playing 40 games with the best record in hockey.

The task is done. The goalie situation is solved; the remaining goalie question is whether to trade Belfour before March 19 for draft capital, and that is a separate deadline decision, not a monitoring job.
