# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-16

Next game vs CAR on Friday 18 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who among the 23-and-under players is getting the games and minutes his scouting file and current production have earned, and who is not. With 58 games down and 24 left, the season is closing on any player who hasn't been given a real run.

**Stahle** is still the loudest one. POTE 96 at 20, 3 games in 58. He got dressed and played three times at 20.0 MPG, which is top-pair ice, so someone believes in him — but 3 out of 58 is nothing. He needs to be in the lineup regularly or the scouting report is meaningless.

**Spezza** is the second loudest. POTE 99, 37 games, 7.5 MPG, and now scratched again. His morale at 86 is the lowest of any young player on this roster. At 21, 7.5 minutes a night builds nothing. He's been available for 64% of the season's games but playing at fourth-line depth minutes. The opportunity is gone if it isn't seized in these final 24 games.

**Alexeev** is the quiet one nobody's raising. 30 points in 55 games at 8.3 MPG. That's 0.55 points per game on less than nine minutes a night. At POTE 94 and 23, that rate on that ice time says he could carry a third-line role with 12+ minutes and produce. He's getting the games but not the minutes. Currently scratched, but when he's in, he's efficient enough to earn more.

**Smirnov** has zero games, POTE 70. At 20 with the lowest ceiling in the young group, the zero games are a fair reflection of where he sits. I wouldn't force him in at the expense of Stahle or Spezza.

**Gaborik** (77 pts, first line, 19.7 MPG), **Chlup** (35 pts, second line, 15.2 MPG at 18), **Nash** (32 pts, third line, 13 MPG), **Klesla** (58 of 58 games, 15.1 MPG) — all getting the games their play has earned. No concerns.

**Koltsov** at 18 points in 34 games (0.53 pts/g) on the fourth line is producing on his minutes. He's the GM's trading chip and he's doing his job earning trade value.

**Spacek, Chistov, Eminger, Upshall, Colaiacovo, Ouellet** — rotation players getting reasonable opportunity when dressed. No individual concern beyond the GM's deliberate rotation philosophy.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: which players are moving, in which direction, and what does that mean for the roster the GM builds after the deadline? The window runs from December 1 through today, 77 in-game days.

**Chlup** is the best thing happening on this roster. Since December 1: 34 games, 0.79 pts/g on 16.9 MPG, up from 0.62 on 11.0 before. At 18, both his production and his trust went up simultaneously. That's a genuine breakout, not a hot streak. He's a first-line winger for next season.

**Spezza** is the worst. Since December 1: 16 games, 0.38 pts/g on 5.3 MPG. His minutes halved again, from 9.1 to 5.3, while his rate also dropped. POTE 99 at 21. I've raised this five times. At 5.3 MPG he is not developing and he is not helping. He either gets 12+ minutes by February or the GM should treat him as expendable.

**Koltsov** has killed his own trade value. Early season: 1.10 pts/g in 10 games. Since December 1: 0.29 pts/g in 24 games on 10.6 MPG. The GM wants him as a chip. Nobody gives a second-round pick for a 0.29 player. If he stays, he's a fourth-liner. If the GM still wants to move him, the deadline is now.

**Mogilny** at 35 is showing the steep part of the slope. First 24 games: 1.62 pts/g. Last 30: 0.87. Minutes stayed the same at 19.2. He was a top-line right wing in October and is a second-line option in February. Plan for that being his ceiling from here.

**Sundin and Roberts** are aging under increasing load. Sundin: 1.46 down to 0.94, minutes up from 16.9 to 20.6. Roberts: 1.29 down to 0.97, minutes up from 16.5 to 20.5. Both are producing less on more ice. The third-line stamina ceiling (ENDU mean 56) is forcing the top nine to carry, and the two oldest are paying for it. Neither can sustain this into the playoffs.

**Fischer** confirms the January 30 flag. 0.63 to 0.41 on minutes up from 20.8 to 21.9. He's 24 with four years at $3.7M remaining. The GM keeps him, and that's his call, but his next contract conversation should assume this trend continues.

**Richards** shows the same pattern at 24: 1.08 down to 0.91 on flat minutes. Small dip, not alarming, but worth watching alongside Fischer. Two 24-year-olds trending down on the same timeline suggests either a system problem or shared fatigue from the top-nine load.

**Eminger** has recovered and that matters for the deadline. Early season: 0.35 pts/g. Since December 1: 0.57 on 17.8 MPG. His season rate will climb past the 0.45 trade threshold. If he holds 0.55+ through March, selling him becomes harder to justify at 21.

**Klesla** at 22 is declining: 0.50 down to 0.32 on flat minutes (14.6 to 15.4). At 22 the direction should be up. This isn't age. Either he's not a top-four defenceman or something has gone wrong in his development.

**Chistov** at 21 is the quiet win. 0.29 to 0.40 on minutes up from 9.5 to 15.0. He's earning a bigger role and delivering on it. Keep giving him ice.

**Upshall** improved his rate (0.33 to 0.43) while his minutes halved (13.4 to 7.7). He's more efficient but seeing less. At 0.43 on 7.7 MPG he's a fourth-liner doing fourth-line work. No promotion case yet, but he's not hurting.

**Smirnov** has zero games. Period. At 20 with a POTE high enough to draft, he's been on the roster for a full season and never put on a jersey. The GM's rotation philosophy has not reached him.

**Stahle** has finally played: 3 games, 20.0 MPG. The January 25 note is retired. Zero points in 3 games means nothing at 20. The 20 MPG means the coaching staff trusts him. Keep dressing him.

**St. Jacques and Safronov** each got 1 and 3 games respectively. Too early to read. Safronov's 13.7 MPG is a reasonable first look.

**No grades moved on the card** for any created or drafted player in this window. All the production shifts above are from form, ice time and usage, not attribute gains or losses. That means the underlying tools haven't changed — it's opportunity and confidence doing the work.

### Defencemen end-of-season read (obligation #1, 11th delivery)

Ranked by recent-window performance and age: **Kaberle** (26, 0.58, 22.4 MPG, rising) is the keeper and the anchor. **Eminger** (21, 0.57, 17.8 MPG, recovering) is the second option cheaply. **Stahle** (20, just started, POTE 96) is the future. **Colaiacovo** (22, 0.38) and **Klesla** (22, 0.32, declining at the wrong age) are third/fourth pair. **Fischer** (24, 0.41) is a keeper by GM order but his production doesn't justify $3.7M. **McCabe** (29, 0.47, $3M x4) is the sell candidate — his recent window is identical to January's, confirming the decline isn't a blip. **Salo** (30, 0.22, minutes collapsed from 20.3 to 14.6) is the easiest cut. **Svehla** (36, 0.56) is a valuable veteran for this year, not next.

## Morale watch

The room is almost entirely at ease; most of the roster sits at 99 and the few who aren't are explainable. Two things are worth the GM's attention tonight and one is just good news.

**Spezza** is at 86, unchanged, on 7.5 mpg against an 80-89 OVR expectation of 17 and a 70-79 band of 10. At OVR 71 he falls in the lower band and still sits below it. I have raised this five times since January. His morale hasn't slipped further so the urgency isn't crisis-level, but 37 games at 7.5 mpg with POTE 99 is a year burning. He needs either a real run on the third or fourth centre spot or a full scratch so he can be dealt with in the off-season. The GM controls this, not me.

**Richards** dropped from 99 to 96 (−3) this save. He is playing 17.0 mpg at an 86 OVR, right on his band, and 55 points in 56 games is his best season. The drop is not a minutes problem. It is the team's results leaking into the room. If we start winning, this fixes itself in ten games. No line change addresses it.

**Chlup** at 92, 15.2 mpg, 85 OVR. Band says ~17. He is 2 mpg short but producing 35 points in 47 games (0.74 pts/g) at 18 years old. Morale is stable. If he dips below 90 I would push him onto the first centre spot more often, but right now no action is needed.

**Stahle** went from 94 to 99 (+5) with 3 games played. He is finally seeing ice. That is the development rotation working.

## Role composition

Unit composition is sound across the board; the lines are built for what they are. The one structural gap is at centre in the circles.

**L1** is the complete line: checking mean 80 with Roberts, McCabe and Fischer all at 83 on the sheet, scoring mean 88 carried by Gaborik 98 and Sundin 92. Sundin's 90 faceoff wins the draws this line needs. No change.

**L2** is the offensive line, and that is by design. Mogilny 92 and Afinogenov 90 scoring, Kaberle 91 playmaking. The cost is checking mean 66 and faceoffs mean 58. Those numbers are low, but the fix would mean pulling a checker off L1 or L3 and weakening a line that already does that job. The design answer is that L2 scores; they are not asked to shut anyone down.

**L3** has the best checking mean of L2/L3/L4 at 73, plus speed mean 86 with Chistov 97. Richards at 74 on draws is the best available backup to Sundin. This is a serviceable 3rd line and the right checkers sit here.

**L4** at faceoffs mean 53 is the worst unit on the roster. For a fourth line that's tolerable; they are there for speed (Koltsov 99) and forecheck, not to win draws. Abid at 82 checking gives them teeth. No change.

**K1** checking mean 78, K2 mean 73. Both acceptable. No change.

**The gap: faceoff depth.** Sundin 90 is the only faceoff man on this roster above 80. Chlup 79 is the next best, Richards 74. If Sundin is out or struggling, every line loses the circle. That is not fixable by moving players between lines; it requires a centre at the trade deadline or in the off-season who wins draws.

## Opponent matchup

The question here is how to handle a hot CAR club that beat us 6-2 the only time we met this season. CAR is 5-0-0 in their last five (LWOOOWWWWW newest first), scoring 3.2 per game across the season, and we need to be better than we were in that first meeting.

**Defensive pairing is the problem.** Our current pair 2 is Kaberle/Stahle (83/70) and pair 3 is Klesla/St. Jacques (83/66). The auto-pairing puts our L2 out with pair 2, which means Chlup's line faces Rucchin (SPEE 80, PASS 84, FACE 86) and Brendl (SPEE 94, SHPW 93). Stahle's SPEE 69 cannot track Brendl's 94. The one game we lost 2-6 likely came on this mismatch. Swapping Klesla and Stahle gives pair 2 as Kaberle/Klesla (83/83, Klesla SPEE 92 handles Brendl) and pair 3 as Stahle/St. Jacques against their L3 (Heerema 71, Vasicek 76, Domenichelli 71), their weakest line. Same 20 players, less damage.

**Luongo starts.** CAR is scoring 3.2 per game on a five-game heater and Weekes (86) is a capable enough goalie that we cannot coast. Luongo at 94 is the easiest comparison on the schedule and we cannot afford to give this team confidence the way we did in October.

**Forward lines stay put.** Our top six (Sundin 90, Gaborik 97, Roberts 87, Mogilny 89, Chlup 85, Afinogenov 85) is 12-18 OVR points above their top six. Our PP at 37% (20/54) against their 17.6% PP should generate goals. The faceoff gap on our L2 (Chlup 79 vs Rucchin 86) and L4 (Spacek 54 vs Druken 71) is real but structural, not fixable this week.

## Owed

This answers the GM's standing request: every game, analyse our defencemen and update who should go at the end of the season. Ten deliveries so far; here is what has moved since February 12th.

**McCabe** is at 50 points in 58 games, 0.86 pts/g. The trajectory keeps bending down: 0.96 on January 26th, 0.89 cumulative by February 12th, now 0.86. At 29 with a $3.0M four-year deal, he is still the loudest sell on the blue line. His production is declining while his contract holds firm, and a contender pays deadline value for a top-pairing left-shot D with 50 points.

**Eminger** reads 20 points in 44 games, 0.45 pts/g. This is exactly where he sat on February 6th when I flagged him as a sell. No recovery in the final ten days. At 21 with an expiring $1.2M, he is tradeable if we are sellers, but the price is now close to nothing with so few games left. A late call to a contender for a cheap prospect D is the best we get.

**Kaberle** at 28 points in 50 games is the keeper, confirmed. GM's words: "Kaberle is definitely a keeper. Kaberle is a star defenseman." Expiring $1.90M, which means the renewal decision arrives this summer regardless of what happens on the ice.

**Klesla** at 23 points in 58 games, 15.1 MPG, 83 OVR at 22, $0.90M for two more years. He stays. The cheapest and most durable D on the roster.

**Svehla** at 24 points in 36 games, 0.67 pts/g, is the GM's MVP on an expiring $3.60M at 36. I proposed him for a trade once and the GM shut it down emphatically. I am not touching that again. The question for season's end is purely financial: renewing a 36-year-old at $3.6M is what I would avoid.

**Stahle** is the change since last time. He was at zero games in 49 on January 25th, a POTE 96 defenceman collecting a salary. He is now at three games, 20.0 MPG each. Three games in 58 does not fix a year, but someone finally put him on the ice. The question for season's end: do we keep developing him or trade the contract ($0.97M x 3 years) while his potential still carries prospect value? Three games is not enough to answer that yet, but it is the first data point.

**Colaiacovo** reads 12 points in 30 games, 0.40 pts/g at 22. His development has stalled. $1.10M expiring. He is a trade candidate if we are sellers, same logic as Eminger.

**Salo** at 8 points in 24 games, 30 years old, $2.60M for two more years. A rental at best. Not producing enough to justify the money or the term.

No change to the sell list since February 12th. McCabe, Eminger and Colaiacovo lead. Svehla is untouchable (GM's standing call). Stahle moves from "wasted" to "three-game sample" and needs February to tell us anything.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-13
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-13

Toronto 40-9-4, 92 pts after 57 games.

## Role coverage

The two gaps that cannot be solved from within are toughness and faceoffs; checking can be, and should be, by putting players the coach already has into the line-up.

**Checking** is not actually a gap. Tucker (29, 83 CHKG, $1.30M) and Upshall (21, 80 CHKG) are both on the roster and in no unit. Dress them and the active checker count goes from four to six, which is adequate for a 28-man roster. This is the coach's call, not a trade target.

**Toughness** is genuinely missing. The best displayed TOUG on the roster is Roberts at 73, and he is 38. There is nobody above 80, and nobody under 30 on the roster who will get there naturally. This requires an external fix. Chara (27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring at OTT) closes it with top-pair offence. Avery (25, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K) closes it with a cheaper body. Either works; Chara is the better player, Avery is the better fit for roster construction because he also fixes faceoffs.

**Faceoffs** has a single source: Sundin at 90, age 34. Chlup at 75 is the long-term answer at 18 but he is not ready tonight. If Sundin misses four games, the club has no one above 75 winning draws. Avery at 93 FACE is the direct fix. The Conroy rental (31, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring) was discussed but he costs Chistov plus a pick, which is too much for a rental when Avery is re-signable.

**Scoring and playmaking** are covered for now and will thin after this summer. Mogilny (35) and Sundin (34) carry 94 and 92 overall. Gaborik (22, 92) and Afinogenov (25, 90) are the future. The age curve means the club must be rebuilding around those two within two seasons, which is a trajectory problem, not a coverage problem today.

**Speed** is the deepest role on the roster: 22 players above 80, led by Gaborik at 98 and Afinogenov at 96. No concern.

**Goalies** are covered. Luongo (25, 2 years) is the starter. Ouellet (23, 1.91 GAA in 9 games, 2 years) is developing as the backup. Belfour (39, $6.50M expiring) is the deadline asset per the standing order. Tellqvist (25, 1 year) is expendable depth.

## Trajectory

Is this club heading for a cliff? No. But July 2005 is the hinge: fifteen contracts worth $25.30M expire, and whether the stars renew or walk decides whether the next three seasons are a contender window or a rebuild. The money is healthy (profit $24.01M on revenue $76.79M), the age shape is close to the manual's target, and the young core carries eight players at POTE 90+ under age 24. The problem is not the roster — it is the calendar.

**The age curve is thin in the middle and that is fine.** Sixteen players at 23 or under, five at 34 or over, one at 30 (Salo, $2.60M, 2 years). The manual wants 5-7 veterans and around 20 young players, and that is almost exactly the shape. The 30-33 gap is a concern only if the veterans break down; if Sundin (34, 5 years) and Mogilny (35, 2 years) hold, the bridge is covered.

**Belfour, Svehla and Roberts are $12.80M leaving the building.** Belfour at 39, $6.50M, 92 base, expiring, Luongo already the starter. Svehla at 36, $3.60M, expiring, 24 points in 36 games. Roberts at 38, $2.70M, expiring, 63 points in 57 games. All three are over-80 expiring assets recoverable for a pick. Moving them recovers three draft selections, which is the single biggest capital problem the club faces: Toronto currently owns one fourth-rounder and nothing earlier. Three mid-round picks plus the existing fourth gives the front office real ammunition for the first time in months.

**Gaborik is the most important contract on the sheet.** 22 years old, 77 points in 57 games, $1.10M, one year left, POTE 90. If he walks, the club loses its best skater and the window likely closes because there is no pick to replace him with. He must go to 5-6 years. Richards at 24, 55 points, $1.00M, one year left, POTE 88, same priority. Nash at 20, 32 points, $1.20M, POTE 95, same.

**The $25.30M expiring splits into three groups and the summer cost depends on which tier gets the long deal.** Stars (Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle, Abid) on 5-6 years at market rates will likely cost $8-12M in raises. Mid-tier (Chistov, Colaiacovo, Alexeev, Eminger, Upshall, Tellqvist) on 2-3 years keeps flexibility. The veterans (Belfour, Svehla, Roberts) leave. Net payroll after the shakeup: roughly $55-60M with the club's $76.79M revenue, leaving $16-21M profit and room to sign from the market.

**Fischer is the one deal that hurts.** 24, $3.70M, four years left, 26 points in 52 games, POTE 90 but declining from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g. He is locked through 2009 at a salary that outstrips his production. There is nothing to do now — no cap, and four years is too long to trade without absorbing pain — but he is the summer-2008 problem.

## Calendar

**Are we buyers or sellers at March 19?** We are buyers with one mandatory sell-side action that happens to fund the buying. At 92 points and 17 clear of second-place NJ, the deadline question is already answered: buy for need. The Coach has named two gaps, faceoffs and toughness, and the roster has a $6.50M goalie we no longer need sitting in the way.

**Belfour** is the clock. Luongo arrived at 91 base, 25 years old, $1.60M, 2 years. Belfour's 92 base and expiring $6.50M make him our only over-80 pick-recovery asset, and the over-80 mechanic has a hard March 19 wall. Move him and we recover capital; keep him and it evaporates in July. This is not a "maybe if the price is right" trade. He goes.

**Chara at OTT** is the lead target. 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 points in 56 games at 27, $1.70M expiring from a 52-point seller with 11 expiring deals. He closes the Coach's toughness gap (nobody on our roster above 71) and brings top-pair offence in one package. OTT is rebuilding, so they want youth or picks. Belfour solves their immediate need if they still have a shot at a spot; if not, a young player plus a pick from a separate Belfour move works. Exact package gets built when negotiations open in late February per the GM's standing order.

**Avery at LA** is the secondary target. 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years. He closes the faceoff gap behind Richards at 72 and adds toughness, and the Feb 12 package (Tucker for Avery) costs nothing we plan to keep. Tucker is 29, $1.30M, in no unit. If LA is still selling at 48 points with 13 expiring deals, this is the cheapest deal on the board. Chara is the priority; Avery complements him.

**Svehla and Roberts** are the second wave of pick recovery. Svehla (D, 36, $3.60M) and Roberts (LW, 38, $2.70M) both clear 80 and are expiring. Together they shed $6.30M and can generate picks via the same mechanic. If Chara or Avery needs a salary-matching body, one of them goes to the trade partner instead of for a bare pick. Either path works.

The sell-side total is Belfour $6.50M, Svehla $3.60M, Roberts $2.70M, a combined $12.80M shed. The buy-side is Chara at $1.70M (rental, this spring) and Avery at $400K (2 years, re-signable). Net payroll relief is roughly $10.70M before any picks come in.

**Gaborik** is the summer priority. 91 base, 22 years old, $1.10M expiring. He cannot be renegotiated mid-contract per the game rules, so the renewal conversation starts at season end. On 5-6 years to avoid a July bidding war. This is the single most valuable re-signing on the roster and the one that cannot slip.

**Nash, Richards, Kaberle, Eminger** join Gaborik on 5-6 year locks. Nash at 20, Richards at 24, Kaberle at 26, Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 (the GM's protected asset). All are $1.00M-$1.90M now, all under 27, all core. Stagger the start dates where possible so they don't all hit the market in the same July.

**The depth eight** (Chistov 21, Colaiacovo 22, Alexeev 23, Upshall 21, Smirnov 20, Abid 24, plus whoever else clears waivers) renew on 2-3 years at or near current salary. Abid stays per the GM's Jan 25 call as the single toughness target, and the coach has him in no unit, which is a lineup conversation not a roster one.

**Tellqvist at 25, $0.80M** renews 2 years as the backup behind Luongo. The GM's Jan 15 order was to give him time, and Luongo's arrival means he is the clear backup rather than a competitor for the starter role. His POTE in the high 90s means he carries trade value as a future asset if Luongo ever needs insurance.

**Deliverable #2 (Luongo/DiPietro goalie window):** Fulfilled. Luongo is on the roster at 91 base with 2 years left, confirmed Feb 7. DiPietro at NYI sits at 79 base, POTE 99, but has produced 7-12-0 at 3.65 GAA this season. Potential has not translated, and NYI will hold rather than deal. No goalie acquisition is needed. The goalie window is now about moving Belfour out, not bringing anyone in.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players on other clubs close Toronto's two structural gaps (toughness, faceoffs) or fill the scoring hole that opens when Mogilny and Sundin decline, and can be acquired from a motivated seller before March?

The broad picture is clear. Three clubs — ATL (54 pts, 11 expiring), LA (54 pts, 13 expiring), and MTL (46 pts, 14 expiring) — hold the best combination of need-to-sell and players-we-need. OTT (52 pts, 11 expiring) and CHI (50 pts, 10 expiring) are secondary. The standout finding is **Komisarek**, a 23-year-old defenceman producing 66 points in 58 games on a $1.10M expiring deal from a 46-point team. He has not been a target before and he is the best player-to-cost ratio on the entire board.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23, 77 base, 80 displayed ovr, 83 TOUG, 66 pts/58 GP, $1.10M expiring, POTE 90) is the single best new find. A defenceman scoring 1.14 points per game at 23 with POTE 90 from the 46-point Canadiens. His 83 TOUG partially fills our toughness gap. MTL has 14 expiring deals and $17.71M profit — they cannot re-sign everyone and will deal a young D who costs $1.10M to free space. This is the target the GM has not seen yet.

**Chara** (OTT, D, 27, 85 base, 82 displayed ovr, 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring) remains the primary toughness fix per the Feb 12 note. OTT at 52 pts with 11 expiring deals are in full rebuild. The displayed 90/91 is his reading today; his stored grades are lower, likely mid-80s. He is confirmed, already the active target, and nothing has changed his situation.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 21, 89 base, 91 displayed ovr, 94 pts/54 GP, $1.10M expiring) and **Heatley** (ATL, RW, 23, 91 base, 89 displayed ovr, 87 pts/51 GP, $1.10M expiring) are still on the same club at the same record (19-26-2, 54 pts, 11 expiring). ATL cannot keep both. The old "first-rounder plus Koltsov" package is dead because Toronto own no pick earlier than a fourth (Jan 26 note). Any package must be player-funded: Koltsov plus a roster piece, or Belfour as the over-80 expiring asset in return. Neither fills toughness or faceoffs, but both close the scoring need.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24, 80 base, 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE, $900K, 2 years, 21 pts/57 GP) remains the cheapest re-signable toughness fix. The Jan 25 veto killed the *faceoff* argument for him (he is a wing, so his FACE doesn't change line construction). The toughness case is different and still stands: 91 TOUG at 24 for two years at $900K. CHI at 50 pts with 10 expiring deals. The Jan 30 package was Colaiacovo plus Safronov, and that structure may still work since Eminger fills the slot Colaiacovo leaves.

**Belanger** (LA, C, 27, 82 base, 96 FACE, 73 TOUG, 77 CHKG, $700K expiring, 11 pts/54 GP) is the best pure faceoff man in the league. LA at 54 pts with 13 expiring. At $700K he is the cheapest option who fixes the Sundin insurance problem. The risk is LA fatigue: we are already negotiating Avery from them per the Feb 12 note. Two packages to the same club in the same window may not work.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 23, 87 base, 72 pts/56 GP, $900K expiring) is the natural add-on to a Chara negotiation. Same club, same situation, both expiring, same rebuild. The Jan 19 veto was about the *specific package* that included Eminger, not about Havlat's value. If Chara moves to us, Havlat goes in the same conversation at no extra pick cost.

**Avery** (LA, C, 25, 79 base, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 94 FACE, $400K, 2 years) is in active negotiation. At $400K with 2 years he closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously, but production is near-zero (6 pts/56 GP). He is the cheapest body who fills gaps, not a scorer.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, 29, 89 base, 83 displayed ovr, 95 pts/57 GP, $3.00M expiring) is the highest point total on the board. CHI at 50 pts. But he is 29, expensive at $3.00M, and with no recorded POTE above 86. He is a rental scorer who fills the same role as Kovalchuk at double the cost and without the age upside. I would not pursue him over the ATL targets.

**Sillinger** (PHX, C, 33, 86 base, 92 FACE, 67 TOUG, 68 CHKG, $1.80M expiring, 35 pts/34 GP) is a faceoff alternative to Belanger. PHX at 51 pts. But at 33 with one year left he is a rental with no re-signing path. Belanger at 27 and $700K is the better version of the same product if LA fatigue permits.

**Thornton** (BOS, C, 25, 94 base, 82 TOUG, 83 CHKG, 80 FACE, $4.00M, 0 years, 73 pts/47 GP) remains a wildcard. Contract_years = 0 means he is a UFA this July. BOS at 61 pts is not a clear seller, and $4.00M is the most expensive acquisition possible. POTE 76 means his ceiling is set. I would not build a package around him over Kovalchuk at $1.10M with 94 points.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what concrete packages do we put on the table before late-February negotiations open, and what does each receiving club get for saying yes? Toronto are 92 points and a buyer. The two gaps (toughness, nobody above 71 displayed; faceoffs, only Sundin at 90) demand external fixes, and Belfour walks in July unless moved by March 19.

**Chara to OTT for Klesla plus Upshall plus the 4th.** Chara at 27, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 pts/56 GP, $1.70M expiring is the single best toughness fix available. OTT sits at 52 points with 11 expiring deals and is in a full rebuild. They hoard young potential, and Klesla (22, POTE 97, $0.90M, 2yr, 23 pts/57 GP) plus Upshall (21, POTE 99, $1.20M, 1yr, 17 pts/45 GP) is exactly the shape: two 21-22 year olds with elite upside, combined $2.10M, already playing. The 4th is a token. OTT pays $0.40M more in salary but gains two long-term assets while shedding a 27-year-old they will not re-sign. We go up $0.80M in salary (give $0.90M + $1.20M, receive $1.70M) but fill toughness and checking and top-pair offence in one move. Eminger (POTE 99) and Colaiacovo (POTE 99) stay untouched, which respects the Jan 19 veto. Acceptance is uncertain: OTT might demand a forward as well, and we have nothing to add beyond these two.

**Komisarek to MTL for St. Jacques plus Safronov plus the 4th.** Komisarek at 23, 66 pts/58 GP, 83 TOUG, POTE 90, $1.10M expiring is the best player-to-cost ratio on the board. MTL are 46 points with 14 expiring deals and $17.71M profit. They cannot re-sign everyone. St. Jacques (24, POTE 94, $0.80M, 2yr, 0 GP) and Safronov (23, POTE 91, $0.90M, 3yr, 0 GP) are two defenders at 23-24 who carry nothing on our depth chart. MTL gets two cheap young bodies for their rebuild on total $1.70M; they give $1.10M and get $0.60M of net salary relief plus two POTE 90+ projects. We get a 23-year-old who already produces like a first-pair blueliner and partially fills toughness. Payroll savings of $0.60M for us. The risk is MTL wanting a forward in return, and we have no surplus one to give without cutting into the top nine.

**Belfour to a contender for a draft pick.** Belfour is 39, 92 base, $6.50M, expiring. Luongo (91 base, 25, 2yr) is the starter with 40 GP. Ouellet (23, 1.91 GAA in 9 GP, 2yr) is the backup. Belfour is surplus. The over-80 expiring mechanic trades him for a pick. A contender needing playoff goalie insurance gets a 92-base netminder for the postseason with no long-term cost. He walks in July otherwise and the capital is gone forever. March 19 is the hard deadline. The specific team, the round, and the exact acceptance are uncertain.

**If none land:** the Avery-for-Tucker deal (already in negotiation) still delivers 83 TOUG, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG at $400K on a two-year deal. That is the floor. Without Chara or Komisarek, we enter the playoffs with Avery plus Tucker and Upshall dressed for checking, and accept that the toughness gap narrows but does not close. The Belfour pick recovery is the one that cannot slip; if he walks in July, the club has one fourth-rounder and nothing else.

## Owed

**Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window:** Luongo is on our roster, task complete. DiPietro has improved sharply but the goalie question has changed shape entirely since this monitoring was set up. Here is where each stands.

**Luongo** was the acquisition target; he is now our number one. 92 overall, 91 base, 40 GP, 2.87 GAA, 0.877 SP, $1.60M, 2 years left. The Jan 15 standing order to "fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender" is fulfilled. There is nothing left to monitor on availability because he is ours.

**DiPietro** has transformed since my Feb 6 note. I reported him at 7-12-0, 3.65 GAA. At Feb 13 he is 22-15, 2.97 GAA, 0.871 SP in 40 games. That is a 15-3 stretch in between, which makes him a heater. But two things keep him untradeable: his base is still 79 (the improvement is form, not grade), and NYI sit at 24-24-3, 59 points. They are not sellers and they are not desperate. Even if they were, a 79-base goalie whose value today is form-driven would not command what a 90+ base goalie commands.

**The goalie trade window question has shifted.** It is no longer about who we can acquire; Luongo covers that. It is now about Belfour. He is 21 GP, 18-3, 2.27 GAA, 0.916 SP, 5 shutouts. 91 overall, 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, 39 years old. The over-80 expiring mechanic makes him our largest pick-recovery asset, but no trades after the deadline (March), and he walks in July. The window to extract a pick for him is now, not later.

**No other 90+ base goalie from a clear seller looks realistic.** Lalime at OTT is 90 overall, 92 base, 30 years old, $1.90M, expiring, and OTT are sellers. But we have Luongo. We do not need a second starter. Giguere at ANA is 93 base on UFCA ($800K, 0 years) which means he walks in July regardless, and we would be paying for a rental we do not need.

| Goalie | Base | Ovr | Age | $M | Yrs | Team Pts | Status |
|--------|------|-----|-----|-----|-----|----------|--------|
| Luongo | 91 | 92 | 25 | $1.60 | 2 | 92 (TOR) | Ours |
| Belfour | 92 | 91 | 39 | $6.50 | 1 | 92 (TOR) | Pick-recovery asset |
| DiPietro | 79 | — | 22 | — | — | 59 (NYI) | In form, not for sale |
| Lalime | 92 | 90 | 30 | $1.90 | 1 | 52 (OTT) | Seller, but redundant |

The one decision this monitoring produces is about Belfour: move him before the deadline or lose the pick capital. The goalie acquisition problem is solved.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-13
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-13

Next game vs OTT on Tuesday 15 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the games his talent and production have earned, and the answer splits into three clear groups: those earning their spot, those being wasted, and those not worth forcing.

**Gaborik** at 57 games, 19.6 MPG and 77 points needs no defence. **Klesla** at 57 games and 15.2 MPG is the same story on blue. **Chlup** at 18 is playing 46 games and 14.9 MPG with 35 points; he is past the development stage and into the "start playing him because he is good" stage. **Nash** (44 GP, 13.2 MPG, 32 points) and **Chistov** (43 GP, 13.3 MPG, 16 points) are both on the third line earning their minutes. None of these five needs a change.

**Stahle** is the loudest case. 2 games in 57, POTE 96, age 20. When he does play he gets 17.0 MPG, which tells me the staff sees something in him when he suits up. Two games is not a development plan. OTT is 19-27; this is a night to dress him and give him real minutes.

**Spezza** at 7.5 MPG, 15 points in 37 games (0.41 pts/g), POTE 99, currently scratched. I have raised this repeatedly. The rate has not improved even at low minutes, so the counter-argument is fair: he might not be ready for 12+ yet. But 7.5 MPG is neither a development allocation nor a production role. The GM needs to pick one direction before the season ends and accept the consequences.

**Alexeev** is the one I would promote tonight. 30 points in 55 games at 8.3 MPG is 0.55 pts/g, which is second-line production on fourth-line ice. At 23 with POTE 94 he is at the upper age limit, but 0.55 on 8.3 minutes says he is producing faster than his minutes allow. He is scratched now; against a 19-27 team he should be back in and given 12+ minutes.

**Smirnov** has 0 games and POTE 70. I will say plainly: his ceiling is not compelling enough to disrupt the roster. He is not being wasted the way Stahle is; he is simply not good enough to displace anyone. The GM can keep rotating through others without guilt.

**Safronov** at 23 with 3 games and POTE 91 is the grey zone. The window is closing but he is older, and three games at 13.7 MPG suggests he got a look and the staff did not keep him. I would not force him in.

## Development trends

The question is which young players are actually developing and which are wasting games, and which veterans are starting to walk off the cliff. With 25 games left and a trade deadline approaching, this determines who gets ice, who gets shipped, and what next season's top six looks like.

**Chlup** is the riser of this window. 0.62→0.82 pts/g while minutes climbed from 11.0 to 16.5. He is 18 and producing top-nine numbers from a bottom-six role. He needs power-play time and a step toward the second centre spot. This is the one clear "give him more" on the roster.

**Stahle** finally suited up: 2 GP at 17.0 MPG. That is exactly what I asked for on January 25th. Zero points in two games is expected at 20 in a first appearance. Keep him in the lineup and let the ice accumulate. Safronov also played 3 games at 13.7 MPG, so the development queue is moving.

**Chistov** is a quieter riser: 0.29→0.41 on minutes that went 9.5→15.2. At 21 he is getting closer to the 0.45 range where he becomes a real third-line piece. Let him keep growing here.

**Spezza** at 5.3 MPG and 0.38 pts/g is the same problem for a sixth consecutive reporting period. He is 21, his potential is enormous, and he is watching hockey from the press box. If the GM is unwilling to give him 12+ minutes before the deadline, that tells us this year is already written off for him and next year starts from nothing.

**Spacek** mirrors it: 0.55→0.39 on 16.0→7.6 MPG. He went from a second-line centre to a fourth-liner getting 7.6 shifts a night. At 19, a full year of 7-minute hockey develops nothing.

**Nash** dropped from 0.83 to 0.60 while minutes held at 13.5. The ice did not move, the production did. At 20 this could be fatigue or the season grinding him. It is not alarming yet, but if the rate falls below 0.50 he stops being a second-line piece.

**Eminger** has a recent window of 0.57 pts/g on 17.8 MPG, well above the 0.45 trade threshold I set. His cumulative sits at approximately 0.455. The trend is clearly pointing up. I am pulling back from "sell" language on him. A 21-year-old on an expiring $1.2M producing 0.57 in the recent window is more valuable as a roster piece or a deadline rental at his peak than as a January fire-sale asset.

**Klesla** is falling: 0.50→0.33 on rising minutes (14.6→15.6). At 22 and 57 GP, he should be trending up. 0.33 is third-pair defence numbers and he is taking first-pair shifts.

**McCabe** is a 0.48 recent rate on 21.6 MPG. Four years at $3M with no recovery. My February 12th assessment stands: he is the loudest sell on the blue line.

**Mogilny** went from 1.62 to 0.90. **Sundin** from 1.46 to 0.94. **Roberts** from 1.29 to 0.97. All three are getting more minutes (18.8, 20.5, 20.5 respectively) while scoring significantly less. At 35, 34 and 38 that is the aging curve. They can still finish this season, but next year's top six cannot be built around the same three men producing 0.90 or less. Richards (0.94) and Abid (1.11) are the only ones holding their early-season rate among that group.

**Svehla** is 0.56 in the recent window on 20.7 MPG, down from 0.78 on 23.8. At 36 that is expected decline. The GM values him as the "real MVP" and I accept that, but planning for next season should assume the drop continues.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy; the only player whose morale is meaningfully below the rest is Spezza, and that is not a new problem I can fix with a line move.

**Spezza** sits at 86 (+1) with 7.5 MPG across 37 games. At 21 with POTE 99 and 15 points, he falls in at least the 80s band expecting 17 minutes, maybe higher if his displayed OVR is in the 90s. He has been at 86 for the entire tracked period. I have raised this five times; the GM has chosen to give Chlup (46 GP, 14.9 MPG, 35 pts) the run instead. That is his call. Spezza's 86 is not a crisis, but it will not move up while he sits, and the +1 is noise from a win streak rather than genuine improvement.

**Alexeev** at 92 (=) with 55 GP, 8.3 MPG, and 30 points. Scratched. If his OVR is in the 80s, 8.3 is under target, but 30 points on 8.3 minutes is efficient production and his morale is stable. The GM's rotation of young wings explains the minutes. No action needed.

**Mogilny** at 92 (=) with 18.0 MPG, 65 points in 53 games. A 90-calibre player getting 18 instead of 20 would normally concern me, but he is 35 and producing at 1.23 pts/g. Lower minutes preserve him. Morale at 92 is fine for a veteran whose body is the constraint.

**Chlup** at 92 (=) with 46 GP, 14.9 MPG, 35 points. At 18, on the second line. If his OVR is 80s he wants 17, and 14.9 is close. His production justifies staying put. No change.

Everyone else is 96 and above. The team's recent run (visible in the +3 to +9 morale jumps across the roster) has lifted the room. No one is under their band in a way that creates risk before Tuesday.

## Role composition

**The L4 is the only unit built wrong, and it's partly a roster gap I cannot fix with a lineup card.**

**L1 and P1** are fine. Sundin (88 faceoffs, 90 scoring) centres Gaborik (96 scoring, 99 playmaking) with Roberts (81 checking) and Fischer (81 checking) providing the structure. McCabe adds toughness (71) and a point man. Nothing to adjust.

**L2** is a scoring line with Mogilny (90 scoring, 88 playmaking) and Afinogenov (88 scoring, 89 playmaking). Checking mean 66 is thin, but this is a power line — it's not supposed to be a checking unit. Chlup (77 faceoffs) wins the draws. The structure fits the role.

**L3** is the most balanced line: Richards (91 stamina, 94 clutch, 72 faceoffs) centres Chistov (95 speed) and Nash. Checking mean 70 is adequate. This line can handle third-minute work and contribute offensively.

**L4** is the problem. Abid provides checking 80 and toughness 70 — he's the only real grinder on the line. Koltsov has 98 speed, second-best on the roster, and he's on the fourth line. Spacek is a young centre still developing and playing 8.3 minutes a night. The checking mean of 64 and faceoffs mean of 51 are both poor. This line cannot shut anyone down.

**The fix within the roster is limited.** If Koltsov moves up to L3, who goes down to L4? Nobody else has checking above 80 besides Roberts, McCabe, Fischer, and Abid — all already on upper lines or as D. Moving Nash from L3 to L4 would bring some physicality but removes speed and scoring from the third line. I don't see an arrangement that fixes L4's defensive profile without weakening L2 or L3.

**The roster gap is a bottom-six checking centre.** Spacek is the current one and he's at 8.3 MPG, which means he's neither developing nor contributing. Abid can check but plays wing. Nobody else on this roster wins draws below Chlup and Richards (77 and 72 respectively). Against a team with elite centres at L3 and L4, we simply cannot match.

**Koltsov placement matters less than the gap.** The GM has him as a trading chip. His 98 speed is a selling point; playing him on L4 where he gets limited minutes doesn't showcase him either. But I'm not touching his assignment without the GM's direction on when that trade might close.

## Opponent matchup

This is a maximize-or-develop question dressed as a matchup question, and the answer is that Ottawa does not force any change. They are 19-27-6, score 2.20 per game, and their power play converts at 12.4% (20/161). We are 40-9-4 at home. The only line worth respecting is theirs, and our first line handles it.

**Ottawa's first line.** White at FACE 81, Havlat at 86 with 99 speed and 93 shot power, Alfredsson at 88 with 94 deking. Genuinely good. But our auto-pairing sends Sundin (88 OVR, 88 faceoff, 90 shot accuracy) and Gaborik (95 OVR, 99 speed) against them, plus Roberts checking 84 and balance 91 for the physical battle. Fischer at 88 checking and 91 speed on the matching defensive pair handles Chara's 96 aggressiveness. This matchup is ours on paper.

**Ottawa's depth.** Van Allen at 76 and age 37 with 59 endurance on the second centre, Smith at 77 and Phillips at 76 on their second defensive pair, and a third line at 72-78. Our second line (Chlup 83, Mogilny 87, Afinogenov 83) with Svehla at 82 and Kaberle at 81 on the back end is deeper than theirs. They cannot match us past one line.

**Faceoffs.** White at FACE 81 is their only centre above 72. We hold the advantage on three of four lines against their other centres (Van Allen 70, Fisher 70, Smolinski 61). The faceoff-center-gap I have flagged all season does not bite us this week.

**Power play.** Our first unit converts at 37% (20/54) against a team that lets 2.50 per game. No special unit change needed. Their 12.4% PP means our kill is not tested.

**Goalie.** Luongo at 92 OVR is the start. Ouellet at 80 is the G2 and there is no reason to roll him against a 2.20-per-game team. I cannot confirm his fatigue icon from this view, but his last start on February 7th led to a 1-0-0 result. If he carries a tired icon, Ouellet is the fallback and the game is still winnable.

**No change.** This game does not demand a matchup adjustment. The lines are right, the pairings are right, and the opponent is beatable at full strength without risk. If the GM wants to give Spacek or Koltsov extra shifts for development, this is the night, but that is a separate call with a development reason class. Nothing in Ottawa's makeup requires it.

**Defensive season review (obligation #1).** I cannot update the per-game defensive analysis this activation — no per-game lines exist. I carry forward the February 12th finding: McCabe is the loudest sell at 0.33 pts/g in his recent window against a 0.89 season rate, and Eminger at 0.45 pts/g crossed the trade threshold on February 6th. Both remain sell-able at the deadline unless February recovers them. Fischer, Svehla, Kaberle, and Klesla stay off the list per the GM's standing positions.

## Owed

The defenceman trade analysis hasn't moved since my last delivery on February 12th — no game was played between the two saves, so the numbers are identical. I'll give you the current picture in brief so you have it fresh before Tuesday, but the conclusion is the same.

**McCabe** — 50 points in 57 games = 0.88 season rate, but his recent window (games 50 onward, 2 points in 7 games = 0.29) confirms the collapse I flagged Feb 12. He's 29, locked at $3M for four more years, and the decay is real. Still the loudest sell on the blue line.

**Eminger** — 20 points in 44 games = 0.455. He added 1 point in 2 games since my Feb 6 note, which is neither recovery nor disaster. He's not dressed, which confirms the coaches see him the same way. Expiring $1.2M, age 21. Sell value is low but real; deadline is the window.

**Salo** — 8 points in 24 games = 0.33 at 30 years old on $2.6M for two more years. Lowest production per minute among dressed defencemen. Not as loud as McCabe but the contract makes him expendable.

**Nobody else moves.** Kaberle is your star. Fischer is your keeper. Svehla is your "real MVP." Klesla is 22 at $0.9M with two years left. All stay.

What would change this: McCabe putting up 2+ points in the next two games would at least pause the sell case. Right now it's the same answer as last time because nothing has happened.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-12

Toronto 39-9-4, 90 pts after 56 games.

## Role coverage

Toughness is the only role Toronto are missing outright: zero players at 80+ across 28 skaters, with the ceiling at 73 (Roberts, McCabe). Checking is thin with a free internal fix available today. Faceoffs are one deep when a team needs four.

**Tucker** at 83 CHKG and 29 is in no unit. **Upshall** at 80 CHKG and 21 is also unlined. Dress either or both and checking goes from 6 to 7 or 8 at 80+ without spending a dollar. This is the coach's call and he flagged it himself in the prior report.

**Chlup** at 75 FACE is the best available centre behind Sundin at 90. Richards at 70 handles third-line duty. That still leaves two lines where the team loses the draw, which the coach cannot fix internally. Only Sundin covers at 90+.

**Roberts** (86 CHKG, 38) and **Svehla** (83 CHKG, 36) carry two of the six checking ratings at 80+. In two seasons they are either gone or declining. McCabe at 29 and Fischer at 24 are the only young 80+ checkers left. That is not a gap tonight but it is the gap in 2006-07.

**Mogilny** at 94 scoring and 35 is the top point producer and the oldest. Sundin at 92 and 33 is next. Gaborik at 92 and 22, Afinogenov at 90 and 25 are the future. Scoring transitions cleanly. No acquisition needed for production.

**Abid** carries the only plausible internal toughness fix at base TOUG 80, but the Feb 9 reading puts him below 80+ in the current group. Until that discrepancy resolves, he is not a confirmed answer to the gap.

The acquisition targets that close both toughness and faceoffs in one move remain **Bell** (CHI, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, $900K, 2 years) and **Avery** (LA, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years). Avery is cheaper and closes the faceoff gap better; Bell is the better pure toughness play. Neither has moved since January.

## Trajectory

**Is the club aging into a cliff?** No — the shape is young and the risk is the opposite: a mass expiration that, if handled badly, loses the core for nothing. The real danger is not 2005 or 2006. It is the summer of 2006 when Fischer's $3.70M deal is the fattest remaining non-core contract on a declining player, and the draft capital is still empty because no one moved an expiring veteran in 2005.

**Gaborik** is the single highest-value renewal on the roster: 76 points at 22 on $1.10M expiring this summer. If he walks in July, the club has nothing. He must go on 5 or 6 years. Nash (32 points, 20, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring) and Richards (54 points, 24, POTE 88, $1.00M expiring) sit in the same window. Kaberle (27 points, 26, $1.90M expiring) is the least urgent of the four but still belongs in the same batch.

**The veteran money is the easy part.** Belfour ($6.50M), Svehla ($3.60M), and Roberts ($2.70M) all expire, all carry 80+ overall, and all qualify for the pick-recovery mechanic. Roberts at 63 points in 56 games is painful to lose for a playoff push, but he walks regardless, and Klesla (POTE 97, 56 GP) plus Eminger (POTE 99, 44 GP) fill the gap next season. All three must be moved by the March deadline or the pick capital is lost permanently.

**The age bridge is thin.** Only two players sit between 30 and 33 (Sundin 33, Salo 30). When Mogilny expires in 2006 at $5.50M and Sundin enters his 34th season, there is no generation between the veterans and the 23-and-under core. That gap is acceptable if the young players are locked long-term and developing; it is fatal if they walk or stall. The Coach's reports about Stahle (2 GP at 20, POTE 96), Spezza (37 GP, 5.3 MPG at POTE 99), and Safronov (3 GP) say the young depth is not yet being developed, which means the bridge is thinner than the sheet suggests.

**Money is not the constraint.** Payroll $65.94M against revenue $76.79M leaves $10.85M of headroom before revenue is touched. If the three veterans walk and are replaced by raises for the young core (say Gaborik to $3M, Nash to $2.5M, Richards to $2.5M, Kaberle to $2.5M, Eminger/Colaiacovo/Upshall at $1.5M each), the payroll rises to roughly $72M. That is workable. Fischer at $3.70M through 2008-09 on declining production (26 points, 0.51 pts/g) is the one contract that will become a liability by 2007.

**Draft capital is empty.** One fourth-rounder from TOR, nothing better. Every trade must be funded with players. The only way to rebuild the cupboard is the over-80 expiring mechanic: move Belfour, Svehla, and Roberts before the deadline for picks, and begin accumulating again for 2006.

**Fischer** at 24, $3.70M, 4 years, 26 points, declining production since January, is a 2007-08 problem. No action is possible now; the note stands.

## Calendar

Are we buyers or sellers at the March 19 deadline, and what happens to the 15 expiring contracts this summer? We are sellers of expiring assets only, buyers of nothing, and re-signers of 12 players in July.

**Belfour** is the single deadline action. 92 base, $6.50M, expiring, 39 years old, redundant with Luongo (91 base, 25, 2 years left) in net. He is the only over-80 asset Toronto must move by March 19 or lose the pick capital permanently in July. A contender needing playoff goalie insurance is the counterparty; they get a proven number one, we get draft compensation. Open that conversation late February per the GM's instruction. No urgency before then.

**Svehla** (36, 85 base, $3.60M, expiring) and **Roberts** (38, 87 base, $2.70M, expiring) are both over-80 walkaways who could theoretically fetch a pick the same way. At 36 and 38, neither will be re-signed regardless. The question is whether keeping them through the playoffs (they still dress and log minutes) is worth more than a pick. With 90 points and a first-round bye likely, the marginal playoff value of two veterans is small. If a contender offers a pick for either in the final week of February, take it. If not, let them walk. Do not spend negotiation bandwidth hunting a return for players this far down the lineup when Belfour is the bigger fish.

**Buying**: There is no gap the coach has flagged that a trade fills. The toughness issue has an internal fix (Abid, 80 TOUG/80 CHKG at $400K). The coach wants young players on the ice, not new ones. The roster depth is sufficient. The only buyer move worth watching is a pure rental centre with elite faceoffs — Conroy at CGY (94 FACE, 63 pts, $2.00M expiring from a 40-point team) fits if CGY is desperate by mid-March — but that is a luxury, not a need, and it costs a pick we can use better on Belfour's return.

**The summer**: 12 re-signings, 3 walkaways (Belfour, Svehla, Roberts, who leave by either route).

**Gaborik** (22, 91 base, $1.10M): five to six years. Most important renewal on the roster. He is a first-line winger at 91 base on a min-exempt salary; letting him hit the market is unthinkable. No mid-contract renegotiation is possible in this game, so this is a July 1 priority.

**Nash** (20, $1.20M): five to six years. Core winger. Same logic.

**Eminger** (21, $1.20M): five to six years. The GM protected him over Chara on January 19 because of POTE 99 at age 21. Lock him long.

**Kaberle** (26, $1.90M): five to six years. Top-pairing defenceman, right-handed, 26 years old.

**Richards** (24, $1.00M): five to six years. Centre, 24, cheap, re-signable. The GM put him at third-line centre on January 25; that is a role for someone the club intends to keep.

**Colaiacovo** (22, $1.10M): three to five years. Young defenceman. If not traded at deadline as part of a Belfour package, he gets a renewal offer.

**Chistov** (21, $1.10M): three to five years if kept; trade bait if Belfour's return requires a player.

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M): three to five years. Young, cheap, re-signable.

**Alexeev** (23, $1.10M): two to three years. Depends on production through the spring; not a star lock.

**Abid** (24, $0.40M): two to three years. Depth at $400K, no urgency to pay more.

**Smirnov** (20, $0.40M): three to five years. Project at minimum salary.

**Tellqvist** (25, $0.80M): two to three years. Backup to Luongo. GM protected him on January 15.

**Mogilny** is not expiring. 90 base, $5.50M, 2 years left. He stays. The December 22 package that would have sent him for Jackman is dead — Jackman is not worth trading a 90-overall centre with 2 years of control for, and the package never executed anyway.

## League scan

The question: which players on losing clubs move Toronto closer to winning in 2005 and 2006 simultaneously? The answer comes down to four players who close the toughness gap (zero at 80+ today) with real hockey value attached, and one offensive swing that changes the franchise's ceiling.

**Chara** (OTT, D, 27) at 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 54 points in 56 games, $1.70M expiring from a 52-point club with 11 expiring deals is the best single value in the league right now. He solves toughness and checking from the blue line while producing more points than most top-four D-men. OTT is the clearest seller on the board. The complication: Eminger (POTE 99, 44 GP) and Klesla (POTE 97, 56 GP) already occupy future top-pair minutes, so Chara means Svehla leaves in any scenario, which was always the plan.

**Kovalchuk** (ATL, LW, 21) at 94 points in 54 games on $1.10M expiring is the highest-scoring player available. ATL at 54 points with 11 expiring deals cannot retain him. If re-signed he goes to 5+ years at $3-4M and sits beside Gaborik (76 pts, 22) for half a decade. The binary with Heatley (87 pts, 23, same club, same deal structure) means ATL will only move one. Toronto should pursue Kovalchuk first; his age and scoring rate are better.

**Thornton** (BOS, C, 25) at 92 overall, 94 base, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 73 points in 47 games, $4M expiring is the most complete player on the board. He closes toughness and checking in one move at centre. The obstacle: BOS at 60 points with $30.32M profit has no urgency, and 13 expiring deals means they have other things to move first. Acceptance is uncertain without a large package. Toronto cannot fund this without stripping depth.

**Bell** (CHI, C, 24) at 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 80 base, $900K with 2 years left is the cheapest player closing all three structural gaps. Only 20 points, but he is not bought for scoring. CHI at 50 points with 10 expiring deals is a seller. At $900K and 2 years, he is low-risk and controllable.

**Conroy** (CGY, C, 33) at 94 FACE and 68 points in 56 games, $2.00M expiring from a 44-point club is the best pure faceoff rental. CGY has nothing to play for and 10 expiring deals. He covers the faceoff gap for the playoff push at the cost of a 3rd/4th-liner we don't keep long-term.

**Avery** (LA, C, 24) at 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K, 2 years, 6 points is the cheapest faceoff fix in the league. The production is almost nil but at $400K and 24 with 2 years left, he is a depth piece that costs nothing and covers a gap for four seasons. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring deals will take almost anything.

I am not pursuing Brashear ($2.10M, 33, 2 years, $8 points) or Domi (ANA at 67 points is not a seller). McCarthy at 32 with 3 points has toughness but no hockey value beyond fighting.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: what concrete packages can Toronto put together right now to close the toughness gap and add playoff depth, and why would each other club say yes? Today is February 12; the GM's standing order is that negotiations open in late February, so these are targets to have ready, not deals to strike this week.

**Bell** is the priority. He closes toughness (95 TOUG on the Jan 25 stored read), checking (93 CHKG) and faceoffs (87 FACE) in one move at $900K with two years of control. He is the only available player who does all three. The restructured price is Colaiacovo plus Safronov: no R2 exists, Eminger and Klesla are untouchable per the GM's veto and the coverage phase respectively, and Colaiacovo at 22 is the most expendable of our three young defensemen. Chicago at 50 points with 10 expiring deals and $26M profit are sellers; they get two blueliners aged 22 and 23 with POTE 99 and POTE 91, which rebuilds their future blue line while they collect nothing of value from Bell's 20 points. Acceptance is uncertain, but the hockey logic is clean on both sides.

**Conroy** is a rental that fills the faceoff hole for the playoffs. At 94 FACE and 68 points in 56 games on $2.00M expiring, he gives Toronto a second center who wins the draw, which only Sundin does today. The cost is Chistov (21, 16 points, $1.10M, POTE 95, expiring) plus our only pick, the fourth-rounder. Calgary at 44 points with 10 expiring deals and nothing to play for get a young forward with upside and a draft slot. The drawback: this is a straight rental, and after the season we have Conroy gone and the fourth-rounder gone, leaving the draft cupboard truly empty. Only worth it if the GM believes the Cup run needs him.

**Avery** is the cheapest gap-closer in the league: 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at $400K with two years left. His 6 points say he is not a scorer, but at that price he is a four-year depth piece that costs nothing. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring deals are the most motivated sellers in the league. The return is Tucker: 29, $1.30M with two years left, CHKG 92 and TOUG 88, in no unit. LA get a veteran checker for a blueliner they lost to injuries; we offload an unused contract. Avery alone does not justify the ask, so the GM should try pairing him with Belanger (LA, 90 FACE, 82 base, $700K expiring, from the January target list) if LA will bundle two centers.

If none of these land, the fallback is pick recovery: Svehla (36, 83 base, $3.60M, 83 CHKG, expiring) and Roberts (38, 84 base, $2.70M, 63 points, expiring) to a contender for a second or third-rounder each via the over-80 expiring mechanic. Both walk in July regardless. Every week they sit is a week the pick capital is not rebuilt. Belfour ($6.50M expiring) is the same class of asset but must move by the trade deadline; no trades after March 19. These three should be the GM's first calls when negotiations open.

## Owed

**#2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.** This task is complete and the goalie trade window has been used. Luongo is on our roster and DiPietro was ruled out as a target back on February 6.

**Luongo** arrived and is now showing 93 overall, 40 GP, $1.60M, 2 years remaining. Since the February 7 finding he has added roughly 7 starts. The Jan 15 mandate to "fetch a really good high-90s goalie" is fulfilled; no further monitoring is needed.

**DiPietro** was checked at 79 base / POTE 99, producing 7-12-0 with a 3.65 GAA. Potential has not translated and NYI will re-sign rather than deal. Ruled out on February 6, nothing has changed.

The remaining live item from this thread is the Belfour decision (92 base, 39, $6.50M expiring, 21 GP). That is tracked under the pick-recovery findings and is a separate deadline question, not a monitoring task.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-12
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-12

Next game at CHI on Saturday 12 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: are our young players getting the games they've earned? At 56 games deep with 26 to play, the window for development is closing fast. Most are fine; two are not.

**Chlup** is the good news. 18 years old, 45 games, 14.7 minutes a night on the second line, 32 points (0.71 pts/g). Morale at 92. He's getting everything he's earned and more. Nothing to fix.

**Gaborik** at 56 games, 19.6 MPG, 76 points (1.36 pts/g) needs no development discussion. He's our best player at 22.

**Klesla** has played every single game at 22, 15.3 MPG. That's exactly what a young defenceman needs. On track.

**Nash** is at 43 games, 13.2 MPG, 32 points (0.74 pts/g) on the third line. Getting his chance and producing. Fine.

**Chistov** at 42 games and 13.4 MPG is a reasonable development load for a 21-year-old on the third line. Producing at 0.38, which is depth-level, but he's learning at a pace that won't hurt him.

**Spacek** sits in the GM's rotation philosophy. 33 games, 10.6 MPG, 0.45 pts/g at 19. The GM scratched him deliberately on January 15th to make room for others. Last recommendation about him went unacted. He's getting some games but not enough at 19 to consolidate. I'd like him at 12+ on nights we can afford it.

**Spezza** is the problem I keep raising and nothing has moved. 37 games, 7.5 MPG, 15 points (0.41 pts/g) at 21 with the highest scouting number on the roster. His minutes have fallen again from the January reading. At 21, a year at 7.5 MPG teaches him nothing. I've raised this six times with no movement. I understand the rotation philosophy, but the rotation philosophy is designed for players like Smirnov and Safronov who need a cup of coffee. Spezza is the most talented forward on this roster who isn't in the top six, and he's sitting on the bench.

**Stahle** has played 2 games in 56. At 20, with the same scouting number as Eminger, and Klesla playing every night at 22, Stahle is being starved. His 2 games averaged 17 minutes, so when he plays he's trusted. He just doesn't play.

**Safronov** at 3 games in 56 is a similar issue but less urgent; he's 23, not 20. **Smirnov** at zero games is also nothing, but his scouting number is 70, the lowest of the group, so less to salvage.

**Upshall** is producing at 0.38 pts/g on 10.7 MPG at 21. That's a fourth-line rate on fourth-line minutes. He's getting what he's earned. No promotion warranted.

**Alexeev** at 55 games but only 8.3 MPG is a curious case. 30 points at 0.55 pts/g is solid production for an 8-minute role, but at 23 he should be closer to 10. Not urgent, but worth watching.

## Development trends

Development trends from December to February tell us who to build around and who to plan around by next October. The answer splits clean: two 18- and 21-year-olds are ascending into real roles, a cluster of young players are going backwards despite being rostered, and four veterans are showing clear age decline that changes next season's math.

**Chlup** at 18 is the standout. Rate went from 0.62 to 0.75 while minutes rose from 11.0 to 16.2. He is the only player on the roster whose production climbed alongside his ice time. At 18, a 0.75 recent rate on 16 minutes is second-line centre production. He is ready for more.

**Chistov** is the other riser: 0.29→0.43 on minutes from 9.5→15.3. Same pattern as Chlup, rate up and minutes up, just one step behind. Both are 21 or under and both are telling you they belong on a better line than the one they are on.

**Eminger** is the one that changes a decision. His early-season rate was 0.35 over 23 games. His recent 21 games produce 0.57. The season rate sits at 0.45, right at the trade threshold I set on February 6th. The recent window suggests he has recovered. The GM should consider keeping him rather than selling a player who is ascending at 21 on a cheap deal.

**Spezza** at 21 with POTE 99: recent rate 0.38 on 5.3 minutes a night. I have raised this six times. The pattern is unchanged and the trend is still negative. I will not raise it again. If the GM does not give him 12 minutes before the season ends, the year is written off.

**Koltsov** collapsed from 1.10 in 10 early games to 0.32 in the 22 games since. His trade value has cratered with his production. The GM is keeping him as a chip, but there is very little left on the chip to trade.

**Spacek** went from 0.55 on 16.0 minutes to 0.41 on 7.9 minutes. Rate and role both collapsed. At 19 this could be recovery next training camp, but February's minutes confirm the GM's rotation philosophy has cost him real development this year.

**Klesla** at 22 dropped from 0.50 to 0.34. Colaiacovo at 22 slid from 0.44 to 0.38. Neither should be going backwards at that age. These are not crises but they matter for next season's blue-line depth.

**Fischer** is the one to plan around. 0.44 recent on 21.8 minutes, down from 0.63. He carries four years left. The GM rightly protects him, but a four-year deal for a player trending down at 24 is a structural risk.

**Kaberle** is the keeper confirmed: 0.54→0.58, minutes 19.4→22.4. The only defenceman whose rate and minutes both climbed.

Among the veterans, **Sundin** at 33 moved from 1.46 to 0.97 while minutes rose from 16.9 to 20.4. **Mogilny** at 35 went from 1.62 to 0.89. **Roberts** at 38 went from 1.29 to 1.00 on minutes up from 16.5 to 20.3. All three are taking more ice and producing less. Next season's top nine has to be younger.

**McCabe** at 29: 1.42 early, 0.50 since. At 29 with no age excuse, this slump is either fixable or it is who he is now. The top pair next season should be Kaberle and Eminger if Eminger holds.

## Morale watch

**The room is healthy; the only minutes problem is Spezza, and it is not a morale problem yet.**

**Spezza** sits at 86, down from the mid-90s the room carried in January, on 7.5 MPG as a 21-year-old first-round-calibre centre (POTE 99). His band is 17 minutes a night. He is getting half of it. The drop is small so far and the results are holding his spirits up, but this is the one morale clock on the roster that is running. I have asked five times; the GM's rotation philosophy is the answer, and it is deliberate. I raise it once more, not as a crisis.

**Stahle** (94, 2 games, 17 MPG in them) and **Safronov** (95, 3 games) and **Ouellet** (96, 8 games as backup) all slipped 5-7 points in the recent window because they sit most nights. That is the cost of the GM's development rotation and it is the right cost against weak opposition, but it is why none of these three will dress in Chicago. Their morale is a result of not playing, not of the building or the record.

**Luongo** is at 99 on 61 MPG a night, exactly his band, and Belfour at 99 on 58 is the same. No goalie issue.

**Richards** at 99 is 17.2 MPG at 24, bang on his band. **Nash** at 99 is 13.2 at 20 on the third line, slightly under but his production (32 points) says this is his role. **Mogilny** at 92 is 17.9 at 35, right where a very good veteran belongs. Everyone else dressed sits inside their band.

No line change is warranted on morale grounds. Spezza is the flag I keep waving; the rest of the room is fine.

## Role composition

The question is whether these units are built for their jobs and whether the roster can staff every role. The short answer: the top three lines, both power plays, and both kills are sensible. The fourth line has an identity problem, but it's a roster gap, not an arrangement error I can fix by shuffling names.

**L1 through L3** are built right. L1 pairs Gaborik's 96 scoring and 99 playmaking with Roberts (81 checking), McCabe (81 checking) and Fischer (81 checking) for balance. L2 leans on Mogilny (90 scoring, 91 speed) and Afinogenov (88 scoring) with Chlup winning 77% of draws and Svehla anchoring the blue line at 83 checking. L3 has Richards (72 checking, 94 stamina, 94 clutch) as the engine and Chistov's 95 speed to break out. Nothing wrong with any of these.

**P1** puts Sundin and Kaberle as quarterback/point with Gaborik in shooting position and Roberts/McCabe for net-front traffic. That's a textbook setup. **P2** is Mogilny shooting with Richards at 72 faceoffs to win entries. Both fine.

**K1** has three 81-checking defenders (Roberts, Fischer, Svehla) around Sundin. **K2** has McCabe (81 checking, 71 toughness) and Chlup (77 checking). Both kills are properly staffed with checking bodies.

**L4 (Spacek, Koltsov, Abid)** is the odd one. Checking mean 64, toughness mean 59, faceoff mean 51. This is supposed to be the energy line but Koltsov is a 98-speed player and Spacek is a developing forward. Abid (80 checking, 70 toughness) is doing all the defensive work alone. However, L4 has no paired D and plays against the opponent's fourth line, so 64 checking is probably adequate for the matchup it actually gets. The identity is confused on paper but the minutes are manageable.

**Faceoff depth** is the structural gap. Sundin (88), Chlup (77), Roberts (73), Richards (72). That's it. Nobody behind Richards wins a draw at a meaningful rate. If either Sundin or Chlup goes down, we have no answer in the circle.

**Toughness ceiling** is low across the roster. McCabe 71, Roberts 70, Abid 70, Fischer 69. Nobody above 71. We have checking but not intimidation. No opponent's tough forward needs to worry about our guys making him pay.

**D audit (obligation #1):** Eminger crossed the 0.45 pts/g trade threshold on February 6th (19 points in 42 games). He's 21, on an expiring $1.2M deal, and he is not on any line this week. He is sellable at the deadline. McCabe's recent window shows 0.50 pts/g against a 1.42 season rate, which at 29 is a decline, not a cold streak. He stays for now but the top pair belongs to Eminger's replacement next season, not to McCabe.

## Opponent matchup

**The question:** This is a 50-point team, 18-27-8. Do we go all out or use it for development? Per the GM's standing order, development applies in games we can afford, and this is one we can afford. The current lineup already has young players in every line (Chlup on the second, Nash and Chistov on the third, Spacek on the fourth, Klesla on the third D pair). No structural change is needed.

**Chicago's top line** — Daze (87 OVR), Zhamnov (85), Sullivan (85) — is their only real threat. Zhamnov has CHKG 57 and SPEE 90 but no speed to burn; Fischer's SPEE 91 and CHKG 88 handle him. Auto-pairing puts Fischer-McCabe against them, which is correct.

**Fleury** at 86 on their second line is the other problem, but Svehla (CHKG 83) is the right body for it, and Bell (CHKG 93, TOUG 95) on that line means we want a physical D pair there. Svehla-Kaberle work.

**Their defense** is thin: McCarthy at 77 is their best, and the rest are 70-75. Our top PP (38.5%) should eat alive against that group. No PP adjustment needed.

**Their PP is 22/175** — 12.6%, bottom of the league. Our kill units can relax tonight.

**Goalie:** Luongo at 93 OVR should start. Easy opponent, 25 years old, needs the work. Check Belfour's fatigue icon as standard procedure but no reason to override the G1 slot.

**Spacek** is already on the fourth line with Abid and Koltsov. If we're up by two in the third, give him extended shifts — this is the kind of game where a 19-year-old gets 12+ minutes without consequence. That's an in-game decision for the GM, not a lineup change.

## Owed

**Standing job #1: defenceman analysis and trade candidates.** Here is where things stand for Chicago night.

**McCabe** continues to cool. He was at 48 points in 50 games on Jan 26 (0.96 pts/g); he is now at 50 in 56, meaning 2 points in his last 6 games (0.33 pts/g). Season rate has slipped to 0.89 and the trajectory is clearly downward. At 29 with $3.0M for four more years, this is the loudest sell on our blue line. He is still good tonight (82 OVR, 99 morale, 22.4 MPG), but his window to fetch a real return is closing.

**Eminger** has not moved since Feb 6. He was 19 in 42 then, now 20 in 44 (0.45 pts/g), with 1 point in his last 2 games. The recovery the threshold was waiting for never materialized. 75 OVR, $1.2M expiring, age 21. The sell-at-deadline call stands unchanged.

**Colaiacovo** is quietly the same case at a lower profile: 12 points in 30 games (0.40 pts/g), 71 OVR, $1.1M x1 year expiring, age 22. Teams paying deadline prices for depth blueliners would take him. We have Salo (81 OVR) and Klesla ahead of him on the depth chart.

**Fischer** is stable at 0.51 pts/g on 21.4 MPG, 83 OVR. GM's keeper, not moving. No new information.

**Klesla** has not scored a point since late January (23 in 56, 0.41 pts/g, 56 straight games). Reliable, cheap, not going anywhere.

**Kaberle** at 27 in 48 (0.56 pts/g) remains the keeper the GM declared on Jan 15.

**Stahle** got his third game of the season somewhere between Jan 25 and now (brief shows 2 GP, same as then). Still not getting dressed. The Jan 25 finding on wasted development still stands.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09

Toronto 39-9-4, 88 pts after 55 games.

## Role coverage

The roster covers scoring, speed, playmaking, and depth at 80+ across most roles, but toughness and faceoffs are structural holes the coach cannot plug with current personnel, and the age curve at the top of scoring means this problem gets worse by next October.

**Roberts** at 73 TOUG and **McCabe** at 73 are the ceiling on the roster. That is 17 points below Bell's 91 displayed today. A fourth line needs one player at 85+ TOUG to exist as a physical unit; nobody here is close. Tucker's 83 CHKG is useful but his 70 TOUG means he gets out-muscled along the boards by a real enforcer line.

**Abid** was dressed on Feb 6 at the coach's request, and his base grades in our records read TOUG 80 and CHKG 80, but he does not appear in the current 80+ toughness group. Either his displayed grades are below 80 today due to form, or the recorded base was inflated by a reading we cannot confirm now. If he is genuinely at 80 stored and the coach is running him nightly, he partially closes the gap at $400K with zero trade cost. The GM should check his number next screen and confirm before spending capital on Bell.

**Richards** at 70 FACE is the second-best draw man after Sundin's 90. Chlup at 75 and age 18 is the best prospect at the dot. Neither gets a fourth line above 55% on draws. The Coach's complaint about fourth-line faceoffs is a roster problem, not a deployment problem.

**Bell** at 80 base with displayed grades of 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, and 83 FACE is the cleanest single acquisition that fixes both gaps. At $900K and 2 years left, he is cheap enough to absorb and young enough at 24 to be a keeper rather than a rental. The package is Colaiacovo plus Safronov; Toronto own no pick better than a fourth. Acceptance is uncertain because CHI are profitable at $26M and will want more for a first-round-centre-grade player, but his displayed grades on a neutral day will be lower than 91, which makes him less attractive to a buyer in February.

**Avery** at 79 base with FACE 94, CHKG 88, TOUG 83, $400K and 2 years is cheaper and better at draws. His liabilities are ENDU 50 and PENA 93: he gasses in 12 minutes and takes penalties at an elite rate. He fixes faceoffs outright and toughness to a degree, but the penalty rate makes him a liability on the PK and a risk of giving up power plays on a contending team.

**Mogilny** at 35, **Sundin** at 33, and **Roberts** at 38 carry the top of the scoring chart. Gaborik (22) and Afinogenov (25) are the young core, but the gap between those two and the next scorer down (Richards at 85) means the team is aging into a scoring problem. Bell's 83 TOUG would at least mean the physical burden falls on him rather than Roberts.

**Ouellet** at 23 with a 1.88 GAA and 0.918 SV in 8 games is the best goalie per-minute on the roster and the third stringer. Luongo has locked the top job for two years. The Coach is right: Ouellet needs to be moved if a deal appears. He is a trade chip at 2 years and $900K with POTE 97.

## Trajectory

Is this club aging into a cliff, and is its money arranged sensibly? The age shape is fine — 16 players aged 23 or under — but the money structure is not. Four players aged 34 or older carry $18.30M in combined salary, Sundin locks another $8.40M for five more years at 33, and every core young player on a one-year deal comes up in the same July. Profit at $22.35M means the club can afford the rebuild. The problem is timing and structure.

**The July cluster** hits 15 contracts worth $25.30M. Six are core: Gaborik ($1.10M, 75 pts), Richards ($1.00M, 54 pts), Nash ($1.20M, 32 pts), Eminger ($1.20M, POTE 99), Abid ($0.40M, 63 pts), Kaberle ($1.90M, 27 pts). Current total on those six is $6.80M. On new five-to-six-year deals they will command $15–22M. That is the payroll jump, and it is the right jump to make.

**Sundin** is the hardest contract to fix. 33, $8.40M, five years remaining, POTE 60. Still producing 63 points in 55 games, but he turns 38 when this deal expires. By 2007-08 he costs 12.7% of today's payroll as a 36-year-old. His trade value is highest now and drops every season. The over-80 expiring mechanic does not apply because his deal runs through 2009-10. The window to move him is summer 2005 or summer 2006, and a straight hockey trade is the only route.

**Belfour** at 39, 92 base, $6.50M, one year left is the club's cleanest asset right now. He qualifies for the over-80 expiring mechanic, should be moved before March for a draft pick, and frees $6.50M. That recovers the only meaningful pick capital the club holds beyond a fourth-rounder. Luongo (25, 91 base, POTE 97, $1.60M, two years) is the number-one goalie.
