The Luongo and DiPietro monitoring task the GM asked for on January 19 is complete; Luongo is on the roster and DiPietro's numbers no longer matter.

**The 30–33 bridge is empty.** Only Sundin (33) and Salo (30) sit in that age band. When Mogilny (35), Roberts (38) and Svehla (36) leave after this summer, the bridge to the young core is Richards at 29, Abid at 29, McCabe at 33 and Tucker at 33. That is four players and two are scratched. Locking Richards and Abid on long deals is what holds the structure together.

**Mogilny** at 35, $5.50M, two years left, POTE 55 is the worst long-term money on the roster. He carries 62 points now, but by 2006-07 he will be 37 on $5.50M. The contract runs to summer 2007 and cannot be renegotiated mid-deal. Ride it out, budget the gap.

**Fischer** at 24, $3.70M, four years remaining is the next Sundin-shaped problem. 25 points in 50 games, declining from 0.63 to 0.41 points per game. Four years means no expiring leverage. Not actionable until he has two years left and can be moved as trade bait.

**Svehla** at 36, $3.60M, scratched, POTE 55 should walk this summer. **Roberts** at 38, $2.70M, 62 points, POTE 52 is a tough call — the production is real, but 38 with POTE 52 is a one-year rental in every sense. Either release him or use the over-80 expiring mechanic for a pick if the market accepts.

**Chlup** at 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95, 31 points in 44 games is the next contract cliff after this summer. His deal expires in 2006 when he turns 19 or 20. Mid-contract renegotiation is impossible under this game's rules, so his price rises before we can act. That is a structural cost, not a management error. Plan the 5-6 year lock for summer 2006.

**Draft capital is gone.** One fourth-rounder from Toronto. The Luongo deal spent the first-rounder. Every acquisition must be funded by players. Belfour's over-80 expiring trade is the pick-recovery play. If it fails, the club enters 2005-06 with nothing worth packaging.

Three moves protect the next three seasons. Lock Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger and Abid on five-to-six-year deals this July — that secures the core and the bridge. Trade Belfour for a pick before March, recovering draft capital and freeing $6.50M. Begin looking for a Sundin trade in summer 2005 while he still carries 63 points and buyers believe it lasts.

## Calendar

**The deadline is 38 days away and we have no reason to be at it; the summer is where the money gets made.** Toronto lead the East by 17 points on 88, own the deepest roster in the conference, and carry only a fourth-rounder as a tradeable pick. There is nothing at the deadline we need that we do not already have, and nothing we can offer a seller that does not cost us a playoff player. The manual's "roster is already strong, do nothing" applies.

**Abid** at 79 base, $400K, and 24 is the coach's toughness answer and he is already on the roster. The coach's report from February 7 says no player carries toughness above 69; Abid's base TOUG is 80 and his CHKG is 80 per January 25 scouting. Either the coach is reading a form-affected displayed grade or he has not checked the sheet since before the trade. This is a lineup problem, not a trade problem, and it does not require 38 more days of window-shopping.

**Belfour** at 92 base, 39, $6.50M, expiring is the single largest pick-recovery asset on the roster. Luongo at 91 base, 25, $1.60M with 2 years is the number one and the standing order from January 15 is fulfilled. Belfour should be kept through the playoffs as insurance — Ouellet at 80 base and Tellqvist at 77 base are thin for a Cup run — then moved in July using the over-80 expiring mechanic. A first- or second-round pick is the realistic return. The same logic applies to **Svehla** (85 base, 36, $3.60M) and **Roberts** (87 base, 38, $2.70M): both are above 80, both are too old to re-sign, both are surplus to our depth chart (we carry eight defensemen and eleven forwards). Moving all three recovers 3–4 picks for a front office that currently owns one fourth-rounder.

## League scan

Which players across the league close Toronto's two structural gaps — toughness and fourth-line faceoffs — and which clubs are positioned to say yes? The answer determines what the GM builds into the late-February negotiation window, and the March deadline behind it.

**Bell** is the #1 target. 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG at 24 on $900K with two years left. CHI at 48 points, 10 expiring, $23.59M profit means they are selling and can afford to take salary back. He is a wing, not a centre, so his 83 FACE does not fix the faceoff gap — that was correctly identified in January. His value is toughness and checking on a top-four minute, and he is the only available player above 90 in both who is young enough to keep. The GM's proposed package (Colaiacovo plus Safronov) is the starting point. Acceptance is uncertain because CHI at $39.27M payroll and $23.59M profit have no salary pressure and may want more than two prospects for a 24-year-old with those physical grades.

**Jackman** is the value play. 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG at 23 on $700K with three years left, 26 points in 53 games from the blue line. STL at 48 points, 9 expiring, $14.63M profit. This is the Chara-type body the GM prefers at a younger age with a longer deal, which respects the January veto on Chara specifically. Three years at $700K means he is still cheap when Eminger is ready, and 26 points at 23 means he plays now. If STL engage, this is the single best value on the board for toughness.

**Avery** is the faceoff fix. 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG at 24 on $400K with two years left. A centre who wins draws and hits. His production is ugly — 6 points in 54 games — and the penalty grade (PENA 93) means he will take minors at an elite rate. He is not a top-six player; he is a fourth-line centre who fixes the draw problem immediately. At $400K for two years, the cost of being wrong is negligible. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring and $17.16M profit are selling everything.

**Conroy** is the best pure rental centre. 93 FACE, 67 points in 55 games at 33, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 44 points, 10 expiring, $15.80M profit. He does not close toughness (60 TOUG) but he closes the faceoff gap and adds real scoring in one move. The cost is Chistov plus a 4th — both assets the trajectory phase says the club does not plan to keep. The issue is rental risk: he is 33 with one year, and unless we extend him (which we cannot do mid-contract), he walks in July. If the coach believes Conroy elevates the playoff run, this is the deal. If the priority is roster building, skip it and take Avery at the same cost with two years remaining.

**Cammalleri and Frolov** together are the five-year solution LA is most likely to deal. Both at 22, POTE 98 and 96, on $1.10M expiring deals. Combined: 76 points in 67 games together, both under 1.2 points per game. They do not address toughness or faceoffs, but they fill two top-six spots for half a decade. LA at 54 points with 13 expiring cannot keep both. The package must be substantial — Koltsov plus Chistov plus Ouellet is the depth available without touching the core. The question is whether LA accept prospects with unrealized potential over a proven lineup piece.

**Chara** remains on the board at 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 54 points in 55 games from the blue line, 27, $1.70M expiring. The GM vetoed him in January for Eminger's timeline, and that position is sound. But his production has climbed since that conversation — 54 points at 27 is a number-one-pairing output. If a deal can be constructed that costs less than the original Chara+Havlat package the GM killed, it is worth revisiting. I will not re-propose the same package.

**Regehr** (CGY, D, 24) at 84 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $1.26M with three years left and 24 points in 40 games is the next-best tough young D after Jackman. CGY at 44 points, 10 expiring. Same logic as Jackman but slightly more expensive and less productive.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, 29) at 83 overall, 92 points in 54 games, $3.00M expiring is the second-highest scorer available. He does not address either gap. At 29 with an expiring deal, he is a rental with no re-signing upside unless production convinces us to extend. The coach's gaps are physical, not scoring. Daze is not the priority.

The ordering for late February: pursue Bell first (structural fix, keeper). Pursue Jackman second (value, young, long deal). Avery or Conroy third depending on whether the GM wants a keeper at 24 or production now at 33. Cammalleri plus Frolov as a parallel conversation if LA respond positively to a prospect package.

## Trade construction

Which packages both sides can actually sign for the toughness and faceoff gaps, ranked by the chance they close? Three proposals below, each funded by players the coverage phase confirms are not toughness contributors, so giving them costs nothing in the coach's area of need. Negotiations open late February per the GM's standing order; these are the proposals to take into the room.

**Bell from Chicago, package one.** We give Colaiacovo (D, 22, $1.10M, 1yr, POTE 99, 12 pts in 30 GP) and Safronov (D, 23, $0.90M, 3yr, POTE 91, 3 GP). We get Bell (C, 24, $900K, 2yr, displayed 91 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 83 FACE). Net payroll: we shed $1.10M. Chicago gain a 22-year-old with POTE 99 on a one-year deal they can flip or develop, and their $23.59M profit means the salary swing is noise. They are at 48 points with 10 expiring — full sell. The risk: Bell's base overall is 80, not 91. The displayed grades are inflated by current form. Chicago may read the same base we do and want a third piece. Start at two-for-one, be prepared to add St. Jacques (D, 24, $0.80M, 2yr, 0 GP) if they push.

**Jackman from St. Louis, package two.** We give Koltsov (LW, 23, $1.10M, 2yr, POTE 94, 18 pts in 31 GP, 96 ACCE) and St. Jacques (D, 24, $0.80M, 2yr, POTE 94, 0 GP). We get Jackman (D, 23, $700K, 3yr, 86 TOUG, 87 CHKG, 26 pts in 53 GP). Net payroll: we shed $1.20M. STL are at 48 points with 9 expiring and $14.63M profit, in a sell posture. Koltsov gives them a 23-year-old with 96 acceleration and 94 potential — a real rebuilding asset. Jackman's three years at $700K means he is still cheap when Eminger steps up, and his 26 points from the blue line mean he plays tonight. This is the best value on the board: 86/87 physical grades at 23 on a three-year deal below $700K.

**Avery from Los Angeles, package three.** We give Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M, 1yr, POTE 95, 16 pts in 41 GP, 89 SPEE) and our fourth-round pick. We get Avery (C, 24, $400K, 2yr, 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG). Net payroll: we shed $0.70M. LA are at 54 points with 13 expiring and $17.16M profit — every available asset is on the block. Avery's 6 points in 54 games makes him a replaceable depth centre for them, while Chistov at 89 speed and POTE 95 is a young player with upside LA can develop. This fixes the fourth-line faceoff gap outright at the lowest cost of the three proposals. The liabilities are real: PENA 93 means he takes minors at an elite rate, and ENDU 50 caps him at 12 minutes. He is a fourth-line centre who wins draws and hits, not a top-six player. At $400K for two years, the cost of being wrong is negligible.

**Belfour runs as a parallel action.** The over-80 expiring mechanic means he can move for a draft pick without a hockey trade. He does not close a gap, but he recovers the only pick capital Toronto hold beyond a fourth-rounder and frees $6.50M. Identify a contender with a goalie need and propose the one-way deal separately.

**If none land.** Dress Abid nightly on the bottom six and accept his displayed toughness is what it is. The coach reports nobody above 69 TOUG on the roster, which means Abid's recorded base of 80 has not held into February. Check his number next screen. If he reads below 75 displayed, the gap is real and unfixable internally, and the March deadline becomes the last chance before next season.

## Owed

**Goalie trade window monitoring (task #2):** This task is complete. Luongo is on the roster and the mandate from January 15 is fulfilled; DiPietro has not become a trade candidate despite his production rebound.

**Luongo** is at 39 GP on Toronto's roster, 92 displayed (91 base), $1.60M with 2 years left. The monitoring job he was set to track arrival and early performance is done. He has played two more games since the February 7 snapshot. No availability question remains because there is nothing to be available for.

**DiPietro** has the most interesting movement: he went from 7-12-0, 3.65 GAA (early season, per the Feb 6 note) to 22-15-0, 111 GA in 2,245 minutes, which is a 2.97 GAA across 40 starts. His base overall remains 79, unchanged from every snapshot. His displayed overall is 84, meaning he is riding a form cycle, not development. NYI will try to re-sign a goalie who just posted a sub-3.00 GAA at $1.10M. He remains off the acquisition list.

**Turco** is the one new finding worth flagging. He sits at DAL, 94 base, displaying 96 today, $600K with 1 year remaining. That is an elite goalie on an expiring bargain from a club whose record I cannot confirm from the brief. If Luongo's development ever stalls or a playoff injury exposes depth, Turco is the cheapest elite option in the league. This is not actionable now but it is the only goalie who fits the "high-90s from a non-contender" profile with real money attached.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-09

Next game vs EDM on Friday 11 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question this phase answers: which of our 16 players aged 23 or under is getting the games his age and potential warrant, and which is not? With nobody currently injured, every scratch is a choice, so the answer is clean.

**Stahle** is the loudest problem. POTE 96, 20 years old, 2 games in 55. He played 17 minutes in those two appearances, so the coaching staff trusted him when they needed a body, then put him back in the press box. This is the biggest development waste on the roster and it has been going since October. He needs to be in the dressings every night from here to the deadline, even if it means sitting Colaiacovo. At 22 with POTE 99, Colaiacovo has already shown he can handle 18.1 MPG in 30 games. Stahle needs the reps more.

**Spezza** — I have raised this five times and nothing has moved, so I am raising it a sixth. POTE 99, age 21, 7.5 MPG in 37 games, currently scratched. He is 15 points in 37 games, which is 0.41 per game. That is not a player who has beaten out a job, but it is also not a player you sit at 21 when his scouting number is the highest on the roster. The fourth line is his to win. If the answer is he is not good enough yet, then POTE 99 is a number nobody is testing.

**Smirnov** — zero games in 55 at age 20. POTE 70 is modest, and I will not pretend he belongs on a line. But zero games means zero information. The GM's rotation philosophy is about giving young players a chance. Smirnov has had no chance. A ten-game stretch on the fourth line tells us something. Twenty-six more games of scratch tells us nothing.

**Safronov** — 3 games in 55 at 23 with POTE 91. Less urgent than Stahle because he is older, but same pattern: the scouting number says "play him," the games played say "we forgot he's here." At 23 the development window is narrowing.

**Colaiacovo** is fine. 30 games, 18.1 MPG, 12 points, POTE 99. When he is in he plays big minutes on the third pair. His 55% share likely reflects healthy rotation with Eminger and Klesla logging heavier loads. No concern.

**Chlup** at 18 is getting 44 games on the second line at 14.5 MPG with 31 points. That is exceptional for a teenager and there is nothing to fix. **Gaborik** (55 GP, 75 points), **Klesla** (55 GP, 23 points), **Alexeev** (55 GP, 30 points), **Nash** (42 GP, 32 points), **Chistov** (41 GP, 16 points), **Eminger** (44 GP, 20 points) — all dressed, all playing, all producing. No complaints.

**Upshall** is sitting and has earned it. 17 points in 45 games at 10.7 MPG is 0.38 per game. That is fourth-line output on fourth-line minutes. The spot is not being stolen from him; he has not outgrown it.

**Koltsov** stays as a trading chip per the GM's standing order. No development recommendation.

## Development trends

The question is who's growing and who's shrinking over the last ten weeks, and whether any of it should change the GM's February plans. The answer: two young guys are genuinely getting better, one is still not playing, Eminger's trend just flipped against my own trade call, and the top of the lineup is aging visibly.

**Chlup** is the story. 18 years old, 0.62→0.74 pts/g with minutes climbing from 11.0 to 16.0. He's the only young player getting more ice and producing at a higher rate on it. That's the definition of development working. He's earned a second-line look.

**Eminger** has pulled back. My Feb 6 note said he crossed the 0.45 trade threshold on season rate (19 in 42). His recent window is 0.57 pts/g in 21 games since Dec 1, which is pulling the season rate back toward 0.46. The trajectory has reversed. I would not sell him this week. If he finishes above 0.45 season, he stays as a cheap young D on a rebuilt pair. If February collapses again, we revisit.

**Stahle** played 2 games at 17.0 MPG. That's the minimum I asked for on January 25th. Two games is not enough to judge anything, but the dressing happened.

**Spezza** is worse. Minutes have dropped further to 5.3 MPG in the recent window, rate at 0.38. That's below where he was on January 31st when I last flagged this. He is not playing hockey.

**Spacek** at 19 is 0.55→0.43 on minutes that collapsed from 16.0 to 8.3. The GM's rotation philosophy explains part of this, but the rate decline alongside the ice decline is the wrong direction. He needs to be either back at 12+ or benched completely; 8 minutes is neither development nor contribution.

**Fischer** continues to fall: 0.63→0.42 while playing 21.5 MPG. At 24, on a four-year contract, this is the wrong slope. I'm not raising him as a trade candidate — he's a keeper — but the GM should know the trajectory is heading down when it should be at its peak.

**McCabe** is confirmed: 1.42→0.52 on 21.3 MPG. The January 31st note was early; now it's the full picture. He cannot be the top-pair D next season.

**Sundin** (33) and **Mogilny** (35) are 0.90 and 0.85 respectively in the recent window, down from 1.46 and 1.62. Expected at their ages. **Roberts** at 38 is holding at 1.00, better than either of them per point of age. None of these are surprises, but the top six production is thinning and there is no internal replacement for any of them.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: morale runs 86 to 100 across the roster with an average of 92. No one is crashing, and no line change is needed tonight to fix a morale problem.

**Spezza** is the only player below 90 at 86, flat for weeks. He sits at 7.5 MPG on 37 games and is still scratched. At 21 with POTE 99, that is the same development flag I have raised five times since January. His morale has not slipped further, so it is not an emergency, but the -1 to his grades is costing us a point or two of performance from a player who could grow into something useful. This remains a recommendation to dress him, not a line-move fix.

**Stahle** dropped 6 points to 94 after two appearances. At 20 with POTE 96 and just 2 GP all season, he is the same development waste flagged in January. The morale dip is a signal, but 94 is not a crisis. One dressing before the deadline would stop the slide.

**Safronov** sits at 95 on 3 GP. Same pattern as Stahle: a young defenceman getting scraps. No action required tonight, but worth a look if a defenceman goes down.

**Everyone else is fine.** Luongo at 99 with 61 MPG, Belfour at 99 on 21 starts, Richards at 99 on 17.4 MPG, Abid at 99 on 18.6 MPG carrying fourth-line duty. The top-four defencemen (McCabe 22.3, Fischer 21.3, Kaberle 20.9, Klesla 15.4) are all at 99. The veterans Mogilny (92, 17.8 MPG) and Sundin (96, 18.7 MPG) are stable. No one is carrying minutes far above their band, and no one is sitting below it with a morale reason to complain.

No change tonight.

## Role composition

Are the units built from the right players for their jobs, and does the roster have enough bodies for each role? The answer is mostly yes on construction, with one structural gap that isn't fixable by shuffling.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, McCabe, Gaborik, Fischer)** — well-built. Three 80-checking players (Roberts, McCabe, Fischer) alongside Gaborik's 96 scoring. The 77 checking mean on a first line is the kind you want: they can play against anyone. No change.

**L2 (Eminger, Chlup, Mogilny, Kaberle, Afinogenov)** — 64 checking mean is soft, but that's the design. Mogilny (90 scoring) and Afinogenov (88) are here to score. Chlup anchors faceoffs at 76. You can't have a checking line and a scoring line be the same line. Accept the softness, accept that L2 gets sheltered starts or draws the third pair. No change.

**L3 (Colaiacovo, Richards, Klesla, Nash, Chistov)** — 68 checking mean, 90 best from Klesla the defenceman. Among forwards on this line, nobody checks above 72. Richards (71 faceoff) is the only draw man. This is a speed line (Chistov 94), not a checking line. It does what it's built for. No change.

**L4 (Spacek, Alexeev, Abid)** — **51 faceoffs, both mean and best.** Nobody on the fourth line wins a draw. Abid (79 checking) is the only real checker on the unit. The faceoff gap matters only if this line takes defensive-zone starts, and fourth-liners naturally don't get many. I'd accept it for now but watch if Edmonton rolls their fourth line against ours on cycles.

**K1 (Eminger, Sundin, Roberts, Fischer)** — 76 checking mean, three 80s among the four. This is the right unit. Sundin's faceoff (87) is a bonus if the kill involves a defensive-zone draw. No change.

**K2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Chistov)** — 70/82 checking. McCabe's 80 is the anchor. Workable second kill. No change.

**P1 and P2** — P1 has Sundin, Gaborik (96 scoring, 98 playmaking), Kaberle and McCabe at the points. Four offensive weapons and Roberts for balance. Strong. P2 has Mogilny (90 scoring) and Eminger shooting from the back end. Fine for a second unit. No changes.

**Roster gap: toughness ceiling.** McCabe tops out at 70 toughness. Abid 69. Nobody above 70 on the entire roster. Against a physical opponent, we can't match their hitting from any line. That's not fixable by shuffling — we don't have the bodies. Flagging it.

## Opponent matchup

**What changes for EDM:** Nothing should change. We are superior on every line, their power play is broken, and the auto-pairing gives our top units the weakest D they'll see all week. This is a maximize-quality night per the GM's own framework, and the lineup already is maximum quality.

**EDM's structure:** They score 2.40 goals a game against our 2.40 against, and their power play is 17 for 157, which is 10.8%. They cannot kill penalties into offense. Their three D pairs read 70/71, 66/66, and 61/61. Our first three forward lines read 88/95/85, 83/83/87, and 84/80/79. The auto-pairing puts our best line against their 70-71 pair and our second line against their 66-66 pair. That's the easiest matchup on our schedule.

**Sundin's line vs Comrie:** Sundin at 88 against Comrie at 79, with Gaborik (95) against Semenov (70) and Hannan (71). The only question is whether we blow them out or grind it. We won the only meeting 4-0.

**Richards' line vs Hemsky:** Hemsky at 21 has 89 shot power and 89 deking, so he's a real scorer in the making, but he's 71 OVR and centring the third line. Richards at 84 handles him. Their third D pair is Baumgartner (61) and Dupont (61). Our Klesla/Colaiacovo at 81/70 can eat alive against those two.

**Faceoffs:** Against EDM specifically, the faceoff gap that usually bites us disappears. Their bottom-two centres are Hemsky (50 FACE) and Rita (50). Richards at 71 and Spacek at 51 win or split those draws. Only Reasoner (77) against Chlup (76) is even. This is one of the few nights the faceoff hole costs us nothing.

**Goaltending:** Luongo at 92 OVR against Salo at 82. EDM scores 2.40 a game. Luongo started Feb 7 and the GM took it. No fatigue flag on him in the brief. Belfour was tired on Jan 19; the GM should check his icon if he wants the veteran in, but Luongo is the clear choice on the numbers.

**No change on defense either.** Kaberle is already reinstated on the second pair. McCabe/Fischer on the top. Klesla/Colaiacovo get a free ride against 61-61 and should be encouraged to join the rush.

## Owed

This is the 11th update on **how our defencemen have played and who should go at the end of the season**.

**McCabe** — His slump since late January is continuing. He went from 48 points in 50 games (0.96 pts/g) on Jan 31 to 50 points in 55 games (0.91) now. That's 2 points in 5 games, a 0.40 rate over the recent stretch. At 29, $3.0M for 4 more years, and 22.3 MPG, this is no longer a blip — it's a decline. He still carries an 81 OVR and his season total is good, but the direction is wrong. He stays on the top pair now because nothing else on this roster matches his production, but next summer he becomes the question at the top of this list.

**Eminger** — No change from Feb 6. He's at 20 points in 44 games (0.45 pts/g), exactly at the trade threshold I set. He's 21, $1.2M expiring, 74 OVR. Sell at the deadline. Nothing has moved him above the line.

**Fischer** — Static. Still 25 points in 50 games (0.50 pts/g), 21.3 MPG. GM's keeper, no proposal made. My declining-age-24 flag holds: at 24 with a four-year $3.7M deal and a rate going the wrong way, this is a planning problem for next October, not a trade call now.

**Kaberle** — 27 points in 47 games (0.57 pts/g), 26 years old, 81 OVR, $1.9M expiring. Keeper per the GM. His renewal is the offseason priority on this blue line.

**Klesla** — 23 points in 55 games (0.42 pts/g) at 22, 81 OVR, $0.9M for 2 more years. Young, cheap, plays top-four minutes. No reason to move him.

**Colaiacovo** — 12 points in 30 games (0.40 pts/g) at 22, 70 OVR, $1.1M expiring. Low production, low grade. He's a candidate if a mid-round pick comes up, but no urgency.

**Svehla** — 0.68 pts/g at 36 on an expiring deal. The GM has called him the MVP and that's settled. Not raising him again.

**Stahle** — Now 2 GP (was 0 on Jan 25). Still the biggest development asset sitting idle with 0 points in 2 games and 68 OVR. He needs to be dressed and playing every remaining game, or we're wasting the asset.

Nothing structural has changed since my last delivery. The only new fact is McCabe's slump extending into February, which strengthens the "question mark next summer" flag.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-07
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-07

Toronto 38-9-4, 86 pts after 54 games.

## Role coverage

At 86 points in 54 games Toronto are the best team in the league; the role-coverage question now is not whether they make the playoffs but whether they survive a seven-game series against a physical club, and on toughness and faceoffs the answer is no.

**Toughness** is the structural hole. Zero players at 80+ TOUG on a 28-man roster. The best is Roberts at 73, who is 38. Tucker sits at 70 unlined, Chlup at 70, Svehla at 69. No lineup shuffle closes a gap where nobody reaches 80. The January finding on Abid's base TOUG of 80 has not translated into his displayed rating this season; whatever his base says, he is not showing it on the sheet now.

**Faceoffs** are the second hole. Sundin at 90 is alone. The next man is Chlup at 75, then Roberts at 75, who is also 38. Against a team with a 90+ centre (Ottawa, Philadelphia, New Jersey), Toronto lose the draw on three of four lines and cede zone entry.

**Checking** is thin only because the coach is not using the depth he has. Roberts 86 and McCabe 86 are lined; Svehla 83, Tucker 83, and Upshall 80 are all "not lined." That is three 80+ checkers collecting a paycheck. Dressing two of them makes checking adequate for the playoffs without a trade.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, stamina, clutch** are all covered to depth. Twelve at 80+ scoring, 22 at 80+ speed, twelve at 80+ stamina. The first three lines carry nine players at 80+ across those attributes. No acquisition needed.

**Age risk clusters at the top.** Mogilny (35) and Roberts (38) are load-bearing on scoring, playmaking, clutch, and checking simultaneously. They are the two players whose decline is most likely within one season. Svehla (36) sits unused and is the only player who bridges checking and stamina in one body.

**Goalies** are solved. Luongo at 25, 38 GP, 2.90 GAA, .873 save percentage on a $1.60M deal with two years left is a franchise starter. Belfour at 2.27 GAA in 21 games provides playoff insurance on an expiring $6.50M. The standing order to fetch a high-90s goalie from a non-contender has been fulfilled by Luongo's arrival.

## Trajectory

The trajectory question is whether 15 contracts worth $25.30M expiring the same July turns this club's depth into a cliff in 12 months. It does not, provided the summer is worked in sequence rather than all at once.

**The shape is right.** 16 players aged 23 or under, 10 in prime (24-29), only 6 at 30 or above. That matches the manual's target of 5-7 veterans and around 20 young players almost exactly. The age curve is young and ascending, not top-heavy. The problem is entirely contractual, not demographic.

**The summer cluster is the binding constraint.** 15 one-year deals, $25.30M, all expire in July 2005. That covers the entire top-9 forward corps (Gaborik $1.10M/74 pts, Richards $1.00M/54 pts, Nash $1.20M/32 pts, Abid $0.40M/63 pts, Alexeev $1.10M/30 pts), two top-pairing defencemen (Eminger $1.20M POTE 99, Colaiacovo $1.10M POTE 99), and three expensive veterans (Belfour $6.50M, Svehla $3.60M, Roberts $2.70M). If all 15 are re-signed at any kind of raise, payroll balloons. If they are all left to drift, the roster collapses.

**The sequence that protects three seasons.** Move the three expensive veterans first, this deadline or early July, freeing $12.80M and recovering draft picks via the over-80 expiring mechanic. Belfour (39, 92 base, $6.50M) and Svehla (36, scratched) are clean sells. Roberts (38, 61 pts, $2.70M) still has rental value for a contender. Then lock the young core on 5-6 year deals at today's prices before their overalls rise: Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Chistov, Upshall. That's seven players at $7.00M combined salary today who will each cost $3-5M in three years. Re-sign the bottom six (Abid, Alexeev, Koltsov who is 2yrs, Smirnov) on 2-3 year deals to push their renewals into summer 2007 and split the cluster.

**Belfour is the single biggest asset decision.** The GM's Jan 15 order said he stays as the number one. That was before Luongo arrived on the roster (91 base, 38 GP, 25 years old, POTE 97, $1.60M with two years). The situation has changed. Luongo is now the starter going forward, Belfour is $6.50M expiring with a POTE of 50 and CONS at 50, and he qualifies for the pick-recovery mechanic. Trade him for a pick at the deadline if the team is safe enough to absorb the risk, or hold him as playoff insurance and trade or release in July. Either way, he does not re-sign.

**Fischer is locked dead money.** $3.70M with four years left at age 24, points per game dropping from 0.63 to 0.41, POTE 90 unrealizing. Not actionable until summer 2008. That is a $3.70M annual drag on a payroll that must absorb star extensions for Chlup (18, $2.34M, 2yrs, POTE 95) and Luongo in summer 2006.

**The 2006 summer is the next wave.** 10 contracts, $18.04M, expire then: Mogilny ($5.50M, age 36), McCabe ($3.00M, age 30), Chlup ($2.34M, age 19 by then), Luongo ($1.60M, age 26), Spezza ($1.00M, POTE 99), Klesla ($0.90M, POTE 97), Ouellet, Koltsov, Salo, Safronov. Chlup and Luongo will command star extensions. If Mogilny is shed after this season (he has 2yrs, so his second year is 2005-06 and he expires summer 2006 at $5.50M), that frees the money for both.

**Draft capital is empty.** Nothing above a 4th rounder, confirmed Jan 26. Every package is player-funded. This is why Belfour and Svehla must go for picks rather than being released, and why the over-80 expiring mechanic is not an oddity but the only path back to draft ammunition.

**Money is not the problem.** Payroll $65.94M against revenue $73.52M and profit $23.15M means Toronto can absorb raises. The problem is that 15 simultaneous renewals at once will spike costs before revenue adjusts, and that mid-contract renegotiation is impossible, so today's cheap contracts are the only window to lock them at today's price.

**On the Coach's development flags:** Spezza ($1.00M, POTE 99, 21, 2yrs) and Stahle ($0.97M, POTE 96, 20, 3yrs) sitting unplayed are trajectory risks in their own right. Spezza's contract expires in 2006; if he hasn't played by then, his renewal value drops and the club loses a year on a potential top-six centre. That is a development decision for the Coach to execute, but it affects the summer 2006 planning.

## Calendar

**Are we buying or selling at the deadline, and what happens to the 15 contracts expiring this summer?**

**Belfour** is the answer to both questions, and his situation has changed since January. The GM ordered him kept on Jan 15 because "he is the best goalie we have and we need a number one." That premise no longer holds. Luongo (91 base, 25, $1.60M, two years left) is on the roster. Belfour at 39, $6.50M, 92 base and expiring is the single cleanest over-80 pick-recovery candidate on the team. Trade him before March 19. He goes for a draft pick plus ideally a young player. If no package materialises, he still goes for a pick via the expiring mechanic.

**Svehla** (85 base, 36, $3.60M, expiring) and **Roberts** (87 base, 38, $2.70M, expiring) are the other two over-80 expiring players we do not intend to keep. Both are pick-recovery candidates. After them we still have four established defencemen (McCabe 82 base 4yr, Fischer 82 base 4yr, Salo 83 base 2yr, Klesla 78 base 2yr) and four forwards scoring at 85+ base (Gaborik, Sundin, Mogilny, Afinogenov). The roster does not need replacement.

**The deadline answer is: sell three veterans for picks, buy nothing.** We are 38-9-4, 86 points, 16 ahead of second place. The manual's "do nothing" applies to buying. The only action is collecting draft capital from men who walk in July otherwise. Open conversations late February per the GM's standing order; execute by March 19.

**Gaborik** is the summer's top priority. 91 base, 67 points in 45 games, age 22, $1.10M. Lock him on five or six years the moment his contract expires. This is not urgent now because renegotiation is impossible mid-contract, but the preparation is: decide the offer before July so no bidding war catches us flat.

**Kaberle** (84 base, 26, $1.90M) and **Richards** (82 base, 24, $1.00M) are the next two renewals. Both are 5-6 year targets. A 26-year-old top-pairing defenceman and a 24-year-old centre at faceoff value for $1M are the kind of players you lock young and cheap.

**Eminger** (76 base, 21, $1.20M, POTE 99) is the GM's protected asset from the Chara veto. He's expiring this summer. Five-year lock. He's the cheapest defence prospect on the roster with the highest upside.

**Nash** (77 base, 20, $1.20M) on five years. **Abid** (79 base, 24, $0.40M) on two to three years — at four hundred thousand dollars he is the cheapest toughness available anywhere. **Chistov** (78 base, 21), **Upshall** (78 base, 21), **Alexeev** (76 base, 23): depth renewals on two years, $1.10M or less. If they walk we replace them with draft picks we just collected.

**Colaiacovo** (72 base, 22, $1.10M) is borderline. Either renew on two years or use him in a deadline package. He is not the Eminger-tier prospect the GM protected.

**Tellqvist** (77 base, 25, $0.80M) stays per the GM's Jan 15 order. With Luongo and Ouellet (81 base, 2yr) ahead of him, he is depth. Renew on two years cheaply or trade him in the summer surplus window.

**Smirnov** (51 base, 20, $0.40M) is released. Zero games in a full season at age 20 with a 51 base overall. He is not developing.

**Mogilny** has two years at $5.50M remaining, which means the December package (Mogilny for Jackman) is dead as a concept. He stays. His form is four points below base (86 overall vs 90 base), worth watching, but not actionable until next summer.

**Obligation #2 (Luongo and DiPietro monitoring):** Luongo is on the roster. 91 base, 2 years, $1.60M. The goalie trade window the GM asked me to watch closed when he arrived. DiPietro is irrelevant — we have Luongo. This obligation is discharged.

**The pick situation confirms every package must be player-funded.** All of Toronto's R1 through R4 are held by other clubs (FLA, DET, WSH, PIT respectively). The only owned pick is a fifth-rounder. The three deadline sales are the only path back to first-round draft capital this cycle.

## League scan

The question is which players on losing clubs fill Toronto's structural holes — zero men at 80+ TOUG, one faceoff man worth a damn — and which of those holes are fixable by March 9 without spending a pick we don't own. The answer is three names at the top: one closes all three gaps at $400K, one is a 23-year-old defenceman with 90 TOUG and 91 CHKG on a three-year deal, and one is a 23-year-old defenceman putting up 64 points for the league's worst club on $1.10M.

**Sean Avery** (LA, C, 25) is the target. 94 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, $400K with two years left. LA are 16-24-6 with 13 expiring deals; they will deal him for depth. The production is thin (6 points in 53 games) but he is a bottom-six centre. No other player in the league closes toughness, checking, and faceoffs simultaneously at that price with control.

**Barret Jackman** (STL, D, 23) is the long-term answer to the toughness gap on the blue line. 90 TOUG, 91 CHKG, 80 base overall, $700K, three years left. 26 points in 52 games at 30.7 MPG means he is already a top-pairing defenceman. STL at 14-27-4 are in a full rebuild and should prefer any package to holding a 23-year-old on a losing roster. The problem is price: STL will want more for three years of control than for an expiring rental.

**Mike Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23) is the best value on the board. 64 points in 54 games at 29.6 MPG, POTE 91, 77 base overall, $1.10M expiring. MTL are 15-30-4 with 14 expiring deals and the lowest record in the East. He is having a breakout year. The question is whether MTL would rather rebuild around him or recoup something now. At 23 with POTE 91, they might keep him — but 14 expiring contracts and 15 wins suggests they are selling everything.

**Kovalchuk and Heatley** (both ATL) remain the highest-ceiling targets. Kovalchuk at 92 points in 52 games, age 21, $1.10M expiring; Heatley at 85 points in 49 games, age 24, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 18-26-2 cannot re-sign both. The binary still applies: get one, accept losing the other. The Jan 5 proposed package (own first-rounder plus Koltsov) is no longer valid because the first-rounder was spent on Luongo. A new package must be player-funded. Svehla ($3.60M, 36, expiring) and Chistov are the obvious assets.

**Martin Havlat** (OTT, LW, 23) at 71 points in 54 games on $900K expiring was rejected only inside the Chara package that the GM vetoed on Jan 19. As a standalone target — priced with Chistov plus a 4th or Svehla as salary filler — the math changes. The GM's objection was giving up Eminger for Chara; that objection does not apply to Havlat on a cheaper package.

**Jay Bouwmeester** (FLA, D, 21) at POTE 95, 81 base, $1.20M expiring, 19 points in 53 games at 32.4 MPG. FLA are 17-27-7 with 19 expiring contracts. He is younger than Jackman with higher potential, but his production is lower and FLA may not be motivated to deal a 21-year-old top-pairing defenceman even in a rebuild.

**Matt Walker** (STL, D, 24) at 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $500K, one year, 7 points in 42 games. A pure playoff-toughness rental. If the trade deadline is March and the goal is a seven-game series against a physical club, he costs almost nothing. STL are 14-27-4 and will take a 4th rounder plus a body.

**Craig Conroy** (CGY, C, 33) at 64 points in 53 games, 87 FACE, $2.00M expiring. CGY at 16-29-6 are selling. As a rental centre for the playoffs he upgrades the faceoff problem without costing a roster spot permanently. Costs Chistov plus a 4th per the Jan 30 note. The issue is whether Toronto want to spend Chistov (a young prospect) on a rental rather than on Avery, who fills the same gap with two years of control at $400K.

**Marc Savard** (ATL, C, 27) at 57 points in 52 games, 89 FACE, $1.00M expiring. Folds into the ATL conversation at no extra cost beyond what a Kovalchuk or Heatley package already requires.

## Trade construction

The question is which packages both sides accept without a draft pick we don't own, and the answer depends on which assets the AI values on the other side of the table. Three proposals, ranked by expected value to Toronto.

**Belfour to a contender for a first-rounder.** He is 92 base, $6.50M expiring, 2.27 GAA in 21 games. The over-80 expiring mechanic recovers a pick without a player return. Luongo (91 base, 38 GP, 2.90 GAA) is the starter; Tellqvist (91 base, 11 GP) and Ouellet (97 POTE, 8 GP) are the depth. A club in the top-8 needing playoff goalie insurance gets the league's lowest GAA on an expiring contract they would not re-sign. We get the first-rounder that has been empty since the Luongo deal consumed it. Risk: if Luongo goes down in the playoffs, we are on Tellqvist. With Luongo at 38 starts and the club at 86 points, that risk is small against the cost of holding $6.50M dead money past July.

**Sean Avery from LA for Chistov plus the 4th.** Avery is 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 94 FACE, $400K, two years, age 25. He is the only player in the league closing our three structural gaps simultaneously on a re-signable deal. LA at 16-24-6 with 13 expiring contracts are rebuilding and should value Chistov at 21 with POTE 95, 89 SPEE, 88 ACCE on a $1.10M expiring deal — a cheap prospect they can develop or re-flip. We give from surplus: Chistov is one of seven players at POTE 94+ on this roster. Acceptance is uncertain because two years of control on a gap-filler may price higher than a 21-year-old prospect from the league's worst offence.

**Matt Walker from STL for Smirnov plus the 4th.** Walker is 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, $500K, one year, 7 points in 42 games at 24. A pure rental for a seven-game series against Ottawa or New Jersey. STL at 14-27-4 want to clear his expiring salary; they will take a 20-year-old with POTE 70 who has played zero games this season plus the 4th to offload him. Cost is minimal because we were never playing Smirnov. This closes the toughness gap for the playoffs without touching the young core.

If none land: dress Tucker (88 stored TOUG, 92 CHKG, 3 GP in 53 games) and Upshall (80 CHKG, 45 GP, unlined) on the bottom six. The Coach's flags and the role-coverage finding point at the same answer. That fills checking without a trade but does not solve faceoffs past Sundin.

## Owed

**Owed item #2 — Monitor Luongo availability and DiPietro ice time/development through February for goalie trade window.**

**Luongo** — Task complete. He arrived on Toronto's roster before the February window opened. The top-60 sheet shows him at **TOR**, 25 years old, 91 base, $1.60M, 2 years remaining. His season line: 38 GP, 16-21-0-1, 2.90 GAA, 87.3% save on 883 shots. The January 15 mandate ("fetch a really good high-90s goalie from a team that will not be a contender") is fulfilled. No further monitoring of Florida is needed.

**DiPietro** — 39 GP for NYI, 22-14-0, 2.94 GAA, 87.3% save on 840 shots. His numbers have improved from the earlier partial reading; he is now carrying a full starter's load at age 22. His displayed overall is 84 against base 79, meaning form is currently helping him. The gap between his 84 and Luongo's 91 is 12 points at base. POTE 99 has not translated to an overall above 84 yet. He remains a NYI re-signing priority on an expiring $1.10M deal, not a realistic trade target for us. No change to the January conclusion.

**What this means now** — The goalie slot is solved: Luongo is the number one with two years of control. The open question shifts to Belfour: 39, 90 base, $6.50M expiring, 2.27 GAA and 5 shutouts in 21 games. He is the cleanest over-80 expiring pick-recovery candidate per the mechanic. Per the GM's standing order, negotiations do not open until late February, but the decision (playoff insurance through a first round versus March asset for a pick) should be made by then so we know what to offer when the window opens.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-07
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-07

Next game vs MTL on Tuesday 08 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: which of our sixteen players under 24 are getting the games their talent says they should, and which are being wasted?

**Spezza** is the headline for the sixth time. POTE 99, 21 years old, 7.5 minutes a night, 0.41 points per game across 37 games. A POTE 99 centre at 21 belongs at 12 or more minutes; he's in the depth-man band. Montreal is 15-30, which is a game we can afford to develop in. Slot him third-line centre tonight and give him 12+. I have raised this five times with no movement. If February passes without change, his development window this year is effectively closed and we are wasting a first-round calibre player on fourth-line garbage time.

**Stahle** is invisible. POTE 96, age 20, defenceman, 2 games in 54. The blue line has Klesla (54 GP), Eminger (43), McCabe, Svehla, and Colaiacovo (29). There is no path through that group this season without a trade or injury. Either dress him tonight against Montreal and let him play five or six shifts, or tell me to put his name on the trade list. A 20-year-old with 96 potential who can't crack a 15-30 opponent's lineup is not going to crack anyone's next season either.

**Upshall** at 45 games, 10.7 MPG, 0.38 points per game. His rate has slid from 0.69 in January to 0.38 now. He got the chance and the signal is fading. No promotion. Keep him fourth line or scratch him; either is fine. The development window for him is closing on its own terms.

**Ouellet** has 8 games at 23 with POTE 97. He is a third-string goalie who cannot develop sitting behind Belfour and Luongo. That is a roster problem for you to solve, not a lineup one, but I am naming it: if a club needs a backup goalie, Ouellet is worth a late pick to us and worth zero to us here.

**No concerns** for Gaborik (54/54, 19.3 MPG, 74 points), Chlup (18, L2 centre, 14.4 MPG, 30 points at 0.70 per game), Nash (76% share, 32 points), Klesla (54/54, 23 points), or Spacek (31 GP at 19, 11.2 MPG, 0.48 per game). They are getting what they have earned.

**Koltsov** and **Smirnov** are scratched by your deliberate design. Koltsov is a trading chip; Smirnov is POTE 70 with 0 games and is not a development priority. Both fine.

## Development trends

The window from December 1st to February 7th separates this roster into those growing into their roles and those sliding, and the line between them is not always age.

**Chlup** is the story. 18 years old, 0.62 to 0.73 pts/g on 11.0 to 15.8 MPG. He has taken the second-line centre job and is producing at a rate that says it belongs to him. At 18, on the rise, with 15.8 minutes a night, he is the most encouraging development on this roster.

**Abid** at 24 went from 1.09 to 1.22 pts/g despite minutes dropping from 20.1 to 18.0. He is scoring more per shift. That is a player still growing, and at his age the window is still open.

**Kaberle** moved from 0.54 to 0.59 on 19.4 to 22.6 MPG. More ice, more output. The GM's star is trending up at 26 and his minutes are the highest of any defenceman on the club.

**Klesla** is a quiet worry. 0.50 down to 0.37 pts/g while minutes went from 14.6 to 16.0. He is 22 and getting more ice but producing less per shift. That is the wrong direction at his age. No card-grade change to confirm it, but the production window is hard to argue with.

**Spezza** remains the problem I cannot fix. 5.3 MPG, down from 9.1, with a rate that slipped from 0.43 to 0.38. He is 21 with POTE 99 and playing fourth-line minutes in garbage time. I have raised this five times. The rotation philosophy explains why Nash and Spacek sit; it does not explain why Spezza is buried on the third or fourth unit while getting less than Upshall and Chistov. At 5.3 a night this year is wasted regardless of how good his ceiling is.

**Koltsov** is collapsing at the worst time for his trade value. 1.10 down to 0.33 pts/g on 12.0 MPG in the recent window. The GM is holding him as a trading chip, but nobody pays for a 23-year-old who just scored at 0.33 over 21 games. If he is being shopped at the deadline, the ask should already be lower.

**Eminger's** season total crossed the 0.45 trade threshold, but his recent window reads 0.35 to 0.55. He is improving, not deteriorating. The threshold was set assuming a player whose rate was heading down. At 0.55 since December, the trade case weakens. I would hold him unless the final three weeks turn back down.

**The veteran slide is steep and broad.** Mogilny went from 1.62 to 0.85 at 35. Sundin from 1.46 to 0.87 at 33. Svehla from 0.78 to 0.56 at 36. Roberts from 1.29 to 1.00 at 38. McCabe from 1.42 to 0.50 at 29. Five of the top-end players are in double-digit percentage decline, and the two on the biggest slopes are the two oldest. The GM should be planning around at least three of these names leaving or being replaced before next October.

**Afinogenov** at 25 dropped from 1.17 to 0.87 on identical 16.8 MPG. Not age yet, but the decline is real and he is on a contract the GM needs to factor into the roster plan.

No card grades moved in this window, so everything here rests on production and minutes. That is the second-best evidence, and at this spread it is enough.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy with one chronic exception I have raised five times and one player to watch.

**Spezza** sits at 86 morale, unchanged across most snapshots, on 7.5 minutes a night and 15 points in 37 games. He is 21 with elite potential and he is the lowest-morale player on the roster by six points. At 86 he is in the minus-1 band, costing him a grade on every stat the game shows. The cause is the GM's deliberate development rotation, which I accept as his call, but the consequence is that Spezza plays with a handicap every time he goes over the boards. I have no line change that fixes a player the GM is scratching.

**Mogilny** is at 92 on 17.8 minutes and 61 points in 50 games. He is a 90-calibre player getting 17-band minutes, and 92 is only two points above the threshold where he loses his morale bonus. If a rough patch drops him below 90, he plays with minus-1 on every grade at 35 years old. No action today, but if his morale hits 89 before the break I would want him closer to 19 minutes even if it means shortening the second line.

Everyone else is at 92 or above with no notable downward trend. Gaborik (96), Sundin (96), Roberts (99), Abid (99), Richards (99) are all in the plus-1 band or better on reasonable minutes. The scratched veterans (Svehla 96, Salo 96, Koltsov 96) are all content. The young scratched players (Smirnov 100, St. Jacques 100) have no minutes to resent.

No line or ice-time change this week. The room is right.

## Role composition

The question is whether these units are built from the right pieces, and whether we have enough of each role to cover a full game. The short answer: the lines are sensible given what we have, but the roster has two real gaps behind the top four checkers and behind Sundin at faceoffs.

**L1** is well-built. Roberts 79 checking and Fischer 79 give it two real grinders alongside Gaborik (94 scoring, 97 playmaking). Sundin at 86 faceoffs wins draws on any night. No change needed.

**L2** runs a 64 checking mean, which is soft. But Mogilny (88 scoring) and Afinogenov (86 scoring, 87 playmaking) are pure skill players, and Chlup at 75 faceoffs anchors the dot. This line is built to score, and the first line carries the checking load. Accept the trade-off.

**L3** is the most balanced unit: Richards at 93 stamina and 92 clutch is the engine, Chistov brings 93 speed, and the checking mean of 67 is adequate for a third line. Nash is producing here. Fine.

**L4** has a real problem: 50/50 on faceoffs. Spacek, Alexeev and Abid can't win a draw. This means whenever this line is on for a defensive-zone faceoff, we're chasing from the whistle. There is no better option on the roster for a fourth-line centre who can take a hit, so it's a roster gap, not an arrangement fix.

**K1** is strong: Eminger, Roberts (79 checking), Fischer (79) give three genuine killers. **K2** at a 69 checking mean leans on Chlup (75) and two defencemen. Behind our top four checkers (all 78-79), there's a cliff. We're thin for two penalty-kill units.

**Toughness** is the wider gap. Nobody on the roster carries above 69. Roberts 69, McCabe 69, Abid 68, Fischer 68. We have no enforcer and no one to match a physical line's intensity. That's a roster problem I can't solve with a line change.

No unit is misassembled. The two structural problems (checking depth behind four, and zero faceoff capability on L4) belong in the GM's hands, not mine.

## Opponent matchup

**The question: does Montreal's roster demand a different Toronto line configuration than we run normally?** No. They have nobody above 79 OVR, they score 2.5 a night, and their power play is 8 on 138 (5.8%). This is the weakest club we've faced this season.

**Koivu** is their entire offense. 79 OVR, PASS 86, SPEE 86 — he carries puck and creates. Bulis and Sundstrom behind him are 72 and 68. Our first pair (Fischer 81, McCabe 80) handles their first line without adjustment, and the auto-pairing already puts them together since our top line and first D pair share the slot. No reorder needed.

**Their PP is irrelevant.** 5.8% conversion means our penalty kill gets a light test. I would not shorten anyone's shift for PK depth here.

**Luongo starts.** 91 OVR against a 2.5-goal-per-game attack is the easy night he needs between tougher outings. No reason to touch Belfour — this isn't a game where we need his experience or his rebound control against skilled shooters.

**Development note (separate from matchup):** The quality gap is wide enough that this is a game the GM can afford to use for rotation if he wants. Scratching a veteran to give Spacek or Nash a first/second-line look costs us nothing against Montreal's third line (Ribeiro 62, Hoglund 65). That's the GM's call based on his development philosophy, not a matchup requirement.

## Owed

**Defenceman evaluation, updated for February 8.** The headline since my last delivery: McCabe's cooling has continued. Since I noted him at 0.96 cumulative on January 26th, he has added just 1 point in 4 games, dropping his season rate to 0.91. That is a third consecutive window of decline at 29 on $3.00M x 3 remaining years. Every week we hold him, his trade value drops.

**McCabe** is the priority. 49 points in 54 games reads fine on the surface but the trajectory is wrong: 0.96 in late January, now 0.91 season-wide because the recent window is running at roughly 0.25. He is still a top-pair defenceman tonight, but as an asset the window is closing. At $3.00M with 3 years left, no contender is going to give a first-round pick for a 29-year-old who is visibly slowing. This should have been done at Christmas. Now it is a "get what you can" sale.

**Eminger** has added zero points since my February 6th note. He sits at 19 in 43, which is 0.44 pts/g. My stated threshold was 0.45; he is below it and has not recovered in the final two weeks of my evaluation window. The expiring $1.20M makes him a rental for any team needing a third-pair body. Move him.

**Klesla** is 23 in 54 on $0.90M x 2 remaining. At 22 with a full season, he is the best value on the blue line. No change, no trade, he stays.

**Fischer** is 24 in 49 at 0.49 season rate. GM's keeper, no action.

**Colaiacovo** is expiring, 12 points in 29 games at 22. Cheap depth with no future here. If McCabe or Eminger are moved and we need to fill a slot he fills it. If not, he is a second rental candidate who will fetch almost nothing.

**Stahle** has appeared in 2 games since my January 25th note of zero. Small step in the right direction for a POTE-96 project.

**Salo** is 8 points in 22 on $2.60M x 2. No production, no urgency to move since nobody is calling.

The bottom line: McCabe and Eminger should be moved at the deadline. Klesla stays. Everything else is either a keeper or too cheap to bother.

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-06
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-06

Toronto 38-9-3, 85 pts after 53 games.

## Role coverage

**The toughness and faceoff gaps are structural, not coaching problems. Checking depth is.** The coach can dress Tucker, Svehla, and Abid tonight for 80+ checking, but zero players on this roster carry 80 toughness, and only Sundin (90) wins draws. Those two holes need an external fix before the deadline.

**Toughness** — zero at 80+. Roberts at 73 is the ceiling. Abid's base TOUG was 80 on the January sheet but he doesn't appear in this brief's top six, suggesting his displayed grade has slipped below 80. Even at his best, one man at 80 does not fill the role. Bell (CHI, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, $900K, 2y) remains the only player who closes this and the faceoff gap simultaneously. Avery (LA, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 93 FACE, $400K, 2y) is the budget version.

**Faceoffs** — Sundin 90, then Chlup 75, Roberts 75, Richards 70. Three of those four are not centres, and Sundin is 33. A team needs at least two centres above 80 to survive a playoff series against a first line that dumps the puck in. Avery at 93 FACE and $400K is the cheapest solution in the league.

**Checking** — Tucker 83, Svehla 83, Upshall 80, all not lined. The coach has the depth he needs on this roster; he just is not using it. McCabe 86 carries the load alone. Dress Tucker or Svehla on the third pairing and the gap closes without a trade.

**Scoring** — 12 players at 80+, but Mogilny 35, Sundin 33, Roberts 38. Gaborik 22 and Afinogenov 25 are the future core, but behind them the next wave is Spacek 19 and Koltsov 23, neither producing at the level the age implies. Koltsov at 92 SPEED sitting unlined is the best internal fix for secondary scoring.

**Goalies** — Belfour at 39 and $6.50M is a one-year rental no matter what the standing order says; he cannot sign the reduced deal the GM wanted. Luongo (91 base, POTE 96, 25) from the Jan 25 brief would give Toronto a top-5 starter behind Belfour's remaining 21 games this season. Ouellet at 85 base with a 0.918 SV in 8 games is the internal depth story.

**Defense age curve** — Kaberle 26, McCabe 29, Eminger 21, Stahle 20. The top is young enough to sustain but the shutdown pairing is one man (McCabe 86 CHKG) and the next-best is 36-year-old Svehla. Komisarek (MTL, 77 base, POTE 91, 22, $1.10M expiring) remains the target to pair with Kaberle for the next five years.

## Trajectory

**The summer 2005 renewal cluster is the single biggest threat to this roster's next three seasons, and the pick drought is what makes it dangerous.** The age shape is healthy — 16 players at 23 or under, only 4 at 34+ — but 15 contracts worth $25.30M expire in the same July, and Toronto owns no pick better than a fourth-rounder. Without expiring-veteran trades, there is no ammunition to fill holes between now and July.

**Belfour** at 39, $6.50M, POTE 50, 21 GP is the obvious candidate for the over-80 expiring mechanic. The GM's Jan 15 order was based on him being the number one. Luongo now carries 37 starts at 25 with POTE 97. Belfour is the third-stringer's salary on a first-place roster. Trading him for a first-rounder before March recovers the one asset class that is currently empty. The GM's "Belfour stays" directive predates Luongo's arrival; flagging the tension rather than overruling it.

**Svehla** at 36, $3.60M, POTE 55, scratched. **Roberts** at 38, $2.70M, POTE 52. Both are over 80, both expiring, both scratched from units. Moving them before March recovers two more picks and frees $6.30M combined. These three trades alone would fill the round-1 and round-2 slots.

**Gaborik** at 22, 73 points in 53 games, $1.10M expiring is the most expensive re-signing coming due. On a 5-6 year deal he will demand $4-5M. **Richards** at 24, 54 points, $1.00M expiring likely commands $3-4M. **Nash** at 20, 32 points, POTE 95, $1.20M expiring must go 5-6 years now. **Eminger** at 21, POTE 99, 19 points, $1.20M expiring is the same story. These four combined cost $4.50M today and will cost perhaps $14-16M renewed. Against $23.95M profit and $12.80M of freed veteran salary, that is affordable. The GM must accept that July 2005 is a spending summer, not a retrenchment one.

**Mogilny** at 35, $5.50M, 61 points, POTE 55, 2 years left is the next cliff. He produces now but POTE 55 means the slide starts immediately. By summer 2006 he is 36, declining, and $5.50M of dead weight on a roster that won't need it. The window to trade him with value is this deadline or next July.

**Fischer** at 24, $3.70M, 4 years left, 0.41 pts/g is locked until 2008. No action possible. It is $3.70M of dead money in a roster that will need every dollar for Gaborik and Richards renewals. The cost of his decline is the next two summers, not this one.

**Chlup** at 18, $2.34M, POTE 95, 29 points in 42 games, 2 years left is the cheapest star on the roster and the easiest lock. He extends naturally in July 2006. If he produces 40+ points by season's end, the renewal price rises sharply. The 42 GP and 29 points through the season's midpoint suggest he will.

## Calendar

**Are we buyers or sellers?** Buyers. Toronto sit at 85 points with a 16-point lead over second-place Carolina and 29 games left; the only question is seeding, not qualification. The manual's instruction is clear: buy for need, prefer young players you keep over pure rentals. The deadline is 41 days out, March 19, and per the standing order negotiations open in late February.

**Svehla** at 85 base overall, 36 years old, $3.60M expiring is the single most valuable deadline asset Toronto has. He is over 80 and will not be re-signed, which triggers the pick-recovery mechanic. Same logic applies to **Roberts** at 87 base, 38, $2.70M expiring. Both are old, expensive, and replaceable. Moving each for a draft pick recovers the pick capital that currently blocks the Luongo deal and every other first-rounder-dependent package. This is the move that changes the summer.

**Luongo** still reads 91 overall and 91 base with FLA as of today. The trade is blocked: Florida demand Aebischer plus a first-rounder, and Toronto own only a fourth-rounder, confirmed as of this save. Even if Svehla or Roberts recovers a pick at the deadline, there is no guarantee it lands as a first. The path to Luongo runs through the pick recovery, not around it.

**DiPietro** at NYI reads 84 overall on a 79 base, 39 games played, 2,185 minutes, which works out to roughly 56 minutes per start. That is a workhorse load for a team at 55 points, eighth in the East. His base is 79, which does not meet the GM's mandate for a high-90s goalie, and he is not the target. He is useful only as a market comparison: goalies on sub-.500 clubs get heavy starts, which is what Tellqvist needs.

**Belfour** stays per the standing order, but the standing order also says to offer a reduced contract at renewal and that he probably will not accept. At $6.50M and 39 years old, that is the likely outcome. The plan is: keep him through the Cup run, offer the reduced deal in July, and have the contingency ready. **Tellqvist** stays, give him the starter's workload next season, and renew on two or three years.

### Summer expiring list, by decision

**Lock 5–6 years:** Gaborik (RW, 22, 91 base, $1.10M), Nash (LW, 20, $1.20M), Richards (C, 24, $1.00M), Kaberle (D, 26, $1.90M), Eminger (D, 21, $1.20M). These five are the young core and the shape the manual asks for. Gaborik is the most urgent — 91 base at 22 on $1.10M will not stay cheap through a July bidding war.

**Renew 2–3 years:** Upshall (RW, 21, $1.20M), Alexeev (RW, 23, $1.10M), Chistov (LW, 21, $1.10M), Colaiacovo (D, 22, $1.10M), Smirnov (LW, 20, $0.40M), Abid (LW, 24, $0.40M). Depth pieces, staggered so they do not all hit the market together. Colaiacovo stays at 2–3 years only if he is not traded before the deadline for Bell or a blueliner.

**Tellqvist:** Renew 2–3 years. POTE in the high-90s per the GM, but he has not been a starter. Two years lets you assess before committing longer.

**Offer reduced, expect departure:** Belfour (G, 39, $6.50M). The GM's own standing order predicts he walks. Plan for it.

**Move before deadline for a pick:** Svehla ($3.60M, 36, 85 base), Roberts ($2.70M, 38, 87 base). Both clear $6.30M in salary and recover draft capital. Mogilny at 90 base is under contract beyond this season so he is not expiring; he stays unless a real trade materializes.

### Deadline plan summary

Toronto are buyers. The priority at March 19 is to move Svehla and Roberts for picks, recover the draft capital that blocks the Luongo path, and use freed payroll to add a blueliner or a scoring forward if the right package appears. The Coach's development flags (Spezza, Stahle, Smirnov) are lineup decisions, not trade needs, but they shape the timeline: the young defence is already deep enough that we do not need a deadline blueliner for next year, only for this playoff run.

## League scan

The question this phase answers: who across the league can Toronto acquire to close the toughness gap, the faceoff gap, and the goalie question, given that we own no pick better than a 4th rounder and cannot open negotiations until late February? The shortlist is split into what is reachable now (player-for-player) and what only becomes reachable after recovering picks from over-80 expirers.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 23) is the single best target on the board. 80 overall, 83 TOUG, 64 points in 54 games at 23 on a $1.10M expiring deal. He has improved from 77 base in January to 80 displayed now, with POTE 91 still intact. MTL at 15-30-4 with 14 expiring contracts are in full rebuild and will not re-sign him at his asking price. He closes toughness from the blueline AND replaces McCabe's declining production with a younger, harder player. Any package without Eminger should be tested.

**Havlat** (OTT, LW, 23) at 86 overall, 70 points in 53 games, $900K expiring, is the highest-scoring available player under 25 that doesn't require a first-rounder. OTT at 18-25-6 with $26.01M profit and 11 expiring deals are the most financially comfortable sellers in the East. He doesn't close toughness (64 TOUG), but he adds top-six scoring at an age that fits Toronto's core. Chara is the other OTT target, but the GM vetoed the Chara package over Eminger's cost. If a lighter package exists (Colaiacovo plus a 4th), the Chara conversation can re-open on its own merits.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24) remains the only player at 90+ TOUG, 89+ CHKG, and 83 FACE on a re-signable two-year deal at $900K. CHI at 15-26-8 with 10 expiring deals are sellers. The GM killed the faceoff argument (he plays wing) and designated Abid as the internal toughness fix. That stands for faceoffs. But Abid at 80 TOUG is one man, and the coverage phase confirmed zero players above 80 on the roster. If the coach needs a second 90-point-toughness body on the third pairing, Bell is the cheapest external answer. His production is low: 10 points in 29 games. He is a role player, not a scorer.

**Meloche** (PIT, RW, 28) is the absurd-value find from this scan. 78 overall, 88 points in 82 games, $400K, 1 year, from PIT at 16-24-6 (52 points) with 14 expiring contracts. No structural gap is closed, but 88 points on $400K as a deadline rental means the coach gets a 25-point pace winger for a half-season for essentially nothing. Even a 4th-round pick in return would be overpaying.

**McAmmond** (CGY, LW, 31) at 82 overall, 92 points in 58 games, 83 FACE, $1.40M, 1 year, from CGY at 16-29-6 (42 points, the worst in the league) with 10 expiring deals. He brings secondary scoring AND a faceoff wing in one package. Pure rental at 31 with no re-signing path, but for a playoff run his production is top-six calibre.

**Markov** (MTL, D, 26) at 79 overall, 79 points in 82 games, $700K, 1 year, from the same MTL rebuild as Komisarek. Doesn't close the defensive gap (54 TOUG), but 79 points from a defenceman at $700K is the cheapest offensive blueliner production in the game. If MTL will package him with or alongside Komisarek, the conversation becomes "best player on the worst team in the East" and Toronto should be at the table.

**Kovalchuk and Heatley** (both ATL, both $1.10M, both 1 year) remain the two highest-ceiling available players. Kovalchuk at 92 overall with 92 points in 52 games and 80 TOUG is the most talented player in the game on a moving deal. Heatley at 90 overall with 85 points in 49 games. Both require a first-rounder, which Toronto does not own. They become realistic only after the over-80 expiring mechanic generates picks from Belfour, Svehla, or Roberts.

**Luongo** (FLA, 25, 91 base, POTE 96, $1.60M, 2 years) remains the GM's confirmed goalie target. Florida's demand is Aebischer plus a first-rounder, confirmed Jan 25. Same block as Kovalchuk and Heatley: no R1 in the bank. If Belfour is traded for a pick before March, that pick funds this deal.

**DiPietro** (NYI, 23, 84 overall, POTE 99, $1.10M, 1 year) is the monitoring item the GM asked for. His 21 starts this season: 7-12-0, 3.65 GAA, 0.849 SV%. Those are backup numbers. Last season's 39 starts were better (22-14-0, 2.94 GAA, 0.873 SV%) but still not close to starter quality. NYI at 23-23-3 with 13 expiring deals are borderline sellers, but DiPietro is 23 and expiring — they will likely try to re-sign him rather than trade. He is not a realistic target this window. The conclusion to report: POTE 99 has not translated into playable results yet, and NYI is not motivated enough to deal him.

**Cammalleri** (LA, RW, 22) at 79 overall, POTE 98, 33 points in 31 games, $1.10M expiring from LA at 15-24-6 (50 points) with 13 expiring deals, is the highest-potential available forward. **Frolov** (LA, LW, 22) at 74 overall, POTE 96, 40 points in 34 games, $1.10M expiring, is his teammate and same price. Both are pure development plays: their current production is mid-range but their potential says top-six for a decade. LA's 13 expiring contracts make them the second-most motivated seller in the West after CGY. A double acquisition fills two top-six forward spots for five years.

**Avery** (LA, C, 24) showed up at 90 FACE, 79 TOUG, 84 CHKG, $400K, 2 years, but with only 5 points in 52 games. The prior finding recommending him as the cheapest 3-gap closer needs revision. His grades are useful but his production is fourth-line. He cannot play top-six minutes with 5 points in 52 games. He is depth, not a solution.

The **GM's pick-drought order** is the constraint that shapes everything. No R1 means no Luongo, no Kovalchuk, no Heatley, no DiPietro deal that demands a pick. The over-80 expiring mechanic is the path to unlocking those. Three trades — Belfour, Svehla, Roberts — could recover two or three picks before March, but Belfour's standing order ("Belfour stays") conflicts with this. The GM must decide whether the standing order survives Luongo's arrival.

## Trade construction

This phase asks: given we own no pick above a 4th and cannot negotiate until late February, what packages do we put on the table when the window opens in three weeks? The answer is three deals that stack without overlapping assets, each funded from surplus (scratched players, high-POTE depth we can afford to lose) and each targeting a confirmed seller with a stated record and motive.

**Komisarek (MTL) for Upshall plus our 4th-rounder.** MTL is 15-30-4 with 14 expiring deals. Komisarek at 23, $1.10M expiring, 64 points in 54 games, POTE 91, 83 TOUG is the single best target on the board and the only one that closes toughness from the blueline for five years. Upshall at 21, POTE 99, 87 CHKG, 17 points in 45 games is elite upside from a position where we already have Spezza (POTE 99) and Chlup (POTE 95) ahead of him on the depth chart. MTL gets a 21-year-old winger with a 99 potential and a 4th; they're collecting youth with 14 contracts expiring this July and have no reason to keep a defenceman they cannot re-sign. We save $0.10M net.

**Havlat (OTT) for Colaiacovo plus Tucker.** OTT at 18-25-6 with $26.01M profit and 11 expiring deals are the most financially comfortable sellers in the East. Havlat at 86 overall, 70 points in 53 games, $900K expiring, age 23 is top-six scoring at the age that fits our core window. Colaiacovo at 22, POTE 99, $1.10M, 12 points in 28 games gives them a young defenceman with a nine-year ceiling who already has NHL seasoning. Tucker at 29, 92 CHKG, $1.30M with 2 years is a checking winger OTT can slot into a bottom-six immediately; he has played 3 games for us and the coach has not used him. We give $2.40M and get $0.90M, a $1.50M saving. OTT's profit absorbs the Colaiacovo salary without pain.

**Conroy (CGY) for Chistov plus Safronov.** CGY at 16-29-6 (42 points, worst in the league) with 10 expiring deals are in full tank mode. Conroy at 31, 63 points, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring is the faceoff answer for a playoff run. Chistov at 21, POTE 95, 16 points, $1.10M expiring gives them a cheap young winger to develop or flip again. Safronov at 23, POTE 91, $0.90M with 3 years is a cost-controlled defenceman for their back end. They shed $2.00M and acquire two players with three total team-years of control. We pay $2.00M for four months of 94 FACE; that is the price of a playoff series against a first line that dumps the puck in.

**Timing.** The GM's standing order says negotiations open late February. These are proposals to have ready on Feb 22, not to execute today. All three sellers are still sellers in three weeks.

**If none land.** Ride the season with 85 points and internal fixes: Abid in the lineup every night at 63 points and $0.40M (his displayed TOUG has slipped below 80 per the coverage check, but at his base 80 he is still the best we have), Tucker on the third pairing for his base 92 CHKG, and the over-80 expiring mechanic (Belfour, Svehla, Roberts) deployed in March to generate summer picks. The gap becomes a summer problem funded by the $6.30M Svehla-Roberts salary and the Belfour $6.50M.

## Owed

**The goalie trade window is closed. The Luongo deal went through around January 25 and he is wearing Toronto's number one.**

**Luongo** is on the roster, dressed, morale 99, overall 91 with a base of 91 and no form inflation. He has played 37 games (16-20, 108 GA, 2262 minutes). The trade confirmed: Toronto sent Aebischer plus the first-rounder to Florida for him, exactly the package you confirmed was the only price Florida would accept. Florida now holds TOR's R1 (Q78 confirms it sits at FLA). This fulfills the January 15 mandate: high-90s goalie from a non-contender, done.

**Belfour** is still here: 90 displayed, 92 base, morale 99, 18-3-0 in 21 starts, $6.50M with one year left. He is splitting work with Luongo and Toronto is 38-9-3. Carry both through the playoffs; the renewal question comes in July, and per your standing note he probably won't accept a reduced deal.

**DiPietro** (NYI): 39 GP, 22-14, overall 84 on a base of 79. He is 21, playing every night on a bad team, gaining experience at volume. With Luongo here at 91/age 25/$1.60M/2 years, he is no longer a target. His development confirms the principle that goalies need 35+ starts to grow; Tellqvist at 11 GP and Ouellet at 0 are behind that curve.

**What changed since January 19:** the trade executed. No further monitoring needed for Luongo availability. The goalie target list can be shelved until the 2006 offseason when Belfour's expiring deal clears the logjam.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-06
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-02-06

Next game at TB on Sunday 06 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who on our under-24 group is getting the games his talent has earned and who is being left to rot while we say we're developing.

**Spezza** is the same wound for the sixth time. POTE 99, morale 86 (lowest on the roster), 7.5 MPG, scratched from the lineup, 15 points in 37 games (0.41 pts/g). At 21 with the highest scouting number we have, his minutes have gone from 9.1 to 5.3 in recent windows and he's now not even in the lineup. The other scratched kids have a reason: Koltsov is a trading chip, Upshall isn't producing, Smirnov has POTE 70. Spezza has none of those excuses. Morale at 86 means he's already losing faith.

**Stahle** has moved from zero to two games since I flagged this on January 25th. Two out of 53. POTE 96 at 20, 17 MPG when he played. That's two dressings in a season and it's still not enough. He needs to be in the lineup regularly or he's a wasted asset.

**Safronov** is 23 with 3 games and 0 points. POTE 91 is decent but at 23 with no production and 6% share, the development window is closing on him. He's getting neither quality minutes nor quantity.

**Upshall** is getting his games (45 GP, 10.7 MPG) but POTE 99 has not converted. 17 points in 45 games is 0.38 pts/g, fourth-line output. He's not wasted on games; he's producing below what the scouting number suggests. Scratching him makes sense.

**Alexeev** is the quiet success story. 30 points in 53 games on 8.4 MPG is 0.57 pts/g on fourth-line minutes. At 23 he's earning a bigger role through efficiency.

**Nash** at 20, 32 points in 40 games (0.80 pts/g), 13.3 MPG on the third line. That's a young player getting his chance and paying it back. No concern.

**Gaborik** is 22, 73 points in 53 games, 19.2 MPG. He doesn't need development attention, he needs the top line to keep feeding him.

**Chlup** at 18, 29 points in 42 games on the second line at 14.3 MPG. Already getting top-nine minutes. No intervention needed.

**Smirnov** has POTE 70, the lowest on the list, and 0 games. Less alarming than Stahle because the scouting number is lower. Still worth a dressing or two to evaluate, but not urgent.

## Development trends

The question is who is getting better and who is getting worse between December and now, and the answer changes who I dress in February and who the GM needs to plan around next season.

**Chlup** is the best story on this roster. An 18-year-old at 0.72 pts/g in 42 games on 15.7 MPG, up from 0.62 in 13. Rate climbing, minutes climbing, age 18. He is not stalling, he is arriving. No change needed, but the GM should know he is the second-line centre of this team going forward.

**Chistov** confirms the January trend. 0.29 to 0.48 in 39 games on 15.3 MPG. Getting real ice and producing on it. At 21 this is the right direction and he belongs on the first line.
