**Eminger** is another one moving the right way: 0.35 to 0.58 in 42 games, minutes up from 15.0 to 17.9. At 21 with that trajectory he is the defenceman this club builds its top pair around. That matters because of McCabe.

**Spezza** is the worst development story. Minutes down to 5.3 MPG from 9.1, rate down to 0.38 from 0.43, now 37 games gone. I have raised this six times. At 21 with POTE 99, this year is being lost. I understand the GM's rotation philosophy, but 5.3 MPG is not development, it is a dressing room. If the rotation is the reason, then the rotation is costing a first-round talent. I need the GM to tell me whether Spezza is in the plan for next season or not, because if he is, this pattern must break now.

**Klesla** is going the wrong way at 22. Rate down from 0.50 to 0.38 while minutes went up from 14.6 to 16.0. More ice, less production. Not a crisis, but if this holds past the deadline he is third-pair material and we should look at depth options.

**Alexeev** is falling on both counts: 0.62 to 0.52, minutes from 11.1 to 6.2. At 23 this is not development stalling, it is a player losing his role. If the fourth line can't carry him, we need to know whether he is part of next season or not.

**Afinogenov** at 25 dropped from 1.17 to 0.86 on roughly the same minutes. That is not age, that is form or confidence. Worth watching through February before making any call.

**Fischer** continues to slide: 0.63 to 0.41 while minutes rose from 20.8 to 21.4. At 24 on a four-year deal, the GM's keeper status means this is a planning issue, not a trade one. The contract was priced for the player he was in December.

**McCabe** is in freefall: 1.42 to 0.48 in 53 games. At 29 this is not aging. The top pair next season is Eminger and Colaiacovo or Kaberle, and McCabe's $4.5M needs to be addressed.

**Sundin** at 33: 1.46 to 0.86. The age is arriving. He still carries 19.8 MPG and 0.86 pts/g, which is respectable, but the October version was a 1.46 player and that version is gone. Next season he is a 70-point man if he stays healthy, not the 100-point man we had.

**Mogilny** at 35: 1.62 to 0.88. Expected decline, but the slope is steep. Planning around him means assuming he is a third-line winger next season at best.

**Svehla** at 36: 0.78 to 0.56. GM has told me Svehla is the MVP and his limited games are deliberate rotation, and I respect that. But 0.56 is the number, and at 36 the number only goes one way.

**Roberts** at 38 holding 1.00 pts/g on 19.8 MPG is remarkable. No concern.

**Smirnov** at 20: still zero games. **St. Jacques** at 24: still zero games. Neither has dressed. Both are development waste on the same scale Stahle was, and Stahle has at least played 2 games now.

**Delivering on task #1 (defenceman end-of-season analysis):** Based on this window, the top pair next season is Eminger (0.58 and climbing at 21) with Kaberle (0.57 at 26, stable, 22.7 MPG). Colaiacovo (0.42 at 22, flat) is the third pair. McCabe (0.48, collapsing) should not be on the first pair. Fischer (0.41, declining at 24) is second-pair on talent but needs to recover. Svehla (0.56 at 36) and Salo (0.29 at 30) are depth. Stahle has finally dressed but 2 games at 0.00 proves nothing.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy going into Tampa; one name needs raising, and it is the GM's call.

**Spezza** is the only man below 90, sitting at 86 with 7.5 minutes a night across 37 games. The 80s band costs a point on every grade tonight. He has been in and around 86 for weeks with no meaningful movement, and his minutes confirm he is being scratched in the GM's rotation. This is the standing development plan, not a problem I fix with a line change tonight.

**Mogilny** read 92, down 4. At 35 and 17.8 MPG with 61 points, he is slightly under the 20-minute band for his calibre. The drop is small, still in the 90s, and the load is age-appropriate. No action.

**Sundin** also 96 down 4. 18.5 MPG, still fine.

**Ouellet** carries the biggest single drop at 7 points but sits at 96 as a backup with 8 games. Goalie morale tracks the team's results more than minutes; no line lever exists here.

**Stahle** at 94 down 6 with 2 games played. I flagged him on January 25th as the biggest development waste; the morale drop confirms it but the fix is dressing him, which is the GM's rotation decision.

**Everyone else** is 96 or above with stable readings. The first line, the defence core, Luongo at 99, Richards at 99: nothing to manage.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit suits its purpose, and whether the roster can staff enough roles for a playoff push. The answer: the top units are well-built, the bottom units are thin by necessity, and we have a real checking-depth problem that no arrangement fixes.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, Fischer, Gaborik, McCabe)** is a textbook first line. Gaborik carries the play (94 scoring, 96 playmaking, 97 speed), Sundin quarterback from centre (87/86, 85 faceoffs), and Roberts and Fischer supply the structure (checking 78, toughness 68 and 67). McCabe on the point adds 78 checking and 69 toughness. This unit can score and can be trusted at five-on-five against anyone. Don't touch it.

**L2 (Mogilny, Afinogenov, Chlup, Kaberle, Eminger)** is a pure skill line and that's its nature. Checking mean 63, toughness 59 — Mogilny at 36 and Afinogenov at 86 scoring aren't becoming checkers. Chlup is the only one providing structure (checking 80 best on the unit, 74 faceoffs). The weakness is real but it's not fixable from within. The cost is that we can't roll L2 against the opponent's top line, which is a slot-order matching problem the GM handles before the game.

**L3 (Richards, Klesla, Nash, Chistov, Colaiacovo)** is meant to be the checking line. Klesla is doing it alone (checking 88 best on the unit). The mean sits at 66. Richards brings 95 stamina and 91 clutch — he's a workhorse, not a hammer. Nash is scratched (GM's rotation). Chistov's speed (92) makes him good for transition but he's checking 55 from earlier notes. This unit is softer than its role demands.

**Abid** on L4 is the only remaining checker on the bench (checking 77, toughness 68). Promoting him to L3 would raise the mean by a few points but gut L4 to two players, which is worse than the current arrangement given Nash is already out. I'd leave the bottom six alone and accept the softness.

**Power play units** are well-composed. P1 has two elite skill players up front (Sundin 87/86, Gaborik 94/96), Kaberle quarterbacking, McCabe second point, Roberts net-front. P2 has Mogilny and Fischer for skill and structure. No issues.

**Penalty kill**: K1 (Sundin, Roberts, Fischer, Eminger) is strong — two 78-checkers plus a faceoff winner. K2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Chistov) is serviceable but checking mean 68 is thin. Kaberle on the second kill rather than resting for even strength is a minor question, but he has 93 stamina so it costs him little.

**The roster gap**: Five players carry checking at 77 or above across the whole roster — Roberts, McCabe, Fischer, Abid at 77-78, and Klesla at 88. That gives us one genuine checking line (L1 with Roberts and Fischer) and one partial (L3 with only Klesla). A playoff series needs two shutdown lines at minimum. We don't have them, and no arrangement of these players produces them. This is a February trade-deadline problem for the GM, not a lineup problem.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether the lineup needs any adjustment for Tampa Bay tonight. It does not.

**The matchup math is clean.** Our L1 (Sundin 87, Gaborik 94, Roberts 84) faces their L1 (Lecavalier 90, St. Louis 87, Modin 82). Gaborik is the best player on the ice by a clear margin and Sundin wins the draw 85 to 66. We are competitive on paper and have the single highest-rated skater. Our L2 (Chlup 82, Mogilny 86, Afinogenov 82) vs their L2 (Andreychuk 79, Hlavac 77, Fedotenko 81): we have the edge. L3 and L4 are mismatches in our favour — their third line centres at 69 OVR.

**TB's offence is not scary.** They score 1.80 a game, the lowest in this matchup by a mile. We score 3.90. Their power play is 17-for-156, which is 10.9 percent. They will not kill us with special teams. Their penalty kill has Keefe at CHKG 93 but our PP at 18-for-47 (38.3 percent) has been finding ways all season.

**Goalie.** Khabibulin is their best asset at OVR 92 and morale 80. He will keep them in games. But Belfour's ENDU 94, GSH_ 87, GSL_ 87 and rebound control 88 suit a lower-event game where you need a goalie who doesn't give up second chances. I have no way to check the fatigue icon from where I sit. If Belfour shows tired on the screen, start Luongo at 91 with AGIL 93 — he can match Khabibulin's numbers.

**No change to any line.** The auto-pairing puts our strengths against their weaknesses on every line from two down, and our top line has the best player on the ice. We have won 2 of 3 this season by a combined 18 to 7. The development rotation (Chlup, Nash, Spacek on the lower lines) is already in place and these are favorable assignments — no reason to disturb either the development plan or the matchup.

## Owed

**Standing job #1 — defenceman evaluation for end-of-season decisions.**

**McCabe** at 48 points in 53 games (0.91 pts/g) on 22.2 MPG. Still the anchor. No change from last week. Keeper on the $3.0M x 4 deal.

**Kaberle** at 25 points in 45 games (0.56 pts/g), 20.9 MPG, 80 OVR. The GM's stated keeper and star. One year left at $1.9M — renewal needs to happen this summer but he's not going anywhere.

**Fischer** at 24 points in 48 games (0.50 pts/g), 21.2 MPG, 81 OVR. The contract flag stands: $3.7M x 4 for a 0.50 rate at age 24 is expensive. GM's keeper, I won't revisit. No change from last week.

**Svehla** at 23 points in 34 games (0.68 pts/g), 22.2 MPG, 36 years old, $3.6M x 1. Not dressed. Let the expiring deal play out. GM's MVP, not my call to move.

**Klesla** at 23 points in 53 games (0.43 pts/g), 15.4 MPG, 80 OVR at age 22 for $0.9M x 2. Best value on the blue line. Core piece, keep.

**Eminger** — this is the change. He's at 19 points in 42 games, exactly 0.45 pts/g. On January 26th I set the threshold: "if season rate drops below 0.45 by the deadline, he becomes tradeable on his expiring $1.2M deal." He's hit it. 73 OVR at 21, expiring, $1.2M. Move him at the deadline while he still has a month of season left on the clock.

**Colaiacovo** at 12 points in 28 games (0.43 pts/g), 69 OVR, $1.1M x 1. Young but the ceiling is low. Expiring. Trade candidate alongside Eminger if a buyer wants depth D.

**Salo** at 8 points in 22 games (0.36 pts/g), 30 years old, $2.6M x 2. Not dressed. Dead money with two years left. This is the clearest "should go" on the blue line.

**Stahle** finally played 2 games (up from 0 at my last check). Still 0 points, 34 total minutes. POTE 96 at age 20 and we're wasting him. Development is the reason class, not this week's game.

**Safronov** and **St. Jacques** remain depth. No change.

What changed: Eminger crossed my own trade threshold. Salo is the dead-weight exit. Stahle is no longer at zero games but still nowhere close to enough.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-31

Toronto 37-9-3, 83 pts after 52 games.

## Role coverage

The roster has scoring, speed, stamina and clutch covered. It does not have toughness or faceoffs, and no internal adjustment fixes either.

**Toughness.** Zero players at 80+ displayed. The highest on the roster is Roberts at 73, who is 38. Abid carries a base of 80 but is showing below 69 right now and the coach has him in no unit. Even fully recovered he is a one-man patch. Every contender the Leafs would face in the east has at least two 80+ Tough. This gap is structural and external.

**Faceoffs.** Sundin at 90 is the only centre drawing more than 75. Chlup is 75, Richards 70. The next-best available is 15 points below Sundin, which means on any draw against an opposing first-line centre outside Sundin's shift, Toronto lose the draw. When Sundin is 34 and producing less, there is no successor at all. Also structural and external.

**Checking.** Six at 80+ but two of them (Roberts 38, Svehla 36) are on the back nine of their careers. Tucker at 83 is dressed-or-not-dressed, not lined. Dressing him adds one regular checker today for nothing. That is the only internal fix available, and it is partial.

**Salo** at 88 base and not lined is the same story on scoring depth: he is the seventh-best scorer on the roster and the coach is not using him. But scoring depth is not a gap. The club has 12 players at 80+ in that role.

**Goalies.** Belfour at 39, $6.50M, one year left, is playing 0.911 SV in 20 games. He is covered today. Behind him: Tellqvist averaging 76 across his grades, Ouellet at 86 GSH in 8 games. Neither is a reliable 1A. The Luongo target fits but Toronto own no first-rounder, which blocks the only confirmed price. The GM's mandate to fetch a high-90s goalie stands; the asset to do it does not.

**Age trajectory on scoring and playmaking.** Mogilny at 35 (0.87 pts/g recently) and Sundin at 33 (0.93 and falling) are both declining. Gaborik at 22 with 92 in both scoring and playmaking is the replacement anchor, but the drop from Gaborik/Afinogenov down to the next tier (Richards 85 playmaking, Spacek 84) is steep. Next season's top-six scoring needs either Mogilny/Sundin to hold or new players.

**The two gaps that share one target.** Avery at 25, 93 FACE, 88 CHKG, 83 TOUG, $400K with two years left, closes toughness and faceoffs simultaneously at the cheapest salary of any player who closes either. He is the primary external target. Bell at 24 with 95 TOUG and 87 FACE is the alternative but costs more. No other available player closes both.

## Trajectory

The question this answers is whether the summer that is about eight months away breaks the team or builds it, because 15 contracts worth $25.30M expire together in July 2005 and Toronto hold no draft pick better than a fourth-rounder. The age shape itself is fine: 16 players at 23 or under, 10 in prime, and only five veterans carrying the 30+ band (Sundin 33, Mogilny 35, Svehla 36, Roberts 38, Belfour 39). That fits the manual's 5–7 veteran shape. The problem is not the age curve; it is that three of those five veterans are expiring with pick-returns available and the young core all comes up at once.

**Belfour, Svehla, Roberts** are the deadline's salary dump. Combined $12.80M, all over 80 overall, all expiring, all qualifying for the over-80 expiring-asset mechanic that converts them into draft picks. Svehla at 36 is already scratched; Roberts at 38 has 59 points in 52 games but no future; Belfour at 39 and CONS 50 is the standing order's "trade him, not release him." Three picks, or two picks and one package, recovers draft capital from nothing.

**Sundin** at $8.40M for five years is the single largest commitment on the book and the one that cannot be undone until summer 2009. His production at 33 is 60 points on 20 MPG (0.93 pts/g), declining from 1.13 last season. By 38, the year that contract expires, he is a memory. There is no action here, but the GM should know the number: $42M in guaranteed salary to a player who will produce at roughly 0.7 pts/g by year three.

**Mogilny** is the next problem. $5.50M for two more years at 35, producing 0.87 pts/g (down from 1.62), declining every save. That is $11.00M over his remaining term for a third-liner. He should be moved at next deadline or in July 2006 while he still has trade value. At 37 with 0.6 pts/g he earns nothing.

**Gaborik, Richards, Nash, Kaberle, Eminger** are the five that July must lock. Combined current salary $6.40M; at renewal they will demand raises, but 5–6 year deals at $2–3M each keeps the core under control for the long term. The manual's warning is exactly what is happening: they all come due at once. The only mitigation is locking them all in the same July, accepting the salary bump, and not having this conversation again until 2010.

**Chlup** at 18, $2.34M, two years left, POTE 95 is the cheapest asset on the roster that will not stay cheap. His deal expires summer 2007. By then he will be 20 and producing at top-nine rates. Lock him 5–6 years the day he is eligible. That is a separate summer from the 2005 crisis, which is the saving grace.

**Afinogenov, Fischer, McCabe** carry four years left ($11.20M combined) and expire summer 2008. Fischer's decline (0.63 to 0.41 at 24) means his $3.70M will be a liability by then. McCabe at 29 with 0.52 pts/g in recent games is also sliding. Neither is urgent, but the GM should note that summer 2008 brings back a $11.20M cluster that includes two players who will be 28 and 33 respectively, with uncertain value.

**The money picture:** payroll $65.94M against revenue $73.52M leaves $7.58M in gross headroom before other costs, and profit reads $24.76M. There is room to absorb renewal raises. The young-core locks likely push payroll to $70–72M by 2006; revenue should hold with a contender. The real financial risk is the Mogilny–Sundin–Afinogenov tail ($18.40M combined) consuming a quarter of payroll on three players whose best years are already past or uncertain.

## Calendar

Are we buying or selling at the March 19 deadline, and how do we handle 15 contracts expiring in the same summer?

**The verdict: buyers.** At 83 points, 16 clear of second place, with 30 games left, we are not selling anything that helps us win a cup. We are buying.

**Deadline — open talks late February, execute before March 19.**

**December package** is the anchor. Mogilny's rate has halved to 0.87 pts/g at 35 and the Coach wants him reduced. Moving his remaining years plus the R2 to STL for Jackman dumps a declining salary and fills the toughness gap without spending an asset we need. Sillinger for R3 and Sutton for Safronov+R4 round it out. None of these three deals costs a first-rounder. This is the highest-value action available and it remains unexecuted as of today.

**Conroy from Calgary** is the secondary rental. 63 points, 94 FACE, $2.00M expiring from a 40-point team. Costs Chistov plus a fourth-rounder. Chistov at 21 and $1.10M is the most movable young piece we have if we are not planning a long-term role for him, and the Coach has not flagged him for development the way he has Spezza or Colaiacovo. Acceptance is uncertain but CGY has every incentive to shed $2M for a prospect and a pick.

**Marleau from San Jose** is the highest-ceiling target: 89 base, 78 points in 50 games, $1.60M expiring from 16-23-7. The problem is funding it. Eminger is protected (POTE 99, GM's call on Chara made that clear), Colaiacovo is protected by development need, and we have no R1. The only way this works is if we move Mogilny first and then have salary to absorb. That sequencing matters: December package first, then revisit Marleau in the second week of February with Mogilny's $4M freed.

**Luongo stays blocked.** Florida demands Aebischer plus R1 per the confirmed 2005-01-25 read. We do not have an R1. This cannot happen unless something else changes in February.

**Abid is already here.** No external toughness trade needed. Dress him.

**Svehla and Roberts are the over-80 expiring pick-recovery candidates.** At 36/$3.60M and 38/$2.70M, both are above 80 base and will not be re-signed. The mechanic (player above 80 you will not re-sign trades for a pick) recovers draft capital we currently lack. Propose them to any contender needing a veteran blueliner or winger at the deadline. This is how we get a second-round pick by June.

---

**Summer — the 15-contract cluster.**

**Gaborik** is the first call. 91 base, 67 points in 45 games, age 22, $1.10M. He is the cheapest top-line winger in the league on a bargain contract. Offer 6 years immediately. If he walks in July, we lose a generational talent at $1.10M relative cost. This is non-negotiable priority number one.

**Richards** at 24 and $1.00M: the only centre who can take draws alongside Sundin long-term. Five years. Sign him in the same conversation as Gaborik to stagger from the 2006 cluster.

**Kaberle** at 26 and $1.90M: top-pair D, already producing. Five years. His $1.90M becomes expensive on a six-year deal but he is worth it.

**Nash** at 20 and $1.20M: five years. He is a first-round talent who needs a home. Do not let the 2006 wave carry him.

**Eminger** at 21 and $1.20M: POTE 99, GM's explicit timeline bet. Five years, cheap now, insurance later.

**Colaiacovo** at 22 and $1.10M: Coach wants him in a top-pair build. Two or three years, not five. Let him prove 700+ minutes before committing a fifth year.

**Tellqvist** at 25 and $0.80M: stays per GM order. Two years, then evaluate against whatever goalie we acquire.

**Upshall, Alexeev, Smirnov, Abid**: all under $1.20M. Two-year deals. They are depth, not stars, and the goal is to spread the renewal cluster.

**Belfour** at 39 and $6.50M: offer two years at $3.5M. He will likely refuse. If he does, he walks and we have a hole to fill. The GM's mandate to find a high-90s starter from a non-contender is the real solution here, not keeping Belfour forever. The summer draft is the next window for that (per 2005-01-22 standing order).

**Svehla and Roberts**: if the over-80 mechanic produces picks at the deadline, they are gone before the summer. If not, let them walk. $6.30M combined freed is the budget for a new starting goalie.

---

## League scan

The question this phase answers: which players on non-contending clubs fill Toronto's structural gaps (toughness, faceoffs, future scoring depth) at a price we can actually pay with players and fourth-rounders, given we own no pick better than a 4th?

**Sean Avery** remains the single best target in the league for our situation. At 25 with 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG on $400K with two years left, he closes both structural gaps in one move. LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals are the most motivated sellers in the West. The proposed price from prior work is Chistov plus a 4th, both assets we have flagged for departure anyway.

**Bell (CHI)** is the alternative if LA refuses. 24 years old, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 80 base, $900K, two years left. Closes all three gaps on a re-signable deal. CHI at 42 points with 10 expiring and $25M profit are sellers, but profitable clubs demand real packages. The revised ask without a second-rounder is Colaiacovo plus Safronov.

**Marleau (SJ)** at 79 points in 52 games on $1.60M expiring is the highest-production available player in the league. SJ at 49 points with 14 expiring contracts cannot re-sign him. The gap he fills is not toughness or faceoffs (TOUG 50, FACE 67 rule him out there) but top-six scoring depth as Mogilny fades. At 25 with POTE 81 he is a five-year asset if retained. The package is the open question; Toronto have no R1 and must fund with players.

**Sturm (SJ)** at 69 points in 52 games, 90 SPEE, $1.00M with one year left is the same SJ conversation at half the salary. At 26 with POTE 74 his ceiling is lower than Marleau's but his speed and production fit a top-six wing role immediately. He replaces Mogilny's declining 0.87 pts/g with a 26-year-old producing at 1.33 pts/g.

**Conroy (CGY)** at 31, 94 FACE, 63 points, $2.00M expiring is the pure rental faceoff fix. CGY at 42 points with 10 expiring and $15.26M profit will deal. Costs Chistov plus a 4th. He solves the problem for this spring and nothing beyond it. If we get Avery, Conroy is unnecessary; if Avery is blocked, Conroy fills the hole for the playoff run.

**Cammalleri and Frolov (LA)** at 22 with POTE 98 and 96 on $1.10M expiring deals are the long-term top-six additions. LA are confirmed sellers. A double acquisition fills two top-six spots for five years, but the salary doubles from the Avery-only package. This competes with Avery for the same Chistov asset.

**Komisarek (MTL)** at 22, POTE 91, 53 points in 44 games, $1.10M expiring replaces McCabe's declining 0.52 pts/g with a young top-pair blueliner in waiting. MTL at 42 points with 14 expiring are in full rebuild.

**Luongo (FLA)** stays on the board but is dead at the confirmed price: Florida only accept Aebischer plus R1, and Toronto own no R1. No path forward unless FLA's price changes or another goalie target emerges from a club with a spare starter.

**Svehla and Roberts** are salary-dump targets in reverse: over-80 expiring assets we trade for picks. Combined $6.30M, both over 80, both qualifying for the expiring-asset mechanic.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: given we own no pick better than a 4th and Belfour stays, what packages do we open with in late February, and what does the other GM see when they look at our offer?

**Avery for Chistov + 4th** is the lead proposal and it ranks first because it costs the least and saves the most. We give a 21-year-old winger producing 0.39 pts/g (15 in 38) whom our top-six does not need, plus a pick we would never convert into a player. LA get a POTE 95 speed winger (SPEE 89, ACCE 88) with two years of team control and a draft pick. At 48 points with 13 expiring, they need young bodies for a rebuild. The $700K net saving on our side is the cheapest gap-filler in the league.

**Bell for Colaiacovo + Safronov** is the alternative if LA refuse. We give two defencemen: Colaiacovo at 22 with POTE 99 (the highest on the sheet) and Safronov at 23 with POTE 91 and 3 years of control. CHI at 42 points with $26M profit need defence bodies for a rebuild, and they will value a POTE 99 blueliner. Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 fills Colaiacovo's slot in our lineup, and Klesla at 22 with POTE 97 is the next man up. The risk is that CHI want more than two D prospects from a profitable club; they can be patient.

**Cammalleri + Frolov for Colaiacovo + Chistov + 4th** is the long-term swing. Two 22-year-olds with POTE 98 and 96 producing 1.17 and 1.18 pts/g on expiring deals from a club that cannot re-sign them. LA get a franchise defenceman (POTE 99) plus a speed winger (POTE 95) plus a pick. The problem: both are expiring, so July brings $2-3M each in renewal demands on top of the existing $2.20M, and this package spends the same assets as proposals one and two. We cannot stack it with either.

**Fallback if nothing lands:** dress Tucker (92 CHKG, 88 TOUG, on the roster, costs nothing) and accept the faceoff gap for this spring. The club is 37-9-3; these gaps cost regular-season games, not playoff series against the east's bottom clubs. If we miss the east's top seed, the gaps matter in round two.

markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-31

Next game at FLA on Saturday 05 February 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question: is every young player getting the games his production and the club's own scouting say he has earned? Three are not, and one is being wasted so badly it deserves a second flag.

**Stahle** is 20, POTE 96, and has played 2 games in 52. I raised this six days ago and nothing moved. He is on the second defensive pair in the lines menu but the GM is not using him. At POTE 96 and 20 years old, two dressings in a season is not rotation, it is a player invisible. The rest of the blue line is aging or declining; there is no reason to not at least test him.

**Alexeev** has 30 points on 8.6 minutes a night. That is 0.58 points per game on fourth-line ice, the most efficient young player on the roster by a wide margin. Nash gets 13.0 MPG and produces 0.79 per game, which is strong, but Alexeev is producing at a similar clip on two-thirds the ice. He has earned 12 minutes.

**Spezza** is 21 with POTE 99 and 7.5 MPG. This is the same flag from January 5th: he needs 12+ minutes to justify the POTE. He is currently scratched entirely, which means the GM has been rotating him in for 37 games at 7.5 minutes and then sitting him. Neither state is giving him a real chance. He needs a line and consistent minutes.

**Smirnov** has zero games at POTE 70. The GM's rotation choice, and the POTE is modest enough that I am not pushing him over Nash or Chistov. Flagging him only so nobody forgets he exists.

**Gaborik** at 72 points in 52 games, **Chlup** at 28 points on the second line at 18, and **Klesla** at 52 games and 15.2 MPG — all getting what they have earned. No concerns.

**Upshall** is scratched at 0.38 points per game on 10.7 MPG. His early-January hot stretch has faded. Fourth-line production on fourth-line minutes is exactly where he belongs right now.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers is: which players are genuinely improving and which ones are the roster starting to lose on us, and does anything change how we plan the blue line for next season?

**Chlup** at 18 is the one moving in the right direction in every column. His rate went from 0.62 to 0.71 while his minutes rose from 11.0 to 15.7. He is being given more game and producing more per shift. At 18, that is exactly the development path you want. He is the young centre this team builds around next year.

**Abid** went from 1.09 to 1.30 pts/g on nearly the same ice (20.1 to 19.2 MPG). At 24, he is in his prime and getting better. He is carrying top-nine weight and his production justifies whatever role he gets on Saturday.

**Eminger** needs a correction on my earlier read. His recent window shows 0.61 pts/g in 18 games at 17.9 MPG, up from 0.35 in the first 23 games. The season cumulative looks low because October drags it down, but the recent trend is real and upward. At 21, with 17.9 MPG and a rising rate, he is a first-pair defenceman for next season.

**Spezza** is the development emergency. 5.3 MPG in his recent window, down from 9.1, and his rate fell from 0.43 to 0.38. He is 21 and getting less than five minutes a night. This is a wasted year. The GM knows I have raised this four times.

**Colaiacovo** is flat: 0.44 pts/g in both windows, minutes down from 18.9 to 17.6. At 22, a player with his pedigree should be trending up. He is not growing here.

**Fischer** at 0.39 (from 0.63) on 21.6 MPG confirms the decline I flagged earlier. At 24, the expected direction is up. Instead he is producing third-pair numbers on first-pair ice with four years left on a $3.7M deal. I am not proposing a trade. I am flagging that this contract looks worse every month.

**McCabe** went from 1.42 to 0.50 in the recent window on 21.1 MPG. That is not a dip; that is a different player. At 29, there is no age excuse. The top pair is Eminger and Kaberle heading into next season, and McCabe needs to be addressed in the off-season.

**Sundin** dropped from 1.46 to 0.89 while getting more ice (16.9 to 19.9 MPG). **Mogilny** went from 1.62 to 0.92 on 18.8 MPG. **Roberts** fell from 1.29 to 1.00. All three are producing less while carrying the same or heavier loads. At 33, 35, and 38, that is the expected direction. The question is how much longer the top line has in it. The answer from these numbers is: not much. Plan around it.

**Afinogenov** is 25 and went from 1.17 to 0.89. That is too young for age-related decline. Either his role shifted or something else is wrong. I cannot see per-game lines so I cannot diagnose further.

**Defencemen planning (task #1, update for February):** Kaberle stays (0.60, rising, 23 MPG, 26, star). Eminger stays (0.61 recent, 21, improving, cheap). Svehla at 36 and declining to 0.56 is the first to go. McCabe at 0.50 and 29 is a cap casualty or a trade the GM needs to open. Fischer and Colaiacovo are the question marks: Fischer is the GM's keeper, Colaiacovo is stalling and may need a change of scenery. Klesla at 0.39 and 22 should be sent down or moved; he is getting no closer to being an NHL defenceman.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy; I have no morale emergency before Florida.

**Mogilny** sits at 87 after a -4 drop, and **Sundin** at 91 on the same -4 move. Both get the minutes their calibre should command (Mogilny 17.9, Sundin 18.5), so this is the results talking, not the ice time. Two losses can do that at this point in the season. Winning fixes it over a ten-game stretch; I cannot line-change my way out of a points-streak dip.

**Spezza** is the floor of the roster at 86. He's getting 7.5 minutes in 37 games and is scratched for the current lineup. The GM knows this is deliberate: young players rotating through to develop. At 86 he's uncomfortable but not broken, and the expected 17 MPG for a player at his level is structurally impossible to give him while the rotation continues. I will revisit if he drops below 80.

**Stahle** dropped 6 to 94, but 94 is not a number that needs attention. He's played 2 games and his morale is fine. The development-waste concern I flagged earlier stands, but that is a roster problem, not a morale one.

No change to any line or unit on morale grounds heading into Florida.

## Role composition

Are our units built from the right personnel for their jobs, and where does the roster simply not give me the pieces? The Florida game on Saturday is against a 17-26 team, so composition correctness matters more than matchup-specific tinkering.

**L1 (Sundin, Roberts, McCabe, Gaborik, Fischer):** Correct unit. Checking mean 79 is the highest of any even-strength line, toughness best 89, and scoring 87/99 means they can also carry the play. No reason to touch it.

**L2 (Eminger, Chlup, Mogilny, Kaberle, Afinogenov):** Checking mean 65 is the lowest of any forward line. This is by design — Mogilny, Kaberle, and Afinogenov are all skill-first. The cost is that this line gets pushed into their own end against physical matchups, which feeds the faceoff weakness below.

**L3 (Stahle, Richards, Klesla, Nash, Chistov):** Checking mean 72 is actually the best of any even-strength line, carried by Klesla at 92. The faceoff mean of 56 is the real problem: Richards tops the unit at 73, and nobody else on L3 is above that. When this line is on the ice, we lose the draw and spend time in our own zone.

**L4 (Spacek, Alexeev, Abid):** Abid at 81 checking and 70 toughness is the enforcer anchor. Faceoff best 53 is the worst on the roster, but for a fourth line that mostly kills penalties and provides physicality, it's acceptable.

**P1 (Sundin, Roberts, McCabe, Kaberle, Gaborik):** Scoring mean 87, best 99. Kaberle and Gaborik on the half-walls with Sundin at point is the right construction. No change.

**P2 (Eminger, Chlup, Mogilny, Alexeev, Fischer):** Scoring mean 79, best 91 (Mogilny). Reasonable second unit.

**K1 (Eminger, Sundin, Roberts, Fischer):** Checking mean 78, best 89. Two 82-grade checkers (Roberts, Fischer) with Sundin's overall. Strong.

**K2 (Chlup, McCabe, Kaberle, Chistov):** Checking mean 72, best 84. McCabe carries this. Acceptable second kill.

**Defencemen (duty #1):** McCabe and Fischer on pair 1 is correct — both at 82 checking, Fischer adds 92 speed, and their 84 and 82 stamina hold up on heavy minutes. Klesla at 92 checking is buried on pair 3 with Stahle (who may still be at 0 games). Moving Klesla up to pair 1 would mean Stahle faces the opponent's top line, which is worse than keeping Klesla on the third. The pair order stays. Fischer's recent rate (0.41 in the recent window) is a trajectory flag for the season, not a lineup problem tonight.

**Roster gap — faceoffs:** This is the structural deficiency. Sundin (89) and Chlup (76) are the only two above 70. When Sundin is off, Chlup is the only draw man, and he anchors the offensive line. L3 gets 56 faceoff mean, L4 gets 51. We will lose the zone entry from the circle on 60%+ of draws outside the first line. No rearrangement fixes this — it requires a center who wins draws.

## Opponent matchup

Florida scores 1.6 goals per game. We're 37-9-3, they're 17-26-6, and we've already beaten them twice 8-4 this season. This is a development-friendly game under the GM's own framework: quality opponents get the veterans, games against the bottom of the league let the kids grow.

**Aebischer** will start in their net at 85 OVR. They generate almost nothing (16 PP goals on 135 attempts, 11.9%), so their entire offense is even-strength volume that barely exists. We don't need our best goalie to handle 1.6 per night on the road.

**Stahle** at 20 years old with 96 POTE has never dressed. Florida's third line is Messier (71 OVR), Nedorost (77), Kolnik (72). Our third pair auto-pairs against that line. This is the lowest-risk exposure a 20-year-old defenceman could get in this league. If he can't handle FLA's third line, he can't handle anyone.

**Nieuwendyk** at 38 has FACE 94, the highest on either team. Sundin is at 89. We lose the draw on the top line every time it goes over. But Nieuwendyk's OVR is 81 and his ENDU is 80, he's a 38-year-old who wins faceoffs, not a player who beats us off the rush. Our first pair of Fischer (92 SPEE) and McCabe handles his line's transition speed easily.

**Bure** on their second wing is the only player who could create a problem: SPEE 94, DEKG 92, SHPW 88 on a 75 OVR frame. He's a one-man highlight reel who doesn't produce enough volume to matter. Our second pair with Kaberle (87 ENDU) and Eminger (84 SPEE) is fast enough to stay with him, and their entire line is 73 OVR and under around him.

**No forward line changes.** Our top nine is 267 combined OVR against their top six of 234. The gap is too large for any matchup cleverness to matter. Keep the lines as they are.

## Owed

**The defence evaluation, updated for the Feb 5 Florida game.**

**McCabe** is the one I keep watching. 48 points in 52 games reads 0.92 season-wide, but he added just 1 point in the last 2 games after a stretch of 0.52 in the 27 games before that. At 22.3 MPG on the top pair, if this continues he's eating first-pair minutes for fourth-pair output. I have no reason to move him yet, but February is the month that tells us if October was a fluke or he's the real thing at 29.

**Eminger** is approaching the threshold I flagged. Season rate has slipped from 0.49 to 0.46 (19 points, 41 games). My line was: under 0.45 by the deadline he's tradeable on his expiring $1.2M deal. Two more games at 0 points pushes him there. Keep watching.

**Stahle** is the positive change. As of January 25th he had zero games played despite a POTE 96 at 20. He's now dressed and logged 2 games at 17.0 MPG. That's the first step I was asking for.

**Fischer** sits at 0.49 season rate (23 points, 47 games). Essentially unchanged from my last report. GM's keeper, so no trade talk, but the contract problem ($3.7M x4) remains for future planning.

**Kaberle** at 0.57 (25 points, 44 games) on an expiring deal. GM says keeper. No change.

**Klesla** at 0.44 on 15.2 MPG for $0.9M x2 is the best value on the blue line and not going anywhere.

No changes to the trade list since last time, except Eminger moves one game closer to the threshold.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-30

Toronto 36-9-3, 81 pts after 51 games.

## Role coverage

**Which roster roles are genuinely staffed and which are structural holes that no line change can fix.** This matters now because at 36-9-3 Toronto look dominant on paper, and the regular season hides the playoff problem: this roster cannot win a physical series.

**Toughness is missing outright.** Zero players at 80+. The roster's best is Roberts at 73, followed by McCabe at 73 and Chlup at 70. That is not a usage problem; no coach decision creates an enforcer from a roster with none. The earlier note that Abid is "the internal fix" needs to be walked back: the brief's toughness ranking puts six players above him, and he does not appear. His displayed base TOUG of 80 from January 25 was likely a form-inflated reading. He is a body with 90 durability and 80 checking range, which has value, but he is not a 90-TOUG enforcer. This gap can only close via trade, and **Bell (CHI, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 24, $0.90M, 2 years)** is still the only available player who addresses it head-on.

**Faceoffs are thin.** One player at 80+: Sundin at 90. Chlup and Roberts are next at 75. A team needs at least two reliable centres for draws across four lines, and Toronto barely have one. Richards at 70 FACE is the coach's ceiling here, which is already his L3 assignment. The Bell package would solve this simultaneously with toughness. If Bell cannot be had, Belanger (LA, 90 FACE, 27, $0.70M expiring) remains the cheapest external fix.

**Checking is thin and aging.** Six players at 80+: Roberts 86 at 38, McCabe 86 at 29, Svehla 83 at 36, Tucker 83 at 29, Fischer 82 at 24, Upshall 80 at 21. The top of this list is two men in their mid-to-late 30s. Tucker and Upshall are not dressed; dressing them adds 83 and 80 checking at no cost, but neither is a true top-pair stopper. This is a "need more bodies" problem as much as a "need better bodies" problem.

**Scoring and playmaking are covered but front-loaded on old players.** Mogilny 94/35, Sundin 92/33, Roberts 88/38 anchor the top of both categories. The young spine is Gaborik 92/22, Afinogenov 90/25, Richards 85/24, Spacek 84/19. The transition is underway but not complete: in two seasons Roberts is 40 and Mogilny 37, and the depth drops sharply below Gaborik and Afinogenov. The coach's flags on Sundin (0.93 pts/g at 20 MPG) and Mogilny (0.87 pts/g at 19.1 MPG) confirm the decline is already in motion.

**Durability is thin.** Only four at 80+: Roberts 98, Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92, Abid 90. A four-round playoff run punishes bodies. The drop to Spacek at 79 and Eminger at 75 is steep, and most of the roster sits in the low 70s. This is a secondary concern compared with toughness and faceoffs, but it compounds them: a team that is neither tough nor durable gets battered deep in the spring.

**Goalies are covered for now and for the future.** Belfour at 39 delivers 16-3 with a 2.35 GAA and 0.910 SV% in 19 starts. Luongo's 0.869 SV% in 37 starts looks poor against his grades (GSH 94, GSL 94, REBC 88, BRKA 88), which suggests a form dip rather than a talent problem; those grades are high-90s in the two glove categories. Tellqvist at 25 and Ouellet at 23 with a 1.88 GAA in 8 starts provide depth. The goalie position is the one the GM already had a plan for and that plan appears to have landed.

**The decision:** toughness is a missing role that cannot be coached away. Bell is the single best fit and addresses faceoffs simultaneously. The package (R2 plus Colaiacovo) costs a prospect who is developing, but Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 fills the same slot, and Bell at 24 with two years left is re-signable. Open that conversation in late February.

## Trajectory

**Is this club aging into a cliff?** No. With 16 players 23 or under and only 4 at 34+, the age curve is young and deep. The threat isn't a cliff — it's a July exodus. Fifteen contracts worth $25.30M expire simultaneously, and they contain Gaborik, Nash, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Richards, and Kaberle. If none are locked, the team that wins 81 points today has no core next October.

**The old guard is the easy money.** Belfour ($6.50M, 39), Svehla ($3.60M, 36), Roberts ($2.70M, 38) = $12.80M in expiring salary for players with combined POTE 157. The GM's standing order protects Belfour, but Svehla and Roberts are both above-80 expiring assets that qualify for the pick-recovery mechanic. That's the only path to a first-rounder this club has.

**Chlup** at $2.34M for 2 more years with POTE 95 is the cheapest star contract on the roster and the one most likely to become expensive if a full top-nine season erases his rookie price. He is not urgent in the same way Gaborik is, because he has a year still to run, but extending before the 2006 summer means locking him at something near current value rather than after a breakout.

**Mogilny** is the most dangerous non-expiring contract. $5.50M for year two at age 37, with production already halving from 1.62 to 0.87 pts/g on 19.1 minutes. This contract outlasts his ability to carry a top-six role, and moving him now with two years remaining is a gift no buyer will pay for. The only fix is accepting a reduced role next season and losing the second year's value entirely.

**Fischer** is a secondary concern: $3.70M locked through 2009, declining from 0.63 to 0.41 pts/g at 24. That is $14.80M of dead money if the decline continues, and there is no exit clause. He's not the priority this summer but should be flagged for a mid-term trade if a club overvalues his POTE 90 and 23 points from last season.

**The 30-33 gap is not yet a problem but is close.** McCabe (29, 0.52 pts/g current form) and Sundin (33, 0.93 pts/g declining) are the only players in that age band. In three years McCabe will be 32 and Sundin 36. Eminger, Colaiacovo, and Klesla must become the 25-27 core by 2008, and Colaiacovo's 53% game share at 22 says they aren't there yet.

**The money is fine.** $65.94M payroll against $73.52M revenue with $25.56M profit. Moving the three old-guard contracts frees $12.80M net, even if re-signing all five stars adds $15-20M back over 5-6 years. The profit cushion is wide enough that this is not a money problem. It is a pick problem.

## Calendar

The question is what we do between now and the March 19 deadline and what happens to the 15 contracts expiring this summer. The answer is constrained by one fact: we own no pick better than a fourth-rounder, so every deadline trade must be player-funded, and every summer renewal decision shapes next season's payroll.

**We are buyers in position and sellers by necessity.** At 36-9-3 with 81 points, 14 clear of second, we finish first. We should add for the playoffs. But the Luongo deal needs a first-round pick we do not own, the Kovalchuk package needs a DET second we do not own, and the Chara deal needed Belfour, whom the GM has vetoed. The only deadline currency we hold is old players we will lose anyway.

**Svehla** (D, 36, $3.60M, expiring) and **Roberts** (LW, 38, $2.70M, expiring): move both before the deadline for draft picks. Both are above 80 overall, both are past their primes, and both are gone in July regardless. The over-80 expiring mechanic converts them into picks. That recovers $6.30M and puts picks back in June where we currently have nothing better than a fourth-rounder. Open conversations late February per the GM's standing order.

**Belfour** (G, 39, $6.50M, expiring) is the largest single payroll decision. GM says he stays, and I agree he is the best goalie we have. Offer a reduced deal at renewal. If he refuses, he becomes a third over-80 expiring chip at the deadline, tradeable for a pick, and we get value instead of losing him for nothing. Either outcome is clean. Do not include him in a multi-player package; the GM's veto is firm.

**Mogilny** at 35 has halved from 1.62 to 0.87 pts/g on 19.1 minutes. He is not expiring, so we cannot renegotiate. No trade partner will take his salary without us offering a pick we do not own. Reduce his role now and plan his replacement from the youth group next season.

**The Luongo, Kovalchuk, and Chara targets are dead this deadline.** They do not reopen before March, and March will not change our pick situation. Do not spend time on them.

**The Coach's flags are development problems, not trade problems.** **Stahle** needs real games (1 appearance in 51), **Spezza** needs 12+ minutes (currently 7.5 at 0.41 pts/g), **Colaiacovo** needs a consecutive run. These are February and March lineup decisions, not deadline transactions. Dress them. The answer to the Coach is ice time, not a new player.

**Summer renewals follow a clean split.** Lock **Gaborik** (RW, 22, 91 base, 67 pts/45 GP, POTE 90, $1.10M), **Eminger** (D, 21, POTE 99, $1.20M), **Nash** (LW, 20, $1.20M), **Richards** (C, 24, $1.00M), and **Kaberle** (D, 26, $1.90M) on five to six years. These are the core and they sign first. **Tellqvist** (G, 25, POTE high 90s, $0.80M) signs on four to five; he is the future starter.

**Abid** (LW, 24, 63 pts/49 GP, base TOUG 80 CHKG 80) at $400K is the cheapest re-signing on the roster and the only internal toughness fix. Sign him three to four years and do not trade him at the deadline. **Colaiacovo** (D, 22, $1.10M), **Upshall** (RW, 21, $1.20M), **Chistov** (LW, 21, $1.10M), **Alexeev** (RW, 23, $1.10M), and **Smirnov** (LW, 20, $0.40M) get two to three year evaluation deals.

**Sundin** at 33 has dropped to 0.93 pts/g on 20 minutes, and **Fischer** at 24 has fallen from 0.63 to 0.41. Neither is expiring. Fischer's decline over four remaining years is a trajectory concern; revisit whether he is a trade candidate next summer if the numbers keep sliding.

If Svehla, Roberts, and Belfour move or walk, the 15-expiring list drops to 12, and those 12 split into six long deals and six short ones. The cluster the December note flagged becomes manageable.

## League scan

The league scan answers one question: who on a club likely to say yes closes Toronto's structural holes in toughness, faceoffs, and scoring depth before March. The answer is that three players in particular address toughness and faceoffs simultaneously, and one of them was not on our target list until now.

**Mark Bell** (CHI, LW, 80 base, 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE, 24, $900K, 2 years, 51 GP 19 pts) remains the cleanest fit. CHI at 42 points are clear sellers, he is re-signable, and he closes all three gaps at once. The package (R2 plus Colaiacovo) was already proposed; nothing has changed since January 25.

**Sean Avery** (LA, C, 79 base, 93 FACE, 83 TOUG, 88 CHKG, 25, $400K, 2 years, 51 GP 5 pts) is a new find from this scan. He solves toughness, checking, and faceoffs in one move at $400K with two years left, from LA at 48 points with 13 expiring deals. Five points is the cost; he is a fourth-line centre who wins draws and throws hits, which is exactly what we lack. Cheaper than Bell and from a more motivated seller.

**Joe Thornton** (BOS, C, 94 base overall, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 79 FACE, 25, $4.00M, expiring, 47 GP 73 pts) resolves the discrepancy from January: his base is 94, confirmed at both the Jan 25 and Jan 30 readings. At 89 toughness he becomes our highest TOUG player by nine points; at 90 checking he becomes our highest CHKG; at 79 FACE he is second only to Sundin. He solves the whole board. The uncertainty is BOS: at 21-20-4 and 56 points they may believe they are in the race, and their $27.45M profit removes financial pressure to sell. With 13 expiring deals they could still decide to liquidate, but acceptance is genuinely uncertain.

**Craig Conroy** (CGY, C, 85 base, 94 FACE, 51 GP 63 pts, $2.00M, expiring) is 63 points and 94 faceoffs at $2M from the worst record in the league (40 points, 10 expiring deals). He does not close the toughness gap but fills the centre-scoring hole that Mogilny and Sundin will leave. If Thornton or Bell fall through, Conroy is the fallback centre.

**Zdeno Chara** (OTT, D, 85 base, 94 TOUG, 95 CHKG, 51 pts in 51 GP, 27, $1.70M, expiring) is the highest toughness available anywhere on a confirmed seller. The GM vetoed the Eminger + Colaiacovo + R2 package on January 19 on the principle that Eminger's ceiling matters more, and that logic holds. But if we want Chara's 94 toughness in the lineup for a playoff run, the price must be rebuilt without Colaiacovo. Svehla ($3.60M, 36, expiring, over-80 pick-recovery candidate) plus a mid-rounder is a cleaner structure.

**Jay Bouwmeester** (FLA, D, 81 base, 95 POTE, 21, $1.20M, expiring, 51 GP 19 pts) is the best young defenceman on a seller's market. FLA have 19 expiring contracts, the most in the league, and sit at 44 points. He fills the Colaiacovo-is-sporadic hole with a 21-year-old whose likelihood of becoming a top-pair blueliner is the highest on the board.

**Mike Komisarek** (MTL, D, 77 base, 91 POTE, 22, $1.10M, expiring, 52 GP 59 pts) produces like a first-pair defenceman at 22 from MTL at 42 points with 14 expiring deals. He was already flagged on January 15; nothing has changed.

**Marc Savard** (ATL, C, 79 base, 88 FACE, 55 pts in 50 GP, 27, $1.00M, expiring) folds into any ATL negotiation. Faceoffs plus production at a million dollars from an 11-expiring seller.

**Eric Belanger** (LA, C, 82 base, 97 FACE, $700K, expiring, 51 GP 10 pts) is the purest faceoff fix available. Ten points is nothing, but 97 FACE on a losing club at $700K is cheap insurance for a playoff draw game.

## Trade construction

The question is: what packages can Toronto actually fund, given we own only a fourth-rounder and must not give from thin roles? Three proposals, ranked by value to us and likelihood of acceptance.

**Conroy from Calgary** is the best value on the board. At 63 points and 94 FACE for a rental that costs nothing in July, it's hard to beat. CGY at 40 points are the worst team in the league with 10 expiring deals; they are liquidating. The cost is Chistov, who is expiring anyway and whom we would either lose for nothing in July or have to re-sign at $1.10M+. We give one young player we had no plan to keep and a fourth-rounder. We get 94 faceoffs and 63 points for the entire playoff run. The $900K salary bump reverses in summer when both deals die. Risk: CGY may want more than a 4th for their best player, or may want to keep him for their development environment. Acceptance uncertain.

**Bell from Chicago** closes the roster's single biggest hole permanently. His 88 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 82 FACE at 24 on $900K for two years is re-signable and fills three structural gaps at once. We give Colaiacovo ($1.10M, expiring, POTE 99) plus Safronov ($0.90M, unused, 3 GP). That's $2.00M out, $900K in, saving $1.10M. CHI at 42 points are sellers; Bell produces 19 points in 51 games for them, which is depth. They get a 22-year-old with POTE 99 and BALA 85 who projects as a top-pair blueliner, plus a 23-year-old with POTE 91. The problem is we only own a fourth-rounder, not the R2 originally proposed. Adding Safronov instead of a pick makes the package heavier but eliminates the pick constraint. The coach wants Colaiacovo developing, but Eminger at 21 with POTE 99 fills the same slot. Acceptance uncertain because CHI must value two unknown D prospects over a known (if low-scoring) forward.

**Svehla to any contender for a mid-round pick** is the enabler. He is 36, $3.60M, expiring, over-80 (CHKG 92, ENDU 94). The pick-recovery mechanic says any over-80 player we won't re-sign trades for a draft pick. Every contender needing veteran D depth for a playoff run is a buyer. This creates the asset that sweetens Bell or funds a second move in February. Saves $3.60M immediately. This one should execute regardless of whether Bell or Conroy land.

If none of the Bell or Conroy approaches land: dress Tucker (92 CHKG, 88 TOUG, $1.30M, 3 GP so far) for free checking depth, execute the Svehla pick-recovery, and accept the toughness gap will persist into the playoffs. It is not fatal at 36-9-3 with Belfour in net; it makes every round longer and uglier.

title: Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-30
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-30

Next game at ATL on Sunday 30 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is who among our young players is getting the games their potential and production justify, and who is not. With 51 games in the book and the trade deadline approaching, a kid sitting on the bench is losing a season we cannot get back.

**Stahle** is the one. POTE 96, age 20, one game played in 51. He is dressed on the third pair but never goes over the boards. Every other young defenceman on this club is playing — Klesla 51, Eminger 40, Colaiacovo 27, Ouellet 8. Stahle gets nothing. At 13 MPG in his single appearance he looked fine for it. He needs a stretch of games before February closes the window.

**Spezza** is the other one I am worried about. POTE 99, age 21, 7.5 MPG and now scratched. His rate has slipped from 0.62 in early January to 0.41 now (15 points in 37 games). He is not being given the 12+ minutes my January note called for, and his production is declining rather than climbing. A POTE 99 centre getting fourth-line scraps and being scratched is the second-biggest waste on this roster after Stahle.

**Colaiacovo** is in between. POTE 99, age 22, 27 games at 18 MPG when he plays. The minutes per game are right for a developing top-pair defenceman. The problem is consistency. 53% share means he sits every other night. At 22 he needs 70+ games at real minutes to consolidate what he showed in those 27.

**Nash** is producing at 0.79 pts/g on third-line minutes (30 points in 38 games). He is outperforming his role. The GM's rotation philosophy explains why he is occasionally scratched, but when he plays he earns more than L3.

**Upshall** has gone the wrong direction. 0.38 pts/g at POTE 99 (17 points in 45 games, down from 0.40 at 43). He is not earning a promotion or even a secure spot. I would not give him more.

**Smirnov** at POTE 70 and zero games is fine. The potential does not justify roster space over what is already dressing.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers: who is climbing and who is sliding, and does anyone's trend change what we should be doing before the trade deadline or in planning next season.

**Chlup** is the best story on the roster. 18 years old, 0.62 to 0.67 pts/g while his minutes went from 11.0 to 15.8. A teenager eating second-line ice and maintaining his rate against better competition. He is not stalling and he does not need protecting from anything.

**Spezza** is the worst. 21 years old, 5.3 minutes a night and his rate fell from 0.43 to 0.38. I flagged this on January 5th when his minutes were already at 9.1. They dropped further. My condition was 12+ minutes to keep developing; he got half that. His window is closing in real time.

**Chistov** is quietly earning his spot: 0.29 to 0.39, 9.5 to 14.7 MPG. Both numbers moving the right way.

**Eminger** at 21 is sitting at 0.65 pts/g in the recent window on 17.9 MPG. My January 26th "cooling" note was premature; this is a first-pair defenceman. He stays.

**Fischer** at 24 dropped from 0.63 to 0.41 despite playing more (20.8 to 21.7 MPG). At that age, the expected direction is up. This is the one I flag to the GM as a planning concern: 24 years old, declining output, and a contract that runs four more years.

**Abid** at 24 went from 1.09 to 1.34 on the same minutes. He is becoming a top-line winger and nobody is asking about him. He should be getting more of the game.

**Stahle** finally played one game. My January 25th note said he needed a dressing and he got one. Still needs far more.

**McCabe** needs a correction to what I told the GM on January 26th. I said he "recovered" at 0.96 cumulative, but that was his season average diluted by a 24-game hot start. The recent window (27 games since December) reads 0.52 pts/g on 21.1 MPG. The slump never ended. He is 29, so this is not aging. If he stays under 0.60 through February, the top pair has a problem that no slot-order change fixes.

**Sundin** at 33 dropped from 1.46 to 0.93 while taking on 3 more minutes per night (16.9 to 20.0). He is carrying more ice for less output. That is the shape of decline.

**Mogilny** at 35 halved from 1.62 to 0.87 on 19.1 MPG. He is 35. The question is not whether he is declining but whether we are asking too much of him too late.

**Roberts** at 38 is at 1.04 in the recent window on 20.1 MPG. Still productive, but the minute load on a 38-year-old is the concern for February.

**Alexeev** at 23 is fading: 0.62 to 0.48, 11.1 to 6.1 MPG. He is sliding out of the picture.

**Koltsov** confirmed dead: 0.33 pts/g in the recent window even with his minutes rising from 8.7 to 12.0. More ice for less production. The roster has no role for him.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Average morale is 94, and the only man who stands out is **Spezza** at 86, which is the floor on this roster and the lowest it has been all season.

**Spezza** sits at 86 morale with a +1 tick, 7.5 MPG across 37 games and 15 points (0.41 pts/g). He is a 21-year-old who belongs in the 80-89 band, where the game expects roughly 17 minutes a night. He is getting less than half that. At 86 his grades carry a -1 penalty across the board. ATL is 17-25 and on the road; this is a night where we can afford to put him back in at second or third-line minutes and get him toward 12+. Reason class: morale.

**Chlup** at 87 has climbed +3 recently and is at 14.2 MPG on the second line as an 18-year-old. That is above his band and his morale is recovering. No action.

**Alexeev** at 87 is at 8.5 MPG on the fourth line with 28 points in 51 games. He is slightly under the 10 MPG band for a 70-79 calibre forward, but his morale has been flat or ticking up. No action needed today.

**Everyone else** sits at 90 or above. Belfour is at 94, Luongo at 94 after a +9 run. The goalies are fine. The veterans (Sundin 91 after +4, Mogilny 91, Roberts 94) are all satisfied. The scratched veterans (Svehla 96, Salo 96, Koltsov 96) are at morale levels that tell me they are content with their reduced role.

The only actionable item is Spezza. Everything else is the right room.

## Role composition

Are our units built from players who fit their job? Mostly yes. The structure is sound; the gaps are roster-level, not arrangement-level.

**L1** — Sundin 88 faceoffs, Roberts 81 checking, McCabe 81 checking, Gaborik 99 speed, Fischer 81 checking. This line wins draws, kills penalties, and scores. Nothing to fix. It's the best unit on the team by every category that matters.

**L2** — This is the softest unit on the roster: checking mean 65, toughness mean 60, faceoffs mean 56. Mogilny at 90 scoring and Afinogenov at 88 playmaking make it a skilled line, but against a strong first centre they will lose the draw and get outworked. The fix is not personnel, it's usage: give them softer matchups by keeping them away from the opponent's top line as much as the auto-pairing allows. No change to composition tonight.

**L3** — Richards (72 checking, 91 stamina, 72 faceoffs) plus Chistov (95 speed) plus Nash is a good third unit. Checking mean 71 is the best of our bottom six. This line is built correctly.

**L4** — Only three forwards (Spacek, Alexeev, Abid) with stamina mean 64 and best 73. Abid brings 80 checking, which is the one thing this unit actually has. The stamina ceiling I noted on January 15 still applies: this unit cannot absorb extra minutes. Keep them short.

**PK** — K1 has Roberts (81 checking) and Fischer (81 checking) giving us two 80+ checkers on the first kill. K2 has McCabe at 81. Three of our four top checkers are on the penalty kill. That's well-allocated.

**PP** — P1 with Sundin, Gaborik, Kaberle, McCabe is four shooters plus a puck-mover. P2 has Mogilny for the shot and Fischer for screening and retrieval. Both units have what they need.

**Stahle** remains the development waste. He's listed on the third pair in the lineup but had 0 games played at January 25. If he's still not getting over the boards, that's a dressing that isn't translating to minutes, and the GM needs to decide whether he plays or rides the bench until the deadline.

## Opponent matchup

The question: does ATL's roster or form require us to change anything for tonight? It does not.

**Goalie — Luongo.** He's 92 OVR, morale 94, no fatigue icon showing. Belfour is 91 and carries the same health as always at 39. Luongo starts. No reason class beyond "best available."

**ATL's first line is elite but unmatchable by design.** Kovalchuk (92 OVR, 99 speed/accel/agility, 99 shot power) and Heatley (90 OVR, 98 speed, 97 shot power) together is the most dangerous combination we've seen since Washington's Jagr line. The auto-pairing system means our L1 (Gaborik 95, Sundin 88, Roberts 85) goes against their defensive pair 1, which is now Tremblay (75) plus a call-up since Sutton (76, their top pair RD) is out until April. We face their weakest first pair tonight. That's in our favor.

**Every defensive matchup favors us.** Fischer/McCabe (82/81) vs Tremblay + callup. Eminger/Kaberle (74/81) vs Brule/Foster (72/72). Klesla/Stahle (81/68) vs Boileau/Kaberle (71/73). No pair is exposed. This answers obligation #1 for this game: no defenceman is at risk of being overmatched, and the season-end evaluation stands unchanged — McCabe and Kaberle are keepers, Fischer is a keeper per GM's standing order, Eminger and Klesla are developing on favorable minutes, and Stahle needs game time.

**Stahle needs to play.** He's 68 OVR and sat at zero games played through the January 25th save. He's in the lineup tonight at the third pair against their third pair (71 and 73 OVR). That is the easiest defensive assignment any of our guys will face all season. If the GM has been rotating him out, tonight is the night to start him and leave him in. This is a development call, not a matchup one — ATL's third pair is soft regardless of who we put against them.

**This is a normal night, not an all-out night.** ATL is 17-25-2 with a 14.2% power play (20 on 141 attempts). Our PP at 36.4% (16 on 44) should eat them alive. We're the 36-9-3 team playing the 48-point team. The season series is 2-1-0 in our favor. Development rotation applies: Nash, Spacek, Chistov, Richards all play their normal roles. No reason to scratch anyone for this opponent.

## Owed

The question: which defencemen should stay and which should go at the end of the season. Here is the read after 51 games.

**McCabe** — 48 points in 51 games, 0.94 pts/g, 22.3 MPG. Off his January hot stretch by a hair but still the best offensive defenceman we have by a mile. $3.0M for four more years is a bargain at this production. Keeper, no debate.

**Fischer** — 23 points in 46 games, 0.50 pts/g, 82 OVR. GM's keeper, off the trade list permanently. Nothing has moved.

**Kaberle** — 23 points in 43 games, 0.53 pts/g, $1.90M on an expiring deal. GM's explicit star. His renewal is the one money decision that matters on this blue line this summer.

**Svehla** — 23 points in 34 games, 0.68 pts/g, $3.60M expiring. He's up from 29 games in mid-January, so the GM is using him again for quality nights. At 36 and $3.6M, the question is whether to extend him or cash him in at the deadline for a pick. I lean trade: 0.68 is good but he has one year left and the price is top-pair money for a 36-year-old.

**Klesla** — 23 points in 51 games, 0.45 pts/g, $0.90M x2. Young, cheap, plays every night, 81 OVR. No reason to touch him.

**Eminger** — 19 points in 40 games, 0.48 pts/g, $1.20M expiring. My threshold was 0.45 by the deadline. He's sitting 0.03 above it. One more scoreless game and he's under. Trade candidate at the deadline unless he gets two points in the next four games. This is what changed: he's now within one bad week of falling under.

**Colaiacovo** — 12 points in 27 games, 0.44 pts/g, 18 MPG, $1.10M expiring. Below Eminger now. His production does not justify first-pair minutes at 18 MPG. Trade at the deadline.

**Salo** — 8 points in 22 games, 0.36 pts/g, $2.60M x2, not dressed. This is dead money with two years left. He goes at the deadline. That has not changed from last week, but it is still the most urgent D move available.

**Stahle** — finally dressed and played 1 game (was 0 games on January 25). One step in the right direction. Still the biggest development waste if he does not get to 15+ games by season's end.

# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-26

Toronto 36-8-3, 81 pts after 50 games.

## Role coverage

The question is whether Toronto's 36-8-3 record reflects a roster with depth or one carried by aging veterans, and the answer is both. Every top-tier role is anchored by someone 33 or older, and two roles, toughness and faceoffs, have no young answer at all.

**Sundin** at 90 FACE and 94 HERO is the best player on the club and the only faceoff man above 80. He is 33 with one year left. Behind him the next-best draw is Chlup at 75, and Chlup is 18 games into a roster spot with no unit. The Coach's L4 faceoff mean of 52 is real; no internal fix closes it.

**Roberts** at 38 is the best checker (86 CHKG) and the best in durability (98) on the roster. He is also the oldest player in the league. When he goes, Toronto loses the only man who blocks, hits, and wins draws in the same shift. McCabe at 29 and 86 CHKG is the successor, but McCabe carries 73 TOUG and no toughness grade above it.

**Tucker** at 29 with 83 CHKG and 70 TOUG is not in any unit. **Upshall** at 21 with 80 CHKG is not in any unit. **Abid** at 24 has base TOUG 80 and base CHKG 80 per the Jan 25 note, but today's display puts him below 80 in both. Dressing these three costs nothing and gives the coach a checking floor. Tucker alone at 83 CHKG would be the second-best checker on the club.

**Koltsov** at 92 SPEE and 23 is in no unit. He is the third-fastest player on the roster and producing at 1.09 ppg per the Dec 4 note. The coach has flagged this twice already.

**Gaborik** at 22, 92 overall, 98 speed, and 90 HERO is the future first-liner and has one year left. **Afinogenov** at 25 and 90 overall is the second. These two carry the forward group forward. Behind them the next scoring tier is Richards at 24 and 85 playmaking, then Spacek at 19 and 84. That is a real gap in production-readiness between ages 25 and 33, and it is the reason this roster will not look the same in 2006-07.

**The goalie picture** is clear. Luongo (91 base, 25, $1.60M, 2 years) is the confirmed target. Belfour at 39 and $6.50M is the best in net today (910 SV%, 16-3) but cannot be re-signed at that number. Ouellet at 23 with 918 SV% in 8 games and POTE 91 is the cheap insurance behind Tellqvist. No acquisition urgency here beyond the Luongo package.

**What can be fixed internally:** toughness (dress Abid, Tucker, Upshall), checking depth (same three plus Fischer at 82 CHKG), speed depth (line Koltsov). The coach should do all of these tonight.

**What cannot:** a faceoff centre above 75 outside Sundin, and a true toughness presence above 80 displayed. Bell (CHI, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 87 FACE, 24, $0.90M, 2 years) closes both at once. This is a late-February conversation per the GM's standing order, not a January one.

## Trajectory

The age curve is not the problem. The contract cluster is.

Sixteen players at 23 or under, six at 30 or older — that's right at the manual's 5–7 veterans, and most of those veterans (Belfour $6.50M, Svehla $3.60M, Roberts $2.70M, Mogilny $5.50M) are expiring within two seasons and shedding naturally. The shape is healthy. The danger is that 15 contracts worth $25.30M hit the same July, and five of them are the franchise.

**Gaborik** at 71 points in 50 games, age 22, $1.10M is the single most consequential contract on the roster. If he walks, the team loses its 1.42 pts/g scorer and the ceiling it's built around. Five to six years locks him through his prime. At his production level, he will command multiples of $1.10M on the open market in July.

**Richards** at 51 points in 48 games, age 24, $1.00M is the second priority. Same logic: his production puts him well above his current salary, and he's at the age where the next contract defines his earning. Five years keeps him through 29.

**Nash** at 30 points in 37 games, age 20, $1.20M is the third. He's behind Gaborik and Richards in urgency because he's two years younger, but at POTE 95 and a 0.81 pace, the same July bidding war applies. Lock him on five years.

**Eminger and Colaiacovo** are both 21, both POTE 99, both expiring, both at $1.20M or $1.10M. They're the defensive core of the next five years. Four-year deals split them out of the 5-6-year group and give Toronto two separate re-negotiation points, which prevents the entire young defence from becoming a free-agent group simultaneously.

**Kaberle** at 26, $1.90M expiring, with 23 points in 42 games, is a serviceable top-pair D but POTE 75 means his ceiling is set. A three-year deal keeps him through 29, and by then Klesla (22, POTE 97, already playing 50 games) has taken the top minutes.

**Draft capital is gone.** The query confirms one remaining pick: a fourth-rounder owned by TOR. No first, no second, no third. Whatever the GM wants to acquire between now and the draft must come from players, not picks. That's a hard constraint on every future trade proposal.

**Two picks can be recovered.** Svehla (36, $3.60M, 1 year) and Roberts (38, $2.70M, 1 year) are both expiring assets. If either is above 80 overall, the mechanic lets the GM trade them for a draft pick without a complex package. That's two third-rounders or better, recovered for players the team won't keep regardless. Worth checking their displayed overalls when the GM opens negotiations in late February.

**Chlup is locked and cannot be touched.** Two years left at $2.34M means no renegotiation until summer 2007. The December note about extending him before a full season erases his rookie price was premature under the no-mid-contract mechanic. He's safe at that number for two more years, and at 18 with POTE 95, the team is getting a bargain.

**The money has room.** $65.94M payroll against $73.52M revenue, $24.71M profit. The renewals don't strain the budget; the danger is all at once. Six five-year deals at market-level raises could push payroll past $80M in one summer, and the revenue won't jump to match unless playoff runs deepen.

The two or three moves that protect the next three seasons: (1) stagger the renewals — Gaborik, Richards, Nash on 5–6 years, Eminger, Colaiacovo on 4 years, Kaberle on 3; (2) dump Svehla and Roberts for picks in late February to rebuild the draft capital that the Luongo trade already spent; (3) let Mogilny ($5.50M, 2 years, age 35) and Belfour ($6.50M, 1 year, age 39) roll off naturally after next season, which sheds $12M and makes room for the core raises.

## Calendar

The question this phase answers: what does Toronto do between now and March 19, and then in the summer, given they sit 14 points clear of second place with 32 games left?

**The deadline answer is simple: buyers.** At 81 points in 50 games with a 14-point cushion, there is no scenario where this club becomes a seller. The manual's contending path is buy for need — goalie, blueliner, scorer — preferring young players with potential. The Coach's open gap is a fourth-line faceoff man (L4 mean 52, best 54) and toughness; Abid at 24 with 80 TOUG, 80 CHKG, $400K is the internal fix if the Coach will dress him. If not, Savard (ATL, 27, 89 FACE, $1.00M expiring) or Bell (CHI, 24, 95 TOUG/93 CHKG/87 FACE, 80 base, $900K) close it externally. The Luongo package (Aebischer + R1 to Florida) is the single biggest upgrade available and lands a 25-year-old with POTE 96 on a two-year deal, solving the goalie question the GM set on January 15. Negotiations open late February per standing order; no artificial urgency today.

**Belfour** at 39 and $6.50M is the summer's biggest decision. GM says he stays as number one. At renewal that is a 2-year deal at a reduced figure (GM's own words), which he probably rejects. If he walks, the club needs Luongo or Tellqvist ready. This is why Luongo at the deadline is not just a luxury — it is insurance against Belfour's renewal failing.

**Svehla** at 36 and $3.60M expiring is the clearest let-go. He is old, expensive, and the roster has Kaberle (26), Eminger (21, POTE 99), Colaiacovo (21), and Komisarek (a target) in front of him. Moving him before expiry for a pick or depth is the above-80-expiring mechanic working for us. If his base is below 80, just let him walk.

**Roberts** at 38, $2.70M, declining per the Coach's report, is a let-go. No renewal.

**The young core on 5-6 years at renewal:**

**Gaborik** (22, 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M) is the priority lock. Star treatment, five or six years.

**Kaberle** (26, $1.90M) is the top-pairing blueliner and gets the same star length.

**Richards** (24, $1.00M) gets 5-6 years per the staggered plan.

**Nash** (20, $1.20M) gets 5-6 years. Lock the 20-year-old before his price rises.

**Eminger** (21, POTE 99, $1.20M) — GM vetoed trading him in January. Commit on 5-6 years. He is the defensive future.

**The middle tier on 2-3 years or decide by performance:**

**Upshall** (21, $1.20M), **Chistov** (21, $1.10M), **Colaiacovo** (21, $1.10M): sign 2-3 years, extend once you can tell prospect from bust. Chistov is not the Luongo chip (Florida wants Aebischer + R1), so he stays as depth or moves in a smaller package.

**Smirnov** (20, $0.40M) and **Abid** (24, $400K): cheap depth, sign 2 years or move for a late pick if the Coach will not dress Abid.

**Alexeev** (23, $1.10M): Coach flagged him as regressing (0.62 to 0.48 pts/g, 11.1 to 6.5 MPG) and a trade candidate while he still carries value. Move before the trade deadline if a package makes sense; otherwise let him walk.

**Tellqvist** (25, $0.80M): GM says give him time. Renew 2-3 years at flat salary.

## League scan

The question this phase answers is: who across the league fills Toronto's gaps, and what does each club get for letting him go? At 36-8-3 the club is contending, so the guide says buy for need with young players you keep. But the first-round pick is gone, and that reshapes every package.

**Thornton** reads 94 base with 73 points in 47 games at age 25, $4.00M expiring from BOS at 19-20-4 with 13 expiring and $26.05M profit. The Jan 22 note recorded his base at 76, and the discrepancy is unresolved. If 94 is correct he is the best player available anywhere and solves scoring and faceoffs (80 FACE) simultaneously. If 76 is correct he is bad value at $4.00M. BOS have no reason to keep him with 13 other expiring deals. This is the single highest-upside target on the board, but the data says verify before opening.

**Kovalchuk** at 87 points in 48 games, age 21, $1.10M expiring from ATL at 15-25-2 with 11 expiring. The binary with Heatley (91 base, 80 pts/45 GP, same club, same contract) means ATL moves one. Without a first-rounder, the package has to be entirely players. Koltsov (23, 92 speed, 1.09 ppg) plus Holden plus Tucker plus the 4th-rounder is the best Toronto can offer. ATL at $20.57M profit have no financial pressure, so they need to want what Toronto sends. Acceptance is uncertain.

**Samsonov** at 89 base, 80 points in 45 games, age 26, $1.90M expiring from BOS at 19-20-4. Comfortable seller with $26.05M profit and 13 expiring deals. A LW who scores like a first-liner at a third-liner salary. Package: Koltsov plus Tucker plus 4th-rounder gives BOS speed and depth they can use. BOS are rebuilding and 23-year-old Koltsov is the right age.

**Marleau** at 89 base, 78 points in 50 games, age 25, $1.60M expiring from SJ at 16-23-7 with 14 expiring. SJ cannot re-sign him at that production level. Same logic as Samsonov: young, productive, expiring, from a full rebuild. If BOS take Samsonov for the Koltsov package, Marleau is the fallback with a different offer (Koltsov plus Holden plus 4th works for both BOS and SJ).

**Havlat** at 87 base, 64 points in 49 games, age 23, $0.90M expiring, POTE 84, from OTT at 16-24-5 with 11 expiring. The best young forward on the board who is not a first-round-pick-level player. Fills the top-six wing gap between Gaborik at 22 and the veterans at 33. OTT at $26.87M profit have no desperation but 11 expiring means they are sorting their future. Package: Holden plus Fischer plus 4th, or Svehla if Toronto chooses the dump-for-pick route.

**Zednik** at 87 base, 83 points in 49 games, age 29, $1.80M expiring from MTL at 13-27-4 with 14 expiring. A rental scorer who would give Toronto a second line alongside Gaborik for the playoff push. MTL are in full rebuild and cannot keep him. He is 29, so this is one year of production, not a rebuild piece. If the GM wants to win this spring, he is the cheapest path to adding a 20-goal winger. Package: a depth defenceman plus a pick.
