# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-18

Next game at MTL on Tuesday 18 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether every young player is getting the games his production and potential have earned, and the answer is mostly yes with one clear failure and one stalled decision.

**Spezza** is the problem. 21 years old, 99 POTE, 14 points in 35 games, but only 7.6 minutes a night on the fourth line. He needs 12+ to consolidate development and he has been at half that for weeks. The fourth line's stamina ceiling (mean 51, best 52) means loading him there risks a fatigue spiral. The only path to 12+ is moving him up to the third line or wing on the second. This has been flagged since January 5th and nothing has changed.

**Safronov** is at 23 with 3 games and zero points. 91 POTE. I flagged this window closing in mid-December and it has now closed further. Either he gets a 10-game audition starting now or he is not in the plan and we should say so plainly. Keeping him scratched indefinitely satisfies neither development nor roster logic.

**Upshall** is at 0.40 points per game (17 in 42), below the 0.55 threshold I set in January. The promotion signal is gone. 11.1 minutes on the fourth line is what he has earned now and no more. I no longer consider him a candidate for increased role.

**Smirnov** has zero games and 70 POTE at 20. He has the lowest scouting number in this group. I am not recommending we find ice for him. He is not being wasted; there simply is not a case.

**Koltsov** produces at 0.60 (18 in 30) which looks respectable, but his checking of 55 is the worst on the roster and his speed 99 is redundant beside Chistov at 98. The GM is holding him as a trade chip, which is his call, but that means he occupies a young roster spot while contributing nothing we cannot get elsewhere.

**Nash and Spacek** scratched tonight is correct. Montreal is 13-25, a game we can win within the normal development rotation. No reinstatement needed. Nash at 0.88 in 34 games is excellent production for a 20-year-old and his turn will come on a night that demands it.

**Gaborik** at 1.48 points per game and 19.2 MPG needs no conversation. He is the team.

## Development trends

This phase asks whether the young players are growing into roles or stalling despite getting games, and whether the veterans are holding or falling off. The answer splits cleanly: three young players are clearly ascending, two are stalling in ways that waste their development window, and the veteran core is declining faster than the ice allocation accounts for.

**Gaborik** is the cleanest case of a young player ready for a bigger game. At 22 he went from 1.42 to 1.55 pts/g while his ice rose from 18.8 to 19.6. He is already our best scorer and still climbing. Nothing to change, just protect his role.

**Eminger** is the second. His rate since December 1 is 0.85 pts/g on 18.9 MPG, up from 0.35 on 15.0 in the first 23 games. The season average looks like 0.53 because of the weak start, but the recent rate is real and sustained over 13 games. My earlier note about regression was tracking the season average, not the recent pace. He is a first-pair defenceman now.

**Nash** at 20 went from 0.83 to 1.00 pts/g on 13.4 MPG since December. First-line production. The GM's rotation philosophy keeps him in and out, and every scratch costs a night of that production. Not a criticism of the GM's framework, just the number on the page.

**Spezza** is stalling and his ice is collapsing at the same time. Rate fell from 0.43 to 0.36 and MPG cratered from 9.1 to 5.3 since December. At 21, he needs 12+ minutes to consolidate development and he is getting half that. My threshold from January 5 was: if he doesn't get 12+ and hold 0.60+, the window closes. He is below both numbers. The window is closing.

**Upshall** at 21 went from 0.33 to 0.50 pts/g but his ice dropped from 13.4 to 8.0. He is producing better on less ice, which means he has earned more minutes, not fewer. Something in the lineup construction is pushing him down while he gets better.

**Chlup** at 18 quietly improved: 0.62 to 0.73 pts/g on 11.0 to 14.7 MPG. More ice, better rate. He is growing into the third-line centre role without needing a promotion conversation.

**Chistov** followed the same path: 0.29 to 0.44 on 9.5 to 14.8 MPG. Both of these kids are developing on schedule.

**Koltsov** is confirmed dead. Was 1.10 in his first 10 games, now 0.35 over 20 games since December on 11.7 MPG. More ice at less than a third the rate. My note said the roster has no role for him and that is now beyond doubt.

**Smirnov** has 0 games at 20. Safronov has 3 games and 0 points on 13.7 MPG. St. Jacques has 0 games at 24. Three rostered players getting nothing. If the GM wants to develop them, they need to play somewhere, even if it means rotating them in for a period or two.

**Sundin** went from 1.46 to 0.91 pts/g while his ice rose from 16.9 to 19.3. That is the aging captain pattern in full: more ice to cover a falling rate. At 33, 19.3 MPG in February is going to bite.

**Mogilny** is worse: 1.62 to 0.83 on 16.9 to 18.7 MPG. His rate nearly halved and he is playing nearly two minutes more a night. At 35, this is the end of the line as a top-six winger.

**Roberts** at 38 held better than expected: 1.29 to 1.14 on 16.5 to 19.3 MPG. Only a 0.15 drop despite 2.8 more minutes. He is the veteran still standing, but 19.3 MPG at 38 in the final third of the season is asking a lot.

**McCabe** collapsed from 1.42 to 0.64 on 23.7 to 20.7 MPG. That is not aging at 29. He is below Eminger (0.85) and Colaiacovo (0.50) in points-per-game while still getting second-most blue-line ice. His contract and his role both need to be addressed by the GM before February.

**Svehla** at 36 went from 0.78 to 0.50 on 23.8 to 20.5 MPG. The GM calls him the MVP and the reduced games are rotation. Fair. But the rate is declining and 20.5 MPG at his age in February is risky. He is still productive, just less so.

**Kaberle** is the steady one: 0.54 to 0.56 on 19.4 to 22.6 MPG. More ice, same rate. The GM is right that he is a star.

**Defencemen end-of-season outlook (obligation #1, second delivery):** The pair for the rest of the season is Kaberle-Eminger, full stop. Eminger at 0.85 since December outplays McCabe at 0.64 and Fischer at 0.45 by a wide margin. Fischer stays because the GM says so, but he belongs on the second pair, not the first. Svehla and Salo are depth and should be planned around as departing at season end. McCabe's collapse makes him a trade candidate on value, not on age. Klesla is flat at 0.45 and Colaiacovo is developing at 0.50, so there is no rush to replace depth.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy. Most of the roster sits at 96 and climbing, which tells me the recent wins are doing the work. One player needs more ice to keep him from sliding, and one dip I cannot fix.

**Spezza** is the one I would move. He's at 86 morale with 7.6 minutes a night. A 21-year-old scoring at 0.62 points per game (14 in 35) is not a 7-minute depth piece. Even if his grade sits in the 70s, the expectation is 10 a night; at 80 he'd want 17. He's below any band. The +1 this save is noise. He's been drifting at 86 for weeks while his production climbs. Give him 12-plus by sliding him up to third-line centre or taking minutes from Chlup's unit.

**Chlup** at 86 and +3 needs no intervention. He's an 18-year-old at 13.3 minutes with 24 points in 35 games. He's getting more than a player his age should reasonably expect. His morale is low relative to the room, not low relative to his ice time. If it keeps creeping up (already +3), leave him alone.

**Alexeev** at 89 and 8.9 MPG is marginally under the 10-minute mark for a 23-year-old on the fourth line producing at 0.54. Minor. One power-play shift or a few more even-strength shifts per game would nudge him over without touching anyone else's role. I would not make a fuss.

**Safronov** dropped 5 to 95. He's played 3 games all season and sits out. That's the GM's rotation choice, not a problem I can solve with a line change. At 95 he's still fine; if it drops below 90 I'll raise it as a dressing decision.

**Mogilny** at 89 with 17.7 MPG is in the right spot for his minutes. The slight low reading is results-driven or age-driven at 35, not something ice time fixes. He's producing 1.29 points per game. Leave him.

No one else in the room needs anything.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit is built from players whose attributes suit its job. The answer is yes, with one structural gap behind the top six that no lineup fix solves.

**L1 (Sundin-Roberts-Mogilny / McCabe-Fischer)** is correct. Sundin at 90 faceoffs anchors the draw, Roberts at 82 checking and 71 toughness is the muscle Mogilny needs beside him, and McCabe/Fischer at 83 checking are the best D we have. This line can win draws, forecheck, and kill. It's doing what it should.

**L2 (Richards-Gaborik-Afinogenov / Eminger-Svehla)** has a faceoff ceiling of 74 from Richards, and the unit mean drops to 60. Gaborik and Afinogenov don't take draws. Richards at 74 loses the dot against centres above that, which happens against most first and second centres. His 93 checking best is genuine though, so he can still play without winning the draw. Against Montreal's centre group tonight this is probably fine, but it's the weakest point across four lines.

**L3 (Chlup-Koltsov-Chistov / Colaiacovo-Klesla)** is a speed line, not a checking line. Checking mean 66 is the worst on the roster. Speed mean 90 is the best. Chistov at 97 and Koltsov at 99 on the same wing pair wastes one of them. Koltsov's checking at 55 is the worst number on the roster by twelve points. But the GM wants him dressed as a trade showcase, and Chlup at 77 faceoffs is our second-best draw winner so he belongs at centre. This line cannot grind, should not take defensive-zone draws, and gets short shifts because stamina 56 mean means it dies under load.

**L4 (Alexeev-Spezza-Upshall)** is development by design. Faceoffs 52 mean, stamina 50 mean, checking 63 mean. None of these players can be asked to do anything except skate short shifts and not make mistakes. The GM's rotation philosophy protects them from bigger burdens. Correct.

**Power play** is well-built. P1 gets Gaborik (98 scoring, 84 stamina) and Sundin (92, 90 faceoffs) for both net-front presence and zone-entry ability. P2 puts Mogilny and Svehla together — Svehla at 93 checking best can keep the puck, Mogilny at 90 scoring can finish. These are fine.

**Penalty kill** puts Mogilny on K1 alongside Roberts and Fischer. The unit mean checking is 75, which is adequate. Mogilny's hands help clear the zone. The trade-off is he's not resting between shifts, but against a 13-25 Montreal club we won't see enough PK to worry about his legs. No change.

**The gap the GM needs to hear:** we have one checking answer. Roberts at 82, McCabe at 83, Fischer at 83. Tucker at 80 is the next man up and he's the one the GM keeps on the roster as "our checking guy." If we face a first line that pushes hard — think Ottawa or Philadelphia in a series — we can deploy one shutdown unit and nothing else. There is no second pairing or second forward line with mean checking above 70 outside L1. That's a roster problem, not a coaching one.

## Opponent matchup

**Does this opponent demand a change to our lines?** No. MTL is 13-25-4, allowing 3.40 goals per game. We are 34-8-1, scoring 4.40 per game. The talent gap is not closable by any adjustment either bench makes.

**Gaborik vs their blue line** is the game. He is at 96 OVR with SPEED, ACCELERATION, and AGILITY all at 99. Their best defenceman, Komisarek, reads 80 with CHKG 90 but only 87 SPEE. He cannot track a man that fast. Their second-pair Markov at 79 is worse still. We should expect Gaborik's line to dominate their second pair all night.

**Ricci and Corson** are their checking line (CHKG 88 and 84 respectively). They will be thrown at our top line. Roberts at 38 with ENDU 69 and Mogilny at 35 with ENDU 73 will feel that in the third period. But there is no better personnel available to shelter them, so we ride it out.

**Gratton at FACE 88** wins draws against Chlup at 77 on the third line. This was already true before this opponent. Against Gratton's line-mates (Hoglund at ACCU 50, Dackell at 73 OVR) the lost draw barely matters -- they cannot convert the puck they win.

**Theodore at 89** is the one thing keeping this team competitive. His SSH_ at 92 means he smothers first chances. We need traffic and rebounds. Our PP at 29.7% against a team that allows 3.40 per game should break through regardless.

**Goalie:** Belfour at 92 starts. Road game, we want the veteran. Tellqvist is not needed here.

**Development rotation:** MTL at 13-25 is not a quality opponent. Per the GM's framework, this is a night where we can afford development minutes. The current lineup already has Spezza, Upshall, Alexeev, Koltsov, and Chlup carrying the bottom six. No need to recall Nash or Spacek.

## Owed

The defense analysis for end-of-season moves, delivered for the Montreal game.

**McCabe has recovered.** I flagged his rate collapse from 1.42 to 0.80 on January 4th. He is now at 48 points in 46 games, which is 1.04 pts/g. He's back on the pace that made him our top pair. The panic is over and the first pair is settled for the season.

**No new candidates to move.** The picture is the same as my last delivery with two small refinements:

**Salo** remains the clearest trade candidate. 30 years old, 81 OVR, 8 points in 21 games (0.38 pts/g), $2.60M x2 years, not even dressing. He is dead money and a body we cannot use. The only question is whether any club will take on two years and $5.2M for a third-pairing defenceman.

**Eminger** at 19 points in 36 games (0.53 pts/g) has settled into what he is: a cheap top-six-minute defenceman at 21 and $1.20M. His contract is expiring. Re-sign or move by February -- but he has value as a depth piece at that price, so there's no rush to sell.

**What hasn't changed:** Fischer is a keeper per your instruction, Svehla is a keeper per your instruction, Kaberle must be re-signed before he walks as a free agent (26, 82 OVR, 0.55 pts/g, $1.90M expiring). Klesla at $0.90M x2 and 0.48 pts/g at 22 is the best value on the blue line. Colaiacovo (0.48 pts/g, 21, $1.10M) is still developing and costs nothing.

title: Coach's report — run 10, in-game 2005-01-15
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 10, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they've earned, and the answer is split: most are fine, two are being wasted, and one is being carried past the point of usefulness.

**Spezza** is the clearest case on the sheet. 99 POTE, 21 years old, 7.8 MPG on the fourth line. He has 14 points in 34 games, which is 0.41 per game on a tiny minutes base, and his morale at 86 is tied with Chlup for the lowest in this group. The L4 stamina ceiling (mean 51, best 52) means I cannot simply slide him to 12+ there without a fatigue risk. The fix has to be a line promotion, not a minutes increase on the same unit. He should be the third-line centre, with Chlup shifting to the wing where his 18-year-old legs handle the defensive responsibility more naturally than Spezza's game suits fourth-line work.

**Safronov** at 23, 3 games, 0 points, 13.7 MPG in those appearances, and a 91 POTE is the same flag I raised on December 15th and nothing has changed. Three games in 45 means the coaching staff is not choosing him, and the GM is not choosing to move him. At 23, the development window does not reopen in September. He needs to be named in with real minutes or released so another club can use him.

**Smirnov** at 20 with 0 games and POTE 70 is the exception where youth does not justify the roster spot. POTE 70 is the lowest in this group and at zero games over 45 he has not demonstrated anything the coaches can work with. He is not being wasted; he is occupying a spot that another body could fill.

**Upshall** at 41 GP and 11.4 MPG is close to the 12+ he earned last month. His 17 points in 41 games (0.41 per game) and 91% share show the coaches trust him. No change, but he is one step from the threshold and I want him there.

**Chlup** at 18 with 23 points in 34 games on 13.3 MPG is getting a generous look for his age. His 0.68 per game rate is the best among our young centres by a wide margin. Morale at 86 suggests he wants more, but the L3 stamina ceiling caps what the line can absorb regardless of his personal capacity. If Spezza moves to L3C, Chlup on the wing gets a role that suits his game without demanding more minutes from a line that cannot give them.

**Nash** and **Spacek** are scratched per the GM's deliberate rotation, not because they have not earned minutes. Nash at 0.88 pts/g in 34 games and Spacek at 0.61 in 23 are both producing. That is a development rotation choice, not a performance issue.

**Koltsov** at 0.62 pts/g on 10.5 MPG and 29 games is a fair use of a player whose checking at 55 eliminates him from any defensive role. He is not being wasted and he is not being overplayed. At 23, this is who he is.

No change needed for Gaborik (67 points in 45 games, 19.3 MPG), Klesla (45 games, 15.2 MPG, iron man), Alexeev (25 points in 45 on the fourth line), Colaiacovo (12 points in 24 games on 17.9 MPG with 99 POTE), Eminger (19 points in 35 on 16.5 MPG), or Chistov (11 points in 31, reasonable for his role).

## Development trends

The question here is who is rising and who is falling between December 1st and today, and whether any of those trends should change the GM's plans for this season or next. No grades moved on the card in this window, so every claim rests on production and minutes.

**Chlup** is the best young story. 0.62→0.71 pts/g on 11.0→14.7 MPG at 18 years old. Rate up, ice up, no ceiling in sight. He's already the first-line centre and he's still growing into it. No action needed beyond keeping him where he is.

**Nash** at 0.83→1.00 pts/g on 12.9→13.4 MPG is the most complete young forward on the roster. The GM rotates him out to give others games, and I respect that, but at 1.00 pts/g in 34 games he's the one whose trend should worry us most if we lose him to a trade deadline deal.

**Gaborik** at 1.42→1.57 on 20.0 MPG at 22 is still getting better. No concerns. **Richards** at 1.08→1.14 on 19.0 MPG is the same, quieter. Both are on contracts the GM should be thinking about extending well before they expire.

**Spezza** is the development emergency. 0.43→0.38 pts/g on 9.1→5.7 MPG. Both numbers falling. At 5.7 minutes a night he's not developing, he's rusting. The window at 21 is closing. The GM's rotation is the mechanism but the effect is the same: Spezza is losing his second-line window while sitting on the fourth line for five minutes a game.

**Upshall** is borderline. 0.33→0.53 pts/g on 13.4→8.5 MPG. The rate jumped, which earned him more, but the GM's rotation cut his ice to 8.5 instead. My threshold was 0.55. He's at 0.53. If he clears it by February the promotion is confirmed. If he doesn't, the rotation has killed his development the same way it is killing Spezza's.

**Spacek** at 0.55→0.67 pts/g but 16.0→10.2 MPG has a similar problem. His rate is improving when he plays but his minutes are slashed by 36 percent. At 19 that's recoverable. At 21 it would not be.

**Eminger** needs a correction to my own earlier note. The brief shows 0.35→0.92 pts/g since December 1st in 12 games. The 0.54 season rate is dragged down by the first 23 games at 0.35. His recent form is 0.92, which is still a first-pair breakout. The regression I flagged was the blending of the early season, not a collapse in current play. He belongs on the first pair.

**Sundin** at 1.46→0.90 on 16.9→19.0 MPG is the classic aging pattern I flagged in December: more ice, less production. He's 33 and the load is shifting onto him because the young guys aren't ready yet. **Mogilny** at 1.62→0.76 on 18.0 MPG at 35 is worse. More than halved. He can no longer be part of a top-six plan. **Roberts** at 1.29→1.10 on 18.8 MPG at 38 is holding, and at 38 a 0.19 decline is nothing.

**McCabe** continues to confirm the collapse. 1.42→0.67 on 23.7→20.3 MPG at 29. That's not aging. That's a player whose game has changed for reasons I can't see from here. At 29 he's still tradeable. By February the 0.67 may be the real number and his value is gone.

**Fischer** at 0.38 pts/g on 21.1 MPG at 24 is confirmed structural failure. The rate has not recovered in 20 games since I first flagged it. He needs to come off the first pair permanently.

**Svehla** at 0.78→0.45 on 20.9 MPG at 36 continues his slide. Done as a first-pair defenceman. **Salo** at 0.40→0.33 on 16.8 MPG at 30 is a mild version of the same.

**Kaberle** at 0.54→0.56 on 22.6 MPG is the blueliner holding steady while everyone around him collapses. At 26 he's the only defenceman whose production and minutes are both moving in the right direction.

**Koltsov** at 1.10→0.37 on 11.5 MPG confirms the role elimination. **Alexeev** at 0.62→0.48 on 6.8 MPG at 23 is declining in both rate and ice. At 23, 6.8 minutes and falling is a sign the coaching staff doesn't trust him, which means the GM should be asking whether he's in the future here.

**Safronov** finally appeared: 3 games, 13.7 MPG, 0 points. That's not enough to judge. The 91 scouting number is still a question mark until he plays 10 or more.

### Defencemen trade list for season end

The GM asked me to update this every game. Here is where we stand as of January 15th:

Trade: **Svehla** (36, 0.45, 20.9 MPG, expiring soon or low-value). Trade: **McCabe** (29, 0.67, collapsing). Trade: **Fischer** (24, 0.38, structural failure, no recovery in 20 games). **Salo** (30, 0.33) is fourth if a deal exists.

Keep: **Kaberle** (26, steady, 22.6 MPG), **Eminger** (21, 0.92 recent), **Colaiacovo** (21, 0.53 and climbing), **Klesla** (22, 0.43, depth), **Safronov** (23, watching).

That leaves five or six blueliners for next season depending on Safronov, which is workable if the three trades come through.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: average morale 96, almost nobody moved. One player has a genuine minutes problem, and one has a role problem that isn't mine to fix.

**Spezza** is the case. Morale at 86, down 4 from the last save. He's 21, dressed on the fourth line at 7.8 minutes a night in 34 games. At his calibre (useful depth man, 70s range) the game expects 10. He's two minutes short and his morale just dipped for the first time this season. He's producing 14 points in 34 games, which at 0.41 has cooled from where it was in early January. Moving him to third-line centre would put him at 11-13 MPG, close his gap, and give his development the minutes it needs. This is the same call I made January 8 that wasn't taken.

**Aebischer** sits at 81, the lowest on the roster, and hasn't moved. He's the backup goalie, scratched the last stretch. That's not a minutes problem a line change fixes — it's a role problem. Belfour is playing and Tellqvist is the other body. Unless the GM wants to shuffle the crease rotation, Aebischer stays where he is. That's his to decide.

**Safronov** dropped 5 from 100 to 95. With 3 games played and a scratched status, this is a new-player number regressing to normal, not a problem. At 95 he's fine.

Everyone else is at 89 or above, and the veterans on the top lines (Sundin at 17.9, Mogilny at 17.4, Roberts at 17.6) are all getting roughly what their bands call for. No one is carrying more than they should. No change needed beyond Spezza.

## Role composition

**The question here is whether each unit's personnel matches its job, and where the roster simply doesn't have the bodies to fill a role.** The answer: L3 is constructed wrong, Koltsov belongs nowhere on this roster, and we have no third faceoff centre or shutdown forward in any arrangement.

**L3** is built from three of our four fastest players (Koltsov 99, Chistov 98, line mean 91 speed) and the result is a line with no identity. Checking mean 67, toughness mean 62, clutch mean 58, stamina ceiling 68. This line cannot close, cannot kill, cannot win a draw (faceoff mean 59), and has no body to hit anyone. Klesla at 91 scoring is the only forward asset, and he's doing it on a line that can't create zone time because nobody can win the puck cleanly. The line is fast at everything except being hard to play against.

**Koltsov** at checking 55 is the worst on the roster. His 99 speed is redundant sitting next to Chistov at 98 on the same line. His production recovered to 0.62 pts/g but that's not saving him, it's the line's speed carrying him in open ice. A checking 55 forward on a third line with no other checker and no stamina ceiling is structurally wrong regardless of the scoresheet. This is the one composition change I'd force.

**Tucker** at 81 checking, 69 toughness, is our fourth-best forward checker and he's scratched. If he's healthy he is the answer to L3's identity problem. He can't score, but he can hit, clear the crease, and take the draws L3 can't win.

**Faceoff depth** is a roster gap we can't arrange around. Sundin 89, Roberts 76, Richards 75, and then Chlup the defenceman at 78. Koltsov's faceoff doesn't show in the top four. After our top two centres, we have nobody who wins draws at the next level. Opposing coaches will know this by February.

**Penalty kill overloads two aging men.** Svehla (36, 94 checking) is on K1, P2, and L2. Mogilny (37) is on K1, P2, and L1. Both are carrying minutes on units that drain them with no youth to relieve. K2 (Eminger, McCabe, Richards, Chistov) is the only other unit and it leans on McCabe's 94 checking and Richards' 87 stamina. If either Svehla or Mogilny gets a knock, we have no replacement PK quarterback.

**P1 and P2 are fine.** Gaborik at 99 scoring and 99 clutch is the one-timer man. P2 has Mogilny 92 scoring and Richards 90 playmaking. The units are structured correctly for what they do.

**Defensive pairings from a role standpoint are sound.** McCabe/Fischer as the first pair gives us the top two forward-grade checkers (84/84, shown as 90 best on L1). Svehla at 94 anchoring the second pair is the right structural use of him. The production has collapsed (McCabe 0.80, Fischer 0.15) but the role fit is correct. I'm not moving them this activation; I'd rather diagnose the production issue separately than create a defensive scramble.

## Opponent matchup

The question this phase answers: does Washington warrant going all out and reinstating Nash and Spacek, or is this a normal development night?

**WSH's 12-for-122 power play** is the fact that decides it. They generate 2.77 power-play chances per game, more than anyone, but convert at 9.8%. Our PK has surrendered 6 PP goals in 45 games. Their single structural advantage is neutralized by their own inability to finish. This is not a game that demands extra bodies.

**Sundin's line vs Jagr's line.** Jagr at 89 OVR with 99 speed and 99 deking is the best player on their side. Lang at centre reads 66 faceoff, which means Sundin at 89 wins those draws. Dupuis at 79 is serviceable but not dangerous. Our top line matches or exceeds theirs, and this is exactly the matchup Sundin/Roberts/Mogilny were built for. No change needed.

**Richards' line vs Bondra's line.** Halpern at 85 faceoff versus Richards at 75 is a draw we lose, but that is the faceoff-center-gap I flagged in December. It is not fixable tonight. Bondra at 86 with 93 speed is legitimate, but Gaborik at 97 is not outmatched by anyone on their roster. The second-line matchup favors us.

**Their bottom two lines are ordinary.** Metropolit at 68, Gamache at 66, Belak at 68. Our third and fourth lines can handle those assignments without help from players above them. The depth that Nash and Spacek would provide is not the depth this matchup requires.

**Defenceman matchup.** Gonchar at 83 with 93 shot power and 88 passing is their offensive weapon from the point. Our first pair (McCabe/Fischer) should take that assignment. Fischer's structural failure (0.15 pts/g) is a season problem, not a Monday problem. Against their second pair (Yonkman/Doig, both 75) and third pair (Fortin at 66, Belak at 68), we have no reason to be short.

**My call to the GM:** keep the development rotation. WSH at 23-14-5 is beatable with the current lineup. Their power play is a non-factor. Do not reinstate Nash and Spacek for this one.

**Obligation #1 — defenceman analysis.** I cannot fulfill this as stated. I have season totals and attributes, not per-game lines. Nobody has tracked who was on the ice for which goal. What I can say from the season picture: Fischer's 0.15 pts/g on first-pair minutes is the worst number on the blue line and he is the most obvious trade candidate if the rate does not recover. Svehla at 36 and 0.40 pts/g is the next one out. Eminger has regressed from his December breakout (now 0.54) and needs to hold 0.65 through February or he is cheap depth. McCabe, Klesla, and Colaiacovo are the three I would build around.

## Owed

**Defenceman review, first delivery.** Here's where every blue-liner stands and what's moved since my last notes.

**McCabe** has recovered. Season rate is now 48 points in 45 games, 1.07 pts/g, up from the 0.80 I flagged on January 4th. At 29 on $3.0M x 4 he's the keeper. No change needed.

**Fischer** is up from 0.15 to a season rate of 0.50 pts/g in 40 games. He's back from the collapse but his problem is the contract, not the production: 0.50 on $3.7M x 4 is a second-pair player on a first-pair salary. He's the one to try and move if the market gives anything for 4 more years of 84 OVR.

**Svehla** reads 19 points in 29 games, 0.66 pts/g, but he's played 29 of 45 and he's 36 on $3.6M x 1. Season average is propped up by October. He's the clearest trade candidate at the deadline for any prospect or pick.

**Eminger** is still at 0.54 pts/g (19 in 35) on $1.2M x 1. I set a 0.65 threshold by February for him to stay. He's on the watch list, not the sell list yet.

**Klesla** is the finding nobody's talking about. 0.47 pts/g at 22 on $0.9M x 2 with 15.2 MPG. He's a cheap, young, stay-at-home who pairs with anyone. Keep him in all scenarios.

**Colaiacovo** at 0.50 pts/g in 24 games at 21 on $1.1M x 1 is a development piece. Keep unless an offer is absurd.

**Salo** is 0.38 pts/g in 21 games on $2.6M x 2 and not dressed. Second sell candidate after Svehla if we can move him.

What's changed: McCabe recovered (was collapsing, now fine), Fischer improved but the contract is the problem not the play, Svehla remains the sell. Nothing else moved.

# Coach's report — run 9, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether every young player is getting the games he has earned, and the answer splits three ways: four young men are earning every minute they get, three are being underused or left in limbo, and two are not earning what they have.

**Nash** is at 30 points in 34 games (0.88 pts/g) at age 20, the most productive young player on this roster, and he is sitting. The GM made this choice deliberately on January 15th to open slots for others, and I respect it. But no slot has been filled by someone producing at Nash's level, so the question for Monday is whether WSH justifies going all out.

**Spacek** at 14 points in 23 games (0.61 pts/g) is the same story at age 19. Deliberately scratched, producing at a second-line rate. Same call as Nash for this opponent.

**Spezza** is the urgent one. 14 points in 34 games at age 21 is 0.41 pts/g on 7.8 minutes a night. I set thresholds at 12 MPG and 0.60 pts/g on January 5th. He is below both, and his rate has dropped from 0.62 to 0.41 since that note. At this usage his development is stalling. He needs 12+ immediately or the window I was watching closes entirely.

**Safronov** has played 3 games all season. Zero points, 13.7 MPG in those three. He is 23 with a 91 scouting number. Either he is in the plan or he is not, and three games does not answer which. This needs a decision before February.

**Smirnov** at 20 has 0 games, 0 points, and a 70 potential. That 70 is the lowest on this list. He does not merit games over Nash, Spacek, Safronov, or Spezza. I am saying plainly: he is not a development case the club needs to solve.

**Upshall** at 21 is now at 17 points in 41 games (0.41 pts/g) on 11.4 MPG. I said on January 8 that if his rate fell below 0.55 the signal was gone. It is at 0.41. The promotion he earned was real but he is not holding it. Give him the 12 MPG one more time to see if the rate recovers; if it stays under 0.55, he is a depth fourth-liner.

**Koltsov** at 23 is producing 18 points in 29 games (0.62 pts/g), but his checking grade of 55 is the worst on the roster and his speed is redundant next to Chistov at 98 on the same line. He is not a development case; he is a fit problem. I would scratch him for Nash.

**Chlup** at 18 with 23 points in 34 games on 13.3 MPG is the best story here. He is earning every shift and belongs where he is.

**Gaborik, Eminger, Klesla, Colaiacovo, Chistov, Alexeev** are all earning their minutes. No concerns.

## Development trends

The window from December 1st to today shows two clubs in one: three young players breaking through while three veterans collapse at the same time, and that gap is what the GM needs to plan around before February.

**Gaborik** is the clearest riser on the roster: 1.42→1.57 pts/g while his ice went from 18.8 to 20.0. He is 22 and getting better on more minutes, which is the profile of a player the franchise builds around. No change needed, just protect his minutes.

**Nash** went 0.83→1.00 pts/g on stable 13-minute minutes at age 20. He was briefly scratched for the GM's rotation policy but his rate tells us he's ready for top-six regularity. When the rotation resets, he goes back in on the first or second wing without debate.

**Eminger** is the confirmed answer at the blue line: 0.35→0.92 pts/g, 15.0→19.3 MPG at 21. He is now our first-pair defenceman by every measure and has been for six weeks.

**Chlup** at 18 is the sleeper: 0.62→0.71 pts/g while his minutes climbed from 11.0 to 14.7. That's a rookie earning his way onto the third line permanently. His trajectory suggests he'll be a checking-centre in the top nine by next season if the pattern holds.

**Spacek** deserves a note to the GM here: his rate rose from 0.55 to 0.67 pts/g during the exact window his minutes were cut from 16.0 to 10.2. The deliberate scratch policy is not hurting him; he's growing even at lower usage. That validates the rotation approach for his age group.

**Sundin** is the alarm. 1.46→0.90 pts/g on MORE ice (16.9→19.0). At 33 that is an aging curve in freefall. He is still the captain and still first-line on paper, but 0.90 on 19 minutes is a second-line number. The top six cannot rely on him carrying it into February.

**Mogilny** is worse: 1.62→0.76. He has halved. At 35 there is no bounce back. Every planning decision for next season should assume he is not a roster player.

**McCabe** is the one that worries me most because he is only 29. 1.42→0.67 is more than a collapse, it is a regression, and it is not explained by age. Whether it is an injury that was never flagged or a matchup problem, his value as a trade asset right now is uncertain in both directions.

**Roberts** at 38 went 1.29→1.10 on rising minutes (16.5→18.8). Still good, but the combination of age and increasing load means he is on a cliff edge in February.

For the defencemen analysis (standing order #1): **Svehla** (0.78→0.45 at 36) and **Fischer** (0.63→0.38 at 24, structural failure confirmed) are the two who should go. McCabe is an unknown quantity at 29 and I would not shop him without understanding why he fell off. Eminger, Colaiacovo, and Kaberle (0.54→0.56, stable at 26) are the blue line going forward. Klesla at 22 has declining rate (0.50→0.43) but is still young enough for one more evaluation.

**Safronov** just played 3 games at 13.7 MPG and recorded zero points. The sample is too small to judge, but his 13.7 MPG means someone is giving him a real look. If the rate stays at zero through January, he is a fourth-pair player and the GM should stop thinking about him as a second-pair option.

## Morale watch

The question is whether any man sits below the minutes his calibre expects, with morale slipping as proof. Three men sit under 90: **Aebischer** at 81 (a scratched third goalie, started 0 games — no line change fixes a goaltender who is not getting starts, that is a roster question for you), **Spezza** at 86, and **Sundin** at 89. Everyone else dressed is 90 or better and the room is holding.

**Spezza** is the lever. He is at 86, the lowest dressed skater, after dropping 4 points, on 7.8 minutes a night on the fourth line while scoring 14 points in 34 games. He is precisely the man the minutes band says is underplayed — a producing young centre on useful-man ice. This is both morale and development: he needs 12+ minutes to satisfy the ice-time expectation *and* to keep his development window open. He is the only player on the roster where the two reasons point the same way. Give him the third-line centre slot and the minutes that come with it.

**Sundin** at 89 after a 4-point drop is the other one. He was at 21.4 minutes in December, is down to 17.9 now, and still leads the club with 54 points in 45 games. His minutes were cut and his morale followed. He is an 89 and producing — he belongs closer to 20 than 18. I flag the tradeoff I flagged in December: at 33 the top six cannot absorb endless extra work into February, but 17.9 is under what he has earned. Bring him back toward 20 on the first line, not beyond.

**Mogilny** at 89 on 17.4 is flat and producing (52 in 41) — leave him. **Richards** at 96, **Roberts** at 96, **Gaborik** at 93, **Alexeev** at 93: all fine for their minutes. Scratches like **Nash** (95) and **Spacek** (96) are sitting by your design and staying happy; that rotation is costing nothing in morale.

## Role composition

**The question this phase answers**: does each unit contain players whose tools match the job it's being asked to do, and if not, is that my arrangement problem or the roster's?

**Koltsov on the third line** — speed 99 alongside Chistov at 98. Two players with the same tool sitting on the same unit, and Koltsov's checking at 55 means the line gets zero defensive return from that speed surplus. The unit checking mean is 67; without him it rises to roughly 70. This is redundancy, not a weakness to develop out of. Upshall on L4 has checking 83 (unit best) and is producing 0.69 pts/g. Moving Upshall to L3 and Koltsov to L4 gives L3 its second checking man and gives L4 the speed it currently lacks (mean 85, best 90). The cost is line chemistry for both units, but L4 only has three skaters right now and L3 has no chemistry worth protecting given its stamina ceiling of 56.

**L4 faceoffs** — mean 53, best 55. The opponent parks their top line on you every draw and starts each shift in the offensive zone. The only faceoff man who could fix it is Chlup at 78, but he's L3C and moving him down costs L3 its sole faceoff asset (mean drops from 59 to roughly 54) and leaves L3 without a draw winner. I don't have a clean fix for this within the current roster. It's a depth problem.

**Toughness across the roster** — Roberts 72, McCabe 72, Fischer 71, Tucker 69. No player above 72. A true enforcer sits at 85+. This means no line can absorb a physical opponent's forecheck and win the puck through contact. Every team with a real power forward will bully us into dumps and chase. This is a roster gap that no line arrangement fixes.

**K1 penalty kill** — Mogilny at 33 sits on the PK alongside Svehla, Roberts, and Fischer. The unit speed mean is 90, which Fischer carries at 94. Mogilny is there presumably for his overall play, but his checking contribution drags the unit mean (76) below what K2 manages with Chistov (74, but K2's best is 94 via McCabe). I don't have Mogilny's exact displayed checking from the brief alone. Given his age and the availability of Tucker (checking 81, currently scratched), this deserves attention, but I won't recommend it without confirming Tucker's status and health.

**P1 and P2** are built correctly: shooting and playmaking concentrated in Gaborik 99 and Sundin 91 / Mogilny 93. No change needed.

**K2** works: McCabe at 94 checking, Chistov at 99 speed, Richards at 87 stamina. This is the best-built unit on the team.

## Opponent matchup

**Can we match Washington's top two lines and their goaltending on the road, or do we need to adjust?**

We're fine. WSH's PP is 12 goals on 122 attempts, a 9.8% unit that cannot hurt us on any night. Their depth after two lines falls off a cliff: Metropolit at 68 and Gamache at 66 are the best the bottom six offers. Our third and fourth lines handle those units without help.

**Jagr** at 89 is the one player who can beat us individually. But he's CHKG 52, TOUG 62, and our top pair is Fischer (CHKG 90) and McCabe (CHKG 85) with Roberts on the wing (CHKG 86). We have more than enough structure to bother him. Lang at 80 and Dupuis at 79 are good, not dangerous.

**Bondra** at 86 with ACCU 90 and SHPW 90 is the second threat. Svehla (CHKG 85) and Eminger on the second pair, with Richards (CHKG 68, ENDU 87) matching Halpern at centre, is sufficient. Their second D pair of Yonkman and Doig are grinders; they won't generate offense.

**Kolzig** is 93 in net. He's good. But we're scoring 4.1 a night as a team with Gaborik at 97 OVR, Sundin at 88, and Roberts at 87. One of those three will solve him. No change to our approach.

**Nash and Spacek.** The GM explicitly asked on January 15th whether Washington warranted going all out. It does. A road game against a team with Jagr and Bondra and a 93-goalie is not a development night. Their bottom six is soft enough that we can absorb the extra cost, but I want two more capable bodies in the top nine if this game is tight late. Reinstate both for this one specifically. Reason class: matchup.

**Belfour starts.** He's 93 OVR, mor 96, and this is a road game with a real goalie on the other side. No reason to hand this to Tellqvist.

**No line changes.** The current construction handles their top two without borrowing from depth. Faceoff issues with Halpern (85) vs Richards (75) on their second line are persistent and not fixable tonight; they're not a matchup-specific problem.

## Owed

**Item #1 — analyse how our defencemen played and update who should go.** First delivery on this, so it covers the whole blue line and establishes the baseline.

**McCabe** is at 48 points in 45 games (1.07 pts/g) on 22.1 minutes. That's a recovery from the 0.80 low I flagged on January 4, though still short of the 1.42 he was carrying in December. He stays. No change to his status.

**Fischer** has improved from the 0.15 rate that prompted the December 29 structural-failure note, but 20 points in 40 games (0.50 pts/g) on 21.0 minutes and $3.70M for four more years is the worst value contract on the blue line. His 84 OVR gives him trade value his production does not justify. He remains the top trade target.

**Svehla** sits at 19 points in 29 games (0.66 pts/g) on 22.7 minutes and $3.60M with one year left. My January 4 call that he's done as a first-pair defenceman holds; the bounce from 0.40 to 0.66 doesn't change that at 36 with an expiring deal. He is a rental. Move him for a pick or prospect before he walks for nothing.

**Eminger** is the change. I called his December a top-pair breakout (1.00 pts/g) on January 1. The full-season number is 19 points in 35 games, which is 0.54 pts/g. The breakout was a hot streak that has come back to earth. At 21 with 76 OVR, $1.20M and one year left, he stays on the roster for now — but if his rate is still under 0.65 in February, he becomes a trade candidate rather than a development asset, because we lose him for nothing in the off-season otherwise.

**Klesla** is the one defenceman I would not move. 21 points in 45 games (0.47 pts/g) on 15.2 minutes, $0.90M, two years left, age 22, 83 OVR. Cheap, young, and the rate should climb as his minutes rise. Keep and develop.

**Colaiacovo** (12 points in 24 games, 0.50 pts/g, $1.10M, 1 yr) is depth at 21 with a 72 OVR. Tradeable if a deal makes sense, but no urgency.

**Kaberle** (22 points in 40, 0.55, $1.90M, 1 yr) is not dressed. Expiring and expendable. Move him for whatever we can get.

**Salo** (8 points in 21, 0.38, $2.60M, 2 yrs) is a healthy scratch with a real number still owed. No trade value at that production. Try to move him as a salary dump; if nobody bites, eat it.

What changed since my last defencemen assessment: Eminger's breakout has stalled and McCabe's rate is partially recovered. Fischer, Svehla and Salo all remain where I put them.

# GM Assistant's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-15

Toronto 33-8-1, 73 pts after 45 games.

## Role coverage

The role that can't be filled from within is toughness, and it will cost a first-round pick to fix — but the faceoff gap is equally real and cheaper to solve, and both get worse next summer when the bodies carrying what little there is turn another year older.

**Toughness** is missing at every level. Zero players at 80+. Roberts at 73 is the ceiling and he's 38. McCabe at 73, Tucker at 70, Chlup at 70. No acquisition target below 80 helps. Chara (OTT, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, 27, $1.70M expiring) is the only player on the board who changes this, and he changes it while also being the best checker available. The coach's flag about no one protecting the skill players is correct and unfixable internally.

**Faceoffs** are a one-man position on this roster and that man is 33. Sundin at 90 FACE is the only 80+ win on the sheet. Chlup 75, Richards 70, Renberg 68. The next-best is 15 points below him. Savard (ATL, 89 FACE, 27, $1.00M expiring) slots in as a second centre who wins draws and costs nothing if folded into the ATL negotiation. This is the cheapest role gap on the roster to fix.

**Checking** is thin but improvable without a trade. Tucker at 83 CHKG is healthy, 29 years old, and not lined. Fischer at 82 is 24. Upshall at 80 is 21. Dressing Tucker nightly gets the club from five to six 80+ checkers and gives the fourth line a body. Beyond that, the depth is Roberts (38), Svehla (36), McCabe (29). A 7th and 8th option at 80+ won't materialise from the current roster.

**Scoring, playmaking, speed, clutch, stamina** are all covered. Thirteen 80+ scorers, twenty-five 80+ speed, twelve 80+ stamina. These are not gaps today. The age risk in scoring is real — Mogilny 35, Sundin 33, Roberts 38 — but the young core (Gaborik 22, Afinogenov 25, Richards 24, Spacek 19) is already lined or close to it.

**Goalies** are covered in terms of quality but are a financial decision. Belfour is 39 at $6.50M on an expiring deal. Aebischer is 26 at $0.50M with a 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV. The role gap here is not quality — it's payroll weight and a contract cliff. Aebischer must be re-signed before July.

**Durability** is thin at three players above 80 and only two of those are under 30 (Afinogenov 95, Fischer 92). Roberts at 98 is 38. This isn't urgent but means the physical core can't carry heavy minutes indefinitely.

## Trajectory

The question is whether Toronto are building toward a cliff or a window, and the answer is window — but only if the summer cluster is broken by June, not July.

**The age shape is correct.** 14 players at 23 or under, 4 at 34 or above. The veterans — Sundin, Mogilny, Svehla, Roberts, Belfour, Renberg — are six, which matches the manual's target. The youth is deep enough to survive any single trade. This is not an aging club.

**Belfour** is the single biggest item. 39, $6.50M, one year left. He is the largest contract on the roster and the oldest player. Trading him before March (the above-80 expiring mechanic) removes $6.50M from the summer cluster and adds a first-round pick. Aebischer at 26, $0.50M is ready. The payroll freed is more than the entire Upshall-Chistov-Alexeev group combined.

**Gaborik** is the most urgent re-signing. 22 years old, 67 points in 45 games (1.49 pts/g), POTE 90, $1.10M with one year left. If you do not lock him on 5-6 years before his 67-point season is priced against the market, he becomes unaffordable or walks. This is a "sign him today" situation.

**Nash, Richards, Eminger, Colaiacovo, Upshall, Chistov** are the next tier: all under 25, all $1.00-1.20M, all expiring, all carrying POTE 88-99. Signing them on 5-6 years at modest raises ($1.5-2.5M) removes $7.70M from the 17-player summer cluster and locks the core through their prime. The remaining expiring players become Belfour, Svehla, Roberts, Renberg, Holden, and the goalies — all replaceable, all old, all easy to walk.

**Chlup** already has 2 years left at $2.34M, which is good. But he is 18 with POTE 95 and 23 points in 34 games. If he takes a step toward 40 points this season, his price at renewal in two years will be $4-5M. Renegotiating now to 5-6 years at $2.5-3.0M is the cheapest lock on the board.

**Sundin** at $8.40M for 5 years is immovable and will outlast his usefulness. At 33 with POTE 60, by the end of this deal he'll be 38 on the books at nine million. There is nothing to do about it — the money is already committed — but it means the young stars cannot all get large raises without profit dipping.

**Payroll headroom:** Revenue $70.20M against payroll $66.97M leaves $3.23M of direct margin, but profit is $25.53M, meaning TV and prestige carry the gap. There is room to add $5-8M in raises for young stars without profit falling to zero. The danger is not affordability — it is doing all 17 renewals at once in July and losing bargaining power.

**Draft capital:** TOR holds their own first-rounder plus DET's, a second, third, and fourth. Two first-round picks is strong ammunition. Trading one (the DET first, since it is borrowed) for a confirmed seller like Kovalchuk or Chara leaves the club with its own pick plus three later rounds — adequate for a rebuild that will not happen while 14 players under 25 are developing on the roster.

**The three moves that protect the next three seasons:** (1) Sign Gaborik, Nash, Richards, and Eminger on 5-6 years by February, splitting the cluster from 17 down to 13 and locking the top-end talent. (2) Trade Belfour before March for a pick. (3) Extend Chlup now at $2.5-3.0M for 5-6 years before the price moves.

## Calendar

**We are buyers at the deadline, and we should be aggressive about it.** Toronto are 33-8-1 with 73 points, 12 clear of second place with 37 games left. The trade deadline is 63 days away on March 19. The coach's two structural gaps, no second faceoff winner and toughness capped at 72, are fixable at the deadline if we commit Belfour.

**Belfour** at 39 and $6.50M is the engine of every plan. He will not be re-signed at any price, and at overall_base 85 he qualifies for the above-80 expiring mechanic. The lead package sends him plus the first-rounder to Ottawa for **Chara** (85 base, 88 TOUG, 89 CHKG, $1.70M expiring, 45 pts/41 GP) and **Havlat** (87 base, 61 pts/42 GP, $0.90M expiring, age 23). Chara closes toughness from 72 to 89 in one move. Havlat is 23 with years left; he is not a rental.

**Kovalchuk** at ATL (92 overall, 69 pts/38 GP, age 21, $1.10M expiring) is the top scoring target. The package is the Detroit second-rounder plus **Chistov** (81 overall, 78 base, POTE 95, age 21, $1.10M). ATL are 13-24-2 with 11 expiring deals. The risk is ATL re-signing both Kovalchuk and Heatley, which kills this target. If they keep one, the other is still available on the same terms.

**Abid** at PIT (86 TOUG, 86 CHKG, 54 pts/43 GP, age 25, $400K) is the cheapest impact available. The return is a third-rounder plus **Holden** (26, $1.20M). PIT are 12-21-5 with 14 expiring. This deal works independently of the other two.

If the big packages die by late February, the December fallback (Mogilny+R2 for Jackman, R3 for Sillinger, Safronov+R4 for Sutton) still fills toughness and faceoffs without spending the first-rounder. Mogilny's decline is confirmed (1.62 to 0.76 pts/g across snapshots), so he is expendable either way.

---

**The summer problem is 17 contracts worth roughly $28.6M expiring the same year.** Here is the disposition:

**Gaborik** (22, 97 overall / 91 base, POTE 90, $1.10M): Lock on 6 years. He is the best player on the roster by 11 base points. Any price is acceptable.

**Nash** (20, 82 / 77, POTE 95, $1.20M): Lock on 5-6 years. At 20 with 95 potential he is the second piece of the young core.

**Upshall** (21, 78 / 78, POTE 99, $1.20M): Lock on 5 years. The highest potential on the roster at 99. His rate doubled from 0.33 to 0.53 while minutes halved, which says the game is generating production when he touches it.

**Richards** (24, 86 / 82, POTE 88, $1.00M): Lock on 5 years. Centre with room to grow.

**Eminger** (21, 76 / 76, POTE 99, $1.20M): Lock on 4-5 years. Same reasoning as Upshall.

**Colaiacovo** (21, 72 / 72, POTE 99, $1.10M): Lock on 4 years. Still 72 overall, so a development bet, but at 99 potential the odds are good.

**Kaberle** (26, 83 / 84, POTE 75, $1.90M): Renew on 4 years, not 6. He is good but POTE 75 says he is close to his peak. $1.90M for four years is manageable.

**Alexeev** (23, 77 / 76, POTE 94, $1.10M): Renew on 3 years. Good potential but still 76 base. Check the trajectory before a fifth year kicks in.

**Aebischer** (26, 86 / 85, POTE 90, $0.50M): Renew on 3 years. He is the future starter; 2.62 GAA and 0.898 SV in 19 starts is not a backup line. $0.50M at 26 with POTE 90 is the best contract value on the roster.

**Tellqvist** (25, 75 / 77, POTE 91, $0.80M): Renew on 2 years. Compete with Aebischer. Do not give him term beyond 2; at 75 overall he is a backup unless his development surges.

**Smirnov** (20, 51 / 51, POTE 70, $0.40M): Let go. 51 overall at 20 with POTE 70 is replacement-level. There are cheaper ways to fill a ninth forward spot in the draft.

**Holden** (26, $1.20M): Gone at the deadline if the Abid trade works. If it does not, let him walk in July. Richards, Sundin and Spezza cover centre.

**Chistov** (21, 81 / 78, POTE 95, $1.10M): Gone at the deadline if the Kovalchuk trade works. If it does not, renew on 3 years. He is 81 overall at 21 with 95 potential; that is not a throwaway asset.

**Belfour** (39, $6.50M): Move at the deadline. Not a summer question.

**Svehla** (36, 84 / 85, POTE 55, $3.60M): Let go. Too old and too expensive. Above 80, so technically tradeable for a pick, but nobody will take a 36-year-old blueliner at $3.60M. Walk away.

**Roberts** (38, 87 / 87, POTE 52, $2.70M): Let go. Same logic. 38, $2.70M, POTE 52. The production is there but the cost-to-retention ratio is terrible for a depth winger.

**Renberg** (32, 78 / 80, POTE 60, $2.00M): Let go. 32 with POTE 60 says this is his level, and $2.00M buys better at that level in free agency.

**Net effect of the summer plan:** shed $14.80M in veteran expiring (Belfour, Svehla, Roberts, Renberg) plus $2.00M in disposals (Holden, Smirnov, Tellqvist worst case). Re-sign the young core on staggered terms so the cluster never renews at once. The payroll that comes back is $13.80M of youth on multi-year deals, which is where a contender wants its money.

## League scan

The question is which players on the seventeen seller clubs fix Toronto's specific holes — toughness at zero, faceoffs at one — and which add a second gear of scoring while this 33-8-1 window is open. The answer is Chara for toughness, Savard for faceoffs, and Kovalchuk or Samsonov for the top line, with one new name that emerged from the data that belongs at the top of a re-signing list.

**Chara** remains the single best target. 94 TOUG base, 95 CHKG base, 85 base overall, 46 points in 43 games on 0.5 blocks per game, 27 years old, $1.70M expiring. OTT are 15-21-4 with 11 expiring deals and $26.27M profit — they are financially comfortable sellers. His displayed 78 overall and 86 TOUG today are depressed by form; the base grades are what a trade screen will price. Pair him with Havlat (87 base, 61 pts/43 GP, 23, $0.90M expiring) from the same club in one negotiation. This closes toughness, checking, and adds top-six scoring.

**Samsonov** (BOS, LW, 26) is a new target the broad scan surfaced. 89 base overall, 80 points in 43 games (1.86 pts/g), $1.90M expiring, speed base 96. BOS are 16-19-4 with 13 expiring deals and $26.25M profit — comfortable sellers. He fills the same top-wing slot as Kovalchuk but with a year more of club control at a similar price. If ATL re-sign Kovalchuk, Samsonov is the replacement and costs less than a first-rounder.

**Komisarek** (MTL, D, 22) is the surprise. 80 displayed overall, 77 base, POTE 91, 53 points in 44 games, $1.10M expiring, one year left. MTL are 12-24-4 with 14 expiring deals. A 22-year-old defenseman with 53 points and 91 potential on a team in full rebuild is the kind of player who changes a blue line for a decade. His toughness is low (76 base TOUG, 83 CHKG) so he does not fill the gap, but he fills a different need: a young top-pair blueliner to replace McCabe's decline.

**Savard** (ATL, C, 27) at 88 FACE base, 79 base overall, 48 points in 43 games, $1.00M expiring, remains the cheapest faceoff fix. ATL at 13-24-2 must deal him. Fold into whatever package addresses Kovalchuk or Heatley — he costs no additional pick.

**Abid** (PIT, LW, 24) at 80 TOUG base, 80 CHKG base, 94 POTE, 56 points in 44 games, $0.40M expiring, is the best value on the board. PIT are 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals. He is not a pure enforcer — his base toughness reads 80, not the 94 that Chara carries — but at $0.40M and 56 points, he is a top-nine winger who also hits.

**Bell** (CHI, LW, 24) at 88 TOUG base, 86 CHKG base, 82 displayed overall, $0.90M with two years left, fills toughness with club control. CHI are 12-23-6 but profitable at $24.48M, so they are not desperate. A third-round pick plus a depth body might move him; acceptance is uncertain given their payroll headroom.

**Jackman** (STL, D, 23) at 89 TOUG base, 90 CHKG base, 83 displayed overall, $0.70M with three years left, is the same gap filled on defense. STL are 10-24-3, 9 expiring, $13.01M profit. He is cheaper than Chara, younger than McCabe, and the three-year deal means he stays. The December package already proposes acquiring him for Mogilny plus a second-rounder.

**Marchant** (CBJ, C, 29) at 94 FACE base, 88 base overall, 55 points in 44 games, $4.88M expiring, is the best pure faceoff centre available. CBJ are 15-20-2 with 8 expiring — the fewest among the bottom twelve — and $12.35M profit, so they are the least motivated seller. His salary makes him expensive. Pursue only if the ATL and OTT targets die.

**Daze** (CHI, LW, 29) at 89 base overall, 79 points in 44 games, $3.00M expiring, is high production on a seller. But 29 years old with a $3M price tag for a rental does not compete with Samsonov at 26 and $1.90M for similar production. Skip unless CHI offer him cheaply.

**What I would not do:** Pursue Pronger ($9.50M expiring) or Tkachuk ($9.00M, three years) regardless of their club's record. The money is prohibitive and neither fills a gap — Toronto have speed and skill. Do not chase DiPietro or Leclaire in goal; Aebischer at $0.50M with a 2.62 GAA is the future and costs nothing.

## Trade construction

The question is what concrete packages Toronto can build that fix the coach's two flagged gaps — zero toughness at 80+, one faceoff winner — while the 33-8-1 window is open, and whether the other GM's incentives line up with ours. Three proposals stack without overlapping assets; all three give from surplus or expiring deals; the combined payroll effect is a $4.70M saving that breaks the summer cluster before it forms.

**Chara + Havlat from Ottawa** is the priority. Chara's 88 TOUG and 89 CHKG base grades are the only ones on the board that move Toronto's toughness ceiling from 73 to something real. Havlat at 87 base and 61 points in 43 games adds top-six scoring in the same negotiation. OTT are 15-21-4, in full rebuild, with $26.27M profit — they don't need salary relief, they need picks. A first-rounder is their currency. Belfour is the engine: he clears $6.50M, he's above 80 so the expiring mechanic applies, and OTT can flip him again by March for another pick or use him as a bridge for their young goalies. They shed $2.60M in expiring salary (Chara $1.70M, Havlat $0.90M) in the process.

**Abid from Pittsburgh** is the best value on the board and the cheapest to execute. 56 points in 44 games, 80 TOUG and 80 CHKG base, 24 years old, $400K expiring. PIT are 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals — they must move him or lose him for nothing. Holden has played zero games this season, carries $1.20M expiring, and is pure salary relief for them. A third-rounder plus a body that doesn't fit is a fair ask for a rebuilding club.

**Kovalchuk from Atlanta** is the most expensive and the most uncertain. 78 points in 41 games at 21, 89 base overall, $1.10M expiring. ATL at 13-24-2 with 11 expiring deals must deal him, but our package is thin: DET's second-rounder (a borrowed pick) plus Chistov. Chistov is 21 with POTE 95 but only 11 points in 31 games — he's a project, not a proven asset. ATL might prefer young players over a second-rounder. The negotiation angle: ATL hold both Kovalchuk and Savard on expiring deals. If they're moving Kovalchuk, they should want to move Savard too (89 FACE, 48 pts, $1.00M expiring, also lost for nothing). Ask for both as a package; if ATL wants a second pick for Savard, give TOR's own second-rounder. That would fill scoring AND faceoffs from one club at the cost of three picks and Chistov.

**Samsonov** (BOS, 89 base, 80 pts/43 GP, 26, $1.90M expiring) is the fallback if ATL re-signs Kovalchuk. BOS are 16-19-4 and profitable, so they're not desperate. He costs more than the ATL package and we've already spent our good picks. Pursue only in the last two weeks of February, and only if Kovalchuk is off the board.

**I would not give Fischer.** His $3.70M for 20 points in 40 games is toxic at four years remaining, but no seller will take on that contract plus give back a difference-maker. He's the coach's problem to solve on the back end, not ours to move at a deadline discount.

**If none of the three land by late February:** Execute the December package. Mogilny + TOR R2 for Jackman (STL, 89 TOUG, 90 CHKG, 23, $0.70M, three years left) is the fallback that fills toughness with a younger, cheaper, longer-control player. He's not Chara (85 base overall vs 87), but three years of club control at $0.70M at age 23 is arguably a better long-term outcome than a one-year rental. The other two legs (R3 for Sillinger, Safronov + R4 for Sutton) add faceoffs and depth. Combined payroll saving: $2.56M.

markdown:
# Coach's report — run 5, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the ice he has earned, and the answer splits into two obvious wastes and one that is already gone.

**Nash** is the loudest problem on the roster. 30 points in 34 games is 0.88 per game at age 20 with a 95 POTE, and he is currently scratched. He is producing at a top-six winger rate on 13 minutes a night and sitting out. This is the pattern my December 29th note flagged, and it has come back. He needs to be back in the lineup immediately.

**Spezza** is at 7.8 minutes a night and 0.41 points per game. My January 15th note says his window is effectively closed at this usage, and the numbers haven't moved enough to change that. The stamina ceiling on the fourth line (endurance mean 51) means he and Upshall cannot both push to 12+ simultaneously. Upshall's recent rate (0.69 in the January 8th reading) exceeds Spezza's (0.41), so Upshall has the stronger claim to those minutes right now. Spezza needs a different path to 12 or this kid's development window shuts.

**Upshall** at 11.4 MPG and 0.41 season-long rate sits just under the 12 threshold he earned in early January. He is at 91% share and should cross that line. One more shift per game gets him there without breaching the stamina ceiling, since Spezza isn't pushing the other direction.

**Safronov** has 3 games and 0 points in 45 team games. A 91 scouting number at age 23 is being wasted by default. Either dress him for stretches or the club stops pretending he is in the plan.

**Spacek** produced 0.61 per game in 23 games before being scratched. At 19 with a 91 POTE that rate earned him a regular spot. Being benched after producing is what kills a kid's development faster than any other pattern.

**Chlup** at 18 is putting up 0.68 per game on 13.3 minutes. He is earning a bigger role. No intervention needed, just keep giving him the game.

**Koltsov** at 0.62 per game looks acceptable on the scoresheet, but his checking is 55, the worst on the roster, and his speed is redundant alongside Chistov at 98 on the same line. There is nowhere on this roster he fits without being a defensive liability or a duplicate. His minutes should go to Nash.

**Smirnov** at POTE 70 and zero games is not a development concern worth the GM's time. Low ceiling, no games played, no signal to act on.

## Development trends

The development picture over the last six weeks splits into two clean stories: a young core that is ascending faster than the lineup is built for, and a veteran top six that is aging into a February scoring hole. The gap between those two is where this team lives right now.

**Gaborik** is the clearest riser. He went from 1.42 pts/g in his first 24 games to 1.57 in the last 21 while his ice climbed from 18.8 to 20.0 MPG. At 22, more ice and a higher rate simultaneously means the coaching is feeding him and he is repaying it. Nothing to change here, just keep going.

**Eminger** made the leap I flagged in January. From 0.35 in his first 23 games to 0.92 in the last 12, on ice that jumped from 15.0 to 19.3 MPG. At 21 he is a first-pair defenceman in every way that matters. The pair is Eminger and whoever survives the McCabe question.

**Richards** quietly moved from 1.08 to 1.14 and from 16.9 to 19.0 MPG. At 24 he is the team's future #1 centre and the present evidence says he already is one. No change, just protection from anyone trying to hand him Sundin's minutes too early.

**Nash** (20) climbed from 0.83 to 1.00 on stable 13 MPG. **Chlup** (18) went 0.62 to 0.71 on ice that grew from 11.0 to 14.7. Both young, both earning their way. Chlup at 18 with 14.7 MPG and a climbing rate is ahead of schedule.

**Spacek** is the one who should have the GM's attention. He went from 0.55 to 0.67 pts/g while his ice was cut from 16.0 to 10.2 MPG. At 19 he is producing better on less. That is a coaching error, not a player problem. He has earned 12+ MPG.

**Upshall** shows the same pattern: 0.33 to 0.53 pts/g while minutes dropped from 13.4 to 8.5. At 21, his rate has doubled and he got less. My Jan 8 note set a 0.55 floor and he sits at 0.53 cumulative, but the recent-stretch rate is what matters, and 0.53 is still well above his season start of 0.33. He is climbing. The L4 stamina ceiling note means I cannot push both him and Spezza onto the same unit, but Spacek is not Spezza. Spacek and Upshall together on the fourth line at 11-12 MPG each is workable; Spezza on top of them is not.

**Spezza** (21) confirms the worst case: 0.43 to 0.38 pts/g on ice cut from 9.1 to 5.7 MPG. Both down. My note from today already says this window is closed at current usage. Unless he gets 12+ immediately, the season is a wasted year for his development.

**Koltsov** (23) went from 1.10 in 10 games to 0.37 in the 19 since, on MORE ice (8.7 to 11.5). More ice, less production, checking 55. The role is eliminated. Confirmed by the brief.

**Fischer** (24) continued his collapse: 0.63 to 0.38 pts/g on 21 MPG that never budged. Structural failure as flagged December 29. He has no role that fixes this.

**Alexeev** (23) slid from 0.62 to 0.48 on ice cut from 11.1 to 6.8. Not a crisis but he is drifting out of the roster.

**Safronov** finally dressed three games at 13.7 MPG with no points yet. Too early to judge, but the fact he is in the lineup is progress.

**Sundin** (33) dropped from 1.46 to 0.90 while his ice rose from 16.9 to 19.0. Getting more of the game for less return. The aging pattern I flagged in December has arrived.

**Mogilny** (35) went from 1.62 to 0.76. A 53% drop in the second half. He is done as a first-line winger regardless of what his name says.

**McCabe** (29) at 1.42 to 0.67 is not aging. He is too young for this rate of collapse and too expensive for it. The GM should think about whether another club will pay a price while his name still carries the first-half number.

**Svehla** (36) at 0.78 to 0.45 on declining ice confirms my January note. Done at this level.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy at 95-96, but three players carry drops that matter and one is at the bottom of the roster with no solution from the bench.

**Spezza** — morale 86, down 4, 7.8 MPG on the fourth line with 14 points in 34 games. He's a 70-79 calibre player getting 2 minutes below his 10 MPG band. I've flagged this since January 5th. The window is closing and the room is watching a 21-year-old sit while producing at 0.41 per game. This is the known one.

**Sundin** — morale 89, down 4 from 93. He's at 17.9 MPG with 54 points in 45 games. A 90+ player expecting 20 minutes per night. He's 2.1 short, and he's sitting exactly one point below the threshold where morale adds +1 to every grade. Moving him to 19-20 per game is the cheapest upgrade available to this team: it pushes his grades up through the morale bonus rather than relying on form. The -4 is new since late December and is the biggest single drop among dressed regulars.

**Richards** — morale 96, down 3 from 99. At 17.9 MPG with 50 points in 45 games, he's at band if he's 80-89, just below if he's 90+. The -3 from near-max is a small flag; if he keeps sliding, he's on the same trajectory as Sundin.

**Alexeev** — morale 93, down 3, 9.1 MPG on the fourth line with 25 points in 45 games. Slightly below his 10 MPG band at 70-79 calibre. The -3 is minor and he's still high enough that no action is needed unless it continues.

**Safronov** — morale 95, down 5, only 3 games played. The -5 on a 23-year-old who isn't playing is development drain, but he's scratched and that's a roster construction call for the GM, not a line adjustment.

**Aebischer** — morale 81, the lowest on the roster by 5 points. Backup goalie, 19 games played at 57.9 minutes a start. There is no minutes fix; he's a backup and knows it. The -1 grade penalty from the 80s is the cost of having a reliable starter. If it drops into the 70s, it becomes -2 across the board and hurts the depth chart if an emergency start comes.

## Role composition

The faceoff gap flagged December 7th is still the defining structural problem, and the bottom-six stamina ceiling is the new one that just became visible.

**Koltsov** — Speed 99 next to Chistov's 98 is the same tool twice on one line. Checking 55 is the worst grade on the roster and pulls L3's checking mean to 67. He's producing at 0.62 points per game, so per the GM's standing order I'm not calling him a liability on the scoresheet. But this is a fit problem: he's fast where his line already has speed, and helpless where his line needs bite. Tucker at checking 81 is sitting out and would be the obvious fix if healthy.

**L3 stamina** — Mean 56, best 68. This unit cannot absorb more minutes no matter who's on it. That means the top nine has to carry heavier loads, and Sundin and Roberts at 34 and 33 are already on the wrong side of that slope.

**L4** — Three men only (Alexeev, Spezza, Upshall) and stamina mean 51. There's no one to rotate into this line if one of them wears down in a game. The fourth line is a one-shortage away from not existing.

**Faceoffs** — Sundin 89 is the only centre above 80. Chlup at 78 is the second-best option and he's on L3. Richards 75, fourth line 53-55. This was flagged six weeks ago and nothing has changed. It's a roster problem, not a lineup problem.

**Units that work** — K1 (Roberts 83, Fischer 84, Svehla high checking) is a proper kill. K2 (McCabe 84, Eminger) gets its bite from the blue line. P1 has Gaborik 99 playmaking and Sundin 91 scoring — no reason to touch it. P2 without Mogilny (if injured) loses its best shooter at 92, which would make it the weaker unit in a way Alexeev at 82 scoring can't cover.

**No change on L1, L2, P1, K1, K2.** These are right. The issues are downstream in L3/L4 and at roster level.

## Opponent matchup

The key matchup question is whether McCabe can handle Jagr's speed on the same side of the ice, and the answer is no.

**Jagr** at 89 overall with 98 speed and 96 acceleration on the right wing faces McCabe (left D, 81 speed, 81 acceleration). That is a 17-point speed gap the first pair cannot close with positioning alone. Fischer has 94/94 on the speed side and 90 checking. He can track Jagr.

**Fischer-McCabe swap.** Move Fischer to left D on the first pair and McCabe to right D. Fischer handles Jagr's speed; McCabe's 85 checking and 81 toughness are adequate against Dupuis (82 agility, 77 checking). This breaks no forward chemistry and is purely about which blue-liner matches which winger.

**Our top three lines are better than their top three.** Sundin (89) wins the draw against Lang (66) by 23 points. Gaborik at 97 against Grier (81) on the second line is the biggest individual mismatch in the game. Richards' 75 faceoff loses to Halpern's 85, but Halpern's 62 accuracy means he does not punish from a draw win.

**Their power play converts at 9.8%** (12 goals on 122 chances). They get volume, roughly 3 per game, but score at an awful rate. Our PK1 of Upshall/Chistov/McCabe/Fischer doesn't need to be perfect against that. Their PK1 is Grier (81), Sutherby (72), Yonkman (75), Witt (78) and our PP converts at 29.7% with Gaborik, Sundin and Roberts at the top. We only get 0.9 PP chances per game, but when we do, we are heavily favored.

**Gonchar** at 93 shot power and 95 hero on the first pair will test our second pair. Eminger (76, ENDU 50) and Svehla (84, TOUG 68) need to keep shots to the outside. Eminger's shot block instinct (his CHKG 79 and the game's defensive play counter) may matter more here than his offense.

**No goalie change.** Belfour at 93 with 95 breakaway and 94 rebound control on the road against a team that scores 3.6 per game is the right start.
