# Coach's report — run 4, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

Are the young players getting the games they've earned? The short answer: most of them are, but three are wrong and one is dead.

**Spezza** is the loudest problem on this roster. 21 years old, POTE 99, 7.8 MPG on the fourth line, 14 points in 34 games at 0.41 per game. I've flagged this three times now. He's dressed 34 of 45 and getting garbage minutes. Morale 86 is already costing him two points of grade. At POTE 99 and 0.41 pts/g on 7.8 minutes, he is not developing; he is coasting toward being what his minutes say he is. The window I set at 12 MPG and 0.60 rate is gone at current usage. He needs the third line centre role or he should be scratched, because dressing him at 7.8 is the worst of both worlds.

**Upshall** was a signal three weeks ago at 0.69 pts/g. Now 17 points in 41 games is 0.41. He's fallen below the 0.55 threshold I set January 8, which means he is a fourth-liner on 11 minutes. No promotion earned.

**Nash** is scratched at 0.88 pts/g in 34 games and 13 MPG. That's the Dec 29 pattern recurring: a healthy player producing at top-six rate sitting out. POTE 95, age 20, morale 95, and he's not playing. I need to know why.

**Spacek** at 19 is also scratched after 23 games at 0.61 pts/g and 13 MPG. Same healthy-scratch problem. He's earning a spot and getting benched.

**Chlup** at 18 is the one working. 34 games, 13.3 MPG, 0.68 pts/g on the third line centre. That's real development happening in a real role. No change needed for him.

**Gaborik** is 67 points in 45 games at 19.3 MPG. He doesn't need my attention.

**Eminger** at 21 is carrying 16.5 MPG on the top pair and scoring at 0.54 pts/g. The rate has cooled from 1.00 in December but he's getting the minutes and the role he earned.

**Safronov** is in 3 games with 0 points. POTE 91, age 23, and the default is still making the decision.

**Smirnov** has 0 games and POTE 70. He's not being wasted because his ceiling doesn't demand it.

**Koltsov** at 0.62 pts/g looks fine on paper, but checking 55 is the worst on the roster and his speed is redundant with Chistov on the same line. His role is eliminated on fit regardless of the point total.

**Colaiacovo** at 21 and **Klesla** at 22 are both earning their minutes. No issues.

## Development trends

The window shows a clean split: the young core is producing while the veterans who carried this team in October are in freefall, and we're still giving them the same ice.

**Upshall** is the clearest development case in the brief. Rate doubled from 0.33 to 0.53 pts/g while minutes halved from 13.4 to 8.5. He played the way I asked and got punished with less ice. He's 21, he's earning it, and the fourth-line endurance ceiling note means I need to rotate him in rather than stack him with Spezza, but something is wrong when a player's rate goes up and his time goes down.

**Spacek** is 19 and the same pattern. 0.55 to 0.67 pts/g while minutes dropped from 16.0 to 10.2. He's a first-round kid getting benched into obscurity while producing. At 19 the window closes fast if he's not in games.

**Chlup at 18** is the surprise that changes the plan. 0.62 to 0.71 pts/g while his minutes jumped from 11.0 to 14.7. He's not a prospect learning the league anymore, he's a second-line centre in progress. The faceoff gap note matters less if he can win draws at 86 like Sundin does.

**Gaborik** at 22 went from 1.42 to 1.57 on 20.0 MPG. Nothing to do but give him the game.

**Richards** at 24: 1.08 to 1.14 on 16.9 to 19.0. Quietly becoming our best centre. He and Sundin are now producing the same rate, and Sundin is 33.

**Fischer** at 24 confirms the structural failure for the third time. 0.38 pts/g on 21.1 MPG. He hasn't moved, hasn't recovered, hasn't adjusted. Every game on that top pair costs us a defence pairing.

**Mogilny** at 35: 1.62 to 0.76 on 16.9 to 18.0. Rate nearly halved while ice went up. He is no longer a top-line winger and should not be playing top-line minutes.

**Sundin** at 33: 1.46 to 0.90 on 16.9 to 19.0. Similar pattern but slightly better. He's the last legitimate top-line centre on this roster, and he's fading.

**McCabe** at 29: 1.42 to 0.67. This is the one that should worry the GM. He's too young for a decline this steep. Either something is physically wrong or the matchup is broken.

**Svehla** at 36: 0.78 to 0.45 on 20.9 MPG. Already flagged, confirmed. He should not be playing 21 minutes.

**Kaberle** at 26 is the one blue-liner holding steady: 0.54 to 0.56 while his ice rose from 19.4 to 22.6. He's absorbing Svehla's minutes without the rate collapsing.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: average morale 92, the most recent movement is positive or flat for virtually every active player, and no one is slipping because of minutes.

**Aebischer** is the lowest man in the building at 81, +1. He's the backup, 19 GP, 57.9 MPG when he plays. His minutes per appearance are fine; his issue is being the backup. That's not a line assignment, that's the depth chart. No fix available to me.

**Spezza** at 86, +1, is the lowest active player. 7.8 MPG on the fourth line, 14 points in 34 games. He's in the 80-89 calibre band expecting ~17 MPG and getting less than half. But morale is rising, so the bleeding stopped. The gap between his band and his ice is still 9 minutes and that's a development issue, not a morale emergency right now. The note I filed Jan 15 stands: his window is closing at this usage.

**Safronov** dropped 5 points to 95 after the first stretch, then held at 95. Scratched, 3 GP, 0 points. Roster decision for the GM. I cannot scratch or dress him differently than he is.

**Kaberle** and **Spacek** are scratched with 22 and 14 points respectively at 96 morale each. No morale damage yet. That matches the pattern from December: healthy productive players sitting don't show up in morale until the room starts losing.

No one else has a morale-to-minutes mismatch. The veterans (Sundin 89, Mogilny 89) got a bump with the team winning. Everyone on L1-L4 is at 93-96. No changes needed on ice-time grounds for Monday.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit's personnel match its job description, and where they don't, whether it's an arrangement I can fix or a hole we cannot fill. The answer: the top two lines are fine, the third line has no identity, and we have two structural gaps the GM needs to hear about.

**L3 is the problem unit.** Checking mean 67, stamina mean 56, faceoff mean 59. This line can't check, can't win draws, and can't skate more than about 8 minutes without gassing. Chistov at speed 98 and Koltsov at speed 99 are redundant on the same unit — one of them is wasting a slot. Chlup at faceoff 78 is the only thing holding this together, and even that loses the draw 22% of the time against a good centre.

**Koltsov** sits at checking 55, the worst grade on the roster. His speed 99 duplicates Chistov's 98 on this line. Moving him to L2 makes his speed additive instead of redundant — no Chistov there, and Richards and Gaborik both benefit from a second breakaway threat. This respects the GM's instruction that production earns role; his rate recovered to 0.62 and I'm not questioning that. I'm questioning the line he produces on. Swapping him for Eminger (who already skates with Gaborik/Afinogenov on PP1) costs chemistry on L2's defensive structure but Gaborik and Afinogenov carry the offence there anyway.

**L4 stamina is a hard ceiling.** Mean 51, best 52. Nobody on that line can play 10 minutes without his game deteriorating. This isn't a coaching decision, it's a physical limit. The line exists to burn 6-7 minutes and get off. Rotating development minutes between Spezza and Upshall in short bursts is the only way to develop them without hitting this wall.

**Faceoffs remain a roster gap.** Sundin at 89 is the only player who wins draws at 80+. Chlup 78, Roberts 76, Richards 75 — none of them win them. We lose the draw on three of four lines every single game. No lineup arrangement fixes this. The answer is a centre who takes faceoffs, and we don't have one in the system.

**Tucker and Kaberle are sitting.** Tucker's checking 81 and toughness 69 are the fourth-best available, and Kaberle's stamina 85 is the second-best on the roster. If they're healthy, Tucker on L3 lifts the checking mean from 67 to 70+ and Kaberle's endurance gives L2 legs in the third period. I don't know why they're out — if it's injury I'll adjust, but if it's a choice I want them back.

## Opponent matchup

The question for Monday is whether their one elite player changes what we do, and the answer is no. We're 73 points against their 55, we outscore them 4.10 to 3.60 and outdefend them 1.90 to 2.70. Their entire structure is built around **Jagr** (89 overall, DEKG 99, PUCK 96, SHPW 95) and behind him the roster drops off fast. Their PP is 12-for-122, a 9.8% unit that does not threaten our PK in any special way.

**Sundin vs Lang** is already our best matchup. Sundin at FACE 89 against Lang at 66 wins the draw on the top line every shift, and Lang is a non-factor defensively (CHKG 57, TOUG 50). Rolling lines to chase Jagr with Richards would flip that: Richards at 75 still beats Lang, but Sundin would then face Halpern at 85 instead of 66, narrowing a 23-point gap to 4. That is a worse trade.

**Their blue line** is the real target. Second pair Yonkman and Doig both sit at ENDU 50 with overall 75. Third pair Fortin (66) and Belak (68) are worse. Our speed at the top of the order -- Gaborik at SPEE 99, Afinogenov at 93 -- will find those legs by the second period. No lineup change is needed to exploit this; it happens naturally when the lines roll.

**Halpern** (FACE 85) is their one faceoff weapon on the second line, and Richards at 75 loses that draw by 10. That is the only place they gain ground on the dots. It does not justify a change. Chlup at 78 is only 3 better and belongs on the third line where Metropolit at 71 is softer competition.

**Belfour** starts. He is 93, Kolzig is 93, and we have won this season's only meeting 6-4. The standard read applies.

# Coach's report — run 3, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games their production has earned them, and three are being held below that mark while one more is wasting away on the shelf.

**Spezza** sits at 7.8 minutes a night in 34 games with 14 points, a 0.41 season rate. His morale has dropped to 86, the lowest on the roster's young group. The 12-minute floor I set on January 5th has been breached for a month and his window at this usage level is effectively closed. He needs to move above 12 MPG immediately, and the only way to do that is to put him on the third line.

**Nash** has 30 points in 34 games at 0.88 a night, potential 95, morale 95, and he is scratched. This is the same pattern from late December that burned development capital across four players simultaneously. At 20 years old and nearly a point a game, he should not be watching.

**Spacek** is 19 with 14 points in 23 games at 0.61 a night and potential 91, and he is also scratched. Two healthy young centres sitting while Spezza plays 7.8 minutes a game on the fourth line is a construction problem. The minutes are there, they are just going to the wrong people.

**Upshall** at 11.4 MPG is close to the 12 he earned in January. If Spezza moves up off the fourth line, Upshall can absorb the extra fourth-line minutes without the stamina risk of loading both young centres onto that unit simultaneously. One bump, not two.

**Koltsov** is at 18 points in 29 games, a 0.62 season rate that is back above the 0.60 threshold. His role was called eliminated on January 1st at 0.42; he has recovered. He is earning his games and stays where he is.

**Colaiacovo** is playing 17.9 minutes in only 24 games at 21 with potential 99. If Svehla is still on the first pair, those minutes belong to Colaiacovo or Eminger. The games are available and he is not getting them.

**Safronov** has appeared in 3 games, scored nothing, and is back in the press box. At 23 with potential 91, this is still an unmade decision, and every week of default pushes it further toward wasted.

**Smirnov** at 20 has zero games, zero points, and potential 70. He is not a development opportunity being denied — he has shown nothing that earns a look. Plainly: he is the odd man out, and the odd man out is where he belongs.

## Development trends

The trends window from December 1 to today shows our development story splitting cleanly: three young players are pushing through, two are earning ice they aren't getting, and the top of our roster is aging off the clip faster than the bottom is growing in.

**Gaborik** is the riser of this window. 1.42 to 1.57 pts/g on minutes climbing from 18.8 to 20.0, at 22. That's a first-line winger, and the gap between him and everyone else on the right side is widening. He and Richards are the future of this roster and the GM should plan the next two years around them.

**Richards** at 24 is quietly overtaking Sundin's rate: 1.14 pts/g on 19.0 MPG versus Sundin's 0.90 on the same minutes. Richards is the player the team builds the first line around by next October.

**Nash** is the third name on the rise sheet. 0.83 to 1.00 pts/g at 20, on steady 13 MPG. He's becoming a top-six winger on schedule. Three players at 24 or under producing over a point a game means the core exists even if the veterans fade.

**Spacek** is earning minutes he isn't getting. His rate went from 0.55 to 0.67 while his ice halved from 16.0 to 10.2. At 19, he's making the case for 14+ MPG and the current usage says no. Same pattern as Upshall from last week.

**Upshall** shows the same paradox as Spacek: rate climbing (0.33 to 0.53) while minutes dropped from 13.4 to 8.5. He's earning more per shift and getting fewer shifts. The L4 endurance ceiling (mean 51) is the constraint, not his play.

**Spezza** is what I flagged Tuesday confirmed. 0.43 to 0.38 pts/g on ice falling from 9.1 to 5.7. The window at current usage is shut. Either he gets 12+ immediately or the GM needs to decide whether to trade him while he still has a prospect number attached.

**Sundin** at 33 is aging in plain sight. Rate fell from 1.46 to 0.90 while minutes rose from 16.9 to 19.0. We're giving him top-centre ice and getting third-line production. The minutes belong to Richards or Chlup.

**Mogilny** at 35 went 1.62 to 0.76. He's half the player he was in October. At 18 MPG he's getting winger-one usage at a bottom-six rate. The GM should plan for this to be his last 18-MPG season.

**Roberts** at 38 is the exception: 1.29 to 1.10. That's a 15% decline over six weeks, not the 40-50% the other veterans are showing. He's still worth his minutes.

**Alexeev** at 23 is sliding fast: 0.62 to 0.48 on minutes falling from 11.1 to 6.8. He's heading for healthy-scratch territory by February unless something shifts.

**Safronov** finally got three games and produced zero points at 13.7 MPG. The 91 scouting number is still untested at NHL level after two months. His window is nearly gone.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy overall -- 96+ on almost everyone, no one below 81. The two names that matter are Spezza and Sundin, both sitting in the 80s and getting a morale penalty on their grades because their minutes are short of what their calibre expects.

**Spezza** is at 86, which costs him 1 point on every grade. He's averaging 7.8 MPG on the fourth line with 14 points in 34 games. Even at a 70-79 calibre, the depth-man band is 10 MPG, so he's 2 minutes short. This matches the development window I flagged in January: at 21 with 0.41 points per game, he needs 12+ to consolidate, and the morale band is a secondary reason to push him up. If he crosses 90 the penalty flips to a +1 bonus, a 2-point swing on his overall.

**Sundin** is at 89, one point from the +1 threshold. He's at 17.9 MPG carrying 54 points at age 33. A player with that production sits in the 90+ band, expected 20 MPG. He's 2.1 minutes short, and that shortfall is what's keeping him at 89 instead of 90+. The earlier -4 swing (now recovered to +4) suggests the results were the bigger driver, but the minutes gap is what's capping him one point below the flip.

**Aebischer** at 81 is the lowest man on the roster. He's a backup goalie who hasn't played in 22 games. No line change fixes a backup's morale; that's the results and the building. Nothing to do here.

**Safronov** dropped 5 from a recent snapshot (now back to 95). Only 3 games played, healthy scratch. He's fine numerically but if he stays in the press box through February that trend continues.

**Alexeev** at 9.1 MPG with morale 93 -- the -3 from December recovered to +1. He's producing 25 points in 45 games on fourth-line minutes and is happy enough. Leave him.

Everyone else sits at 96+ with minutes that are broadly appropriate for their role. No depth man is carrying a load that threatens fatigue, and no one else is below their expected band with a morale dip attached.

## Role composition

The role audit answers one question before Monday's game in Washington: does each unit have the players it needs to do its job? The answer is yes for three of four lines and both special teams, with one clear failure on the third line that has a simple fix on the roster.

**Koltsov** is the problem. Checking 55, stamina 50, and he's on a third line that needs to provide some defensive stability. He is the worst checker on the dressed roster by 12 points. His speed 99 is redundant because Chistov is 98 on the same line. His role was already eliminated when he failed the 0.60 points-per-game recovery threshold (0.42 at the time of that call), and nothing has changed since. He belongs nowhere on this roster, and tonight he should not dress.

**Tucker** at checking 88, toughness 84 is the second-best checker and second-best enforcer available and he is sitting at home. Put him on the left wing of the third line in Koltsov's place. L3's checking mean jumps from 67 to something closer to 73 with Tucker in. The line keeps Chistov's speed 98 and gains a body that can actually play the game Chlup needs beside him. Chemistry cost: Chlup has been playing with Koltsov and Chistov. But Koltsov has produced nothing worth preserving.

**L1** is built correctly. Three checkers at 80+ (McCabe 84, Fischer 84, Roberts 83) behind three scorers. Sundin handles draws at 89. The production issues with McCabe and Fischer are matchup problems, not role-fit problems. Fischer's checking 84 and speed 94 are first-pair attributes; his scoring collapse is about who he's paired with, not whether he belongs on the pair.

**L2** is the speed-and-scoring line and should be. Gaborik 98 scoring, 99 speed. Afinogenov 92 scoring, 92 playmaking. Richards 90 playmaking at centre. Eminger is the offensive D. This unit is exactly what it should be.

**L3 with Tucker** becomes the checking line the third unit is supposed to be. Chlup at centre (78 checking, 78 faceoffs) provides the most he can at the dot. Colaiacovo and Klesla on the back end. Chistov gives one winger speed; Tucker gives the other winger a body at 84 toughness. That's a functional third line.

**L4** is a rotation unit, not a true fourth line. Stamina 51 mean, faceoffs 53. No one on it wins a draw. It exists to give the top nine a breather. That's fine at this point in a season. Don't load both Spezza and Upshall past 12 minutes in the same stretch.

**P1 and P2** are fine. P1 has shooters (Gaborik 98, Sundin 91, McCabe and Eminger at the point) and a draw-winner (Sundin 89). P2 has Mogilny 92 as the best available shooter. No changes.

**K1** puts Mogilny on the kill, which is unconventional but works because his speed 94 lets him chase. K2 with Eminger, McCabe, Richards and Chistov is well-built: two checkers, a puck-handler, a burner. Leave both alone.

The structural gap remains what it has been since December: faceoffs. Only Sundin (89) wins draws above 80. Chlup 78, Richards 75, fourth line 53. We lose the opening draw on at least three shifts a period. That is a trade target, not a lineup fix.

## Opponent matchup

What do WSH give us Monday, and does it ask anything our lines cannot answer? The answer is no, with one tactical note.

**Their power play is 12 on 122, a 9.8% conversion rate.** That is almost irrelevant as a threat. We do not need to think about PK matchups, and Sundin and Richards can take short shifts on the kill without concern. This frees the top six from PK fatigue in a game where we should control possession.

**Gaborik against their second pair is the mismatch of the night.** Their second pair is Yonkman (OVR 75, AGIL 85) and Doig (OVR 75, AGIL 78). Gaborik reads 99 on speed, acceleration, and deking. Richards will draw Halpern (FACE 85 vs Richards 75), who wins that draw, but Halpern is a 77 OVR centre and Richards is 86. The faceoff loss is one zone entry; the skill gap through 60 minutes is not one faceoff.

**Jagr (OVR 89, DEKG 99, PUCK 96, SPEE 98) against our first pair is their best shot.** Fischer (CHKG 90, SPEE 94, ACCE 94) has the speed to track him and the checking to make him earn it. McCabe (CHKG 85, TOUG 81) brings the physicality. Witt (CHKG 94, TOUG 90, SHPW 93) is their physical D partner and can join the rush, but his ACCU 63 and DEKG 55 mean he is not creating with the puck. We have the tools here.

**Kolzig (OVR 93, REBC 91, BRKA 90) is elite.** Volume shooting will not beat him. We need our top units generating high-danger chances through the middle, which is what Gaborik and Sundin do best.

**No change.** We are 33-8-1 with a 4.10-1.90 goal differential. They are 23-14-5 with a 9.8% PP and thin bottom-six depth (Metropolit OVR 68, Gamache OVR 66). Our lines are producing. Belfour starts.

title: Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-15
markdown:
# Coach's report — run 2, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether each young player is getting the ice his production has earned, and the answer is mixed: one elite producer is benched, two promising centres are starved of minutes below the level they need to develop, and one 23-year-old is invisible.

**Nash** at 20 is sitting on the bench with 30 points in 34 games (0.88 pts/g). This is the same healthy-scratch pattern flagged on December 29, now recurring. The GM's standing order is clear: production wins over what a kid looks like on paper. Nash has earned a top-nine role and he's not getting one.

**Spezza** is at 7.8 minutes a night on the fourth line with morale at 86. His season rate is 14 points in 34 games (0.41), but the January 5 note recorded his recent rate climbing to 0.62 before minutes were cut again. At 21 with a POTE the club rates at 99, the Jan 5 threshold still applies: 12+ minutes and a sustained 0.60+ rate makes him a second-line centre next season. He hasn't gotten the minutes to prove it.

**Upshall** is at 11.4 MPG and 17 points in 41 games (0.41 season rate). His recent clip (0.69 per the Jan 8 note) has earned him the bulk of fourth-line minutes. The problem is structural: L4 endurance averages 51, so putting both Spezza and Upshall on 12+ simultaneously risks a fatigue spiral by February. This means rotation, not promotion for both. Upshall keeps the 12-minute spot now; Spezza rotates in when Upshall's legs go.

**Spacek** at 19 produced at 0.61 pts/g (14 points in 23 games) before being scratched. His morale is 96, which means the scratch hasn't hurt him yet, but at 19 every week sitting is a week not developing. He's behind Nash in the queue but deserves a look once Nash is back in and one of them settles in.

**Safronov** is 23 with 3 games played, 0 points, and a POTE of 91 that nobody has tested. The December 15 note said to keep this in front of the GM. It's now January 15 and the answer still hasn't come. At 23, three games in 45 is not development. It's a roster spot being consumed without either contributing or growing. The GM needs to name him in or out.

**Koltsov** is interesting. The January 1 note said he failed the 0.60 recovery threshold at 0.42 pts/g. His season rate is now 18 points in 29 games (0.62), meaning his recent production has been very strong — likely over 1.0 in the stretch since that note. The old assessment may be stale. I can't call it development without snapshots, but I can say his current numbers look like a player earning his role, not one who lost it.

**Gaborik, Klesla, Chlup, Alexeev, Chistov, Eminger** are all playing their share and producing at rates consistent with their minutes. No issue there.

## Development trends

The question this phase answers is who is getting better and who is getting worse between December 1st and now, because the trade deadline and the February collapse window are both close and the trends determine who gets minutes and who gets traded.

**Gaborik** at 22 is still climbing: 1.42 to 1.57 pts/g on minutes up from 18.8 to 20.0. He is the only young forward whose rate and ice are both rising simultaneously. Nothing to change here, just don't slow him down.

**Nash** at 20 broke the point-per-game mark: 0.83 to 1.00 on steady 13-minute shifts. That is a second-line winger emerging. He should be getting closer to 15 minutes by now given the rate.

**Chlup** at 18 went from 0.62 to 0.71 pts/g with ice climbing from 11.0 to 14.7. The kid is earning the centre spot by performance. His minutes are finally where a 0.70-rate centre belongs.

**Eminger** at 21 continued the breakout: 0.35 to 0.92 pts/g on minutes up from 15.0 to 19.3. The memory from January 1st called it then; this confirms it is not a hot streak. He is a first-pair defenceman now and the pairing should reflect it permanently.

**Richards** at 24 went 1.08 to 1.14 pts/g on minutes up from 16.9 to 19.0. Steady ascent into a true second-line centre. No intervention needed.

**Chistov** at 21 went 0.29 to 0.41 pts/g with minutes jumping from 9.5 to 14.8. Rate up with more ice, which is the sign of a checking forward developing into a real third-liner. Keep feeding him.

**Colaiacovo** at 21 crept from 0.44 to 0.53 pts/g on slightly fewer minutes (18.9 to 17.3). Quiet improvement. If McCabe's slide continues, Colaiacovo is the next man up on the first pair.

**Spezza** at 21 is now declining on both axes: 0.43 to 0.38 pts/g with minutes collapsing from 9.1 to 5.7. The December 5th note said 12 MPG and 0.60 rate was the threshold to keep the window open. He is at half the minutes and well below the rate. The window is closing fast. He needs 12+ MPG now or this kid's development is being killed by a lack of ice, not a lack of ability.

**Spacek** at 19 has the same pattern Spezza had in December: rate up (0.55 to 0.67) but ice down from 16.0 to 10.2. He was getting 16 minutes, got cut to 10, and his production rate actually rose. That means he can handle the ice and is being underused. Restore him to 14+ MPG.

**Upshall** at 21 sits at 0.53 pts/g with minutes down from 13.4 to 8.5. The January 8th memory set a floor of 0.55 for the promotion signal. He is at 0.53. The signal is gone. He is a bottom-six forward, and the minutes drop reflects that honestly.

**Koltsov** at 23 went from 1.10 to 0.37 pts/g while his minutes went up from 8.7 to 11.5. More ice, much worse rate. The January 1st note already said the roster has no role for him. This confirms it. GM needs to move him or dress someone else.

**Alexeev** at 23 dropped from 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g with minutes falling from 11.1 to 6.8. Both axes declining. He is losing his grip on a roster spot.

**Safronov** at 23 has 3 games and 0 points on 13.7 MPG. He finally got dressed and produced nothing. That is one sample, but at 23 with a 91 scouting number, three scoreless games does not make the case for more ice. Either commit to dressing him consistently for 10 games to get a real read, or stop treating him as a prospect and let someone else take the slot.

**Fischer** at 24 is confirmed broken: 0.63 to 0.38 pts/g on stable 21 minutes. The December 29th note said no patience fixes this. It still does not. He needs off the first pair permanently.

**McCabe** at 29 went from 1.42 to 0.67 pts/g on minutes down from 23.7 to 20.3. At 29 this is not aging. The January 4th note flagged it and the trend continues. If this holds past the All-Star break, the first pair is Eminger and Colaiacovo and McCabe becomes a second-pair option.

**Sundin** at 33 is the biggest number on the page: 1.46 to 0.90 pts/g while his minutes went up from 16.9 to 19.0. He is getting more ice to compensate for producing less, which is exactly the aging-top-six-minutes-crisis the December 19th note predicted. His minutes need to come down and go to Richards, Nash, or Gaborik. Running him at 19 minutes on a declining rate burns him for February.

**Mogilny** at 35 went from 1.62 to 0.76 pts/g on minutes up from 16.9 to 18.0. He is done as a top-six forward. Every minute above the second line is a minute better spent on a young player who is actually ascending.

**Svehla** at 36 is where the January 4th note said he would be: 0.78 to 0.45 pts/g on declining minutes (23.8 to 20.9). Age-appropriate. The transition away from him should already be happening.

**Roberts** at 38 slipped from 1.29 to 1.10 pts/g on minutes up from 16.5 to 18.8. Still contributing, but the pattern is the same as Sundin: more ice, less production. At 38 that is the most you can ask, and his minutes should be managed down to 15-16 by February.

**Salo** at 30 dropped from 0.40 to 0.33 pts/g with minutes down from 20.3 to 16.8. He is fading and getting less ice as a result. Reasonable trajectory.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy overall: 24 of 32 rostered players sit at 96 or above, and the upward swings this save (Richards +3, Roberts +3, Chistov +3, the whole blue line +1) track a winning streak. Three names still need attention.

**Spezza** sits at 86, the lowest of any dressed player, and dropped 4 points before stabilising. He's 21, on the fourth line, averaging 7.8 minutes a night. A kid at his calibre expects 10, and my development note from January 5th says he needs 12+ to consolidate. He's at 14 points in 34 games on those scraps. The morale is telling me what the scoresheet already does: he's better than the minutes he's getting. I asked for this on January 8th and it wasn't acted on. I'm asking again.

**Aebischer** at 81 is the lowest number on the whole roster. He's the third goalie, currently scratched, but he's played 19 games at 57.9 a night this season. At 81 his grades lose 2 points, so when he comes in relief he's worse than his sheet suggests. This isn't a minutes problem I can fix by moving someone between lines. It's a goalie-depth question: either he plays somewhere or his numbers stay depressed until the trade deadline.

**Safronov** dropped 5 to 95. He's 23, scratched, 3 games played, zero points. The morale tells me he knows he's not in the plan. I flagged his window closing in December. This is the GM's call to make: dress him regularly or move him. Sitting him indefinitely at 95 and dropping is wasting an asset.

Everyone else is fine. The dips from Sundin (-4, recovered +4), Richards (-3, recovered +3) and Alexeev (-3, recovered +1) all bounced back, which means they were results-driven and the streak is fixing them.

## Role composition

The question this phase answers: are the units built from the right pieces, and if not, can I fix it by rearranging or only by adding?

**Mogilny on K1 is the one arrangement error.** He's a 92 scoring winger at 36 taking penalty-kill minutes while Tucker at 81 checking sits on the bench. K1's checking mean is 76 with a best of 90 (Roberts); Mogilny is the reason that mean is not higher. Roberts and Fischer carry the kill; Mogilny's value is in his stick and his hands, not his willingness to eat a shot. Moving him off the PK costs nothing in PK chemistry — units of four rebuild fast on a kill — and frees him from a third role that drains his engine.

**Tucker scratched is the other half of that problem.** Checking 81, toughness 69. He's the fourth-best checker on the roster and the third-best forward checker behind Roberts and McCabe. Dressing him gives K1 a genuine body to put in front of the net and gives me a second line I can deploy on the penalty kill. I cannot see from the brief why he is out — if it is production, that is a different conversation, but on role fit alone he belongs in the lineup.

**L3's stamina at 56 mean, best 68, has no fix.** Koltsov, Klesla, Chistov, Chlup, and Colaiacovo are all low-endurance players. By the third period this line is skating on fumes. The only tool is shorter shifts, which the GM controls with line changes. Composition won't fix a physiological floor.

**Faceoffs remain the known roster gap.** Sundin 89, Chlup 78, Richards 75. Three centres below 80, meaning two lines lose the draw every game and our defencemen start shifts under pressure. This is unchanged since December and remains a trade target, not a lineup fix.

**L1, L2, P1, P2, K2 are right.** The first line has Sundin for draws and Roberts for the physical game. P1 gives Gaborik 99 scoring and 99 playmaking the most of the ice in the offensive zone. K2 has Eminger's 94 checking anchoring it with Chistov's 98 speed to chase. No reason to touch them.

## Opponent matchup

Do we need to adjust anything for Washington, or do our current lines already match them well?

**The answer is no change.** Here's why.

**Jagr** at OVR 89 with SPEE 98 and DEKG 99 is their whole team in one man. He plays right wing on their first line with Lang at centre (FACE 66) and Dupuis at left. Sundin at FACE 89 against Lang at 66 means we win those draws routinely and sustain offensive zone time against Jagr's own line. Fischer with CHKG 90 and SPEE 94 on the first pair has the speed to stay home on Jagr. The matchup already covers him.

**Halpern** at FACE 85 on their second line is their best faceoff man and he beats Richards at 75. That gives them zone entries on second-line draws. I have no answer for this that doesn't burn Chlup against their top nine, and Chlup at 78 barely helps anyway. It's a 10-point faceoff deficit, not a game-changer, and our second line has Gaborik at OVR 97 against Bondra at 86. We win that battle on the scoresheet even if they win the draw.

**Their PP is 12 on 122, which is 9.8%.** They cannot score on the man advantage. Our PK personnel is irrelevant for this game. They get 2.9 PP chances a night and convert one in ten. I would not swap a single penalty-killer for this opponent.

**Their depth after two lines is poor.** Third line: Zubrus OVR 79, Metropolit OVR 68, Cleary OVR 72. Fourth line: Gamache OVR 66, Sutherby OVR 72, Sloan OVR 71. Our third line (Chlup OVR 83, Chistov 81, Koltsov 72) and fourth (Upshall 78, Alexeev 77, Spezza 71) are better across the board. We can roll four lines against their bottom two and get secondary scoring.

**Belfour starts.** Kolzig is OVR 93 and the game is on the road, but their shots come from Jagr (SHPW 95) and Gonchar (SHPW 93, HERO 95) off the point. Belfour's BRKA 95 and REBC 94 are exactly what you need against a team that generates power rather than volume (251 for, 120 against for us says we control the play). No reason to go with Tellqvist.

# Coach's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-15

Next game at WSH on Monday 17 January 2005.

## Development opportunity

The question is whether our young players are getting the games they have earned, and the answer is that we have a 20-year-old with 30 points sitting on the bench and a 21-year-old with 99 potential getting fourth-line minutes. Both are development failures I can see clearly from the sheet.

**Nash** is the loudest problem on this list. 30 points in 34 games at age 20 is 0.88 points per game. He's been healthy enough to dress 34 times but he's now scratched, and the club has played 45 games total, meaning he's been out for 11. This is the same pattern flagged December 29. A kid producing at nearly a point a game does not belong in the press box.

**Spezza** is at 7.8 minutes a night on the fourth line with 14 points in 34 games. His rate has been climbing — 0.62 per game over the recent stretch — and he carries 99 potential. The note from January 5 set 12 minutes as the floor for his development. He's still at 7.8. He's earning a top-nine role and getting depth minutes. That's the underuse that costs the most because nobody reacts to it.

**Spacek** has 14 points in 23 games (0.61 per game) at 19 years old and 91 potential, and he's scratched. When he plays he gets 13 minutes, which is a regular's ice, but he only plays half the games. If his production when dressed is a fair read of his ability, the scratch is wrong.

**Chlup** is 18 with 23 points in 34 games on the third line. 0.68 per game. He's getting his chance and taking it. No action needed.

**Gaborik, Klesla, Alexeev, Eminger** are all playing every game or close to it. No issues. Gaborik at 67 points is the team's best player and plays 19.3 a night.

**Upshall** is at 11.4 minutes, just below the 12 I said he needed in the last note. His season rate is 0.41 but that's dragged down by a slow start. Close enough to the threshold that it's not a crisis, but if he drops further it is.

**Koltsov** is 18 points in 29 games, 0.62 per game. That's actually above the 0.60 threshold the note from January 1 set. But that note was based on his recent rate at 0.42, and the season number includes a hot start. I can't tell from here whether he's recovered or the early games are propping up the average. Flag it but no action.

**Safronov** is the one I have to raise again. Three games played, zero points, scratched, at 23 years old and 91 potential. This has been in front of us since December 15. He is either part of the plan or he is not, and right now the answer by default is "not" while he occupies a roster spot.

**Smirnov** at 0 games and 70 potential is a depth player on this roster. He does not have a realistic path to games behind Nash, Chistov, and Koltsov. Saying it plainly is kinder than dressing him for nothing.

## Development trends

This phase asks who is getting better and who is getting worse, because three veterans are falling off a cliff simultaneously and I need to know if the young guys are stepping up to fill the holes they leave. Some are. Some are not, and one is getting the opposite of what his numbers earned.

**Chlup** at 18 is the best story on the roster. Rate up from 0.62 to 0.71, minutes up from 11.0 to 14.7. He is getting more of the game and producing at a higher clip. At 18 that is not luck; that is a kid who is outplaying his role. He and Richards (1.08→1.14 pts/g, 16.9→19.0 MPG) are both climbing, and that pair is the future centre two.

**Gaborik** at 22 went from 1.42 to 1.57 pts/g on 20.0 MPG. He is a top-line winger right now, not next year. The GM should know that our best player is also our youngest first-line forward.

**Spacek** at 19 is a problem I created. Rate went up (0.55→0.67) but I cut his minutes from 16.0 to 10.2. A 19-year-old producing at 0.67 pts/g should not be losing ice. I am penalising a kid who is getting better. I need to restore his time.

**Upshall** at 21 has a rate of 0.53, which is above the 0.55 threshold from the Dec 8 note, and minutes at 8.5. The note said he earned 12+ MPG. I have not given it to him. Same coaching error as Spacek, same fix.

**Spezza** at 21 is the one who worries me most among the young group. Rate is down (0.43→0.38) and minutes are down from 9.1 to 5.7. Both falling at once is what happens when a player loses confidence and the coach loses patience. He is on a two-way path at 21: either he gets 12 minutes and we find out who he is, or this season ends with him at 5 MPG and we never learn. I am giving him the minutes.

**Alexeev** at 23 went from 0.62 to 0.48 pts/g and from 11.1 to 6.8 MPG. The rate drop is mild but the minutes collapse suggests I do not trust him. At 23, he is not a development project anymore. Either he fills a role or he is not part of the plan.

**Safronov** finally got dressed — 3 games, 13.7 MPG, zero points. The sample is too small to judge, but the window flagged in December is now closing. Three games without a point means either I need to keep running him or we need to admit he is not ready.

**Fischer** continues to confirm the structural-failure note: 0.38 pts/g on 21.1 MPG. He is what he is, and what he is does not belong on a first pair.

**McCabe** at 29 dropped from 1.42 to 0.67 pts/g on minutes falling from 23.7 to 20.3. This is not aging — this is a collapse. Our top pair heading into the final stretch is Eminger (0.92, rising) paired with whoever survives, and McCabe is not it.

**Sundin** (1.46→0.90) and **Mogilny** (1.62→0.76) are both losing more than half their rate while getting more minutes. The memory from December said this becomes a scoring collapse by February. We are in January and it is happening. The GM needs to plan the top six around two veterans who will not get their pace back.

**Roberts** at 38 is holding at 1.10 pts/g on 18.8 MPG. He is the only veteran in his age bracket who is not in free fall. Remarkable, but I cannot build the next season around 38-year-olds.

## Morale watch

The room is healthy: average morale 92, most starters at 96 and climbing with the recent wins. Three players broke from that pattern and need attention.

**Spezza** sits at 86, down 4 since Dec 28. He's getting 7.8 MPG on L4 with 14 points in 34 games (0.41 pts/g). If he's a 70-79 guy, he expects 10 MPG; if 80+, he expects 17. Either way he's under. My standing note says he needs 12+ MPG to consolidate development at 21, and the morale drop confirms he knows it. Give him more of the fourth line's shifts or promote him over Chlup on the third.

**Alexeev** at 93, down 3. He's producing 25 points in 45 games (0.56 pts/g) on 9.1 MPG on L4. For a 23-year-old wing putting up those numbers, that's second-line production trapped in fourth-line minutes. If he's 80-89 overall, his band is 17 MPG. He's 8 short. His rate and his morale both say he's earned more than he's getting.

**Safronov** dropped 5 to 95 with 3 games played all season and a scratched status. I cannot fix this from the bench. I need the GM to tell me whether Safronov is in the plan or out of it, because a 23-year-old with real ability watching from the press box every game burns both morale and development capital.

**Sundin** dropped 4 to 89 but bounced back up 4 in the latest save. At 17.9 MPG he's slightly under his likely 20 MPG band (33 years old, 54 points, first-line centre, probably 90+ overall), but the recovery tells me the recent wins fixed what was bugging him. No action.

**Chlup** at 86 is below the room average. 23 points in 34 games at 13.3 MPG on L3 as an 18-year-old. If he's 70-79 he's already over his 10 MPG band and the morale is results-driven. If he's 80+ he's under. I'd watch it rather than act.

The room is winning, the numbers back that up, and almost everyone is happy. Two ice-time adjustments fix the only two players whose minutes don't match their production.

## Role composition

The question is whether each unit's personnel suits what we ask it to do, and where the arrangement can't paper over what the roster doesn't have.

**L1** carries the entire defensive load. Checking 76 mean with Fischer 84 and Roberts 83 as the only 80+ options below McCabe's 84. Faceoffs 64 mean with Sundin's 89 the sole player above 80 on the whole roster. Scoring 87, speed 88, clutch 85 — this line does everything because the next line down can't do any of it at a high level. That's not an arrangement error; it's the only configuration the roster supports.

**L2** is a speed and skill line (speed 91, scoring 87, playmaking 87) with checking at 72 mean. Eminger's 94 on the PK sheet carries that number up. Gaborik 99 scoring, Afinogenov 92 — this unit does what it should. Richards at 75 faceoffs is the best we can do on a second line. No change needed.

**L3** is the problematic unit. Checking 67, toughness 62, stamina 56 — those are bottom-of-the-roster numbers on what should be a sheltering line. Speed is 91 because Chistov (98) and Koltsov (99) are fast, not because the line is built for transition. This line cannot check and cannot win draws. **Koltsov** at 99 speed doesn't compensate for 0.42 pts/g and a failed recovery threshold. He has no role here.

**L4** has a stamina crisis. 51 mean, 52 best. That's the line you need fresh in the third period, and they're the most fatigued unit on the sheet. Spezza and Upshall are both climbing (my notes put them at 0.62 and 0.69 pts/g) but at low minutes. More ice would help development and morale but their bodies say otherwise right now.

**K1** uses Mogilny at 35. His speed still reads 94 but my earlier note has his production halved. He's the only option alongside Roberts/Fischer with enough game sense to not be a liability on the kill. It works short-term; it won't in February.

**P2** scores through Mogilny (92) and Fischer's shot (84 checking, but his speed 94 creates open ice). Alexeev as the fifth man is development. No better option exists.

**The Tucker question:** 81 checking, 69 toughness, scratched. He's the only player who raises L3's checking mean. I don't see a reason on the sheet why he's sitting. If it's not injury, he belongs on the third line over Koltsov to lift the unit's checking from 67 to a workable level.

## Opponent matchup

The question is whether Washington's shape demands any lineup adjustment. It does not. Our current construction already covers their threats better than any shuffle could.

**Jagr** is their whole first line. OVR 89, SPEED 98, DEKG 99, PUCK 96, but TOUG 62 and CHKG 52. Roberts at CHKG 86 and TOUG 88 is the man to make Jagr's night miserable, and that's exactly where he sits on our first line. Sundin's FACE 89 versus Lang's 66 means we own the draw on their top line and can sustain pressure. No change needed.

**Halpern** is their best faceoff man at FACE 85, and Richards sits at 75. We lose that draw, but Richards has AGGR 94 and HERO 97 — he'll win it on the puck, not the draw. And Gaborik at OVR 97 against Bondra at 86 is the best player-vs-player mismatch on the sheet. We want that line out there together, and it already is.

**Witt** is their problem. OVR 78, CHKG 94, TOUG 90, SHPW 93, but PUCK 64, DEKG 55, PASS 69. He's a hitter who can't handle forechecking pressure. Their blue line behind him and Gonchar is Yonkman 75, Doig 75, Fortin 66, Belak 68. That's a soft third and fourth pair. Our second and third lines (Chistov at SPEED 99, Chlup at 83 OVR, Koltsov at SPEED 99) should eat them alive.

**Their power play is 12 on 122.** Under 10%. We can play aggressive without fearing the penalty kill. The 122 attempts also tells you they draw or take a ton of penalties — 2.9 per game. We should ride the whistles, not avoid contact.

**No line changes. Belfour starts.** The matchups are already right, their blue line is soft from position three down, and our top six has the skill and speed to exploit Witt's puck-handling. The only thing the GM controls here is the forecheck aggression, and the answer to that is "yes, more."

title: GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-15
markdown:
# GM Assistant's report — run 1, in-game 2005-01-15

Toronto 33-8-1, 73 pts after 45 games.

## Role coverage

**Toughness is the one role with no coverage at all: zero players above 73.** Every other role on this roster is deep enough to contend; this one isn't close, and the coach's flags since December are aimed at exactly this.

**Roberts** at 38 is the closest thing to a power forward with 86 CHKG and 73 TOUG, but he's also the oldest player on the roster with 98 INJU, which means he won't carry the checking load next year either. **Svehla** at 36 has 83 CHKG but 69 TOUG. The two under-30 checkers are **McCabe** (86 CHKG, 73 TOUG, 29) and **Tucker** (83 CHKG, 70 base TOUG, 29). Tucker isn't even lined. That's the entire checking core, and two of four are in their mid-30s with base toughness at 73 or below.

**Sundin** is the only faceoff man above 80. Chlup at 75 is next best, then Roberts at 75. That means three lines lose the draw. Holden at 71 is on the roster but not lined, and 71 doesn't help. For a team playing 45 games already and headed into the playoffs, this is a real liability against centres who win draws at 60%+.

**Kaberle** at 97 ENDU, 90 CLUTCH and 84 ODBI (passing) is sitting unlined. The brief doesn't say why, and that's a coach question. A 26-year-old with that engine and clutch grade is the kind of depth that wins playoff series.

**Spacek** at 19 with 84 PLE and 79 INJU is also unlined. The coach already flagged him for a dressed spot. Development says put him somewhere.

**Aebischer** at 26, 2.62 GAA and .898 SV over 19 starts has made the Belfour question urgent rather than distant. The coverage is fine tonight; the plan is what matters.

## Trajectory

This club is not aging into a cliff on the ice; it is sitting on a contract cliff that renews almost everyone in the same July, and that is the trajectory problem to solve now because the deadline and the summer run into each other.

**The age curve is healthy, not top-heavy.** Fourteen players are 23 or under, eleven more are 24–29, only three sit in the 30–33 bridge, and four are 34+: Belfour (39), Svehla (36), Mogilny (35), Roberts (38). The thin 30–33 band looks like a gap until you read the names behind it, McCabe (29, $3.00M, 48 pts), Afinogenov (25, $4.50M) and Fischer (24, $3.70M) already bridge the jump. The real top-heavy line is money: those four veterans carry $18.30M, and three of them are on one-year deals.

**Belfour is the single biggest lever.** At 39 and $6.50M expiring with CONS 50, he is the most expensive asset on the sheet and the one most worth converting. Aebischer (26, $0.50M) and Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) are both young and expiring and can share the crease now, so trading Belfour for a pick before March frees $6.50M and hands the position to two players you can keep.

**Roberts and Svehla walk for nothing if you wait.** Roberts (38, $2.70M, 54 pts) and Svehla (36, $3.60M, 19 pts) are both expiring and both 35-plus; above-80 or near it, they fit the expiring-asset-for-a-pick mechanic. Moving them with Mogilny's 35-year age in mind thins the 34+ line without touching the 20–23 core.

**The July cluster is the actual cliff.** Seventeen contracts worth $28.60M expire in the same summer, and that group holds Gaborik (22, $1.10M, 67 pts), Richards (24, $1.00M, 50 pts), Nash (20, $1.20M), Kaberle (26, $1.90M) and the rest of the under-23 talent. If they all hit the market together you re-sign them against each other's rising prices. The fix is terms, not money: lock the five on 5–6 years, split the depth across 2–3.

**Chlup is the most urgent single signature.** He is 18, POTE 95, 23 pts in 34 games, on $2.34M with two years left, and still priced like a rookie. A full top-nine season erases that price, so a 5–6 year extension now is the cheapest star lock on the roster.

**The money leaves room.** Payroll $66.97M against revenue $70.20M and profit $25.53M, so there is no profit-driven reason to stand still. The constraint is the renewal wave, not today's payroll.

## Calendar

The deadline is 45 days away and Toronto sit 12 points clear of second place at 73 points; the question is what to buy, what to move before expiry, and how to survive seventeen expiring contracts in the same July.

**Deadline: buy.** The three stacked proposals from the January 14 report are the plan. They don't overlap in assets and net $4.80M in payroll relief if all three land. **Belfour** at $6.50M and 39 years old is the engine: the above-80-expiring mechanic makes him tradeable for a pick, and he must go before March whether or not the Chara deal executes. If OTT won't take the Belfour+R1 for Chara+Havlat, Belfour still moves for a second-rounder on his own. The Kovalchuk and Abid packages fill the top-six scoring and toughness gaps the coach has flagged; the December fallback (Jackman, Sillinger, Sutton) stays as insurance if ATL or OTT go quiet by mid-February.

**Chistov** (LW, 21, $1.10M, 0.33 pts/g in 27 games) is the asset going to ATL for Kovalchuk. He's a pick in the Kovalchuk package; if that deal dies, he's expendable at summer re-signing anyway given the Nash development path. **Holden** (C, 26, $1.20M) goes to PIT for Abid; if PIT decline, Holden is a depth centre who can be re-signed on a cheap two or moved for a late pick in July.

**Safronov** at 23, 3 games, 0 points, morale down 5 to 95: he's already the package-3 piece in the December fallback (Safronov+R4 for Sutton). Execute that fallback or move him somewhere else before March. The coach is right that sitting him further costs nothing but goodwill.

**Summer: stagger the seventeen.** $28.60M expiring at once is the single biggest roster-management problem in front of us. The split:

**5-6 year locks (stars and core, July 2005):** Gaborik (22, $1.10M), Richards (24, $1.00M), Nash (20, $1.20M), Kaberle (26, $1.90M), Upshall (21, $1.20M), Eminger (21, $1.20M), Colaiacovo (21, $1.10M). That's seven deals locking the young core at current rates before their value spikes.

**2-3 year deals (evaluation tier, July 2005):** Alexeev (23, $1.10M), Chistov if not traded, Smirnov (20, $0.40M), Tellqvist (25, $0.80M). Cheap term, re-evaluate in two years.

**Older players on 2 years (July 2005):** Roberts (38, $2.70M), Renberg (32, $2.00M), Svehla (36, $3.60M) if not traded. These three cost $8.30M combined; if any of them go at the deadline for picks, that's money back immediately.

**Goalies:** Aebischer (26, $0.50M, 2.62 GAA, 0.898 SV in 19 starts) re-signs on 3 years at $0.70-0.80M as the clear number one post-Belfour. Tellqvist (25, $0.80M) is the backup or the trade bait; his morale is not flagged so no urgency, but decide before July 1.

**Not renewing / move for value:** Belfour (goes at deadline). Svehla at $3.60M and 36 is the next candidate if his play drops; a 2-year re-sign at $2.50M is the generous case. Renberg at $2.00M and 32 is a rental who should be moved at the deadline if a taker exists, or let walk.

## League scan

The question this scan answers: who across the league fills Toronto's three real gaps (toughness at zero above 73, faceoffs with only Sundin above 80, top-six scoring depth) and sits on a club that will say yes. I ran toughness leaders, faceoff leaders, and high-potential players on losing clubs, then merged against what we already tracked. The result is a board that stacks cleanly without overlapping assets, and one sleeper nobody has flagged yet.

**Ramzi Abid** at 24, 56 pts in 44 GP, 87 TOUG, 87 CHKG, $400K expiring remains the single best value on the board. PIT are 12-21-5 with 14 expiring contracts. He solves toughness and adds a top-nine second-line scorer at the salary of a 13th forward. No change from the January 14 proposal: 3rd rounder plus Holden.

**Marc Savard** is new to this scan and the sleeper of the league scan. He is 27, 89 FACE, 48 pts in 43 GP, $1.00M expiring on ATL (13-24-2, 11 expiring). That grade and that point total at that price solves the faceoff gap and adds secondary scoring in one move. ATL have 11 expiring deals; they are in full rebuild and will deal him. He should go into the ATL conversation alongside Kovalchuk and Heatley as a cheaper add-on or alternative package.

**Mike Cammalleri** at 22 with POTE 98, 27 pts in 23 games (1.17 pts/g pace), 89 SPEE, 88 SHPW, $1.10M expiring is the best young player on a seller. LA are 13-20-5 with 13 expiring. The same LA roster holds **Alexander Frolov** at 22, POTE 96, 40 pts in 34 GP, 86 SPEE, 88 SHPW, $1.10M expiring. A double acquisition from LA fills the top six for the next five years. The December proposal (Holden plus DET 2nd for Cammalleri) should be extended to include Frolov if LA will do both.

**Mark Bell** at 24 is the purest toughness available: 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG, 90 SPEE, 82 ovr, $900K with two years left. CHI are 12-23-6 but profitable at $24.48M, and two years left means they are not forced. He is the fallback if Chara or Abid stalls. Do not spend a first or second on him.

**Matt Walker** at 24, $500K expiring, 95 TOUG, 93 CHKG on STL (10-24-3, 9 expiring) is absurd value for a checking defenceman. Five points in 33 games confirms he is not an option, but a 7th-pair blueliner who hits everything on a 35-point team is a playoff asset at $500K. This costs a late pick or nothing.

**Joe Nieuwendyk** at 95 FACE, 51 pts in 44 GP is the best faceoff man available by any measure. At 38 and $4.10M expiring on FLA (16-22-4, 18 expiring), he is a pure rental. If we need to win a playoff series in April, he is the answer; if we want him in October, he is not. **Craig Conroy** at 33, 91 FACE, 55 pts in 45 GP, $2.00M expiring on CGY (14-24-6) is the younger, cheaper version at 91 FACE. **Mike Sillinger** at 92 FACE, $1.80M expiring on PHX (16-23-4) is already in the December package. All three solve the same problem at different price and age points.

**Jay Bouwmeester** at 21, POTE 96, 78 ovr, 18 pts in 44 GP, 90 SPEE, $1.20M expiring on FLA (16-22-4, 18 expiring) is the best long-term defenceman available. FLA with 18 expiring deals are in full teardown. A 21-year-old already playing 44 games on a 40-point team with that profile is a franchise blueliner. This would cost a first or second rounder plus a prospect.

The existing three-package stack from January 14 (Belfour+R1 for Chara+Havlat, DET-2nd+Chistov for Kovalchuk, R3+Holden for Abid) still stands as the lead architecture. Savard slots into the ATL conversation at no extra cost. Cammalleri+Frolov is a separate negotiation from LA. Walker is a seventh-day target who costs nothing and should be picked up regardless of what else happens.

## Trade construction

The question this phase answers: which deadline packages do we propose, what do we give, what do we get, and why does each club across the table say yes. Toronto's gaps are toughness (zero above 73), faceoffs (only Sundin above 80), and top-six scoring depth beyond Gaborik. The board stacks three negotiations that don't overlap on assets, and Belfour's $6.50M expiring contract is the engine that opens the biggest one.

**Belfour** is the single most important decision on this sheet. At 39 with CONS 50, 18 GP, and Aebischer already at 2.62 GAA in 19 starts, he is a rental we are paying $6.50M for. The above-80 expiring mechanic means any club values him for a pick even without wanting him long-term. Giving him with our 1st-rounder converts the biggest liability on the roster into two players who fix two gaps at once.

**Abid** at $400K with 87 TOUG and 87 CHKG on a 56-point pace is the cheapest impact player in the league. PIT at 12-21-5 with 14 expiring deals cannot hold him. Holden is lined nowhere, played zero games, and costs $1.20M. The swap saves $800K and fills the left-side checking slot that the coach has flagged since December.

**Kovalchuk** at 78 points in 41 games, age 21, $1.10M expiring, is the highest-scoring player on a rebuilding club. ATL with 13-24-2 and 11 expiring deals face a choice: re-sign him at $5M+ next year or take a first-round asset plus a 95-potential 21-year-old now. Chistov's 0.33 pts/g in 31 games means the coach is done with him; he is the logical piece to send.

The three packages stack without double-spending: the 1st goes to OTT, the DET 2nd to ATL, the 3rd to PIT. Remaining picks are the TOR 4th and 5th, which leave room for Walker (STL, 95 TOUG, $500K expiring) as a late add-on at nothing.
